Before the court order, students had staged protests on campus demanding that the election be held as scheduled. The demonstration began around 10:15am at the university roundabout and later moved to Administrative Building-1, which the protesters locked until around 2:15pm.

At around 2:20pm, students blocked the Sylhet–Sunamganj highway, disrupting traffic in the area.

During the protests, students chanted slogans rejecting what they described as attempts to derail the election process. They also voiced opposition to a sit-in programme staged by Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal in front of the Election Commission headquarters over the Sucsu polls and other issues.

After a 28-year hiatus, the Sucsu election was scheduled for tomorrow (Tuesday).

title: US Embassy warns Bangladeshis against paying visa bond before interview
body:
The US Embassy today urged visa applicants not to pay any bond in advance, warning that early payments neither guarantee visa approval nor ensure safety from fraud.

“Paying early does not guarantee you a visa, and third-party sites can be scams,” the embassy said in a statement posted on its verified Facebook page.

It added that any payment made before a visa interview is non-refundable, while the bond will be returned only if the visa holder complies with its terms.

Starting January 21, Bangladeshi citizens approved for a B1/B2 (business or tourist)US visa will be required to pay a bond of up to $15,000. The requirement will not apply to those holding a valid B1/B2 visa issued before that date.

Earlier this month, the administration of US President Donald Trump added 25 more countries, including Bangladesh, to a list of nations whose citizens may be required to post bonds of up to $15,000 to enter the United States, Reuters reported on January 6, citing the US State Department website.

According to the website, citizens or nationals travelling on passports issued by any of the listed countries, if otherwise eligible for a B1/B2 visa, must post a bond of $5,000, $10,000, or $15,000. The amount will be determined at the time of the visa interview.

Applicants must agree to the bond terms and make payments through the US Treasury Department’s official online platform, Pay.gov, the state department said.

The list, which now includes 38 countries, consists largely of nations from Africa, Latin America, and South Asia. The policy for the newly added countries will take effect on January 21.

The US government said the bond requirement is intended to deter visitors from overstaying visas issued for tourism or business purposes.

title: Nahid, Patwary reply to show-cause notices over electoral code violations
body:
Nahid Islam, convener of the National Citizen Party, and its chief coordinator Nasiruddin Patwary have responded to the show-cause notices issued against them for alleged violations of the electoral code of conduct.

According to officials at the returning officer’s office, written replies were submitted on their behalf around 2:00pm today. Nahid submitted his reply first, followed later by Patwary. Representatives of the two leaders delivered the responses to the returning officer.

In their replies, the two leaders sought withdrawal of the show-cause notices and assured the authorities that they would refrain from violating the electoral code of conduct in future.

Officials at the RO’s office confirmed the matter to The Daily Star. However, the returning officer declined to make any immediate comment, the officials added.

The show-cause notices were issued over alleged violations of the electoral code of conduct ahead of the 13th parliamentary election.

Separate letters, signed yesterday by the Returning Officer and Dhaka Divisional Commissioner Sharaf Uddin Ahmed Chowdhury, asked both leaders to explain their actions. The matter was confirmed by Dhaka Additional Divisional Commissioner Azmul Haque.

The notices directed the NCP leaders to remove all billboards across the city by 9:30am today. They were also asked to explain why punitive action should not be taken against them for breaching election rules, with a deadline of 11:00am to submit their responses.

title: No floods, no silt: Farmers struggle as Brahmaputra chars miss seasonal floods
body:
For farmers living in the char (river island) areas along the Brahmaputra river, floods are both a curse and a blessing. For years, floodwaters have deposited silt [fine soil and sand carried by river water] on char farmlands, enriching the soil and ensuring good harvests at low cost.

This year, however, the familiar pattern changed as no floods occurred along the Brahmaputra. With no silt deposited, farmers are now being forced to use extra fertiliser, increasing production costs while uncertainty grows over expected yields.

Mansur Ali, 65, a farmer from Char Karai Barishal on the Brahmaputra riverbed in Chilmari upazila of Kurigram, said four out of his 12 bighas of cultivable land are slightly elevated.

Usually, floods naturally deposit silt on these lands, boosting soil fertility. But as there was no flood this year, no silt was deposited. As a result, he had to use additional fertiliser to prepare the land for cultivation -- something he had never done before.

Mansur said, “This is the first time in my life that I have not seen a flood. All these years, I have only seen floods as suffering. But this time, I am realising how big a blessing floods are for our land. Because there was no flood, no silt was deposited on the fields. That is why I have to use extra fertiliser. Even then, I am not sure whether I will get the expected yield.”

Other farmers in Char Karai Barishal shared similar concerns. Nadir Uddin Mondol, 70, Jahir Ali, 75, Abdul Kader, 65, and Jomir Uddin, 70, who own between 10 and 20 bighas of land each, said floods usually leave behind large amounts of fertile silt, reducing the need for fertilisers and pesticides.

Nadir said, “The silt that accumulates on the land during floods produces bumper crops. There is little need for fertilisers and pesticides. But this year, as there was no flood, no silt was deposited. As a result, costs have increased, yet the fear of lower yields remains.”

He added, “It is true that we did not face major suffering due to floods this year, but we are now facing a new crisis regarding crop production.”

The situation is the same in Char Montola. Abdur Rahman, 70, a farmer there, said no silt was deposited on his 15 bighas of land this year.

He said, “This time I am realising that floods are not just a curse but also a blessing.”

Shahidul Islam, 50, a farmer from Char Daikhawa in Ulipur upazila, said he was initially relieved that there was no flood, but later realised how important floods are for farming.

He said, “During floods, huge amounts of silt come with river water and settle on the land. Later, all kinds of crops grow well on that soil. But this year, due to the absence of silt, I have to spend an additional Tk 1,500 to Tk 2,000 per bigha on fertiliser. Even after spending so much, it is uncertain whether the expected yield will be achieved.”

Out of his 14 bighas of land, eight bighas received no silt this year.

Chan Mia. 60, a farmer from Char Parbati in Kurigram Sadar upazila, said floods are closely linked to the lives of char dwellers.

He said, “It is true that we suffer during floods. But this year, as there was no flood, life in the chars has been turned upside down. Crop cultivation is our main livelihood. Because silt accumulates on char lands, all kinds of crops can be grown. But this year, out of my 19 bighas of land, 10 bighas received no silt. I have to use extra fertiliser to prepare these lands. Now I understand that floods are not just suffering -- they are an important part of our lives.”

Deputy Director of the Kurigram Department of Agricultural Extension, Abdullah Al Mamun, said floods usually carry silt that improves soil fertility.

He said, “Almost all kinds of crops grow well on silt-laden soil, and there is little need for fertilisers and pesticides. But this year, as there was no flood along the Brahmaputra, silt was not deposited on most lands. There are more than one hundred thousand hectares of cultivable land on the Brahmaputra riverbed. To make silt-free land suitable for cultivation, farmers are having to use extra fertiliser, putting them under additional financial pressure.”

Executive Engineer of Kurigram Water Development Board Rakibul Hasan said floods usually occur in char areas when the Brahmaputra flows above the danger level.

“As the river water remained far below the danger level this year, there was no flood along the Brahmaputra. The absence of floods is an example of the negative impacts of climate change.”

title: JnU teachers form human chain demanding separate pay scale
body:
Members of the Jagannath University Teachers’ Association today formed a human chain to press for a separate pay scale for university teachers, officers and staff, alleging "discrimination" and "disregard" by the National Pay Commission.

The programme was held in front of the university’s Shaheed Minar at 11:00am.

Speaking at the human chain, Dr Mostafa Hasan, a professor of social work, said teachers in neighbouring countries with lower per capita income enjoy better pay and status than university teachers in Bangladesh.

“Why should our teachers lag behind those countries? Following their example, our teachers should be placed in a dignified and respectable position. We hope the government will bring reforms in this regard,” he said.

General Secretary of the association Prof Dr Imranul Haque said there are three teachers among the government advisers.

“We want to know how such a decision could be taken while you are in those positions. We will submit our demands to the government in writing,” he added.

Association President Prof Dr Rais Uddin said a sub-committee on university teachers’ pay had proposed three terms of reference: ensuring meritorious individuals enter the teaching profession, retaining talent within the country, and encouraging research and innovation.

“None of these have been accepted,” he said.

Addressing the interim government, he questioned whether it truly wants talented individuals to join university teaching and strengthen research and innovation.

title: Two held for cheating in RU ‘C’ unit admission test
body:
Two candidates were held while attempting to cheat during the “C” unit undergraduate (honours) admission test for the 2025-26 academic session at Rajshahi University (RU).

They were identified as Dibya Jyoti Saha and Shams Azmain.

They were nabbed from Jagadish Chandra Bose Building and Rabindranath Academic Building on the university campus during two separate shifts of the test.

Both examinees were later taken to the university proctor’s office.

Dibya allegedly used a mobile phone to take photographs of the question paper and tried to find answers using an AI application, according to the proctor’s office.

Proctor Prof Mahbubur Rahman said the other examinee, Azmain, also confessed to entering the examination hall with a mobile phone to look for answers.

Two more candidates were detained in Dhaka for cheating on the same day, added the proctor.

For the second consecutive year, Rajshahi University is conducting its admission tests simultaneously at centres outside the campus, including Dhaka, Chattogram, Khulna, Rangpur and Barishal. The “C” unit admission tests took place today at 11:00am and 3:00pm.

title: Tarique Rahman, family attend civic memorial honouring Khaleda Zia
body:
A civic memorial meeting in honour of former BNP chairperson and former prime minister, Khaleda Zia, began shortly after 2:30pm today at the South Plaza of the Jatiya Sangsad Bhaban in Dhaka.

BNP Chairman Tarique Rahman attended the event along with his wife Zubaida Rahman and daughter Zaima Rahman. Shamila Rahman, wife of Khaleda Zia's younger son Arafat Rahman, and other family members were also present.

Senior BNP leaders, including members of the party's standing committee, joined the programme.

Diplomats from various countries stationed in Bangladesh also attended the event.

Entry to the venue was restricted to invited guests only, with invitation cards sent in advance.

Members of various law enforcement agencies, including the army, police, Rapid Action Battalion (Rab), Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB), Coast Guard, and Ansar, have been deployed to ensure security.

Bangladesh's first female prime minister and a lasting political icon, Khaleda Zia, died on December 30 last year in a Dhaka hospital after a long bout of health complications.

The 79-year-old BNP chief had been suffering from a number of complications for a long time.

She was laid to rest at Zia Udyan with state honours the following day.

title: Inqilab Moncho holds protest demanding justice for Hadi
body:
Inqilab Moncho today held a demonstration demanding justice for its slain spokesperson, Sharif Osman Bin Hadi.

The protesters organised a procession from the central mosque premises of Dhaka University after Juma prayers. During the demonstration, they chanted slogans including: “We want justice,” “Lal sobujer potakay, Hadi tomay dekha jay”, “Amra sobai Hadi hobo, juge juge lore jabo”, “Tumi ke, Ami ke, Hadi, Hadi”, and “Delhi na Dhaka, Dhaka, Dhaka”.

A Dhaka court yesterday directed the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) to carry out further investigation into Hadi’s murder case.

Dhaka Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Jashita Islam passed the order after the complainant expressed dissatisfaction with the initial investigation and submitted a no-confidence motion against the charge sheet, requesting a further probe.

The court also ordered the submission of the investigation report by January 20, said Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) Deputy Commissioner of Prosecution Miah Mohammad Ashis Bin Hasan.

Osman Hadi, who was also a prospective candidate for the Dhaka-8 constituency, was shot in the head on December 12 last year in Paltan.

He was later airlifted to Singapore for advanced treatment, where he died on December 18.

title: Prolonged cold wave batters Panchagarh, slashes incomes of daily wage earners
body:
The ongoing cold wave sweeping across the northern region, particularly Panchagarh, has intensified the suffering of disadvantaged communities, while daily wage earners are facing declining incomes as adverse weather conditions force them to reduce their working hours.

As Panchagarh’s Tetulia upazila recorded the country’s lowest temperature for the eighth consecutive day today, this correspondent spoke to people from different sections of the area.

They expressed difficulties in coping with the prolonged cold spell.

Workers Taherul Islam and Nazirul Islam of Buraburi Balabari village in the upazila, who earn their livelihoods by extracting stones from the Mahananda River, said they have been forced to cut their working hours due to adverse weather.

Usually, they work from 8:00am to 5:00pm throughout the year. However, for more than a week now, they have been going into the river only after 10:00am and wrapping up work by 3:00pm, as cold winds continue to blow throughout the day.

They said they earn between Tk 800 and Tk 1,100 a day if they can work for eight to nine hours. But with shortened working hours, their daily earnings have dropped to around Tk 400.

Shafiqul Islam, a rickshaw-van puller from Aziznagar area, said it has become increasingly difficult to pull his van amid the cold weather. He said he can work for four to five hours during the daytime, but it is almost impossible to stay on the road in the early morning and evening.

Apart from livelihood challenges, poor people -- especially children and the elderly -- are bearing the brunt of the prolonged cold spell.

Amena Bewa, 72, of Sardarpara village said surviving the cold has become increasingly difficult.

“During the daytime, I somehow manage by sitting in the sun. But nights are unbearable. Even after wrapping myself in two or three blankets and a katha, I can't stay warm,” she said.

To support cold-stricken poor people, the government and various non-government organisations have been distributing blankets and warm clothes, though the supply remains inadequate compared to demand.

Contacted, Afroz Shaheen Qhosru, upazila nirbahi officer of Tetulia, said 3,500 blankets have already been distributed among people, with around 400 more in the pipeline.

Tetulia recorded the country’s lowest temperature for the eighth consecutive day today, with the mercury dropping to 8.5 degrees Celsius at 9:00am today.

Meteorological officials say icy winds sweeping down from the Himalayan region are intensifying the cold spell across northern Bangladesh, particularly in the districts of Panchagarh and Thakurgaon.

According to forecasters, the conditions are expected to persist, with no significant change likely over the next few days, prolonging discomfort for residents in the region.

Meanwhile, hospitals in the districts have reported an increase in patients, particularly children and elderly people suffering from cold-related ailments.

Agriculture officials advised farmers to take precautionary measures to protect crops, especially Boro seedbeds, which have already been affected in some areas.

title: Govt appoints Khalilur Rahman, Faiz Ahmad Taiyeb, Akhtar Ahmed as Biman directors
body:
The interim government has appointed three key officials of the administration to the board of directors of the state-run Biman Bangladesh Airlines, according to a gazette notification issued by the Ministry of Civil Aviation and Tourism yesterday.

Dr Khalilur Rahman, national security adviser and high representative for the Rohingya issue; Faiz Ahmad Taiyeb, special assistant to the chief adviser at the Ministry of Posts, Telecommunications and Information Technology (with the rank of state minister); and Akhtar Ahmed, senior secretary of the Bangladesh Election Commission, have been made the three new directors, the notification said.

The gazette added that the appointments were made in the public interest and would take effect immediately.

The order to include them on the board less than a month ahead of the February 12 election has raised questions among insiders in the aviation industry.

Earlier, the government had appointed Commerce Adviser Sk Bashir Uddin as chairman of the Biman board.

Previously, on August 26 last year, Sk Bashir Uddin -- who also serves as adviser to the Ministry of Commerce -- was appointed chairman of Biman’s board while serving as adviser to the Ministry of Civil Aviation. At the time, many raised questions about his appointment as chairman of a company under his own ministry, saying it amounted to a conflict of interest. The adviser, however, rejected the allegations.

Aviation expert Kazi Wahidul Alam told The Daily Star that he was “out and out surprised” by the government’s decision to include Khalilur, Taiyeb and Akhtar as directors of the Biman board at the fag-end of the interim government’s tenure.

“In my view there might be several agenda of the interim government including strengthening relations with Boeing, from which Biman is going to buy aircraft,” he added.

title: Our record speaks for itself: Shafiqul Alam tells Al Jazeera
body:
Weeks ahead of the national election, Al Jazeera interviewed Shafiqul Alam, press secretary to the chief adviser of Bangladesh, regarding the country’s current socio-political situation, the election, and related issues.

In the interview published today, Shafiqul was asked about the upcoming polls and the challenges involved.

“The government is in control. If you look at the past week alone, there were at least three major political events -- massive events -- and all three broke records in terms of crowd size. Our security forces managed to keep things peaceful and hold those events according to expectations,” he responded.

Regarding thelaw and order situation, when Al Jazeera referred to the murder of youth leader and Inqilab Moncho spokesperson Sharif Osman Bin Hadi, as well as two prominent media houses being set on fire, Shafiqul said, “There were attacks by mobs, and we sent our troops to prevent them. Unfortunately, they couldn’t prevent the attacks. They rescued journalists who were trapped in The Daily Star building, but they couldn’t stop the attack itself.

“We sent police and military there. We are investigating why they failed to take action.”

Al Jazeera also referred to a remark by Nurul Kabir, editor of New Age, who was assaulted by a mob outside the media offices and alleged that the government had allowed the incident to happen.

Shafiqul rejected the allegation, calling it “an absolute lie”.

“He should provide evidence before making such allegations. This is nonsense. If he believes part of the government was involved, he should show proof. We sent police. We sent the military,” he said.

“Dozens of people have been arrested. We reviewed video footage and arrested almost everyone identified,” he added.

Al Jazeera further mentioned comments by the UN special rapporteur on freedom of expression, who said the mob attacks were a consequence of the interim government’s failure to address impunity. Shafiqul rejected the claim, saying, “Look at our records. We’ve been in power for only 17 months. Go to the police and check crime records over that period.”

“This is one of the finest cabinets we’ve ever had -- academics, top former bureaucrats, retired senior military officers, diplomats and human rights activists,” he added.

Regarding the government’s decision to bar the Awami League from contesting the national polls, the CA press secretary said, “They have robbed themselves of the right to be a political party… It’s not only security forces who were shooting people. Awami League activists -- their student wing, their youth wing -- also had guns, some of which were supplied by security forces. They were killing people.”

Responding to Human Rights Watch’s claim that many detentions of individuals allegedly connected to the Awami League appeared arbitrary and politically motivated, Shafiqul said, “There are valid reasons to detain these people. There are charges against them. Most of them are in jail because of the charges they face.”

“The chief adviser has met dozens of heads of government and hundreds of diplomats. Not a single foreign national came here and said, ‘Why don’t you lift the ban?’ Because they’ve seen what kind of character the Awami League had when Hasina was in power,” he added.

“We have not banned the party. We have banned the activities of the party,” he said.

Asked about the cancellation of the decision to recruit music and physical education teachers for primary schools, reportedly following pressure from Islamist groups, Shafiqul said the move was taken because it was impossible to implement, not due to Islamist pressure.

Asked about attacks on minorities in Bangladesh, including the burning to death of a Hindu man accused of blasphemy, Dipu Das, the press secretary said the government had responded adequately and claimed that some reports of widespread communal violence were exaggerated or misleading, particularly in sections of the Indian media.

He said the killing of Dipu Das was treated as a hate crime and that law enforcement agencies had investigated the incident, leading to several arrests.

Shafiqul argued that overall crime data did not indicate a breakdown of law and order, urging critics to examine official statistics. He said the number of murders, rapes and other serious crimes remained largely consistent with the previous year, with only slight increases in some categories.

He also dismissed concerns that mob violence had increased due to a sweeping amnesty granted by the interim government, saying the amnesty applied only to those who participated in the uprising and not to individuals involved in mob violence or acts of revenge.

Turning to relations with India, Shafiqul said there was no diplomatic crisis despite ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina remaining in exile in New Delhi. He claimed that since the interim government took office, Indian media outlets had circulated misinformation portraying Bangladesh as undergoing a violent Islamist takeover.

On the issue of extradition, Shafiqul said Bangladesh had formally communicated its position to India under an existing extradition treaty and remained confident that Hasina would eventually be returned. He described her as a “notorious mass murderer”.

Addressing allegations that Hasina, while in India, had incited supporters to carry out violent acts in Bangladesh, Shafiqul said intelligence agencies were monitoring her communications, including audio recordings circulating on social media, and stressed that investigations were ongoing.

As the election approaches and the interim government prepares to hand over power, Shafiqul defended the record of Chief Adviser Dr Muhammad Yunus, saying he had taken office amid severe economic disruption and widespread public anger.

“He inherited a broken economy,” Shafiqul said, comparing the situation to a major natural disaster. He credited Yunus with restoring stability and said history would judge his leadership favourably.

“Our record speaks for itself,” he said. “The economy has recovered. Law and order have improved. Peace and stability have been restored.”

Shafiqul also said that the chief adviser’s approval rating never fell below 70 percent during the government’s 17-month tenure.

title: Former DNCC chief heat officer quizzed by ACC
body:
The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) has interrogated Bushra Afreen, daughter of former Dhaka North City Corporation (DNCC) mayor Atiqul Islam and the city’s first chief heat officer.

According to ACC Public Relations Officer Aktarul Islam, Bushra was questioned at the commission’s headquarters today from 9:30am for about one and a half hours.

She declined to speak to journalists after leaving the office.

Following the political change of power after the July movement, the ACC has been conducting inquiries and investigations into corruption allegations against Atiqul, who is currently in jail after being arrested. At the same time, on January 7, a court imposed a travel ban on his wife, Shaila Shagufta Islam, and daughter Bushra.

Atiqul was arrested on October 16, 2024, from the Mohakhali DOHS in Dhaka.

title: Chhatra Dal protests at CU, demands resignation of VC and pro-VCs
body:
Bangladesh Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal leaders and activists of Chittagong University (CU) staged a sit-in programme today, demanding the resignation of the vice-chancellor and two pro-vice-chancellors over allegations of nepotism and irregularities in recruitment.

The programme began around 10:00am in front of the main gate of the university's administrative building and continued till the filing of this report at 4:30 pm.

Due to the protest, Pro-Vice-Chancellor (Admin) Prof Kamal Uddin was initially unable to enter the administrative building through the main gate.

During the sit-in, protesters chanted various slogans, including “Dalali aar korish na, pither chamra thakbe na,” “Proshashoner dalalera hushiar shabdhan,” “Shikkhar naame boishommo cholbe na,” “Shikkhar naame niyog cholbe na,” “Obilombe proshashoner podotyag chai,” “Quota na medha, medha medha.”

Speaking at the programme, Chhatra Dal's CU unit General Secretary Abdullah Al-Noman alleged that partisan and regional considerations had dominated recruitment over the past one and a half years.

"All illegal recruitment must be cancelled immediately. The VC, pro-VCs, and the registrar must resign. Otherwise, we will be forced to launch a tougher programme. This administration has no sense of shame or accountability," he said.

Around 4:30pm, the protest was postponed after Noman declared a 48-hour ultimatum for the resignation of the VC and pro-VCs.

Organising Secretary Sajjad Hossain Hridoy claimed that more qualified candidates had been overlooked in favour of the daughter of a pro-vice-chancellor.

"The university must disclose the recruitment process publicly," he said.

Earlier, allegations surfaced that 153 staff members were to be recruited in various categories. However, the university administration rejected the claim and issued a press release stating that a total of 113 staff members had been recruited.

title: Ali Riaz dismisses claims July charter will remove 1971 references from Constitution
body:
Professor Ali Riaz, special assistant to the Chief Adviser Prof Mohammad Yunus, today clarified that the proposed “July charter” contains no provisions to remove references to 1971 or the phrase “Bismillah” from the Constitution, dismissing such claims as “motivated propaganda.”

“A certain quarter is spreading rumours that if the July charter is passed, 1971 will be erased from the Constitution and ‘Bismillah’ removed. This is entirely false,” he said while speaking as chief guest at a divisional Imam conference at Chattogram Stadium.

“Those making these claims are either misunderstanding the charter or deliberately spreading misinformation.”

Reflecting on the past 15 years, he said the country had been governed under a system that granted the prime minister virtually absolute power.

“The prime minister’s authority was limitless. Even a convicted murderer, whose death sentence was upheld by all courts, was pardoned by the president on the prime minister’s advice. All political parties now agree that this system must change. That is why the July charter is necessary,” he added.

Ali Riaz emphasised that the charter was “written in blood” during the July uprising and stressed the collective responsibility of citizens to uphold it.

He also outlined the significance of the upcoming referendum in decentralising power, noting that while Bangladesh held referendums 35 years ago, much of the current population has never participated in one.

“This referendum differs from those under Zia or Ershad, which were largely about seeking confidence in an individual. This vote concerns a charter reached through consensus by over 30 political parties,” he said.

Key reforms linked to a “Yes” vote include reducing the prime minister’s absolute power, decentralising the judiciary, ensuring transparency in the Public Service Commission (PSC) and Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC), establishing an Upper House in Parliament for proportional representation, and reforming presidential elections and government spending.

He added that the ACC had previously been used to suppress opposition parties.

“Our responsibility is to establish a system where no mother has to lose her child again. This is the mandate given to us by our brave martyrs and the people,” he said.

He concluded that while the Liberation of 1971 and the 2024 uprising were decades apart, both aimed to achieve the same goal: the establishment of justice.

title: No legal bar to Pabna-1 and 2 elections on February 12: SC
body:
The Appellate Division of the Supreme Court today ruled that there is no legal obstacle to holding elections in the Pabna-1 and Pabna-2 constituencies on February 12.

The polls in the two constituencies will be held according to the boundaries set out in the gazette issued by the Election Commission on September 4 last year following the delimitation.

Accordingly, the apex court said Sathia Upazila will fall under the Pabna-1 constituency, while Sujanagar and Bera upazilas together will form the Pabna-2 constituency, court sources said.

A four-member bench of the Appellate Division, headed by Chief Justice Zubayer Rahman Chowdhury, passed the order after hearing a leave-to-appeal petition against a High Court verdict that had declared illegal the EC gazette notification of September 4 last year, which had attached four unions and Bera municipality of Pabna-1 to Pabna-2.

The SC also stayed the HC verdict till disposal of the appeal against the judgement, sources at the court said.

Barrister Muhammad Nazibur Rahman Momen, Jamaat-e-Islami candidate for Pabna-1, filed the leave to appeal petition on Monday, seeking an order directing the Election Commission to lift its stay on election activities in the two Pabna constituencies.

Barrister Imran Siddiq appeared for Nazibur Rahman during hearing of the leave to appeal petition today.

On January 10, citing an Appellate Division order related to constituency delimitation for the 13th parliamentary election, the EC decided to stay election-related activities in Pabna-1 and Pabna-2 until further instructions.

Earlier, on January 5, the Appellate Division stayed the amended gazette notification issued by the EC on December 24 last year, which redefined the boundaries of the two constituencies.

The stay order will remain in force until the hearing of the leave to appeal filed against the HC judgment, the SC had said.

title: Reforms remain superficial and thus, fail: Debapriya
body:
CPD Distinguished Fellow Debapriya Bhattacharya today said reform efforts in Bangladesh have repeatedly failed because they focused on surface-level institutional changes while ignoring the need to organise social and economic forces that could defend democracy.

“Changing the superstructure alone cannot bring a new political settlement. Unless the forces that support democracy are organised and empowered, reforms will always be captured by vested interests and traditional politics,” he said.

Referring to past reform initiatives, Debapriya said political actors had prioritised constitutional changes, governance, and administrative behaviour without addressing deeper socioeconomic power relations at a briefing on policy recommendations and suggested national programmes for the next government.

“We have had caretaker governments before. Those arrangements were also dismantled. So the question is not whether reforms are necessary, but whether there is a social force capable of protecting them,” he said.

He said the promise of a new political settlement ultimately failed because its proponents did not mobilise citizens and stakeholders beyond politicians.

“There was dialogue, but it was largely among political leaders. There was no national awakening, no broad-based participation of stakeholders to carry this idea forward,” he said.

As a result, he said, many of those who claimed to be architects of a new settlement became part of the old one by entering expensive electoral politics.

“They joined the old system, thinking they could change it from within, while vested interests regrouped. Business elites returned, politicians resurfaced, and the bureaucracy came back stronger,” he said.

Debapriya said the bureaucracy has historically been the strongest guardian of the old political settlement and regained influence due to institutional weaknesses.

He also criticised the current interim government, saying it failed to demonstrate the openness, capacity, and stakeholder engagement needed to implement meaningful reforms.

“The interim government spoke of reform, but could not create the conditions required to carry it out. Eventually, it became hostage in many cases to a small and aggressive group,” he said.

This failure, he added, has raised serious questions about whether the interim administration can conduct a neutral and credible election.

“The question now is whether they can even hold a proper election impartially. That concern is real,” he said.

On media freedom, Debapriya said successive governments ignored key recommendations of the media commission, including ensuring financial transparency of media houses.

“If media owners cannot ensure transparency in their own finances, their moral authority to demand accountability from others becomes uncertain,” he said.

He also criticised professional media organisations for failing to play an independent role due to political divisions.

“When media professionals are politically divided, their collective voice loses credibility, and they cannot protect their profession,” he said.

Debapriya stressed the need to ensure fair wages, incentives, and professional

development and a pressure-free working environment for journalists.

“Media workers must be able to publish their work without fear or pressure. Their safety and professional dignity must be ensured,” he said.

However, responding to a question about why media safety receives special attention, Debapriya said media freedom cannot be separated from broader citizen security.

“If citizens are not safe, media workers cannot be safe either. Media freedom exists within the larger framework of democracy and civic rights,” he said.

He also acknowledged the role of citizens, saying civil society had not always taken sufficient risks to defend democratic values.

“We spoke well, but we did not monitor enough. We did not always return to the streets when needed. We too remained within old patterns of behaviour,” he said.

Debapriya said the experience of failed reforms must be used to genuinely change the political settlement in the future.

He said a new brand of politics is required, not just words, but actions that match those words. "That is the lesson we must carry forward.”

title: Students block Dhaka roads for 2nd day demanding central university ordinance
body:
Students of proposed Dhaka Central University blocked Science Lab and Technical intersections this afternoon, demanding the issuance of an ordinance for the university.

Due to the blockade for the second consecutive day, vehicular movement through the Science Lab intersection remains halted, said eyewitnesses.

Anwar Hossain Khan, inspector (investigation) of New Market Police Station, said the students blocked the intersection around 1:00pm.

Witnesses said the students of Dhaka College and Eden Mohila College brought out a procession from the campus and blocked the street. They chanted slogans in favour of the issuance of the ordinance.

Students of Government Bangla College blocked the Technical Intersection around 1:00pm today with the same demand, bringing vehicular movement in the area to a complete halt, said SM Jakaria, officer-in-charge of Darussalam Police Station.

Witnesses said police attempted to divert vehicles to alternative routes following the blockade.

Meanwhile, social media users warned others to avoid roads blocked by the students, with many seeking updates on traffic conditions in different parts of the city.

Yesterday,Dhaka experienced severe traffic congestion for at least five hours due to protests and blockadesat key points by the students of the seven college and Tejgaon College, causing immense suffering for commuters throughout the day.

Tejgaon College students blocked the Farmgate area yesterday, demanding justice for their fellow student, while students of seven colleges blocked Science Lab, Technical Intersection, and Tanti Bazar in Old Dhaka, demanding the issuance of an ordinance for Dhaka Central University.

Before leaving Science Lab yesterday, the students announced to block roads at the three points today again.

title: Deforestation threatens Sylhet's ancient culinary heritage
body:
Sylhet’s centuries-old culinary tradition, Chungapura pitha, is on the verge of extinction as essential ingredients and customs fade from the region.

Once a vibrant winter-night celebration in rural areas featuring straw fires that burned through the night, this cherished practice has nearly disappeared. The traditional dish was accompanied by lightly spiced fried fish–locally known as ‘maas biran’, featuring varieties such as rui, katla, chital, boal, koi, and magur from local fish fairs or nearby haors and rivers.

Traditionally, no guest or newlywed son-in-law would leave a household without being served Chungapura pitha, fish curry, and coconut pitha. Failing to do so was considered deeply shameful.

However, these customs are now fading fast.

The primary reason is the scarcity of slanted bamboo and binni variety rice. Bamboo, once abundant in the Patharia Hills of Barlekha, Lathi Tila of Juri, Rajnagar, Kamalganj, Chungabari, tea gardens, and the surrounding hill tract, has drastically diminished.

Local journalist, Salahuddin Subho, said rampant deforestation caused by illegal logging, land grabbing, and hill cutting has nearly wiped-out bamboo groves. Bamboo is now rare and expensive in local markets.

Chungapura pitha cannot be prepared without this specific bamboo variant, which contains a natural oily substance preventing it from burning, whilst its high moisture content allows the pitha to cook evenly. Preparing it also requires large quantities of straw for burning, he added.

Praneet Debnath, who visited Munshibazar in Kamalganj upazila to buy bamboo for making this pitha, said: “These items are no longer readily available. You might find small quantities only during Paush Sankranti. Ten or fifteen years ago, bamboo sticks were everywhere. Now, they are disappearing with time. My family asked me to bring bamboo to make pitha, but I had to search several markets. Finally, found a small supply in Munshibazar.”

Local writer and poet, Sajjadul Haque Swapan from Kamalganj, echoed similar concerns, “Inside the bamboo lies a hidden delicacy–rich in taste and tradition. Chungapura pitha is not just food; it is an ancient heritage of Sylhet. However, slanted bamboo has become extremely rare. What once flourished is now almost extinct.”

title: Girl hit by stray bullet from Myanmar put on life support at NINS
body:
A nine-year-old girl from Cox’s Bazar, who was struck by a stray bullet fired from Myanmar on Sunday, has been placed on life support at the National Institute of Neurosciences and Hospital (NINS) in Dhaka.

"Her condition is still very critical, and she is under observation at the Intensive Care Unit (ICU)," Humayun Kabir Himu, an associate professor at NINS, and her uncle, Shawkat Ali, told The Daily Star today.

Huzaifa Afnan, a class-3 student from the Teschi Bridge area of Whykong union, was shot during intense clashes between the Arakan Army and Rohingya armed groups inside Myanmar.

She was rushed to Chattogram Medical College Hospital and later shifted to NINS last night after doctors at CMCH failed to remove the bullet lodged in her throat.

Humayun said the bullet remained stuck in her throat, but she suffered a stroke as it damaged the veins that supply blood to the brain.

This also increased pressure on her brain, and she was put on mechanical ventilation (life support), he said, adding that she had been given medication to reduce the pressure.

She is very young and is showing some response -- two positive signs -- but nothing can be said for certain at this stage, Humayun said. The next procedure may be carried out once the pressure on her brain eases, he added.

A board led by NINS Director Prof Kazi Gias Uddin Ahmed is overseeing her treatment. No decision has yet been taken about sending her abroad for better treatment.

title: 'Let them come with regular visas, not on arrival'
body:
Bangladesh has suspended the on-arrival visa facility for all eligible countries to prevent "any untoward environment" in the country during the elections.

“We have been instructed because untoward incidents may be created during the elections…unexpected people may come here. They should not come here all of a sudden,” Foreign Adviser Touhid Hossain told journalists at the foreign ministry today.

“We are not stopping visas. Let them come with regular visas, not on arrival,” he said when asked about the suspension of on-arrival visas from January 15 to February 15.

Earlier on Monday, the Ministry of Home Affairs issued guidelines to streamline the entry procedures of foreigners while maintaining security and effective monitoring during the election period.

According to the order, existing visa policies must be strictly followed when issuing all types of visas, including visas on arrival. The verification of required documents and coordination among concerned agencies should also be strengthened, it said.

On the recent conflicts in Rakhine and its spillover into Bangladesh, Touhid said the ministry summoned the Myanmar envoy and protested the incident of firing that injured a child in Teknaf and sought to prevent any such incident in the future.

He said Myanmar government does not recognise the rebel group as a legal entity and thus Bangladesh cannot formally communicate with it.

He said the problem began long ago and is not likely to end anytime soon.

On the reports of Bangladesh and China working on signing a military drone factory in Bangladesh, the adviser said Bangladesh's military capacity needs to be developed, and efforts are underway to achieve this.

“We will not do anything so that the relations with any country deteriorates. We will make a balance,” he said.

title: ‘Act before any incident happens’: DMP issues strict pre-election directives
body:
Senior officials of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) have instructed field-level officers to step up intelligence gathering and take preventive action against those suspected of trying to create disorder ahead of the13th national election and referendum“before any incident happens”.

The field officials were also instructed to coordinate duty with magistrates and act early if there are signs of trouble around polling centres.

The instructions were given during the DMP’s monthly crime review meeting at the Bangladesh Police Auditorium in Rajarbagh today. At least four officers, who were present at the meeting, later confirmed the development to The Daily Star.

An officer, present in the meeting, requesting anonymity, said, “One of the main directives was to perform duty in coordination with magistrates. If anyone wants to commit a crime or cause disturbance, action has to be taken. If it seems someone may try to create a gathering at a polling centre or obstruct the process, measures should be taken in advance.”

The officer said the senior officials also stressed intelligence-led policing.

“Intelligence should be collected about what fascist elements are trying to do, and action should be taken against them before an incident occurs by anticipating their moves in advance,” he said.

“Then, police were told to use body-worn cameras and to ensure they do so properly. Everyone will use body cameras,” the officer said.

The officer also said officers-in-charge of police stations were instructed to avoid comments that could be construed as partisan, and to stay away from social media activity that might influence the public.

Addressing the meeting, DMP Commissioner SM Sazzat Ali told officers to rise above party lines and deliver what he described as a flawless election.

Police must ensure that no allegation is raised against any member during the election, as the polls would “remain part of history,” he said.

The commissioner also warned that violations of the election code of conduct could create risks to candidates’ security, and asked police to monitor whether the code is being followed properly.

He said police must also remain vigilant so that any banned organisation cannot disrupt the election environment. No one should be allowed to exploit any incident for political gain, he added.

At the same meeting, Additional Police Commissioner (Admin) Md Sarwar, also an additional inspector general of police, said all officers assigned to election duty must perform their responsibilities in line with the election code of conduct.

Additional Police Commissioner (Crime and Operations) SN Md Nazrul Islam said that miscreants would be identified and brought under legal action to keep the law-and-order situation normal during the election.

During the monthly crime meeting, the DMP commissioner also awarded officials of different ranks in several categories in recognition of their work in maintaining law and order, controlling crime, and ensuring public safety in Dhaka in December.

DMP senior officials were present at the conference, along with 50 police stations OCs and zonal assistant commissioners.

title: Dhaka-13 returning officer serves show-cause notice to Mamunul Haque
body:
The Dhaka-13 constituency returning officer today issued a show-cause notice to Bangladesh Khelafat Majlis candidate Maulana Md Mamunul Haque over allegedly violating the electoral code of conduct ahead of the 13th National Parliamentary Election.

In the notice, Mamunul was asked to submit a written explanation within three days over an allegation of campaigning three weeks before the polling day, in breach of the code of conduct for political parties and candidates.

The letter was issued by Dhaka-13 Returning Officer and Dhaka Regional Election Officer Md Yunus Ali.

Citing media reports, the letter stated that on January 12 at around 5:00 pm, Mamunul distributed leaflets among the public outside the Election Commission building.

Meanwhile, a press release by Khelfat Majlish today said that Mamunul didn't conduct any electoral campaign in front of EC's headquarters, neither for himself nor for any candidate on that day.

The statement said that Mamunul was providing his opinion and campaigning in favour of the "Yes" vote for the referendum.

Mamunul said in the statement that taking a position in favour of "Yes" or "No" in a referendum does not fall under election campaigning for any parliamentary candidate or symbol.

title: Two shots fired in Dhaka’s Badda targeting housing company office, not Nahid’s election office: Police
body:
Authorities have dismissed rumours circulating on social media that miscreants fired shots at the election office of National Citizen Party (NCP) Convener Nahid Islam in Dhaka’s Badda.

Police clarified today that the incident targeted the office of a housing company instead.

A rumour spread on social media this afternoon claiming there was a shooting at Nahid Islam’s election office. NCP said that shots were targeted at an office beside their local organisational office, not an election office.

Azharul Islam, inspector (operations) of Badda Police Station, told The Daily Star that police visited the site after receiving the report around 9:00pm on Tuesday night. “Upon visiting, I learned the incident actually happened in the afternoon. No formal complaint has been filed so far,” he said.

Md Asaduzzaman, assistant commissioner of Dhaka Metropolitan Police’s Badda Zone, said two shots were fired at the office of a housing company in north Badda on Tuesday.

He said that until last November, the site had housed an NCP office. “It cannot be said that the shooting targeted the NCP office,” he added.

Clarifying the confusion regarding the office location, NCP Dhaka City (North) Joint Convener Omar Faruk explained the layout of the premises where the shooting occurred.

“The office consists of two spaces separated by a glass partition. One section is used by the NCP, while the building owner uses the other," he told The Daily Star.

“To access the premises, one must enter through the section used by the NCP. Although the bullet struck the glass partition on the owner’s side, the shooter had to enter through the NCP office area to fire the shot," he said.

Addressing claims that the office was inactive, Faruk noted, “Our members regularly used the space for organisational work. It is well-known locally as the NCP’s Ward 38 office.”

He further clarified, “This is not an electoral office for Nahid Islam. His election office is located separately in Aftabnagar, opposite East West Medical College.”

title: ACC raids Chittagong University over recruitment irregularities
body:
The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) today conducted a raid at Chittagong University (CU) to probe allegations of irregularities and nepotism in the recruitment of teachers and officers amid mounting criticism over recent appointments.

The drive was carried out from 12:00pm to 3:00pm at the office of Pro-Vice Chancellor Prof Dr Shamim Uddin at the university’s administrative building.

ACC Assistant Director and team leader Sayed Alam said the operation was launched based on complaints regarding several recruitment processes carried out during the tenure of Vice Chancellor Prof Dr Muhammad Yeahia Akhter.

“We are reviewing various recruitment-related documents. In the case of the Farsi Department, preliminary records suggest that the appointment was made without a recommendation from the planning committee,” Sayed told reporters.

However, he said the marksheets could not be found, making it difficult at this stage to conclusively determine whether the recruitment process was lawful.

He added that documents related to appointments made at the university’s 565th syndicate meeting were also being scrutinised.

“If necessary, expert opinions will be sought, and a report will be submitted to the commission within the next 48 hours,” he said.

Responding to allegations that between 100 and 150 people were appointed, Sayed said, “Eighteen teachers were appointed at the latest syndicate meeting. Not all of these were fresh appointments; some were regularisations. The exact number of total appointments can be confirmed only after reviewing the records.”

Meanwhile, CU Pro-Vice Chancellor (Academic) Prof Mohammad Shamim Uddin Khan said transparency was essential in all activities of public universities.

“There were many unauthorised appointments in the past. After assuming office, we are regularising those appointments in line with University Grants Commission (UGC) conditions. Every recruitment has been carried out with integrity,” he said.

He further said the departments of Drama, Music, and Sports Science were facing an acute shortage of faculty members, and without necessary recruitment, academic activities would have been disrupted.

“Despite pressure from students, we followed due process in appointing teachers,” he added.

Regarding the Farsi Department appointment, the pro-VC said the recruitment circular had been published in 2021 during the tenure of former VC Prof Shirin Akhter.

“At that time, the process was halted after a conversation went viral before the formation of the selection board. The current administration has completed the process,” he said.

The ACC team also included Deputy Assistant Directors Hamed Reza and Sabuj Hossain.

On January 9, the university administration issued a press release stating that a total of 113 people were appointed in various categories following decisions taken at the 565th syndicate meeting.

title: Ducsu launches month-long campaign for ‘Yes’ vote in referendum
body:
The Dhaka University Central Students’ Union (Ducsu) has announced a month-long programme ahead of the upcoming referendum and national election, aiming to mobilise support for “Yes” votes.

At a press conference today, held in front of the Ducsu building at Dhaka University campus, student leaders outlined 15 planned activities, including direct public outreach across the country, visits to educational institutions, online campaigns, exchange meetings with student organisations, journalists, activists and members of civil society, discussion programmes, and the publication of various media contents in favour of the “Yes” vote.

Through the programme, Ducsu called upon all anti-fascist political parties, including Jamaat-e-Islami, BNP, and NCP, along with student bodies, professional organisations, civil society groups, and students and citizens from all walks of life to unite and create a nationwide support of a “Yes” vote in the referendum.

Other programmes announced by Ducsu include street theatre and mime shows for public awareness, presenting arguments in favour of a “Yes” vote through debates, a discussion titled “Thoughts of the July Injured,” and debates.

In a press release, Ducsu said the decision to undertake these activities was taken to uphold democracy, ensure respect for public opinion, guarantee people’s participation in major state decisions, and raise awareness across the country ahead of the referendum.

"By delivering a 'Yes' vote in this referendum, the fascist structure will be permanently dismantled to ensure that massacres like those in Pilkhana, over the protests against Allama Sayeedi's verdict, Shapla Chattar, or the July uprising never occur again," the press release said.

Ducsu said a victory for the “Yes” vote would pave the way for the implementation of the July Charter, establish a balance of power in the state, limit any individual from serving more than two terms as prime minister, strengthen the independence of constitutional institutions, ensure transparency in public sector recruitment, and guarantee public participation in major constitutional changes.

title: ACC files 12 cases against PK Halder, 34 others over embezzling Tk 433cr
body:
The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) today filed 12 cases against 35 people, including former managing director of NRB Global Bank and Reliance Finance Limited Prashanta Kumar Halder (PK Halder), on charges of approving and embezzling fake loans worth Tk 433.96 crore in the names of 12 shell and paper-based companies.

The accused include Md Siddiqur Rahman, former chairman of FAS Finance and Investment Limited; Mahfuza Rahman Baby, Mohammad Abdul Hafiz, and Abdul Motalib Ahmed.

ACC Deputy Director Md Mashirur Rahman and Assistant Director Md Imran Akon filed the cases at the commission’s Dhaka Integrated District Office.

According to statements of the cases, the accused created loan accounts in the names of several fake companies. In some cases, only one or two instalments were paid, while in others no instalments were paid at all. Despite this, the loans were later rescheduled by board meetings without any objections, which allowed the accused to continue the fraud.

The ACC further alleged that fake documents were prepared to show the existence of businesses that, in reality, had no operational activities. Loans were disbursed to these companies even though they did not exist in practice.

Investigation of official records found that the addresses shown as the head offices of these companies do not exist and no business operations are currently being conducted at those locations.

title: Former ACC commissioner Zahurul Haque questioned over corruption allegations
body:
As part of an investigation into allegations of bribery, abuse of power and fraud, the Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) questioned its former commissioner Md Zahurul Haque for nearly three hours today.

He arrived at the ACC headquarters in Dhaka’s Segunbagicha around 10:30am, accompanied by his wife, and left the office after the questioning at around 1:30pm. He did not respond to any questions from journalists while leaving.

ACC Public Relations Officer Akhtarul Islam confirmed that Zahurul Haque had been interrogated, but declined to provide further details.

The ACC is investigating allegations that Zahurul abused his power to take financial benefits from accused persons in ongoing cases, fraudulently obtained a plot from Rajuk, received huge bribes from two major telecom operators, and laundered that money abroad to acquire assets in different countries.

To probe these allegations, a three-member investigation team was formed in January last year, led by ACC Director SMM Akhtar Hamid Bhuiyan.

On December 3 last year, the ACC filed a case against Zahurul and five others over allegations of illegally reducing international incoming call termination rates and revenue-sharing, causing the state a loss of nearly Tk 9,000 crore.

The home ministry has already cancelled Zahurul’s passport and imposed a travel ban on him.

Zahurul, a former district and sessions judge, also served as a judge in the BDR massacre case. He retired in 2014. The Awami League government later appointed him as a commissioner of the BTRC and subsequently as its chairman.

He joined the ACC as a commissioner on March 10, 2021, and resigned on October 29, 2024, following the change of government.

title: Reconciliation requires admission and remorse for crimes: Chief adviser
body:
Chief Adviser Prof Muhammad Yunus yesterday said no matter who says what, elections will be held on February 12 -- not a day before, not a day after.

Prof Yunus reaffirmed his government’s commitment when two former senior United States diplomats Albert Gombis and Morse Tan called on him at the State Guest House Jamuna in Dhaka, CA press wing said in a statement today.

The chief adviser said the interim government would remain completely neutral during the elections, ensuring an unbiased administration and a level playing field for all political parties.

He said there had been a flood of fake news and deliberately spread confusion surrounding the elections, but stressed that the government remained firm in its commitment to hold the polls on February 12 and to hand over power to a democratically elected government once the results are announced.

The vote would be free, fair and peaceful, and held in a festive atmosphere, he added.

Gombis, a former acting under secretary of state, and Tan, a former ambassador-at-large, are visiting Bangladesh ahead of the crucial elections.

During the hour-long meeting, the chief adviser and the visiting diplomats discussed a wide range of issues, including the forthcoming elections, the July Revolution and its aftermath, the rise of young protesters, the July Charter and the referendum, fake news and misinformation targeting the vote, the Rohingya crisis, and the prospects for truth and reconciliation in a post-July Bangladesh.

The chief adviser said his government was campaigning for “Yes” votes in the referendum, noting that the July Charter -- set to be endorsed by the people -- would usher in a new era of democratic governance and leave no room for future autocracy.

Prof Yunus said supporters of the former autocratic regime were spreading fake news and misinformation in an attempt to create confusion about the elections. “But people are alert. Increasingly, they can detect AI-generated misinformation videos,” he said.

Former under secretary Gombis agreed that fake news had emerged as “one of the main enemies” of democracy worldwide and stressed the need for greater efforts to combat the threat.

Both diplomats praised Prof Yunus for his crucial role in steering the country over the past one and a half years.

They asked whether a truth and reconciliation initiative -- similar to post-apartheid South Africa -- was possible in Bangladesh.

Prof Yunus said as a friend of late Nelson Mandela, he closely followed South Africa’s truth and reconciliation process, but he saw no possibility of a similar move in Bangladesh right at this moment due to the continued denial by the former regime of its crimes.

“Time is not right. Where do you start? Truth and reconciliation come when you admit that you were wrong, when you repent and show remorse for your crimes, and when you create the right atmosphere,” he said.

“But so far, there is no remorse, no repentance. Instead, they claim that the young people killed during the July uprising were killed by terrorists. There are stacks and stacks of evidence of their crimes -- absolutely barbaric crimes -- yet they remain in complete denial.”

SDG Coordinator and Senior Secretary Lamiya Morshed was also present at the meeting.

title: Protests bring Dhaka to a standstill as students block Farmgate, Science Lab
body:
Traffic movement on key Dhaka roads came to a complete standstill today as separate protests blocked major intersections, including Farmgate and Science Lab.

The protests caused immense suffering for commuters, with many having to walk several kilometres to reach their destinations.

At Farmgate, students of Tejgaon College blocked one of the busiest intersections in the city, demanding justice for their peer, Sakibul Hasan Rana, who died on December 10, four days after sustaining injuries in a dormitory attack.

The blockade began around 11:15 am, bringing traffic in Farmgate and surrounding areas to a halt, police said.

Rana, 18, died around noon on December 10 while undergoing treatment at the intensive care unit (ICU) of a Moghbazar hospital. Fellow Tejgaon College students alleged that Rana was attacked for protesting drug abuse and claimed that members of both groups involved were associated with Chhatra Dal.

Meanwhile, students of the proposed Dhaka Central University -- comprising seven colleges -- blocked several major intersections, including Science Lab, Technical Intersection, and Tanti Bazar in Old Dhaka, demanding the issuance of an ordinance for the university.

Students of Dhaka College and Eden Mohila College blocked the Science Lab intersection around 12:30 pm. They first gathered on their campuses and later marched towards Science Lab. As a result, vehicular movement in the area came to a halt.

Students of Government Bangla College blocked the Technical Intersection around 12:00 pm with the same demand.

They continued the protest at the time of filing of this report around 2:45 pm, according to SM Jakaria, officer-in-charge of Darussalam Police Station.

The traffic situation in the area worsened as a result, he added.

Students of Government Shaheed Suhrawardy College and Kabi Nazrul Government College blocked the Tanti Bazar area around 11:15 am, creating a huge tailback in Old Dhaka.

The students left the area around 2:15 pm, said AKM Mahfuzul Haque, officer-in-charge of Bangshal Police Station.

title: ICT allows display of July uprising evidence at memorial museum
body: The International Crimes Tribunal today allowed evidence seized in several crimes against humanity cases linked to the July 2024 uprising to be displayed for one month at the July Uprising Memorial Museum.The museum is scheduled to be inaugurated on January 20.The order was passed on today by the tribunal Chairman Justice Md Golam Mortuza Mozumder, following a prosecution plea.Speaking to reporters at the ICT’s premises after the hearing, prosecutor Gazi Monawar Hossain Tamim said the museum has been set up at the former residence of ex-prime minister Sheikh Hasina, widely known as Gono Bhaban.After August 5, 2024, the premises has been converted into the July Uprising Memorial Museum, he added.Based on the prosecution’s application, the tribunal permitted the brief exhibition of the materials, allowing the public to witness the evidence, the prosecutor said.

title: Death toll from Shariatpur bomb explosion rises to two
body:
The death toll from a bomb explosion in Zajira upazila of Shariatpur has risen to two after Md Nabin Hossain, 22, succumbed to injuries while undergoing treatment at Dhaka Medical College Hospital (DMCH).

Another injured, Arman Nayan Molla, 25, remains in critical condition.

The explosion occurred early Thursday morning inside a tin-shed house in Beparikandi village of Bilashpur Union, destroying the dwelling and blowing away its roof.

Police later recovered bomb-making materials from the site.

Md Faruk, in-charge of the DMCH police camp, confirmed Nabin's death around 4:30 pm.

Nabin worked as a mechanic and sustained severe injuries to his face and hands.

His body has been kept at the morgue.

In the same explosion, the mutilated body of Sohan Bepari, 32, was recovered from a crop field about half a kilometre away from the explosion site.

Police are investigating how his body ended up there.

Saleh Ahmed, Officer-in-Charge of Zajira Police Station, said, "Primarily, we believe the explosion occurred while bombs were being made." He added that police are probing the circumstances surrounding the deaths and injuries.

The incident follows violent clashes on January 4 at Budhairhat Bazar, where rival groups detonated more than 100 cocktail bombs in a dispute over local dominance.

Police recovered four buckets of abandoned bombs during a subsequent drive.

Locals said the tin-shed house where Thursday's explosion occurred had been built two months ago by Sagar Bepari.

Additional Superintendent of Police Tarvir Hossain, who visited the scene, said bloodstains were found on the road and evidence suggested cocktail bombs were being prepared as part of ongoing rivalry between supporters of UP Chairman Kuddus Bepari and rival leader Jalil Madbar.

Police sources confirmed that clashes between the two factions have been recurring, with both sides resorting to bomb attacks.

Previous explosions in Bilashpur on April 5 and November 2 last year prompted cases under the Explosives Act against both leaders and their supporters. While Kuddus Bepari was later released on bail, Jalil Madbar remains in jail.

Locals said the deceased Sohan Bepari was a supporter of Kuddus Bepari. Currently, supporters of Kuddus led by Mannan Bepari and followers of Jalil led by Nasir Bepari are vying for dominance in the area.

title: Govt eases data localisation rules, drops jail terms for tech firms
body:
The government has largely removed data localisation requirements for technology companies from thePersonal Data Protection Ordinanceand scrapped jail terms for violations by tech firms, including global giants such as Meta and Google.

The amendments were approved at a meeting of the advisory council in Dhaka today.

Under the revised ordinance, only data related to government-designated Critical Information Infrastructure (CII), as defined in the Cyber Security Ordinance, will be required to be stored within Bangladesh.

The blanket requirement for technology companies to keep local copies of user data has also been eased.

Under the original ordinance, gazetted in November last year, technology companies were required to store at least one synchronised real-time copy of data inside Bangladesh.

Under the amendment, this requirement will now apply only to restricted personal data, for which at least one synchronised real-time copy of cloud-stored data must be kept within the country.

The amendment also revises the punishment provisions. Previously, violations of the ordinance -- including breaches of personal data or infringement of users' rights -- could result in both imprisonment and financial penalties.

The revised ordinance removes the provision for imprisonment, leaving financial penalties as the sole form of punishment.

"Millions of people in Bangladesh use Facebook and Google, and companies such as Meta and Alphabet raised some concerns regarding certain provisions of the Personal Data Protection Ordinance.

Two changes were made to address those concerns," said Shafiqul Alam, press secretary to the chief adviser.

"With this amendment, we hope Bangladesh will now be able to attract more investment in data and cloud-related services," he added.

Restricted personal data refers to any personal data that may impact national security, public order, defence, critical infrastructure, or an individual's fundamental rights and freedoms, and is therefore subject to the strictest controls. It may also include classified datasets, critical health- or security-related information, or any other personal data designated as "restricted" by the authority or the government.

title: Visa sections of three Bangladesh missions in India closed on security grounds
body:
The visa sections of three Bangladesh missions in India have been closed temporarily on security grounds, Foreign Affairs Adviser Touhid Hossain said today.

"What I have done is that I have asked our three missions to keep their visa sections closed for the time being. It's a security issue," he told reporters at the foreign ministry, responding to a question on whether Bangladesh missions in India had restricted tourist visas for Indians.

He did not name the missions. However, diplomatic sources said the visa sections of the Bangladesh High Commission in New Delhi, the Deputy High Commission in Kolkata, and the Bangladesh Assistant High Commission in Agartala have been closed.

The visa sections at Bangladesh missions in Chennai and Mumbai, however, remain operational, sources said.

Over the past few weeks, protests have taken place near Bangladesh missions in India.

Following the ouster of the Awami League regime, the Indian High Commission restricted tourist visas to Bangladeshis, citing security concerns.

Touhid was also asked about the dropping of Bangladeshi cricketer Mustafizur Rahman from the Indian Premier League amid anti-Bangladesh protests in India, and Bangladesh's decision not to send the national cricket team to India for the upcoming T20 World Cup.

The adviser said he fully supported Sports Adviser Asif Nazrul's stance on not sending the team to India for safety reasons and demanding that Bangladesh's matches be relocated to co-host Sri Lanka.

"We will certainly play outside India," Touhid said.

He added that both players and supporters would have to travel to India and said the government must consider their security.

Asked about the impact on bilateral relations, Touhid said such issues arise from time to time and each has some impact.

He said Bangladesh would take decisions based on its national interest. "We have an interest in our players' safety in not sending them to India. If we have interest in buying rice from India, we will buy it," he added.

title: Govt to form Narayanganj Development Authority: Ministry
body:
The government is set to establish the Narayanganj Development Authority (NDA) to develop the city and its adjoining areas into a modern, well-planned one.

The Ministry of Housing and Public Works today issued a draft ordinance in this regard and sought opinions from relevant authorities.

According to the ministry officials, the proposed authority will help prevent unplanned urbanisation, maintain ecological and environmental balance, ensure disaster-resilient urban management, promote information technology and tourism industries, and improve the overall quality of life for citizens.

According to the draft, the Narayanganj Development Authority will consist of a chairman and four full-time members.

Besides, five representatives from different sectors will be included.

The chairman's tenure will be three years, and no individual will be appointed as chairman or member for more than two terms.

The authority will be empowered to formulate master plans, purchase or lease land, acquire land, levy land taxes, and collect development fees. However, land use will be strictly governed by the approved master plan. Any violation of this provision will be punishable by up to one year in prison or a fine of up to Tk 10 lakh, or both.

The authority will also have the power to take strict action against illegal excavation of artificial water bodies, filling of low-lying areas, or obstruction of natural water flows. It may order the suspension or closure of such activities if necessary.

Violation of such orders may result in up to two years' imprisonment or a fine of up to Tk 2 lakh for the first offence. Repeat offences may attract imprisonment ranging from two to ten years and a fine of up to Tk 10 lakh, or both.

The draft ordinance further mentioned that the flow of water in rivers, canals, ponds, wetlands, and other natural reservoirs cannot be obstructed without prior permission from the authority.

Besides, the provisions of the Playgrounds, Open Spaces, Gardens and Natural Reservoirs Conservation Act, 2000 will apply to any change in the classification of playgrounds, parks, gardens, and natural water bodies, the draft added.

On December 18, Narayanganj City Corporation (NCC) Administrator Dr Abu Nasar Mohammad Abdullah sent a letter to the Local Government Division seeking the formation of a Narayanganj Development Authority.In the letter, he said around 2 million people live within the NCC area of about 72.43 square kilometres, where the urban growth rate is 5.7 percent, compared to the national average of around 3 percent and 3.4 percent in Dhaka. As the city’s boundary and population are expected to expand further, he said, a “Narayanganj Development Authority” is needed to strengthen NCC’s capacity to manage planned urban development.

title: Indemnity Ordinance for July warriors on the cards: Law adviser
body:
Law Adviser Asif Nazrul today said a draft ordinance will be placed at the next meeting of the Council of Advisers, aiming to give indemnity to theJuly warriors.

"The July warriors freed the country from fascist rule by risking their lives. Of course, they have the right to get immunity," he wrote in a post shared on his verified Facebook account.

Asif Nazrul said there is also a need to enact a law granting them immunity for the preventive activities they carried out against the murderers of fascist Sheikh Hasina during the July uprising.

"Such indemnity laws were enacted in different countries after the fall of governments during the Arab Spring or in contemporary revolutions (or mass uprisings)," he said.

The law adviser said Article 46 of the Constitution of Bangladesh allows the law of indemnity, and an indemnity law was enacted for freedom fighters in 1973 after the Liberation War.

"In the light of these precedents and laws, the law ministry has prepared a draft of the Indemnity Ordinance. In sha Allah, it will be presented, for approval, in the next meeting of the Council of Advisers," he said.

title: ‘Unfortunate but not abnormal’: Foreign adviser reacts as US tightens visa rules
body:
Foreign Affairs Adviser Md Touhid Hossain today termed the latest decision by the US administration against Bangladesh as very unfortunate.

However, he said such a decision is not abnormal, given the immigration related problems.

"This decision is not just imposed on Bangladesh alone. Bangladesh is among the countries which have immigration related problems. To me, it's nothing abnormal, certainly unfortunate. It hurts us," he told reporters while responding to a question at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

The adviser said this policy-related problem had been continuing for a long time, but this government, from day one, raised its voice against irregular migration.

US President Donald Trump's administration has put 25 more countries, including Bangladesh, on a list of nations whose citizens could be required to postbonds of up to $15,000to apply for entry into the US.

Any citizen or national travelling on a passport issued by one of these countries, who is found otherwise eligible for a B1/B2 visa, must post a bond of $5,000, $10,000, or $15,000," the State Department website said.

Applicants must agree to the terms of the bond through the US Treasury Department's online payment platform, Pay.gov, the State Department said.

The list mostly includes countries from Africa, Latin America and South Asia. It has a total of 38 countries as of Tuesday. The policy for the newly added nations will go into effect on January 21.

title: CU ‘D’ unit results published; 65.94% candidates fail
body:
Chittagong University (CU) has published the results of the 'D' unit admission test for the 2025–26 academic year under the Faculty of Social Sciences.

A total of 16,156 candidates passed the examination, representing a pass rate of 34.06 percent, while 65.94 percent failed. The highest scorer on the merit list secured 90.50 marks.

The results were published today, confirmed Prof Mohammad Enayet Ullah Patwary, coordinator of the 'D' unit admission test.

He said candidates can view their results on Chittagong University's official website, while detailed results will be available after logging into individual profiles.

The admission test was held on January 3 simultaneously in Chattogram, Dhaka and Rajshahi.

A total of 51,505 candidates applied against 849 seats under the 'D' unit.

title: Coast Guard rescues three hostages, arrests pirate gang in Sundarbans
