Spurs have won just four of their last 17 games in all competitions to slip to 14th in the Premier League and bow out of both domestic cups.

Frank is on the brink of joining a long list of managers who have failed to make the grade in north London, including Nuno, who lasted just 17 games as Tottenham boss in 2021.

The Portuguese coach, already sacked once this season by Nottingham Forest, has managed just two wins in 16 Premier League games since joining the Hammers in September.

West Ham desperately need a quick upturn in results as they sit seven points adrift of safety in 18th place,

Top of both the Premier League and Champions League, the Gunners are on course for an unprecedented quadruple after FA and League Cup victories this week.

But Mikel Arteta’s men must overcome a poor record at the City Ground against a Forest side keen to make amends to their furious manager.

Arsenal have won in just one of their last five visits to Nottingham.

Forest were dumped out of the FA Cup by second-tier Wrexham on penalties last weekend, sparking an outburst from Sean Dyche.

‘It’s unacceptable to me, but it’s unacceptable to the badge as well,’ he said of his side’s first-half performance left them battling back from 2-0 down before drawing 3-3.

title: Litton replaces Nurul as Rangpur captain
body:
Litton Das has replaced Nurul Hasan as the new captain of the Rangpur Riders in the Bangladesh Premier League, with two games left in the league stage on Friday.

Rangpur, who have eight points from the same number of matches, are yet to confirm their place in the play-off as they have suffered three consecutive defeats.

Rangpur head coach Micky Arthur said that Nurul willingly stepped down from the role.

‘Sohan came to me a couple of days ago and wanted to stand down as captain,’ Arthur told the reporters on Friday. ‘He felt that he wanted to work on his own performance. It just shows the type of person he is.’

Litton said that his sole focus would be on Rangpur.

‘At the moment, the World Cup is not on my mind. Since I am playing as part of a franchise, my full dedication will be to my franchise here,’ he said.

‘When they willingly wanted this, and when a franchise asks you to take on this responsibility, as a player it is my duty to accept it. I believe I have made the right decision,’ he added.

Litton also acknowledged the added responsibility that captaincy brought. However, he  stressed that it would not alter his approach with the bat.

He said, ‘The effort never falls short. Whenever I have played as a batsman, I have always tried to give 100 per cent. Of course, as a captain there will be more responsibility. At the same time, when I am batting, I am a batsman first. My job is to score runs.’

title: Shoriful’s five-for knocks Noakhali out
body:
Shoriful Islam’s career-best figure of 5-9 led Chattogram Royals to a five-wicket victory over Noakhali Express as the Bangladesh Premier League resumed on Friday, following a day of boycott at the Sher-e-Bangla National Stadium in Mirpur.

Noakhali, after being asked to bat first, managed only 126 runs in 18.5 overs in their must-win match. Chattogram got home with three overs left as skipper Mahedi Hasan remained unbeaten on 49 off 36 with four fours and two sixes.

While Chattogram toppled Rajshahi at the top of the table with the win, Noakhali were officially knocked out with one match remaining.

Noakhali, coming to the match with two consecutive wins, started brightly as Soumya Sarkar and Hassan Eisakhil added 34 runs in three overs for the opening partnership.

However, after Mahedi got the first breakthrough by dismissing Soumya, Chattogram tightened the screw. Six out of the first seven batters got started but couldn’t make big scores, as Shoriful and Mahedi were all over them. Mahedi claimed 3-12 from three overs.

‘As a bowler—whether you are a pacer or spinner—everyone has that dream of taking five wickets, especially in the T20s. So it feels good, alhamdulillah,’ Shoriful later said after taking his maiden five-for in the format.

After getting hit for a four on his first ball of the innings, Shoriful’s remaining spell was boundary-less. He was at the brink of a hat-trick when he had Hasan Mahmud and Mehedi Hasan Rana in consecutive deliveries in the 16th over.

The left-arm pacer completed his maiden five-wicket haul in his last over when he dismissed Sabbir Hossain and Ihsanullah.

It was doubly special for Shoriful, as he was also adjudged the player of the match.

‘Of course, I have enjoyed it a lot. We have won the match,’ he said.

‘And one more thing, I have said that as long as I play, I will give the prize money of the player of the match to the people in need in my area. So this money will go to them, and that gives me added pleasure,’ he added.

The left-arm pacer also hailed his personal analyst, Sabbib Bin Sattar, for his recent performances.

‘He sends me everything after every match. Where I make mistakes and what I should not repeat,’ he said.

While Shoriful’s bowling put Noakhali under immense pressure, Hasan Mahmud and Ihsanullah brought them into the fight early in the innings.

Chattogram lost four wickets for only 29 runs, including Mohammad Naim, who made 18 off seven. Mahfijul Islam’s struggle was quite visible as he made an eight-ball duck.

However, Mahedi calmed things down with a 30-run partnership with Hasan Nawaz before adding another 59 runs with Asif Ali.

Asif remained unbeaten on 36 off 30 while hitting two fours and two sixes.

title: Khaleda’s ideals termed guiding force for nation
body:
Top civil society figures attend civic memorial service

Civil society leaders on Friday said that Khaleda Zia’s ideals were widely regarded as a guiding force for Bangladesh’s democratic and political life.

At a civic condolence meeting at the South Plaza of the Jatiya Sangsad Bhaban in Dhaka, they said that upholding her principles today could help the nation navigate challenges, resolve divisions, and ensure that governance remained fair and transparent.

In this way, they said, Khaleda Zia’s vision would continue to inspire the nation and shape the path towards a more resilient and democratic Bangladesh.

The condolence meeting was attended, among others, by BNP chairman Tarique Rahman, his wife Zubaida Rahman, daughter Zaima Rahman, and family members including Shamila Rahman, the wife of Khaleda Zia’s younger son Arafat Rahman Koko.

Former chief justice JR Mudassir Husain called for Begum Khaleda Zia to be recognised and treated as a national leader, arguing that her political life formed an inseparable part of Bangladesh’s constitutional and democratic history.

‘I would urge the current government to confer the highest honour upon Khaleda Zia,’ he said.

Calling on the current authorities to accord Khaleda Zia the highest respect on behalf of the nation, Justice Mudassir said that progress depended on choosing justice and peace over malice and falsehood.

He concluded that honouring Khaleda’s legacy was not a party demand but a national responsibility as she embodied a significant part of Bangladesh’s democratic identity.

Speaking at the event, economist Mahbub Ullah delivered an emotional address, remembering Khaleda Zia as a leader defined by patriotism, courage, honesty, and resilience in the face of continued oppression.

He said that Khaleda’s deep love for the country and its land was reflected in her lifelong struggle to uphold national sovereignty and independence.

Mahbub Ullah stressed that Khaleda Zia’s death did not mark the end of history, arguing instead that her ideology would remain a driving force shaping the future political trajectory of the country and the wider region.

Law adviser Asif Nazrul, also speaking at the programme, said that Khaleda Zia had secured a permanent place in the hearts of the people, while her  political rival had been relegated to political exile and public marginalisation.

He said that Khaleda Zia’s values — including honesty, determination, self-sacrifice and tolerance — must be internalised by the public to ensure the country’s long-term well-being and democratic resilience.

Shafik Rehman, editor of daily Jaijaidin, said that if today’s condolence meeting was truly to be meaningful, this grief must be transformed into strength.

The question, he said, is how that strength should be channelled, answering that it must be done through voting and by taking people to the polling centres.

He, therefore, urged everyone not to allow the election to be disrupted.

Shafik Rehman said that Khaleda Zia’s greatest quality was that she spoke honestly, adding that she was a patriot who genuinely loved the country.

Writer Mohiuddin Ahmed traced Khaleda Zia’s political journey as an evolutionary one, beginning with her emergence as an uncompromising leader and culminating in her transformation into a symbol of public resilience and empathy.

He highlighted her historic distinction as the first prime minister elected through a free and fair vote, as well as her quick rise to executive authority.

Mohiuddin said that she had maintained dignity and elegance in an often coarse political environment, setting her apart from many contemporaries.

He recalled that in her final video message after her release, Khaleda Zia explicitly called for an end to what she termed the ‘politics of vengeance’, a message he described as a guiding blueprint for the nation’s future.

Speaking at the event, Khaleda Zia’s medical board member FM Siddiqui alleged deliberate negligence in her treatment at the Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujib Medical University and called for immediate legal and investigative action.

He demanded a high-powered legal committee to examine three key areas: the composition of the government-appointed medical board and its accountability, identification of all doctors involved and any evidence of negligence, and the obstruction to Khaleda Zia’s personal physicians despite formal requests.

SMA Faiz, chairman of the University Grants Commission, highlighted Begum Khaleda Zia’s commitment to merit, intellect, and institutional integrity, recalling her approach to public appointments during her time in office.

He said that a significant number of senior and distinguished officers currently serving in the cadre service had entered the civil administration during Khaleda Zia’s tenure, securing their positions solely on the basis of academic achievement and professional merit.

According to Faiz, Khaleda’s approach helped foster an environment in which intellectual merit and academic integrity were valued and protected.

The Daily Star editor Mahfuz Anam said that his respect for Khaleda Zia stemmed from her conduct as prime minister and her commitment to democracy and a free press.

Khaleda Zia, he said, demonstrated tolerance, accepted criticism and respected diverse views, creating space for independent journalism and accountability.

Mahfuz Anam credited her with making a meaningful contribution to strengthening democratic practice in the country.

Economist Debapriya Bhattacharya paid tribute to Khaleda Zia as a leader whose guidance was deeply missed at a time of national challenges.

Recalling several policy discussions with her during her terms in office, he said Khaleda Zia listened patiently to technical arguments, assessed them against national realities and made firm decisions grounded in political conviction.

Debapriya urged today’s policymakers to learn from this approach, concluding that her absence was keenly felt.

New Age editor and Editors’ Council president Nurul Kabir said that with her death, Begum Khaleda Zia proved that she was not just the leader of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party.

She had become a true leader of the people and the nation, as reflected by the millions who joined her funeral prayers across political lines.

Kabir praised Khaleda Zia for her remarkable restraint and dignity, noting that despite enduring political attacks, personal hardships, and family sufferings, she never publicly expressed anger or resentment.

The New Age editor said that this quality was extremely important in today’s intolerant political climate in Bangladesh, adding that it would ensure that she was remembered throughout history as a truly unique figure.

He recalled that on the day of her funeral, standing amid the vast sea of people, a BNP leader promised millions that the party would be run according to Begum Khaleda Zia’s democratic ideals.

Nurul Kabir said that he would earnestly and humbly appeal to them to make every effort to keep that promise.

Amar Desh editor Mahmudur Rahman placed Khaleda Zia within a broader historical context, arguing that few political figures over the past century matched the enduring popularity of the Zia family.

He described late President Ziaur Rahman and Khaleda Zia as a rare example of a married couple who both enjoyed sustained public support throughout their political lives.

Mahmudur Rahman said that the massive public mourning at their funerals reflected their moral authority, adding that their son, Tarique Rahman, now carried the heavy responsibility of preserving that legacy.

Bangladesh Puja Udjapan Parishad president Basudev Dhar said that any history of democratic struggle -- past or future -- would remain incomplete without Khaleda Zia’s contribution included in that.

He urged citizens not to squander the current opportunity to establish democracy, arguing that ensuring no citizen faced discrimination would be the highest tribute to Khaleda Zia’s memory.

A former diplomat M Anwar Hashim, who served as an ambassador during Khaleda Zia’s tenure, recalled her deep sense of empathy, citing her emotional response during a visit to a concentration camp decades ago.

He said that Khaleda built on the foreign policy foundations laid by President Ziaur Rahman, strengthening bilateral relations, promoting regional cooperation through the SAARC and ensuring active engagement with multilateral bodies, including the United Nations.

title: Fire guts 26 rooms in Gazipur
body:
A fire broke out at a residential colony in Kashimpur area of Gazipur on Friday morning, destroying at least 26 rooms.

The incident occurred in a colony owned by a man named Biplob, located near GMS Garments factory in Sardaganj area of Kashimpur.

On receiving information, a unit of DBL Fire Service rushed to the spot and brought the blaze under control after about half an hour of efforts.

DBL Fire Service in-charge Atikul Islam said the fire originated from a room in the colony and quickly spread to adjacent rooms, leaving 26 rooms completely gutted.

‘The exact cause of the fire and the extent of losses will be determined after investigation,’ he added.

title: Two confess to raping woman on moving bus
body:
Two accused in the rape case of a woman on a moving bus in Tangail confessed to their involvement before the court on Friday.

The accused bus driver Mohammed Altaf, 25, and one of his assistants, Mohammed Rabbi, 21, gave confessional statements under section 164 at the senior judicial magistrate Rumelia Siarjam’s court in Tangail.

The court later sent the two accused to jail, court inspector Sajjad Hossen confirmed.

On early Thursday, a 26-year-old woman was allegedly raped on a moving bus by its driver and staff after she boarded the bus in Savar, on the outskirts of the capital, to go to Ashulia.

The driver took the bus towards Tangail, and when it reached the Korotia Underpass area of Tangail Sadar upazila on Thursday afternoon, the police, sensing something suspicious, seized the bus, detained the driver and two assistants, and rescued the victim, according to the police.

Later, the victim filed a case against the trio Thursday evening.

Meanwhile, Samajtantrik Mahila Forum in a statement on Friday condemned the incident and demanded exemplary punishment for all involved in the rape incident.

The incident once again proved that women were not safe in public transports as such incidents have happened several times earlier, the statement read.

title: RAB arrests two over Chhatra Dal activist murder in Narsingdi
body:
The Rapid Action Battalion has arrested the two main suspects in the murder of Chhatra Dal activist Zahidul Islam, 25, in Narsingdi.

Ariful Islam, additional superintendent of Police and camp commander of RAB-11, confirmed this at a press conference held at the RAB-11 Narsingdi office.

They were arrested on Thursday afternoon during a joint operation by RAB-11 Narsingdi and RAB-12 Kushtia in Bottoil, Bhadalia area of Kushtia district.

The arrested couple, Rajon, 37, and his wife Zara, 30, are from Nawapara area under Madhabdi police station.

During initial questioning, they admitted to being directly involved in the killing.

They are handed over to Madhabdi police station for further legal proceedings.

RAB said the operation to apprehend other suspects involved in the murder is ongoing.

Zahidul Islam, a union-level Chhatra Dal activist, was killed on December 29 after being lured from his home in Gayeshpur area of Zinaradi Union, Palash upazila.

His father, Mosharaf Hossain Bhuiya, filed the murder case naming Rajon, Zara, and four to five unidentified individuals as accused.

title: Two killed in clash over establishing dominance in Cumilla
body:
Two men were killed in a violent clash between two groups over establishing dominance in Nangalkot upazila of Cumilla on Friday.

The deceased are identified as Delwar Hossain Nayan, a migrant worker who returned home from abroad a month ago, and Saleh Ahmed, a former member of Bakshaganj union, according to the police.

The incident occurred at about 11:30am on Friday at Aliara village under Bakshaganj union in the upazila, said Arifur Rahman, officer-in-charge of the Nagalkot police.

‘Two people were killed and four to five others were injured in the clash,’ he said.

The injured were undergoing treatment at hospitals in Cumilla and Chattogram, he added.

OC Arifur said that the situation was brought under control and additional law enforcers were deployed at the scene.

According to eyewitnesses, the clash took place between Abul Khair group and the group led by Saleh Ahmed over their long-standing rivalry for establishing dominance.

According to local people, a former union parishad member named Alauddin was killed in a clash between the same groups on August 3, 2025.

Following the incident, one of the groups vandalised and set fire to the houses of their rivals in the village, forcing several families to leave the area.

Recently, when the families returned to their homes with the intervention of the army, tension arose again resulting in the Friday’s violent clash.

title: Hadi’s brother Omar gets contractual job at Bangladesh mission in UK
body:
The interim government has appointed Omar Bin Hadi, brother of slain Inquilab Mancha convener Sharif Osman Hadi, as second secretary on a three-year contract at the Bangladesh Assistant High Commission in Birmingham in the United Kingdom.

The public administration ministry issued a gazette to the effect on Thursday.

Omar has been the contractual appointment to the post at the Bangladesh mission in the UK on condition that he will have to leave his any other profession, business or links with any government, semi-government or non-governmental organisations, according to the official order signed by joint secretary Abul Hayat Md Rafiq.

Omar completed his bachelor’s and master’s degrees in Islamic history and culture from Jagannath University.

Osman Hadi, also one of the 2024 July Mass Uprising front leaders, was shot in the head in the Dhaka city on December 12, 2025 while he had been conducting his campaign as an independent candidate for the Dhaka-8 constituency in the upcoming general election.

He later died under treatment at a Singapore hospital on December 18, 2025.

title: US officials hold virtual meeting with BNP, Jamaat on bilateral trade
body:
Officials of the United States Trade Representative under the Trump administration held virtual meetings with Bangladeshi political leaders on Friday to discuss tariff-related issues and explore ways to strengthen bilateral trade ties.

The US delegation, led by US Trade Representative ambassador Jamieson Greer, held seperate virtual meetings with Bangladesh Nationalist Party chairperson Tarique Rahman and Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami amir Shafiqur Rahman.

Citing Saleh Shibly, press secretary to the BNP chairperson, the BNP media cell said that Tarique Rahman and a BNP representative joined the virtual meeting from Dhaka at about 9:00am on the day, while the US delegation participated from Washington, DC.

During the meeting, Tarique Rahman emphasised the importance of deepening trade engagement and developing broader cooperation in areas of mutual interest to further enhance Bangladesh-US economic ties.

From the BNP side, Humaiun Kabir, joint secretary general and foreign affairs adviser to the BNP chairman, also joined the discussion.

In April 2025, the US imposed sharply higher reciprocal tariffs on several countries, including Bangladesh, and raised the duty on apparel shipments to the US to 37 per cent. The tariff was later lowered to 35 per cent and then to 20 per cent,  following a series of negotiations on July 31 of that year.

Since August 7, 2025, Bangladeshi apparel items have faced a 20 per cent reciprocal tariff, in addition to the regular 16.5 per cent tariff.

In a separate virtual meeting with USTR ambassador Jamieson Greer, Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami amir Shafiqur Rahman discussed bilateral trade, reciprocal tariffs and future economic cooperation between Bangladesh and the United States.

Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami’s US spokesperson Mohammad Nakibur Rahman also joined the meeting.

Shafiqur Rahman expressed gratitude to Greer for his cooperation regarding discussions on reciprocal tariff issues involving Bangladesh, according to a media release issued by the party.

At the meeting, Greer informed Shafiqur Rahman that he had personally met US president Donald Trump last week to discuss reducing reciprocal tariffs on Bangladesh.

The Jamaat amir also thanked the United States for its move to consider special tariff facilities for garments manufactured using 100 per cent US cotton or US-produced man-made fibres.

Describing the proposal as a ‘win-win’ formula, Shafiqur said it would boost Bangladesh’s garment exports while simultaneously benefiting the US agriculture and industrial sectors.

He said that the reciprocal tariff arrangement had laid a strong foundation for improving bilateral trade and economic relations between the two countries.

He added that Bangladesh had already begun implementing key aspects of the agreement and was taking special measures to reduce the trade deficit between the two nations.

He further said that if Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami formed the government after the national election scheduled for February, his party would continue to implement the agreement in full and work sincerely to deepen trade and investment relations with the United States.

Shafiqur also welcomed ambassador Greer’s support for Bangladesh’s access to funds from the US Development Finance Corporation, saying that opportunities for DFC financing in private sector investment would be a highly effective tool for rapidly expanding bilateral trade and investment between Bangladesh and the US.

At the conclusion of the meeting, Shafiqur Rahman invited Jamieson Greer to visit Bangladesh, expressing hope that such a visit would further strengthen mutual understanding and partnership between the two countries.

During both meetings, participants on the US side included assistant USTR for South and Central Asia Brendan Lynch, director Emily Ashby, deputy assistant USTR Rick Switzer, USTR chief of staff Sam Mulopolous and senior policy adviser to the deputy USTR DR Seckinger.

title: Decomposed bodies of missing mother, daughter recovered in Keraniganj
body:
Decomposed bodies of a mother and her daughter were recovered at a house in Muktirbagh area of Keraniganj on Thursday night, 21 days after the victims went missing on December 25, past year.

The deceased were identified as Rokeya Rahman, 32, and her daughter Fatema, 14.

Keraniganj model police station officer-in-charge M Saiful Alam on Friday morning told New Age that the police on Thursday evening took some individuals into custody for primary questioning and arrested home tutor Mim Akter, 22, and her younger sister, who was a minor girl, in connection with the incident.

According to police, the two families had a financial dispute and the home tutor’s sister and Fatema locked in an argument when Fatema went to her tutor’s house on December 25. At one point, she strangled Fatema to death. The home tutor informed Rokeya over a phone call that Fatema fall ill and asked her to take the daughter at home.

The police also said that the two sisters killed Rokeya wrapping a scarf around her neck when she went to the house for her daughter. The duo hide a body under a bed and one from a bathroom ceiling.

Mim’s husband Humayun, a painting contractor, started noticing odd smell in the house after January 10 but Mim used to burn incense to reduce the smell telling him that the smell was from outside, said police, adding that Humayun discovered the body under the bed on Thursday evening while identifying the source of the odd smell.

On information, the police went to the house after local people came to know about the incident from Humayun shouting. Later, teams of Criminal Investigation Department and Police Bureau of Investigation went to the spot to collect evidence.

According to the police victims’ family filed a general dairy with the police station on December 27 over the missing and later Rokeya’s husband Shahin filed a kidnaping case against unidentified people on January 6.

‘Mim and her sister confessed about the murders during primary questioning,’ said OC Saiful, adding that further legal proceedings are under way.

title: Machado says she ‘presented’ Trump with Nobel medal
body:
Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado said Thursday she ‘presented’ her Nobel Peace Prize medal to Donald Trump, in a bid to win over the US president who had sidelined her since overthrowing Nicolas Maduro.

Her ‘wonderful gesture of mutual respect,’ as Trump called it Thursday, comes after the Republican said the award should have gone to him instead – and after he refused to back Machado following the January 3 US military operation to capture Maduro.

‘He deserves it, and it was a very emotional moment,’ Machado later told broadcaster Fox News in an interview.

Despite the gesture, Trump has backed Maduro’s vice president Delcy Rodriguez over Machado – so long as she toes Washington’s line, particularly on access to Venezuela’s vast oil reserves.

‘I presented the president of the United States the medal of the Nobel Peace Prize,’ Machado told reporters outside the US capitol, where she met with lawmakers after having lunch with Trump at the White House.

Machado, 58, said it was ‘recognition for his unique commitment with our freedom.’

It was not immediately clear if Trump actually kept the award following the closed-door meeting.

The Norwegian Nobel committee says its prizes cannot be transferred.

Trump had campaigned hard to win last year’s Nobel Peace Prize for what he says are his efforts to stop eight wars.

Instead it went to Machado, who appeared in Oslo last month to collect her prize – following a daring escape from Venezuela by boat – and then dedicated it to Trump.

Venezuela’s opposition has argued and presented evidence that Maduro stole the 2024 election from the candidate of Machado’s party, Edmundo Gonzalez Urrutia – claims supported by Washington.

But Trump has said that Machado does not have enough support among Venezuelans, and opted to stick with former Maduro loyalist Rodriguez.

Trump and Rodriguez had their first telephone call on Wednesday and the White House said Thursday he ‘likes what he’s seeing’ with Venezuela’s interim leaders.

Rodriguez said however that Thursday her government was ‘not afraid’ of a diplomatic clash with Washington.

‘We know they are very powerful. We know they are a lethal nuclear power...we are not afraid to confront them diplomatically, through political dialogue,’ said Rodriguez.

Rodriguez was delivering Maduro’s state of the nation address to parliament while the toppled Venezuelan leader is in a New York jail facing drug trafficking charges.

By contrast Machado, who campaigned for years to end leftist Maduro’s rule, was greeted by jubilant supporters as she left the White House.

White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt said as the lunch started that Machado was a ‘remarkable and brave voice for many of the people of Venezuela.’

But while Leavitt said Trump was ‘committed to hopefully seeing elections in Venezuela one day,’ she would not give a timeline.

Since Maduro’s capture, Trump has said the United States will ‘run’ Venezuela – exerting pressure through a naval blockade and threats of further attacks – but has appeared content to let Rodriguez remain in power so long as oil keeps flowing.

US forces on Thursday seized a sixth oil tanker in its campaign to control the South American country’s critical fossil fuel sector.

Separately, the first US-brokered sale of Venezuelan oil, worth around $500 million, has been finalized, a US official told AFP on Thursday without identifying the buyer.

Rodriguez in her speech also announced plans for legal reforms to Venezuela’s oil sector – which currently limit the involvement of foreign entities – but did not give specific details.

Washington has also hailed the release of dozens of political prisoners in the past week, though hundreds remain behind bars.

Meanwhile the shockwaves from the lightning US raid that toppled Maduro continue to reverberate.

Cuba paid tribute on Thursday to 32 soldiers killed in the operation, some of whom had been assigned to Maduro’s protection team, in a ceremony attended by revolutionary leader Raul Castro.

title: Six killed as seven-storey building catches fire in Uttara
body:
At least six people were killed after a fire broke out on the second floor of a seven-storey residential building in the capital’s Uttara area on Friday morning.

The deceased Fazle Rabbi Rezvy, 38, Mohmmad Harez, 48, and Heshan Uddin Rahaf, 17, were brought dead to Kuwait-Bangladesh Friendship Government Hospital, according to the hospital authority.

Kuwait-Bangladesh Friendship Government Hospital medical officer at the Emergency unit AFM Mahbub Hossain said that they had handed over the bodies to police in the presence of the families of the dead.

Rezvy’s wife Afroza Akter aged 30-32, died at the Dhaka Medical College Hospital, their son Md Rishan, 2.5, died at the Bangladesh Specialised Hospital while Mohamamd Harez’s niece Rodela Akter, 14, died at the Lubana General Hospital and Cardiac Centre, both facilities at Uttara, according to police.

Fazle Rabbi Rezvy hailed from Cumilla and worked in a pharmaceutical company while his wife Afroza and son lived with him, according to police and the family.

Uttara West police station officer-in-charge Kazi Md Rafiq Ahmed said that Fazle Rabbi and his family lived on the fifth floor while Harez, his son Rahaf, and niece Rodela lived on the sixth floor.

‘Although the fire originated on the second floor, people living on the fifth and sixth floors died from suffocation due to smoke,’ he added.

Harez, Rahaf, and Rodela were from Mymensingh district, according to police.

Rimi, sister-in-law of Fazle Rabbi, who received his body from the hospital, said in grief that all the father, mother and children died in the same day.

‘I am not in a condition to talk about anything,’ she said.

Fire Service and Civil Defence station officer Talha Bin Jashim said that the incident took place at about 7:50am and they were informed at about 7:54am, when two units of fire fighters reached the spot within four minutes.

He said that two units of fire fighters brought the fire under control at about 10:00am.

Fire Service Uttara station in-charge Mohamamd Alam Hossain said that they suspected room heater and electricity were behind the fire’s origin in their preliminary investigation.

‘We need more investigation to know the exact cause of the fire,’ he added.

He also said that three people were declared dead at Kuwait-Bangladesh  Friendship Government Hospital and they had rescued 13 people alive and got them admitted to different city hospitals.

In the afternoon, a large number of people were seen thronging in front of the house to see the affected building after the Jumma prayers.

Atul Sarkar, caretaker of the house next to affected building, told New Age that after hearing screaming they came out of their building and saw the fire in the building.

‘Although the fire was on the second floor, smoke affected the entire building. Many took shelter in the rooftop to save their lives,’ said Atul, who witnessed the fire incident.

Dhaka Metropolitan Police Uttara Division deputy commissioner Md Shahriar Ali said that they would complete the legal proceedings after determining the number of the casualties.

‘We came to know that about 13 people were admitted to hospitals and the number was still the same,’ he added.

People in the capital city are often losing their lives due to fire incidents.

According to Fire Service statistics for the year 2023, when 102 people were killed across the country it said that most of the fire incidents originated from electric short circuits, burning cigarettes, oven and gas pipeline leakages.

On October 14, 2025, at least 16 people perished in a fire at a garment factory and its adjacent chemical warehouse in Rupnagar Residential Area of Shialbari in the capital’s Mirpur area.

title: Dhaka’s air ranks world’s most polluted
body:
Dhaka, the overcrowded capital of Bangladesh, topped the list of cities with the worst air quality on Friday morning, recording an Air Quality Index (AQI) score of 273 at 8:25am.

The air was classified as ‘very unhealthy’, according to the global air quality and pollution city ranking.

An AQI reading between 151 and 200 is considered ‘unhealthy’, while levels between 201 and 300 are deemed ‘very unhealthy’. An AQI between 301 and 400 is classified as ‘hazardous’, posing severe health risks to residents.

China’s Shanghai and India’s Delhi ranked second and third on the list, with AQI scores of 232 and 216 respectively.

The AQI is an index used to report daily air quality, indicating how clean or polluted the air is and the potential health effects associated with exposure.

Bangladesh’s AQI is calculated based on five pollutants: particulate matter (PM10 and PM2.5), nitrogen dioxide (NO₂), carbon monoxide (CO), sulphur dioxide (SO₂), and ozone.

Dhaka has long struggled with air pollution, with air quality typically deteriorating during the winter months and improving during the monsoon season.

According to the World Health Organisation (WHO), air pollution causes an estimated seven million deaths worldwide each year, primarily due to increased mortality from stroke, heart disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, lung cancer, and acute respiratory infections.

title: 68 to vie for a seat in RU admission tests
body:
About sixty eight students will vie for a single seat in the admission for first-year undergraduate programmes at Rajshahi University under the 2025–26 academic session.

The admission tests will begin tomorrow at five regional centres – Dhaka, Chattogram, Khulna, Rangpur and Barishal – with more than 272,000 applicants competing for 4,017 seats, said pro-vice chancellor professor Mohammad Main Uddin at a press conference on Thursday.

He said that the admission tests would start with unit C (science and engineering groups) on Friday, followed by unit A (humanities and social science groups) on Saturday, while those of the unit B (commerce group) would be held on January 24.

The A and C unit tests would take place in two shifts—from 11:00am to 12:00pm and from 3:00pm to 4:00pm—while the test of unit B would be held from 11:00am to 12:00pm, he added.

Professor Mohammad Main Uddin said that of the total applicants, 115,515 would sit for unit A, 30,886 for unit B, and 126,225 for unit C.

He said that the one-hour tests would be held under the multiple-choice question system. While candidates had to enter examination halls at least 30 minutes before the test begins, no one would be allowed to leave during the examination period.

All admission-related information would be available on the university’s official website, he added.

title: BPL resumes Friday after players and BCB reach agreement
body:
A revised schedule for the remaining matches—including two postponed on Thursday—of the ongoing Bangladesh Premier League was published after the Cricketers Welfare Association of Bangladesh declared to resume cricket following a meeting with the Bangladesh Cricket Board.

The announcement came following a meeting between the cricketers and the BCB at the Navana Tower in Gulshan in Dhaka on Thursday night.

The two matches scheduled for Thursday, which were boycotted by the players, would now be held on Friday. The matches originally scheduled for January 16 and 17 will be shifted by a day and will be held on January 17 and 18, respectively.

The Eliminator and Qualifier 1, scheduled to be held on January 19, have been shifted to January 20. There will be no reserve day for the play-off. However, the final, slotted on January 23, will have one reserve day.

The BCB also announced that they would refund the tickets of the Thursday’s games. Tickets purchased earlier for fixtures scheduled on January 16 will also remain valid for the rescheduled matches on the same day, in accordance with the revised itinerary.

Mohammad Mithun, the president of the CWAB, announced that they were returning for cricket’s interest after boycotting two BPL matches demanding the resignation of the BCB director, M Najmul Islam.

‘No one, not even us, is bigger than cricket. We also want to play. For cricket’s interest, we will resume playing from tomorrow,’ Mithun said at a press conference on Thursday night.

The decision came after the BCB assured them that they would continue to take action against director Najmul, whose comment sparked the chaos created in the country's cricket.

Iftekhar Rahman, the member secretary of the governing council of the BPL, said that they tried to reach Najmul but were unable to do so. He also said they wanted to bring him to the press conference.

‘He has been removed from his committee, and, following procedure as we operate under the constitution, he has been served a show-cause notice. He has been given 48 hours, which will expire at noon on the 17th, to submit his reply,’ Iftekhar said.

‘After that, the matter will go to the disciplinary committee. In the meantime, we tried all day to contact him. We wanted to bring him here today, but we could not reach him. [But] we all agreed that we wanted cricket to resume. I am very happy that we were able to reach a conclusion,’ he added.

‘The incident that happened wasn’t acceptable at all. We don’t accept and support this. We have come here and sat with the board president, Mithu Bhai [Iftekhar], and the other directors,’ said Mithun.

‘They confirmed us—because we can only control what is controllable. As he cannot be reached at the moment, they committed us to reach him as early as possible to fulfil our demand,’ Mithun added.

Mithun also stated that they were not in a position to play the second match scheduled on Thursday, even after the BCB removed Najmul from the finance committee.

The CWAB president also said that the BCB assured them about taking their other demands seriously.

Bangladesh national team Test captain Najmul Hossain Shanto and the ODI captain Mehidy Hasan Miraz were also present at the press conference.

title: Chhatra Dal demands resignations of CU VC, pro-VCs, registrar
body:
The activists of Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal, the students’ wing of BNP, staged a sit-in at Chittagong University on Thursday, demanding the resignations of the vice-chancellor, two pro-vice-chancellors and the registrar over the allegations of illegal recruitment.

The programme was held from 10:00am to 3:00pm at the main gate of the university’s administrative building. During the sit-in, pro-vice-chancellor (administration) Professor Kamal Uddin could not enter the office through the main gate and later entered through a pocket gate.

CU Chatra Dal joint general secretary Jalal Siddiquee said, ‘Over the past one and a half years, Chittagong University has been turned into a model of politicisation and nepotism in recruitment. All illegal recruitments must be cancelled immediately and the VC, two pro-VCs and the registrar must resign.’

He said, ‘We have given the university administration a 48-hour ultimatum. If they do not resign within the time, we will announce tougher programmes.’

Professor Kamal Uddin could not be reached for comment over the matter despite repeated calls.

Earlier, the Anti-Corruption Commission conducted a drive at Chittagong University on Wednesday afternoon after receiving allegations of irregularities.

ACC Chattogram office assistant director Sayed Alam led the drive, while deputy assistant directors Md Hamed Reza and Md Sabuj Hossain accompanied him.

ACC assistant director Sayed Alam said, ‘There are allegations that the daughter of pro-vice-chancellor (education) and a nephew of pro-vice-chancellor (administration) were appointed as teachers.’

He added that around 250 people were appointed after the current administration took charge, but not all were new recruits, as most were regularisation of appointments. Approval has been given for the appointment of 18 teachers in the latest syndicate meeting, but there was no proof of any recruitment beyond necessity, he said.

‘After verifying all documents, we will submit a full report to the commission. The report will be published within the next 48 hours. Interested persons can collect the report under the Right to Information Act.’

In this regards, CU registrar Mohammed Saiful Islam said, ‘After we came to the administration, the number of appointed people is 321.’

Among them, 88 are grade-three, 139 are grade-four, 16 are officers and 78 are teachers. These recruitments are mainly based on advertisements.

‘The word ‘corruption’ is not at all consistent with the administration of Professor Muhammad Yeahia Akhter. I spoke with the ACC team. We provided what they asked for,’ he added.

title: Tarique hears NTRCA-registered job-seekers’ demands
body:
Bangladesh Nationalist Party chairman Tarique Rahman on Thursday listened to the demands of job-seeking teachers registered with the Non-Government Teachers’ Registration and Certification Authority as they stood on the street outside his party office at Gulshan in Dhaka.

The interaction took place in front of the BNP chairperson’s political office in Gulshan in the afternoon, said Shayrul Kabir Khan, a member of the party’s media cell.

‘Tarique Rahman arrived at the Gulshan office by car from his nearby residence. At that time, a group of job-seeking teachers registered with NTRCA had gathered outside the office gate to press their demands,’ he said.

The teachers expressed their long-standing grievances over delays in recruitment and sought effective steps to ensure timely appointment to non-government educational institutions.

title: Politics turns into profit-driven business: Sujan
body:
Sushasoner Jonno Nagorik central secretary Badiul Alam Majumder on Thursday said that Bangladesh had witnessed a serious erosion of moral and democratic values, with politics degenerating into a profit-driven business through affinity with state power.

‘There has been a deep decline in compassion and moral values in society, accompanied by a sharp deterioration in political culture. Politics in Bangladesh has effectively turned into a business, where wealth is accumulated through political engagement,’ he said.

He made the remarks while addressing a divisional dialogue as chief guest at a city hotel in Rajshahi on Thursday afternoon.

Referring to city corporation elections held in 2008 and 2013, including those in Rajshahi, Khulna, Barishal and Sylhet, Badiul Alam said that although the 2013 polls were widely regarded as free and fair and candidates backed by the then ruling party were defeated, the personal wealth of several mayors increased dramatically within just five years.

‘Even at a time when corruption was not as pervasive as it is now, their assets rose sharply,’ he said, adding that corruption has now reached an alarming level across the country.

Badiul Alam said that his organisation had analysed candidates’ affidavits submitted ahead of the 2024 national election, a disclosure mechanism introduced following court rulings initiated by Sushasoner Jonno Nagorik.

While acknowledging that affidavits often contain incomplete or misleading information, he said that they nonetheless reveal significant trends in political finance.

‘In 2008, the average income of Bangladesh Nationalist Party candidates was higher than that of Awami League candidates because BNP was in power at the time. But after 2008, the average income of Awami League candidates increased astronomically, while the income of BNP candidates rose only marginally,’ he said.

This, he added, clearly demonstrated that wealth accumulation in Bangladesh was closely linked to access to state power.

‘Politics has become a lucrative business, and a form of democracy has emerged that can be bought with money,’ he said.

Warning of long-term consequences, Badiul Alam said that unless political culture changed and the ongoing decay of democratic values was halted, the country could not be able to move forward as a nation.

title: Iron pipe causes construction worker death in city
body:
A construction worker was killed after being struck by a falling iron pipe from the 6th floor of an under-construction building in Dhaka’s Maghbazar area on Thursday.

The deceased is Mohammad Taijul Islam, 20, hailing from Akand Para village under Nageshwari upazila in Kurigram.

He had been residing at the construction site in Moghbazar. His father’s name could not be known immediately.

The accident occurred at around 12:00pm at a 13-storey under- construction building near Maghbazar crossing in Ramna area, locals said.

Taijul sustained critical injuries when an iron pipe fell on his head from the sixth floor while he was filling sand into sacks on the ground floor.

His co-worker Altaf Hossain said they immediately rescued and took him to the emergency department of Dhaka Medical College Hospital, where doctors declared him dead at around 1:30pm.

Inspector Mohammad Faruk, in-charge of the DMCH police outpost, said the body has been kept at the hospital morgue for autopsy and the matter has been informed to the concerned police station.

title: Ord approved to establish Microfinance Bank
body:
The interim government on Thursday approved the draft Microfinance Bank Ordinance, 2026, with the aim of creating a scope for establishing microfinance banks alongside conventional banks for the first time in the country.

The council of advisers approved the draft ordnance at a meeting chaired by chief adviser Professor Muhammad Yunus at his Tejgaon office in the capital Dhaka.

The council of advisers also approved drafts of several other ordinances, a proposal on three conventions of the International Maritime Organisation and the draft of an agreement between the governments of Bangladesh and Azerbaijan.

Mentioning that the draft Microfinance Bank Ordinance, 2026, contained 35 clauses, chief adviser’s press secretary Shafiqul Alam at a briefing at the Foreign Service Academy in the capital Dhaka said that the responsibility for granting licences to these banks would lie with the Bangladesh Bank.

According to the draft ordinance, the authorised capital of a microfinance bank will be Tk 500 crore, while the paid-up capital will be Tk 200 crore.

Of the paid-up capital, 60 per cent will be contributed by the borrower-shareholders of the bank, while the remaining 40 per cent will be provided by the entrepreneurs.

However, the bank will be run as a social business enterprise, said Shafiqul.

The draft stated that such banks were necessary to ensure the proper and effective management of microcredit operations, and to create employment and reduce poverty.

However, these banks will not be allowed to be listed on the capital market.

Under the draft, applicants must apply to the Bangladesh Bank for a licence, and the Bank Companies Act will also be applicable to these banks. However, before obtaining a licence, the institution must first be registered under the Companies Act, 1994.

On May 17, 2025, at the inaugural ceremony of the new building of the Microcredit Regulatory Authority in the capital’s Agargaon, chief adviser Yunus emphasised the need for establishing microfinance banks in order to develop young people and marginalised communities as entrepreneurs.

On that day, he said that microcredit was the future of banking. This bank will not be like conventional banks, loans will be given without collateral, based on trust and confidence, and the main goal will be to expand social business.

Currently, microfinance operations in Bangladesh are conducted by non-governmental organisations.

According to Microcredit Regulatory Authority data, there are 683 microfinance institutions in the country.

The leading microfinance institutions in Bangladesh include BRAC, ASA, Bureau Bangladesh, TMSS, SSS, Sajeda Foundation, Uddipan, Jagorani Chakra Foundation, Palli Karma-Sahayak Foundation and Shakti Foundation.

The council of adviser also gave a final approval to the drafts of the Registration (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 2026 and the Protection and Conservation of Fish (Amendment) Ordinance 2026.

The council also approved the proposal on giving consent to the three International Maritime Organisation conventions — the International Convention on Civil Liability for Oil Pollution Damage, 1969, the International Convention on Civil Liability for Bunker Oil Pollution Damage, 2001, and the Nairobi International Convention on the Removal of Wrecks, 2007.

The meeting also approved the drafts of the agreement between the Government of Republic of Azerbaijan and the Government of People’s Republic of Bangladesh on exemption of visa requirements for holders of diplomatic, official and service passport.

title: Govt appoints 3 top officials to Biman board
body:
The interim government has appointed three key officials of the administration to the board of directors of Biman Bangladesh Airlines Limited.

The new appointed are national security adviser Khalilur Rahman, special assistant to the chief adviser Faiz Ahmad Taiyeb and senior secretary of the election commission secretariat Akhtar Ahmed.

A gazette notification was issued in this regard by the ministry of civil aviation and tourism on Wednesday.

The order, issued by the president’s command and signed by the ministry’s senior assistant secretary Shakila Pervin, stated that the appointments were made under Section 30(b) of the Bangladesh Biman Act, 2023.

The order comes into effect immediately in the ‘public interest’, according to the notification.

title: European military mission in Greenland as US aim ‘remains intact’
body:
A European military mission was taking shape in Greenland on Thursday, drawing a sharp rebuke from Russia, as Denmark said Washington still aimed to take control of the mineral-rich Arctic island.

Greenland’s prime minister Jens-Frederik Nielsen insisted meanwhile that ‘dialogue and diplomacy are the right way forward’, hailing in a Facebook post the fact that a dialogue was now ‘underway’.

The developments came a day after a White House meeting failed to resolve ‘fundamental disagreement’ over Greenland, an autonomous Danish territory that president Donald Trump insists the United States needs to ensure its security.

Two Danish troop transport planes landed in Greenland on Wednesday.

Britain, Finland, France, Germany, the Netherlands, Norway and Sweden have also announced the deployment of military personnel as part of a reconnaissance mission to Greenland’s capital Nuuk, under Denmark’s ‘Arctic Endurance’ exercise organised with NATO allies.

The modest military reinforcements — 13 soldiers from Germany, for example — are meant to prepare armed forces for future exercises in the Arctic, according to European defence sources.

‘A first team of French service members is already on site and will be reinforced in the coming days with land, air, and maritime assets,’ French president Emmanuel Macron said Thursday.

Germany’s defence ministry said the aim was to ‘explore the framework conditions for possible military contributions to support Denmark in ensuring security in the region’.

The foreign ministers of Denmark and Greenland met with US vice president JD Vance and secretary of state Marco Rubio in Washington on Wednesday.

Danish prime minister Mette Frederiksen said in a statement Thursday that ‘a working group’ was being set up to discuss how Arctic security could be improved.

‘However, this does not change the fact that there is a fundamental disagreement, because the American ambition to take over Greenland remains intact,’ Frederiksen said, hailing the arrival of European military personnel in Greenland.

‘There is consensus within the NATO alliance that a strengthened presence in the Arctic is crucial for European and North American security,’ she said.

Trump has argued that if the United States does not take Greenland, ‘China or Russia will’, deriding Danish efforts to increase security for Greenland as amounting to ‘two dogsleds’.

Denmark says it has invested almost $14 billion in Arctic security.

The Russian embassy in Belgium, where NATO is headquartered, said the arrival of NATO forces to Greenland was concerning.

‘The situation unfolding in the high latitudes is of serious concern to us,’ the embassy said in a statement late Wednesday.

NATO is ‘building up its military presence there under the false pretext of a growing threat from Moscow and Beijing’, it added.

On the streets of Nuuk, where red and white Greenlandic flags fly in shop windows, on apartment balconies and on cars and buses in a show of national unity, some residents have described anxiety over the geopolitical tensions.

‘It’s very frightening because it’s such a big thing,’ said Vera Stidsen, a 51-year-old teacher.

‘I hope that in the future we can continue to live as we have until now: in peace and without being disturbed,’ she said.

After attending the White House talks, Denmark’s foreign minister Lars Lokke Rasmussen posted Thursday on Facebook that ‘We agree on the objective: enhancing long term security in the Arctic. But we disagree on the method.’

‘This is 2026 — you can trade with people, but you don’t trade people.’

After the meeting, Trump for the first time sounded conciliatory on Greenland, acknowledging Denmark’s interests even if he again said he was not ruling out any options.

Trump has insisted Greenland is ‘vital’ for his planned ‘Golden Dome’ air and missile defence system, as it lies on the shortest route for missiles between Russia and the United States.

title: ACC to sue Anis Alamgir for Tk 3.26cr illegal wealth
body:
Five cases approved against children of ex-MPs Shamim Osman, Hanif

The Anti-Corruption Commission on Thursday decided to file a case against journalist Anisur Rahman Alamgir, also known as Anis Alamgir, on charges of amassing wealth worth Tk 3.26 crore beyond known sources of income.

Anis Alamgir is currently in jail in a case filed with the Uttara West police station under the Anti-Terrorism Act.

The commission also approved five cases against the sons and daughters of former Awami League lawmakers Shamim Osman and Mahbubul Alam Hanif for failing to submit their wealth statements to the commission within the stipulated time.

The decisions were made at a meeting held at the ACC headquarters in the capital’s Segun Bagicha, ACC director general (prevention) Akhtar Hossain told reporters at a press briefing.

Following the decisions, ACC assistant director Akhtaruzzaman will file a case against Anis Alamgir with the commission’s integrated district office, Dhaka-1.

According to ACC findings, Anis Alamgir’s total wealth stood at Tk 4.25 crore, while his net assets declared in his latest income tax return amounted to Tk 57.99 lakh.

The commission found that he accumulated Tk 3.26 crore beyond known sources of income and concealed the information in his wealth statement.

A team of the Detective Branch picked up Anis Alamgir from his residence in the capital on December 14, 2025, for questioning and took him to the DB office in Dhaka.

On the same day, a person named Arian Ahmed, claiming to be a member of an organisation, filed a complaint against Anis Alamgir and three others, accusing them of conspiring to destabilise the state and of links with a banned organisation.

The complaint was lodged with the Uttara West police station under the Anti-Terrorism Act and was later registered as a case.

Meanwhile, the ACC approved two cases against former Narayanganj-4 lawmaker Shamim Osman’s son Imtenan Osman and his daughter Labiba Zoha Angana for failing to submit their wealth statements.

The commission also approved three cases against former Kushtia-3 lawmaker Mahbubul Alam Hanif’s son Fahim Afsar Alam and his daughters Farhan Sadik Alam and Tanisha Alam on the similar charges.

title: Worker killed over suspicion of extramarital affair
body:
A jute mill worker was beaten to death with a hammer in Gazipur’s Sreepur upazila over suspicion of an extramarital affair with the assailant’s wife.

The deceased was Billal Hossain, 40, from Jamalpur district. He was a worker of Timex Jute Mills Limited at Sreepur.

Quoting witnesses, Sreepur police station officer-in-charge Mohammad Nasir Ahmed said that Janu Mia suspected that his wife, who also works at the jute mill, was having an extramarital affair with Billal.

Over the suspicion, Janu on Wednesday evening allegedly attacked Billal from behind with a hammer in front of the factory, leaving him severely injured, said Nasir, adding that Billal was taken to Mymensingh Medical College Hospital and later was taken to Dhaka Medical College Hospital, where the duty doctor declared him dead on Thursday morning.

Brother of the deceased filed a murder case while the police arrested Janu from Sreepur on Wednesday, said the police.

Janu was sent to jail after the police produced him before a court on Thursday afternoon.

Meanwhile, wife of Janu Miah denied having any extramarital affair with the deceased.

She said that her husband would sometimes behave irrationally and suspect her whenever she went outside or to work, which might lead to the incident.

title: Joint forces recover 28 firearms, arrest 325
body:
Joint forces, led by the Bangladesh Army, recovered 28 firearms and 419 rounds of ammunitions, 14 crude bombs, locally made weapons and drugs from January 9 to January 15 in drives across the country.

During the timeframe, joint forces also arrested 325 suspects red handed, including crime suspects, drug peddlers, drug addicts, members of robbery ring, teenage gangs and smugglers, said an Inter Services Public Relation Directorate press release issued on Thursday.

ISPR said that the detainees were handed over to the police after completing necessary interrogations and legal proceedings.

‘Bangladesh Army is conducting patrols and security drives in different parts of the country with the aim of ensuring public security. Besides, the Army is performing its duties to control unwarranted workers dissatisfaction in the industrial areas,’ said the ISPR.

The release said that the army would conduct such activities to keep law and order.

ISPR requested people to inform the nearest army camp when they would sense any suspicious or abnormal activities.

The Army was deployed across the country in aid to civil power following the ouster of Sheikh Hasina-led authoritarian regime on August 5, 2024 amid a student-led mass uprising.

On September 17, 2024, the interim government gave magistracy to commissioned army officers operating under the district magistrates.

title: RU officials abstain from work, demand safe workplace
body:
A group of officers and employees of Rajshahi University on Thursday observed a three-hour work abstention, protesting against recent attacks and harassment targeting university officials and demanding for them a safe and secure workplace.

Under the banner of Rajshahi University Officer Association, they also sat in near the university administrative building from 9:00am to 12:00pm.

Addressing the sit-in, RU officer association general secretary Reaj Uddin said that outsiders had recently been assaulting university employees during office hours and while returning home.

‘We are protesting these incidents and demanding a secure campus environment,’ he said, adding that repeated appeals to the university administration had failed to produce effective measures.

Association member and Bangladesh Mahila Dal’s Rajshahi divisional organising secretary Roksana Begam said that if there were allegations against anyone, the police and administration should act according to law.

‘But dragging officials away, beating them, extorting money, and threatening them with violence are unacceptable, those responsible for such disgraceful acts must be brought to justice,’ she added.

Earlier, the group of officers and employees formed a human chain on Wednesday, following the recent arrests of two pro-Awami League officials on Sunday and Monday.

On Monday afternoon, a group of locals detained Ahsan Habib, deputy registrar of Shah Makhdum Hall and a leader of Rajshahi city Awami League’s Ward 30 unit, at Binodpur Bazar while he was returning home from his office.

He was later handed over to Motihar police, who arrested him and sent him to jail in a case filed against him on charge of carrying out an attack on the student-led procession on August 5.

In a separate incident on Sunday, Hanif Md Palash, deputy registrar of Sher-e-Bangla Hall and organising secretary of the Awami League’s Paba upazila unit, was detained by a group of people at the Meherchandi Koraitala intersection in the city.

Police later arrived at the scene and arrested him in a case filed over an alleged attack on a student-led procession on August 5.

title: DU accounting dept chair resigns from Nat’l Pay Commission
body:
Professor Md Maksudur Rahman Sarker, chairman of the Dhaka University accounting department, has resigned from his position as a part-time member of the National Pay Commission.

He announced his resignation at a press briefing held at the Dhaka University registrar building on Thursday.

Professor Maksudur Rahman said that following verbal instructions from the finance adviser and written directives from the pay commission chairman on August 18, 2025, a four-member subcommittee was formed for all public universities in the country.

The subcommittee was tasked with preparing recommendations under three specific terms of reference.

He said that the subcommittee prepared a total of 33 implementable and justified proposals and recommended their phased implementation. Most of the proposals clearly suggested linking pay and allowances with quality of work and performance.

Maksudur Rahman said that, as the representative of Dhaka University, he had requested that the subcommittee report be placed as a separate agenda for discussion at a full commission meeting, but the request was not accepted.

He further said that the final report presented at the commission’s latest meeting held on January 8, 2026, did not adequately consider the key issues proposed for public universities.

He expressed concern that this would hinder the improvement of the quality of higher education in the country, adding that he chose to resign as he could no longer make an effective contribution under the circumstances.

The government formed the 22-member National Pay Commission through a gazette notification on July 27, appointing professor Maksudur Rahman as a part-time member as the representative of Dhaka University.

title: 1 held over patient’s death in ambulance obstruction
body:
A man was arrested in connection with the death of a patient in an ambulance which was obstructed twice allegedly by a local ambulance syndicate in Shariatpur.

Jamshed Ali Dhali, 65, died as he did not get treatment timely as the ambulance carrying him was stopped at two locations for around one and a half hours on the way to Dhaka, said his family.

Jubayer Hossain Ruman Dhali, grandson of the deceased, filed a case against four identified and six unidentified people with Palong model police station Wednesday night, said Shah Alam, officer-in-charge of the police station.

Police in a drive arrested Sumon Khan, ambulance driver, in this connection from Shariatpur district town on Thursday.

The other accused in the case are—Sajib, 18, Pervez, 26 and Hannan, 25.

Shariatpur deputy commissioner Tahsina Begum said an emergency meeting was held at the deputy commissioner’s office Wednesday afternoon with members of the Ambulance Owners’ Welfare Association where the owners assured not to obstruct ambulances, demand extra fares, or harass patients in the future.

However, local people demanded strict punishment of those responsible for the death.

Efforts are on to arrest the other accused, said police.

title: Chobi Mela XI begins today
body:
The 11th edition of Chobi Mela, an international festival of photography featuring 58 artists from 18 countries across five continents under the theme ‘Re’, will begin today in the capital.

Co-organised by Drik Picture Library and Pathshala South Asian Media Institute, the festival has evolved since 2000 into one of the world’s most inclusive photography events.

Local and foreign photographers, artistes and enthusiasts are expected to participate in an opening rally from the National Press Club to the Bangladesh Shilpakala Academy, followed by an inauguration ceremony at the Jatiyo Chitrashala Auditorium.

The 25th anniversary of Chobi Mela will showcase nine exhibitions across five venues in Dhaka - the Bangladesh National Museum, Bangladesh Shilpakala Academy, Alliance Française de Dhaka, DrikPath Bhobon, and the Bangladesh National Parliament.

A four-day evening programme comprising artist talk, panel discussions, lectures and film screening will be held at the Joyeeta Foundation of Dhanmondi, said festival director ASM Rezaur Rahman at a press conference held at BSA on Thursday.

Festival chief advisor Shahidul Alam, artistic directors and curators Munem Wasif and Sarker Protick, photographer and researcher Jannatul Mawa, Indian guest curator Tanvi Mishra and Sudanese photographer Muhammad Salah Abdulaziz spoke at the event.

Shahidul Alam said that the festival is a movement since the theme of the current edition is related to Bangladesh which as a country is going through reconstruction after the mass uprising.

‘We had expectations of a different Bangladesh. This must come not just politically, but also through cultural, social, and educational systems. This festival challenges western imperialism, aggression, occupation, and power dominance both domestically and internationally, he said.

Sarker Protick mentioned that Chobi Mela has always commemorated Bangladesh’s renowned photographers, adding that this time, the retrospective of photographer Amanul Haq is showcased at the National Museum.

In this edition’s programme, Jannatul Mawa discussed the exhibition focused on women’s participation and presence in the July mass uprising.

Adviser to the Ministry of Cultural Affairs Mostofa Sarwar Farooki will inaugurate the 16-day festival which will end on January 31.

title: Gono Bishwabidyalay holds 28th academic council meeting
body:
The 28th academic council meeting of Gono Bishwabidyalay was held on Thursday on its campus in Savar of Dhaka district.

Vice-chancellor Professor Md Abul Hossain presided over the meeting, said a press release.

The council reviewed and approved the minutes of its previous meeting and endorsed the results of undergraduate and postgraduate examinations of different sessions.

Trustee of Gono Bishwabidyalay Professor Abul Kashem Chowdhury joined the meeting online. Among others present were Dhaka University political science Professor Sabbir Ahmed, Jahangirnagar University pharmacy department Professor Md Sohel Rana, university registrar Md Ohiduzzaman, deans of various faculties, and other members of the academic council.

title: Abrar urges technology integration for green industrialisation
body:
Education adviser Professor CR Abrar on Thursday said that the integration of science, technology and creativity could play key role in ensuring green industrialisation and positive climate change.

‘Effective integration of science, technology and creativity is essential to achieving green industrialisation and addressing global climate change challenges,’ he said.

He made the remarks while speaking as the chief guest at the inaugural session of the two-day international conference titled ‘2nd International Conference on Frontiers in Science: Innovation and Technology for Greener Industry’ held at Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology in Dhaka.

The theme of the conference is ‘Let the People Breathe Green.’

The adviser said institutions and research initiatives that successfully combine engineering with basic sciences are likely to become the nucleus of sustainable solutions in the future.

‘This conference has created an important platform for knowledge exchange and interdisciplinary collaboration among young researchers, students, and established scientists and engineers,’ he said.

Referring to climate change, Abrar stressed that greening efforts must go beyond symbolic activities and focus on scientific solutions to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. ‘In this regard, research and technological innovation are most important.’

He further emphasised that coordinated efforts among universities, the government and the private sector are indispensable to promoting scientific research in the country.

The adviser also emphasised the importance of patenting and intellectual property rights in tackling climate challenges and promoting green industrialisation.

title: Scoping deal signed for Youth Entrepreneurship Policy’s NAP
body:
The Ministry of Youth and Sports signed a scoping document with Plan International Bangladesh and the United Nations Development Programme at the ministry on Thursday to develop a National Action Plan for the Youth Entrepreneurship Policy 2025.

The ceremony was chaired by Md Mahbub-ul-Alam, secretary, Ministry of Youth and Sports, and was attended by Sardar M Asaduzzaman, UNDP’s assistant resident representative and head of its Resilient and Inclusive Growth Cluster, and Kabita Bose, country director, Plan International Bangladesh, as well as senior officials of the three organisations.

The agreement was signed by Sheikh Mohammad Jobayed Hossain, joint secretary and head of Youth Division, Ministry of Youth and Sports, Plan International’s country director Kabita Bose and UNDP’s assistant resident representative Sardar M Asaduzzaman.

Addressing the signing ceremony, youth and sports secretary Md Mahbub-ul-Alam said, ‘This national action plan will serve as an important foundation for the implementation of the Youth Entrepreneurship Policy 2025. It will be helpful in creating opportunities for youth from vulnerable and marginalised communities to meaningfully participate in economic development.’

Other speakers said that the deal will strengthen inter-ministerial coordination and integrate the initiatives of the government, private sector and development partners. The action plan will give special emphasis on the inclusion of marginalised and disadvantaged youth, including rural areas and the Chittagong Hill Tracts.

title: Journalist Manik Saha remembered
body:
Politicians, journalists and cultural activists in Dhaka and Khulna on Thursday remembered freedom fighter and Ekushey Padak–winning journalist Manik Chandra Saha, calling on the authorities to take initiatives to reinvestigate and retry the case over his killing.

They made the demands in separate programmes to mark the 22nd anniversary of the death of the journalist.

Manik, a senior staff correspondent of New Age, was bombed to death in front of Khulna Press Club in Khulna city on January 15, 2004.

In Dhaka, friends and admirers of Manik, under the banner of ‘Sangbadik Manik Sahar Suhridbrinda’ held a commemoration meeting at the Dhaka Reporters’ Unity in the morning.

Former general secretary of the Communist Party of Bangladesh, Ruhin Hossain Prince, said that Manik Saha was a brave journalist who never feared any attack for the disclosure of truth.

He alleged that anti-liberation and communal forces were involved in the planned murder.

Speakers in the meeting also demanded a reinvestigation and retrial of the case of the killing to bring the killers to book.

Presided over by senior journalist Ashis Kumar Dey, the meeting was addressed, among others, by Hawkers’ Union general secretary Sekendar Hayat, journalists CK Sarkar, Rafiqul Islam Sabuj, Shakila Ruma, and Sundarban O Upakul Surokhkha Andolan coordinator Nikhil Chandra Bhadra.

In Khulna, Family members of Manik Saha, Khulna Press Club, Khulna Union of Journalists, Manik Saha Smriti Parishad, Khulna unit of CPB, Bangladesh Chhatra Union, and Ratan Sen Public Library separately placed wreaths at the Shaheed Sangbadik Smritistambha on Khulna Press Club premises.

They also held separate discussions in the city to mark the day. Born at Kalia in Narail on June 10, 1956, Manik Saha was the president of Khulna Press Club.

He was a Khulna-based stringer for BBC Bangla Service and the Khulna chapter president of Amnesty International.

The journalist was posthumously awarded the Ekushey Padak in 2009.

On November 30, 2016, nine people were jailed for life for killing Manik, but the family members and the journalist community rejected the verdict and demanded a retrial and reinvestigation into the murder case.

title: US immigration officer shoots Venezuelan man in Minneapolis
body:
A federal immigration agent shot a man Wednesday in Minneapolis, city officials said, urging the public to ‘remain calm’ a week after agents shot and killed an American woman in the same city.

Minneapolis Police Chief Brian O’Hara said the shooting resulted from a struggle in front of a residence between a man and an Immigration and Customs Enforcement agent on the north side of the city Wednesday evening.

‘During the struggle, the federal agent discharged his weapon, striking one adult male,’ O’Hara told reporters at a press conference.

The man suffered a non-life-threatening gunshot wound to his leg and was transported to a hospital for treatment, officials said.

The shooting marked the second time in a week an ICE agent had shot someone in Minneapolis, with the previous shooting resulting in the death of 37-year-old Renee Nicole Good on January 7, sparking on-going protests against the presence of federal agents in the northern US city.

‘We understand there is anger,’ officials wrote on the midwestern city’s X account, adding that ‘the City of Minneapolis again demands that ICE leave the city and the state immediately.’

O’Hara said Wednesday’s shooting generated a crowd of protesters around where it happened, with some throwing fireworks at officers.

Department of Homeland Security officials confirmed the shooting in a post on X, saying ‘an illegal alien from Venezuela’ was targeted for a traffic stop and resisted arrest.

‘While the subject and law enforcement were in a struggle on the ground, two subjects came out of a nearby apartment and also attacked the law enforcement officer with a snow shovel and broom handle,’ DHS said.

The officer then ‘fired a defensive shot to defend his life,’ hitting the initial subject in the leg.

Elected officials in Minneapolis and the state of Minnesota have decried the actions of Department of Homeland Security agents, including those with ICE.

‘This is not sustainable,’ Minneapolis mayor Jacob Frey told reporters, adding: ‘We have ICE agents throughout our city and throughout our state who, along with Border Patrol, are creating chaos.’

‘This is not the path that we should be on right now in America.’

In a video posted to social media earlier Wednesday, Minnesota governor Tim Walz decried ‘the chaos, disruption and trauma the federal government is raining down on our community,’ describing door-to-door interrogations by ‘armed, masked, undertrained’ ICE agents.

title: NATIONAL ELECTIONS: 60 get back candidacy on 6th-day hearings
body:
On the sixth day of appeal hearings against Returning Officers’ decisions upon nomination scrutiny for the upcoming 13th Jatiya Sangsad elections, a further 60 candidates had their nominations reinstated on Thursday.

The hearings took place on Thursday at the Election Commission auditorium at Agargaon in the capital Dhaka, where the commission approved the appeals.

According to EC sources, appeals numbering from 351 to 420 were disposed of on the sixth day.

Of these, 60 appeals were accepted while 34 were rejected.

Decisions on another 10 appeals were deferred pending the resolution of legal complexities and verification of required documents.

Since the appeal hearings began on January 10, a total of 337 candidates have regained the validity of their nominations over the first six days.

In contrast, 115 appeals have been rejected while decisions on 33 appeals have remained pending.

The Election Commission has announced that appeals numbering from 421 to 490 would be heard today.

Hearings for appeals numbering from 491 to 560 are scheduled for Saturday, while the final day of hearings would be held on Sunday, when all remaining appeals from number 561 and onwards will be considered.

A total of 645 appeal applications were submitted to the commission.

According to the announced election schedule, the deadline for the withdrawal of candidacy is January 20.

Electoral symbols will be allocated on January 21 while election campaigning will commence on January 22.

After 19 consecutive days of campaigning, all campaign activities must end at 7:30 am on February 10.

The voting for the 13th Jatiya Sangsad elections and the referendum on the July National Charter will take place nationwide on February 12, from 7:30 am to 4:30 pm.

title: Mia Saheb’s Maidan Khanquah to observe Shab-e-Meraj on Friday
body:
Mia Saheb’s Maidan Khanquah Sharif at Luxmibazar in Dhaka will hold religious discussion, Fateha Khwani, zikir, milad and doa mahfil marking holy Shab-e-Meraj.

Ninth incumbent religious leader Hazrat Shah Sufi Sayed Ahamadur Rahim (damat barakatuhum), who is also mutwalli of Sayed Abu Yousuf Abdullah (Ra) Waqf Estate and director of Mia Saheb’s Maidan Shah Saheb Bari Jame Masjid, will conduct religious discussion, the doa mahfil and akheri munajat.

A discussion on the holy night of ‘Lailatul Shab-e-Meraj’ and doa mahfil have been organised after Magrib prayers on the occasion on Friday.
