The Board remains fully committed to upholding the honour and dignity of all players under its jurisdiction.

‘In this regard, the BCB hopes that all cricketers will continue to display the highest standards of professionalism and dedication to the betterment of Bangladesh cricket during what is a challenging period for the game and will do their utmost to ensure continued participation in the Bangladesh Premier League,’ it added.

The last time the players boycotted cricket was in 2019, demanding the improvement of the country's overall cricket structure and system.

title: Polar Ice Cream offers new flavours, VR adventure at DITF
body:
Polar Ice Cream, a brand of Dhaka Ice Cream Industries Limited, has joined the 30th Dhaka International Trade Fair 2026 being held at Bangladesh-China Friendship Exhibition Center in Purbachal, said a press release.

At its General Pavilion – 14, visitors can enjoy the full range of Polar’s ice creams, along with exclusive new amazing flavours.

The pavilion also offers exciting attractions, including the immersive VR game ‘Ice Cream Ovijan,’ engaging on-ground activities and 50 per cent discount coupons for Fantasy Kingdom.

title: CWAB announces conditional return after boycott
body:
The Cricketers Welfare Association of Bangladesh announced it would return to ground on two conditions after boycotting two matches of the ongoing Bangladesh Premier League on Thursday, demanding the resignation of the Bangladesh Cricket Board director M Najmul Islam.

The match between the Chattogram Royals and Noakhali Express—scheduled at 1:00pm—followed by the match between the Rajshahi Warriors and Sylhet Titans—scheduled at 6:00pm—didn’t go ahead, as no teams showed up at the Sher-e-Bangla National  Stadium in Mirpur.

The Bangladesh Cricket Board announced the release of M Najmul Islam from his responsibilities as chairman of the finance committee with immediate effect after the first match was hit by the players’ boycott.

BCB stated that the board president, Aminul Islam, assumed the role of acting chairman of the finance committee.

However, that couldn’t convince the players to go to the ground, as the president of the CWAB, Mohammad Mithun, had earlier stated that they would resume playing only after getting a guarantee that Najmul would be removed from the BCB altogether.

But later in a press release, the CWAB said that they had reconsidered their position considering the Women’s T20 World Cup Qualifier, Under-19 World Cup, and the importance of the BPL.

Welcoming the decision of removing Najmul from his position, the CWAB said, ‘As he was given a show cause notice and the BCB asked for time for the process of his director role, we want to give that time. But we hope that the process will be continued.’

‘Besides that, as the director, M Najmul Islam made derogatory comments on the cricketers openly; we hope that he will apologise openly. We have notified the BCB that if he apologises openly and the process of his director’s role continues, then we’re ready to return to play,’ it added.

It was learnt that the two matches on Friday would go on as per schedule. Regarding the two postponed matches, a decision was yet to be made.

Earlier, the spectators waiting for the matches to resume were ejected soon after 5:30pm from the stadium, the scheduled time for the toss of the second match.

However, there was no announcement made on the giant screen at the ground. It was also unclear whether the tickets would be refunded.

There was also chaos outside the stadium as the army personnel were seen to scare off some spectators outside the stadium premises.

The players’ boycott came after Najmul made some comments on Wednesday regarding the uncertainty of Bangladesh’s participation in the forthcoming T20 World Cup scheduled to be held next month in India and Sri Lanka.

The CWAB then threatened to boycott all forms of cricket until Najmul resigned. On Wednesday, the BCB issued a press release stating that the comments made by Najmul were his own but reiterated its regret over the objectionable comments.

However, the cricketers remained firm in their stance of boycotting. The players’ boycott also disrupted four matches of the Dhaka First Division Cricket League on Thursday.

Cricket in the country has been going through a turmoil in recent times, as the BCB already requested the ICC to relocate their matches of the forthcoming T20 World Cup outside of India.

The BCB’s stance came after the Indian Premier League franchise Kolkata Knight Riders removed Bangladesh pacer Mustafizur Rahman from its squad upon receiving ‘advice’ from the Board of Control for Cricket in India.

title: SEB aids NSTU for agricultural research activities
body:
Southeast Bank PLC, as part of its special corporate social responsibility, has extended special financial support under its ‘Special CSR Fund’ to Noakhali Science and Technology University for conducting agricultural research activities, said a press release.

Southeast Bank chairman MA Kashem handed over the financial assistance cheque to NSTU vice-chancellor professor Mohammad Ismail at an event recently.

This financial assistance reflects Southeast Bank’s ongoing commitment to supporting agricultural research and contributing to national agricultural development as part of its social responsibility initiatives, it said.

Other senior officials from both organisations were also present at the event.

title: Indemnity ord for July activists okayed
body:
The interim government on Thursday approved the draft ‘July Mass Uprising Protection and Liability Determination Ordinance 2026’ to provide legal protection to those who took part in the July uprising.

The approval came at a meeting of the interim government council of advisers with chief adviser Muhammad Yunus in the chair at his Tejgaon office in Dhaka.

Speaking at a press conference at the Foreign Service Academy in the capital, law adviser Asif Nazrul said that the move fulfilled a prior commitment made to the July uprising participants.

‘We expect that it will be enacted into law through a gazette notification within the next five to seven days,’ he said.

According to Asif Nazrul, the ordinance grants legal immunity to those who took part in the July mass uprising for actions carried out for the purpose of political resistance.

‘By political resistance, we mean all actions organised with the objective of overthrowing a fascist government and restoring democratic governance. For such activities, July uprising participants have been granted exemption from criminal liability for acts carried out in July and August 2024,’ he said.

If any criminal cases have already been filed against July uprising participants for actions undertaken as part of the political resistance, the government will withdraw those cases, he said.

‘From now on, no new cases can be filed against them for actions carried out during July and August [of 2024] which were part of the organised political resistance,’ he added.

According to the adviser, killings or crimes committed for the purposes of personal gain, greed, or revenge, however, are not covered by the ordinance.

‘If, during July and August, anyone committed killings or other crimes in the name of political resistance in personal or narrow interests, they will not be exempted from criminal responsibility,’ he said.

He said that the responsibility for determining whether a killing was part of political resistance or driven by personal motives has been given to the National Human Rights Commission.

If a victim family believes that the family’s father, brother or relative was killed in someone else’s personal or narrow interest and that the killing had no connection to the fall of the fascist government, they may apply to the Human Rights Commission, he said.

‘If the commission finds that the killing was carried out in personal or narrow interests, it will conduct investigation and submit a report to the court, which will be treated like a police investigation report.’

‘If the commission determines that the killing occurred as part of the organised political resistance, no criminal liability will arise. But if it was in personal interests, the perpetrator will not be exempted,’ he added.

The law adviser said that the indemnity will apply to activities carried out between July 1 and August 31, 2024.

According to Asif Nazrul in response to a question, such laws are legal and were enacted in several countries after the fall of governments during the Arab Spring and other revolutions.

Article 46 of the Bangladesh constitution allows indemnity laws, he mentioned, noting that a similar law was enacted for freedom fighters in 1973.

The country’s first indemnity ordinance was issued on February 28, 1973, a presidential order that granted immunity for acts connected to the War of independence (March 1–December 16, 1971) and actions taken until February 28, 1972 to maintain or restore the law and order.

The second indemnity ordinance was issued on September 26, 1975, blocking any legal action against those involved in the killing of the country’s founding president Sheikh Mujibur Rahman and his family. The ordinance was repealed in 1996 after the Awami League returned to power.

After the alliance of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party and the Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami took office in 2001, the army-led Operation Clean Heart was launched. Allegations of extrajudicial killings led to the Joint Forces Operation Indemnity Act 2003, which protected security forces from prosecution.

The High Court declared it unconstitutional in 2015 after a writ by lawyer ZI Khan Panna as around 58 people reportedly died during the operation.

In 2010, Quick Enhancement of Electricity and Energy Supply (Special Provisions) Act, which barred court challenges to energy contracts and became known as an indemnity law.

The High Court on November 14, 2024 declared illegal the indemnity provision of the act. The interim government repealed the act on November 30, 2024.

title: Savor Int’l, Lanka Exhibitions to host INFRACON 2026 in Sri Lanka
body:
Savor International Limited (Bangladesh) and Lanka Exhibitions and Conference Services (Pvt) Limited (Sri Lanka) have announced staging of Infrastructure & Construction Exhibition or INFRACON 2026 to be held from July 3 to July 5 at Sirimavo Bandaranaike Memorial Exhibition Centre in Colombo, Sri Lanka.

The announcement was made at a press meet held on Tuesday at Jubilee Ballroom, Galle Face Hotel in Colombo, said a press release.

At the event, Savor International managing director Md Faizul Alam, ASHRAE Sri Lankan Chapter president Dayani Gunawardhana, Lanka Exhibitions chief executive officer Aasim Mukthar, chief operating officer Husnie Rauf and Solar Industries Association president Jawid Kamil were present.

Savor International is one of Bangladesh’s leading exhibition and MICE management companies, with extensive experience in organizing international trade exhibitions across infrastructure, energy, HVAC-R, construction, maritime, medical, and renewable energy sectors, the release said.

Through its partnership with Lanka Exhibitions, Savor is bringing global expertise, international exhibitors, and cross-border business opportunities to Sri Lanka via INFRACON 2026.

INFRACON 2026 will showcase solutions from five major industry segments, namely HVAC-R and Cold Chain, Power and Energy, Green Grid, Safe Water and Building Materials.

The exhibition will bring together policymakers, developers, engineers, contractors, architects, and technology providers.

With over 200 exhibitors and more than 5,000 trade visitors expected, INFRACON 2026 aims to position Sri Lanka as a regional hub for infrastructure and construction development while promoting sustainable, future-ready solutions.

The event is supported by Solar Industries Association and ASHRAE Sri Lankan Chapter.

title: Hosting.com launches operations in Bangladesh
body:
Global web hosting service provider hosting.com has commenced its business operations in Bangladesh through a formal launch ceremony on Wednesday at Hotel Sheraton in the capital, said a press releas.

Faiz Ahmed Taiyeb, special assistant to the chief adviser of the Ministry of Posts, Telecommunications, and Information Technology, attended as chief guest.

At the event, it was announced that hosting.com will offer Bangla-language customer support, enable local currency payments and ensure affordable hosting services tailored for Bangladeshi users.

The ceremony was attended by several distinguished guests, including Seb de Lemos, chief executive officer of hosting.com; Panos Kesisis, co-founder and chief operations officer; Ben Gabler, chief product officer; Daphne Monro, head of website and content; Imran Hossen, Bangladesh operations manager of hosting.com, and Shish Haider Chowdhury, secretary of the ICT Division.

Local technology experts and industry representatives were also present.

Speaking at the event, Faiz Ahmed Taiyeb said that the launch of hosting.com in Bangladesh would accelerate the growth of server infrastructure, cloud-based solutions, AI bot technology, search engine optimisation, and the domain business, among other digital services.

He noted that increased competition would enhance service quality, improve user experience, and open new opportunities, while also helping to build a strong digital ecosystem that would generate employment, boost skill development, and expand innovation in the knowledge, and technology-driven sectors.

Seb de Lemos said that the company had received significant feedback regarding pricing and service packages and is taking the matter seriously.

‘Very soon, we will introduce special pricing and packages for Bangladeshi customers, keeping local culture and market needs in mind,’ he said.

title: Bank Asia, BB to train SMEs in Sylhet
body:
Bank Asia PLC, in association with the Bangladesh Bank, has launched a month-long ‘Entrepreneurship Development Programme’ for SME entrepreneurs in Sylhet, said a press release.

Bangladesh Bank (Sylhet Office) executive director Khaled Ahmed inaugurated the programme on Monday as chief guest.

BB additional director and SICIP programme director Md Nazrul Islam and Bank Asia small business head Mohammad Saifuddowla were present as special guests.

Bank Asia zonal head (Sylhet and East zone) Md Nazmus Sakib presided over the programme.

The training programme has been designed to equip new entrepreneurs with essential business skills, enabling them to contribute to the country’s economic growth by fostering employment generation.

The programme is funded by the Asian Development Bank and managed by the Skills for Industry Competitiveness and Innovation Programme of the Finance Department, Ministry of Finance.

title: Ansar-VDP Unnayan Bank launches 15-day initiative
body:
Ansar-VDP Unnayan Bank, on the occasion of its 30-year anniversary, launched fortnight-long services from January 15 to 29, said a press release.

Managing director Mir Mofazzal Hossain inaugurated the initiative on Thursday with the objective of enhancing service quality and service coverage, as well as increasing deposit mobilisation, loan disbursement and loan recovery.

At the event, deputy managing director Sachindra Nath Samaddar, general manager Md Atikul Islam, Md Alauddin, along with other executives and officers and employees, were present.

In addition, all regional managers, regional audit heads, and all branch managers of the bank were connected through online platform.

Mir Mofazzal Hossain stated that the commitment of the initiative should be to transform the bank into a leading institution among specialised banks through the provision of standard, modern, information-technology-based services.

title: Xiaomi unveils REDMI Note 15 Series
body:
Handset and global technology brand Xiaomi has launched three new smartphones under its REDMI Note Series, said a press release.

The new lineup offers strong performance, long battery life, a premium design and AI Engine.

The REDMI Note 15 Series is now available at all official Xiaomi stores across Bangladesh.

The lineup includes REDMI Note 15 Pro+ 5G, Redmi Note 15 5G and Redmi Note 15 4G.

Ziauddin Chowdhury, country manager of Xiaomi Bangladesh, said, ‘Considering the immense expectations driven by the widespread popularity of the REDMI Note series, we have brought the REDMI Note 15 series to the Bangladeshi Xiaomi fans. This series will surpass all previous experiences of Xiaomi users with powerful performance and outstanding experience.’

The Redmi Note 15 Pro Plus 5G with 12GB storage and 512GB RAM is priced at Tk 62,999. The Redmi Note 15 5G (8GB + 256GB) is priced at Tk 36,999. Meanwhile, the Redmi Note 15 4G is available in 6GB + 128GB and 8GB + 256GB variants, priced at Tk 26,999 and Tk 29,999 respectively.

title: TECNO launches SPARK Go 3
body:
Global innovative technology brand TECNO has introduced SPARK Go 3 on the Bangladesh market, bringing an advanced smartphone experience with cutting-edge AI capabilities and robust features at an accessible price point, said a press release.

The SPARK Go 3 incorporates comprehensive AI-powered tools designed to enhance daily productivity. Features include Ask Ella for instant assistance, Web Summary for quick information digestion, Photo-Based Problem Solving, Photo Editing capabilities, AI Writing assistance and Hi Translate for seamless language communication.

It is equipped with a 6.75-inch display, powered by UNISOC T7250 Octa Core processor, offers IP64 dust and water resistance alongside drop protection up to 1.2 metres and a robust 5000mAh battery supporting 15W fast charging.

title: SSC, equivalent exams begin April 21
body:
This year’s Secondary School Certificate and its equivalent examinations will begin on April 21 and conclude on June 14.

The Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education, Dhaka published a schedule of the examinations on Thursday on its web site.

The theoretical examinations will be held between April 21 and May 20 and the practical ones between June 7 and June 14, according to the schedule, signed by the Bangladesh Inter-Education Board sub-committee convener professor SM Kamal Uddin Hyder.

The examinations will be held on all subjects and will start from 10:00am.

In the routine, 14 special instructions were given.

No one, except for the exam secretary, will be allowed to carry mobile phones in the examination centres.

All examinees have been requested to enter their respective examination halls 30 minutes before the starting time, fill up the OMR portion of the answer papers properly, collect their admit cards from own educational institutions at least three days before the examinations, and use calculators approved by the authorities.

They have been requested not to bend the answer paper and not to take part in the subjects which are not mentioned during their registrations.

The examinations will be held in the time mentioned in the question paper and at first the multiple choices part of the examinations will be held followed by the essay [theoretical] part of the examinations without any gap.

The examinees will have to pass the multiple choices, the theoretical and the practical parts of the examinations separately and can apply for re-evaluation of the answer papers within seven days after the publishing of the results.

title: Tarique Rahman, family call on Yunus at Jamuna
body:
Bangladesh Nationalist Party chairTarique Rahman, along with members of his family, met chief adviser Professor Muhammad Yunus on Thursday evening.

Neither the chief adviser’s office nor the BNP disclosed details of what was discussed during the meeting, which lasted for more than an hour.

Tarique arrived at the state guest house Jamuna at around 7:30pm with his wife Zubaida Rahman and their daughter Zaima Rahman.

In a brief statement, the chief adviser’s press wing said that Tarique and his family members spent more than an hour with  Professor Yunus and his daughter, Deena Yunus.

It said that members of the two families exchanged greetings during the meeting.

Tarique Rahman and his family left Jamuna at around 9:10pm.

In a post on its official Facebook page, the BNP described the visit as a courtesy call.

Sources at the Chief Adviser’s Office also described the programme as a family occasion, noting that a dinner was hosted by Professor Yunus for his guests.

This was the first meeting between Professor Yunus and Tarique since the latter assumed the post of BNP chairman.

Following the death of BNP chairperson and former prime minister Khaleda Zia on December 30, Tarique was elected as the BNP chairman on January 9.

The two leaders last met on June 13, 2025 during Professor Yunus’s visit to London, when Tarique Rahman was serving as the party’s acting chair.

That meeting took place at the Dorchester Hotel, after which representatives of both sides issued a joint statement.

The meeting concluded with an announcement that Bangladesh’s next general elections would be held in February 2026.

After spending 17 years in exile in the United Kingdom, Tarique returned to Bangladesh on December 25.

Upon his arrival at the Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport, he spoke by phone with chief adviser Muhammad Yunus from the VIP lounge.

According to the EC schedule, the 13th parliamentary election is set to be held on 12 February.

A referendum on reforms and the implementation of the July National Charter will also take place on the day.

title: DU bus vandalised during blockade by 7 colleges’ students
body:
A bus of Dhaka University was vandalised at the Science Laboratory intersection in Dhaka on Thursday during a blockade enforced by students of seven government colleges, leaving at least two students injured.

The incident occurred around 2:30pm when a Dhaka University bus was halted due to the blockade, said witnesses.

They said an argument broke out between students travelling on the bus and the protesting students of the seven colleges.

When members of the university’s proctorial team arrived and were escorting the bus away from the area, bricks were thrown from behind, shattering the bus windows and damaging its exterior.

Assistant proctor Rafiqul Islam said two windowpanes of the bus were broken after bricks were hurled at it and the outer part of the vehicle was also damaged.

Two DU students were injured in the incident, he said.

Later, at around 4:00pm Dhaka University students took position at the Nilkhet intersection in protest.

Dhaka University Central Students’ Union literary secretary Musaddiq Ali Ibn Muhammad said in a Facebook post that Dhaka University students were attacked and their bus was vandalised under the guise of a movement.

He demanded that those involved in the attack be identified through video footage and brought to justice.

Students of the seven colleges blocked the Science Lab and Technical Mor intersections, demanding the swift approval of the updated draft ordinance on Dhaka Central University.

The blockade which began after 12:30pm caused severe traffic congestion and widespread public suffering.

Earlier on Wednesday, the students also observed blockade programmes at several locations in Dhaka.

title: SC to hear plea to upgrade Hasina, Kamal’s sentence to death Jan 20
body:
The Appellate Division of the Supreme Court on Thursday fixed January 20 for holding hearing on an appeal filed by the ICT prosecution seeking enhancement of the sentence awarded toSheikh Hasinaand Asaduzzaman Khan Kamal in the crimes against humanity case stemming from the July Mass Uprising.

‘Fixed on 20.01.2026,’said the short order passed by Appellate Division Judge-in-Chamber Justice Md Rezaul Haque.

The apex court passed the order after going through a plea for holding an early hearing of the petition. The matter was listed as item number 58 on the cause list of the Appellate Division Chamber Judge Court this morning.

The ICT prosecution filed the appeal with the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court on December 15, 2025.

In the appeal, the prosecution prayed for upgrading the sentence of imprisonment till natural death to the death penalty for their conviction on certain counts of crimes against humanity committed during the July Mass Uprising.

The prosecution filed ‘Criminal Appeal No 96/2025: Chief Prosecutor vs Sheikh Hasina and another’ on eight grounds with the Appellate Division on that day.

On November 17, ICT-1 convicted Sheikh Hasina and Asaduzzaman Khan Kamal of crimes against humanity committed during the July Mass Uprising, holding them guilty under the doctrine of superior command responsibility.

The three-member tribunal, headed by Justice Golam Mortuza Mozumder, delivered the verdict after finding them guilty on multiple charges.

Under charge number one, the tribunal found both Sheikh Hasina and Asaduzzaman Khan Kamal guilty on three counts and sentenced them to imprisonment till natural death.

Under charge number two, they were found guilty on three counts and sentenced to death for those offences.

The tribunal also found former Inspector General of Police (IGP) Chowdhury Abdullah Al-Mamun guilty of the same charges but sentenced him to five years’ imprisonment, considering his full disclosure of events and cooperation with investigators as an approver.

In addition, the tribunal ordered the confiscation of all properties owned by Sheikh Hasina and Asaduzzaman Khan Kamal in favour of the state and directed the authorities to ensure adequate compensation for the families of the July martyrs and those injured.

title: MIST civil engineering dept organises 5th Industrial Advisory Panel
body:
The civil engineering department at the Military Institute of Science and Technology organised its 5th Industrial Advisory Panel meeting on Thursday, said a press release.

The three-hour session was chaired by the MIST civil engineering department head Brigadier General A N M Foyezur Rahman, ndc, psc, and featured a distinguished group of leaders from both the industrial and academic sectors.

Professor Ishtiaque Ahmed, head, Department of Civil Engineering, BUET; M A Sobhan, managing director, DPM; Brigadier General Rezaul Karim, managing director, SKS; Brigadier General Syed Obaidullah Hel Shafi, Directorate of Works & Chief Engineer (Army); Brigadier General Md Shamim Iftakhar, DW&CE (Navy); Professor Syed Ishtiaq Ahmad, member BPERB, IEB; Syed Hasan Imam, chief engineer, CEIP, BWDB; Md Golam Yazdani, superintendent engineer, LGED; Fahima Shahadat, country manager, Menard South Asia; Nashid Islam, director, ABC Limited; Md Abdullah Al Hossain, convener, BASE; Galib Mohammad, CEO, AKIJ ISPAT; Md Saiful Islam, head of Materials, GPH Ispat and Md Masudur Rahman, country manager (BD), SMEC; Lt Col Shakil and Professor Zoynul Abedin participated in the meeting.

The panel members commended MIST’s progress in areas such as research, academic excellence, and industry-driven projects, offering valuable insights for future development.

In his remarks, Brigadier General A N M Foyezur Rahman appreciated the recommendations made by the panel and sought support from the industry.

The suggestions of the discussants will be reflected in producing competent civil engineering graduates. Besides academic requirements, this occasion develops new networks in the industries for MIST graduates and further develops academia-industry collaboration, added the press release.

title: New US ambassador to Bangladesh presents credentials to president Shahabuddin
body:
United States ambassador-designate to Bangladesh Brent T Christensen on Thursday presented his credentials to president Mohammed Shahabuddin at Bangabhaban in the capital.

‘Today I had the honour of presenting my Ambassadorial credentials to president Shahabuddin. The United States is proud to call Bangladesh a friend,’ the new US ambassador said in a statement shared by the US embassy in Dhaka on submission of his credentials.

‘In over 50 years of partnership, we have worked together to promote regional stability, economic growth benefiting both our countries, and the sovereignty of our great nations. I look forward to continuing this work and further strengthening the US-Bangladesh relationship,’ he added.

Ambassador Brent Christensen along with his wife, Deanne Dao, arrived in Dhaka on Monday.

Christensen was confirmed by the Senate as ambassador to Bangladesh on December 18, 2025.

He served most recently as the senior official performing the duties of under secretary of state for Arms Control and International Security in January–October 2025, according to a release of the US embassy shared earlier.

In this role, he oversaw the Department of State’s global efforts on security cooperation, security assistance, counterterrorism, counternarcotics, and nonproliferation, it added.

A career member of the Senior Foreign Service, Christensen previously served as the foreign policy adviser to the commander of United States Strategic Command and as counsellor for political and economic affairs at the US Embassy in Dhaka.

Christensen has held additional assignments overseas in the US missions to the Philippines, El Salvador, and Vietnam.

His other domestic roles include serving as deputy director at the Office of Regional Security and Arms Transfers, Bureau of Political-Military Affairs, as special assistant to the Special Representative for North Korea Policy, as a fellow on the US House of Representatives Committee on Foreign Affairs, and as Bangladesh country officer in the Bureau of South and Central Asian Affairs, said the release.

Christensen also served as one of two career foreign service members of the Foreign Service Impasses Disputes Panel, part of the US Federal Labor Relations Authority.

A distinguished graduate of the National War College, Christensen earned a Master of Science in National Security Strategy.

Christensen likewise holds a Master of Science in Statistics from Texas A&M University and a Bachelor of Arts in Economics and Managerial Studies from Rice University.

Before joining the Foreign Service in 2002, he worked as a management consultant in Houston and New York City.

title: BCB releases Najmul after players boycott BPL match
body:
The Bangladesh Cricket Board on Thursday released M Najmul Islam from his responsibilities as chairman of the finance committee with immediate effect after the first match between the Chattogram Royals and Noakhali Express was hit by a players’ boycott.

President of the Cricketers Welfare Association of Bangladesh Mohammad Mithun stated that they would resume playing only after getting a guarantee that Najmul would be removed from the BCB altogether.

Thursday was supposed to be the first day of the Dhaka leg of the ongoing Bangladesh Premier League. However, no teams were seen as the players held their stance of boycotting all cricket, demanding Najmul’s resignation.

CWAB then announced that Mithun would conduct a press conference at a city hotel in Dhaka around 1:00pm. However, it was then deferred to 2:30pm.

More than 50 cricketers, including national team Test captain Najmul Hossain Shanto, ODI captain Mehidy Hasan Miraz, and T20I captain Litton Das, were present during the press conference.

‘We’ve had a discussion among the players. We have been hearing the word ‘procedure’ a lot. At one point, they wanted to OSD him, but we didn’t accept that,’ Mithun said.

‘Then they wanted 48-hour time, as they needed it according to the procedure. But the question we’re having is this: if he doesn’t resign after 48 hours, we will still have to suspend the game. Now they are requesting us to play,’ he added.

‘Now we’ll go to the ground on one condition. If the BCB commits in front of you [the media] that he won’t be in the BCB after 48 hours, and if he still remains, then the responsibility won’t be upon the players, and it will be upon the BCB,’ Mithun further said.

‘We can return to the field in this condition. We have already contacted them. But we weren’t given any assurance,’ said Mithun.

The CWAB president also said that the BCB president, Aminul Islam, didn’t contact them for a single time. When the players called for a press conference, Aminul was seen at the Sher-e-Bangla National Stadium, looking at the wicket of the match.

Two and a half hours after Mithun’s press conference, the BCB announced the release of Najmul.

‘The decision has been taken in accordance with the authority vested in the BCB president under Article 31 of the BCB Constitution and is aimed at ensuring the continued smooth and effective functioning of the Board’s affairs,’ a BCB press release read.

‘Until further notice, the BCB president will assume the role of acting chairman of the Finance Committee. The BCB reiterates that the interests of the cricketers remain its highest priority. The Board remains fully committed to upholding the honour and dignity of all players under its jurisdiction.

‘In this regard, the BCB hopes that all cricketers will continue to display the highest standards of professionalism and dedication to the betterment of Bangladesh cricket during what is a challenging period for the game and will do their utmost to ensure continued participation in the Bangladesh Premier League,’ it added.

However, while filing this report, the teams of the second match—Rajshahi Warriors and Sylhet Titans—were yet to arrive at the stadium.

title: SC clears way for holding polls in Pabna-1, Pabna-2 constituencies on Feb 12
body:
The Appellate Division on Thursday cleared the way for holding the elections in Pabna-1 and Pabna-2 constituencies on February 12 in accordance with the boundaries specified in the Election Commission’s September 4 gazette.

An Appellate Division bench, led by Chief Justice Zubayer Rahman Chowdhury, passed the order.

As per the order, Sathia upazila will constitute Pabna-1 constituency while Sujanagar and Bera upazilas will form Pabna-2.

Acting attorney general Arshadur Rouf additional attorney general Anik R Haque stood for the EC while Barrister Imran Abdullah Siddique and Barrister HM Shanjid Siddiaue represented Jamaat-e-Islami and BNP respectively.

On January 14, the High Court fixed January 15 for hearing on the leave-to-appeal petition filed challenging the validity of the gazette issued by the Election Commission.

On January 10, the Election Commission suspended the election in Pabna-1 and Pabna-2 constituencies until further order from the court.

The decision was taken in line with an order issued by the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court on January 5 over a dispute regarding the demarcation of the two constituencies, the parliamentary constituencies No 68 Pabna-1 and No 69 Pabna-2.

According to an EC circular issued on January 6, the commission decided to keep the elections scheduled for February 12 in the two constituencies suspended until further directives from the court.

On September 4 last year, the Election Commission published a gazette on the delimitation of the country’s 300 constituencies bringing changes to the boundaries of 46 constituencies, including Pabna-1 and Pabna-2. As per the gazette, the Pabna-1 was formed with the entire Santhia upazila, while Pabna-2 comprised Sujanagar and Bera upazilas.

But the EC on December 24 last issued a revised gazette to restore the previous boundaries of the two constituencies in compliance with an order of the High Court.

Following the High Court order, the Pabna-1 (Constituency No 68) was formed with Santhia Upazila and parts of Bera Upazila, including Bera Municipality and the unions of Haturia Nakalia, Natun Varenga, Chakla and Kaitola.

The Pabna-2 (Constituency No 69) was again formed with Sujanagar Upazila and the remaining areas of Bera Upazila, excluding Bera Municipality and the four unions—Haturia Nakalia, Natun Varenga, Chakla and Kaitola.

Later, Jamaat-e-Islami candidate for Pabna-1 Mohammad Najibur Rahman and the election commission filed separate petitions with the Appellate Division, seeking a stay on the High Court verdict.

On January 5, the Appellate Division stayed the effectiveness of the election commission’s revised gazette until leave-to-appeal petitions would be filed.

title: Schoolgirl, abducted in Khulna, rescued from Sylhet
body:
Members of the Rapid Action Battalion, in a drive on Wednesday, rescued a Class 8 female student who was abducted from Khulna on January 1, from Dakkhin Surma upazila of Sylhet.

The elite force also arrested Shohagh Mia, 29, son of Nur Islam of Chhatak upazila in Sunamganj district, from the spot.

According to RAB, the victim went to school on January 1 but did not return home, said KM Shahidul Islam, additional superintendent of police (media officer) of RAB-9.

Failing to trace the girl, her family later learned that three to four unidentified assailants had forcibly abducted her from the Phulbari Gate bus stand under Khanjahan Ali Police Station in Khulna and taken her away in a CNG-run auto-rickshaw.

Later, the victim’s father filed a case with Khanjahan Ali Police Station.

title: BNP demands seat-wise postal ballots
body:
The Bangladesh Nationalist Party on Thursday demanded constituency-specific postal ballots featuring candidate names and symbols, accusing the Election Commission of running a flawed and biased system that was disadvantaging the party.

The BNP proposed that the postal ballots should carry only the names and symbols of the candidates contesting a specific seat to avoid confusion among voters.

A BNP delegation, led by standing committee member Salahuddin Ahmed, met chief election commissioner AMM Nasir Uddin at the EC headquarters in Dhaka to place a number of complaints and proposals before the commission.

Speaking to reporters after the meeting, Salahuddin said that the BNP was particularly alarmed by the first-ever introduction of expatriate postal voting, which he claimed was already showing serious signs of manipulation.

He referred to social media footage showing  hundreds of ballot papers allegedly found in single residences abroad, with some of those ballots reportedly being seized.

Salahuddin also cited allegations that postal voting had begun in certain places even though the official date was set for the January 22 while ballots were being collected by people other than the registered voters in some cases.

The postal ballots sent to expatriates, he said, have not been properly considered, as the BNP has pointed out earlier, adding that those involved in preparing and distributing the ballots, as well as the EC, must provide clear explanations.

He said that videos circulating on social media showed 200 to 300 ballots being found in single residences, some being seized in different places and in some cases postal voting had already started despite being scheduled for January 22.

Salahuddin said that there were reports of ballots being received in one person’s name by someone else, indicating widespread irregularities.

He said that while some errors could be expected as expatriate voting was being introduced for the first time in Bangladesh the current problems were turning the BNP into victims and causing the party harm.

The BNP leader alleged that certain actions had been taken in favour of a particular political party, commenting that this was no longer merely a suspicion but was now being borne out by evidence.

Alongside its concerns about expatriate voting, the BNP pressed for a major change in the way domestic postal ballots are designed and used.

Salahuddin said that postal ballots within Bangladesh should be constituency-specific, rather than using a single generic format.

‘For each constituency there is already a standard ballot paper with the names and symbols of all the candidates contesting that seat. That same ballot should be used as the postal ballot for that constituency,’ he said.

The BNP delegation also raised wider issues, including enforcement of the electoral code of conduct and the conduct of some election officials.

Salahuddin alleged that while BNP chair Tarique Rahman had postponed activities in deference to the commission’s requests, other political leaders continued to issue statements and videos in the breach of electoral rules without facing any action.

He also claimed that several returning officers were showing a partisan behaviour.

According to the BNP, the Election Commission had said that it would consider the party’s proposals and complaints, including those related to postal ballots and the code of conduct.

However, Salahuddin stressed that the party was seeking immediate and clear answers, particularly on the expatriate postal voting process, which was already damaging confidence in the election.

Meanwhile, election commissioner retired Brigadier General Abul Fazal Md Sanaullah later on the day said that the Election Commission had found no evidence of any irregularities in the postal ballots sent to expatriate Bangladeshis abroad after reviewing several video clips circulating on social media regarding the distribution of postal ballots.

The election commissioner made the remarks while briefing reporters at the Nirbachan Bhaban in the city.

title: Ordinance sets 2-year penalty for harming wetlands
body:
The president promulgated ‘The Bangladesh Haor and Wetland Conservation Ordinance, 2026’, introducing stringent penalties of up to two years’ imprisonment or fines of up to Tk 10 lakh to protect the country’s haors and wetlands from destruction and misuse.

The ordinance was issued by the legislative and parliamentary affairs division of the ministry of law Wednesday evening.

Under the ordinance, violation of any order or directive will result in a maximum of two years’ imprisonment or a fine of Tk 10 lakh, or both. However, violation of a protection order will carry the same punishment.

The crime and punishment under the ordinance is cognisable, non-bail able and non-negotiable, according to the law.

The ordinance also provides that violating bans in protected haor and wetland areas will be punishable by two years in prison or a fine of Tk five lakh, or both.

Extraction or use of water in a manner that damages the aquifer, aquatic animals or plants will attract the same penalty.

Illegal occupation, filling, unauthorized excavation or conversion of haors, wetlands or sandbanks will lead to up to two years’ imprisonment or a fine of Tk 10 lakh.

The same punishment will apply for construction of infrastructure or activities that disrupt the normal flow of water.

For polluting water, soil or the environment, the ordinance stipulates two years’ imprisonment or a fine of Tk 2 lakh, or both.

According to the ordinance, an official list of haors and wetlands across the country will be prepared.

Based on the information provided by district administrators, the government will publish the list through a gazette notification, which may be revised or updated from time to time.

The ordinance mandates that the concerned department will formulate a master plan for the protection, conservation, development and integrated management of haors and wetlands and update it regularly.

This plan must align with the government’s existing policies, plans and strategy papers.

The government has also been empowered to declare any haor or wetland a protected area, in which case it will be mandatory to take opinions from relevant authorities, organizations and stakeholders.

Before undertaking any development project related to haors or wetlands, the opinion of the Haor and Wetland Development Department must be obtained.

The ordinance clearly states that no project can be implemented without following this prescribed procedure.

If the activities of any individual or organization damage the ecosystem of haors or wetlands, the director general may determine the amount of damage and order compensation.

If necessary, corrective measures may also be ordered, and compliance will be mandatory.

The ordinance lists several specific offences and punishments. Extracting soil, sand, stones or other natural resources from haors, wetlands or sandbanks without permission will be punishable by two years’ imprisonment or a fine of Tk 10 lakh.

Fishing by prohibited nets, electric shocks, poison baits or toxic substances will also result in two years in prison or a fine of Tk 10 lakh.

Additionally, harvesting fish or aquatic resources in a manner that disrupts reproduction or production will be punishable by one year’s imprisonment or a fine of Tk 5 lakh.

The ordinance further states that hunting migratory birds or protected aquatic animals, destroying wet forests or sandbanks, or destroying animal habitats will be punishable by two years’ imprisonment or a fine of Tk 5 lakh, or both.

title: People suffer as 7-college students block roads again
body:
City dwellers suffered for hours as students of the seven government colleges, formerly affiliated with Dhaka University, on Thursday blocked major crossings in the capital for the second day, causing huge traffic congestion while demanding a university ordinance.

The protesters on the day announced a mass gathering at the Science Laboratory crossing on Monday, as the revised ordinance for the proposed Dhaka Central University was not approved at Thursday’s advisory council meeting, which they had been demanding.

Tertiary-level students of seven government colleges, Dhaka College, Begum Badrunnesa Government Women’s College, Eden Mohila College, Government Bangla College, Government Shaheed Suhrawardy College, Government Titumir College and Kabi Nazrul Government College, which were once affiliated with Dhaka University, on Thursday blocked the Science Laboratory, Technical and Tatibazar crossings between 12:00pm and 5:00pm.

They had been demanding that the government approve the revised ordinance of the proposed Dhaka Central University by Thursday and issue the ordinance immediately.

A few hundred students, mostly from Dhaka College, Eden Mohila College and Begum Badrunnesa Government Women’s College, brought out a procession from the Dhaka College and blocked the Science Laboratory crossing from about 12:45pm to 5:00pm.

Addressing a press briefing at the Science Laboratory crossing before ending that day’s demonstration, Dhaka College student Nayim Howlader said that the students of the seven government colleges blocked city roads demanding that the government to approve the proposed Dhaka Central University ordinance in the advisory council meeting on Thursday.

‘We did not receive any positive responses from the authorities regarding our demand,’ said Nayim.

Announcing Monday’s mass gathering at the Science Laboratory crossing, Nayim said that a stage, ‘Oddhadesh Moncho’, would also be launched there to press home the demand for issuance of the university ordinance.

During the four-hour blockade, heated arguments between students and motorcycle riders, rickshaw pullers, bus drivers and city commuters took place at Science Laboratory crossing.

A group of protesting students and Dhaka University students, who were in a university bus, also locked in arguments and clashed as the bus was stuck due to the blockade, while the group also broke the glasses of the bus.

Long tailbacks of vehicles were seen in the Science Laboratory crossing’s surrounding areas, including Dhanmondi, Mirpur road, Azimpur and Shahbagh.

Dhaka Metropolitan Police assistant commissioner for Dhanmondi zone, Mostafa Tariquzzaman, said that police tried to convince the protesters to lift the blockade as people were suffering. ‘But, they refused to withdraw the blockade.’

The students of Government Shaheed Suhrawardy College and Kabi Nazrul Government College blocked the Tatibazar crossing for about one and a half hours from 12:00pm to 1:30pm before joining the protesting students at Science Laboratory crossing.

The students of Government Bangla College blocked the Technical crossing for about four hours from 1:00pm to 5:00pm.

DMP assistant commissioner for Mirpur zone traffic, Md Sharif Ul Alam, said that the blockade severely disrupted traffic in the area and the police diverted vehicles at Mazar Road crossings to ease the sufferings of the people who entered the capital using the Gabtoli entry point.

Students of the seven colleges on Wednesday blocked the Science Laboratory, Technical and Tatibazar crossings and Mohakhali’s Amtoli road between 11:30am and 6:00pm pressing the demand.

On January 27, 2024, Dhaka University authorities decided to cancel their affiliation with these colleges following a longstanding student movement for a separate university for the seven colleges.

On March 16, a decision was made to name the new university Dhaka Central University.

A section of teachers and students of the seven colleges, however, opposed the structure of the proposed university after the publication of the draft ordinance.

Tertiary-level students of the seven government colleges held a blockade and two-day sit-in in the Shikkha Bhaban area from December 7, 2025, demanding the issuance of the ordinance.

title: Interim govt on wrong track over energy plan: CPD
body:
Centre for Policy Dialogue on Thursday said that the draft of the Energy and Power Sector Master Plan 2026-2050 presented by the interim government was faulty and would compound the already threatened energy security.

The draft that was presented before the advisory council committee on January 6 at the chief adviser’s office is yet to be made public by the Ministry of Power, Energy and Mineral Resources.

At a press conference at its office in the city, the CPD, a local think-tank, said that the new draft almost echoed the master plan hurriedly prepared by the previous Awami League regime before being ousted in August 2024 amid a mass uprising.

In July 2023, the Ministry of Power, Energy and Mineral Resources had prepared the master plan for the energy and power sector titled ‘Integrated Energy and Power Master Plan’ amid criticisms over flaws in demand estimation, over-emphasis on the liquefied natural gas import and unfeasible solution for renewable energy expansion.

It was expected that the new master plan would address all the key challenges that came from the previous plan and would come up with a better and more supportive energy transition.

Highlighting different aspects of the new draft, CPD research director Khondaker Golam Moazzem said that the interim government led by Muhammad Yunus was walking on the wrong track.

He blamed over-reliance on bureaucrats for the faulty draft of the Master Plan, the implementation of which would increase dependency on fossil fuels.

Besides, the much-sought after transition towards renewable energy will remain elusive, said the research director.

The new draft has forecast the power demand at 40,836 megawatts by 2040 and 59,351 MW by 2050 compared to the forecast of 50,335 MW by 2040 and 70,000 MW by 2050 in the ‘Integrated Energy and Power Master Plan’ in 2023.

Calling projections on demands overestimated, the CPD said that the demand should not be more than 30,000 MW in 2040.

The CPD also said that the new draft was projecting an investment of $25 billion to $30 billion for LNG terminals but made no projection on required investment on renewable energy.

Responding to a question, the CPD research director said that pressures from external sides on the interim government were not unlikely since both the United States and Japan sought commitment over energy security.

Dhaka has finalised the Economic Partnership Agreement with Tokyo and is negotiating over a new preferential trade arrangement with Washington.

Questioning the hurry by the Ministry of Power, Energy and Mineral Resources, the CPD has urged the interim government not to finalise the draft before the Jatiya Sangsad elections on February 12.

The CPD suggested that the new elected government should prepare the draft with the assistance of an independent panel of resource persons.

title: Mild coldwave sweeps parts of Bangladesh, Met Office says
body:
A mild coldwave is sweeping over parts of Bangladesh and it may continue in some places, Bangladesh Meteorological Department said on Thursday.

According to the regular Met Office bulletin, ‘Mild coldwave is sweeping over the districts of Dinajpur, Panchagarh, Kurigram and Chuadanga and it may continue and spread.’

Light to moderate fog may occur at a few places over the country during late night to morning.

Panchagarh’s Tetulia recorded the country’s lowest temperature at 7.5 degrees Celsius on Thursday morning.

Night and day temperatures may fall slightly over the country.

Weather may remain dry with temporary partly cloudy sky over the country.

title: Two motorcyclists killed in B’baria road accident
body:
Two motorcyclists were killed after being hit by a truck in Ashuganj upazila of Brahmanbaria on Wednesday night.

The accident took place in the Sonarampur area of the upazila on the Dhaka-Sylhet highway.

The deceased were identified as Saimon, 20, son of Shahidul Islam of village Lakshmipur in Bhairab upazila of Kishoreganj district, and Abdur Rahman, 23, son of Makrul Molla of the same village.

Shafiqul Alam Chowdhury, officer-in-charge of Ashuganj Police Station, said that the two youths were travelling from Bishwaroad in Sarail towards Ashuganj when their motorcycle collided with a truck coming from the opposite direction in the Sonarampur area.

Both riders were seriously injured in the crash and were taken to the Ashuganj Upazila Health Complex by local people.

After receiving the news, family members went to the hospital and took the bodies home.

‘Legal action in this connection is underway,’ the OC added.

title: Dhaka becomes most polluted city with AQI score of 271
body:
Dhaka, the densely populated capital of Bangladesh, ranked first among the world’s most polluted cities on Thursday morning, recording an Air Quality Index of 271 at 9:13am.

Today, the city’s air was classified as ‘very unhealthy’, indicating a serious health threat, according to the AQI report.

Bishkek in Kyrgyzstan, Karachi in Pakistan, and Kolkata in India occupied the second, third, and fourth spots on the list, with AQI scores of 215, 208, and 200 respectively.

According to the AQI scale, a reading between 50 and 100 is considered ‘moderate’, with generally acceptable air quality, though sensitive individuals should limit prolonged outdoor exertion. AQI levels of 101–150 are ‘unhealthy for sensitive groups’, 151–200 is ‘unhealthy’, 201–300 is ‘very unhealthy’, and readings above 301 are considered ‘hazardous’, posing severe health risks.

The AQI, which reports daily air quality, informs residents how clean or polluted the air is and highlights potential health effects. In Bangladesh, the AQI is calculated based on five key pollutants — particulate matter (PM10 and PM2.5), nitrogen dioxide (NO2), carbon monoxide (CO), sulfur dioxide (SO2), and ozone.

Dhaka has long struggled with air pollution. Air quality usually deteriorates in winter and improves during the monsoon season.

The World Health Organisation estimates that air pollution causes about seven million deaths worldwide each year, primarily from stroke, heart disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, lung cancer, and acute respiratory infections.

title: EC approves 73 more appeals on 5th day
body:
The election commission on Wednesday approved 73 more appeals on the fifth day against the order of acceptance and cancellation of nomination papers of the returning officers in the forthcoming 13th national elections.

EC secretariat senior secretary Akhtar Ahmed told reporters in the evening that 100 appeals were heard on the day against the decisions of the returning officers.

Out of these, he said, 73 appeals were approved, while 17 appeals were rejected and 10 were kept pending.

He said so far, the EC have accepted the hearing of 380 appeals. Out of those, 277 appeals were approved, 81 were rejected or cancelled and 23 appeals are pending for various reasons.

He further said 645 appeals were heard and the EC will hear the appeals till January 18.

The appeal hearing began at 10:00am Wednesday at the auditorium of Nirbachan Bhaban at Agargaon in Dhaka. The appeal hearing was held till 5:00pm with a one-hour break at noon by the full commission chaired by chief election commissioner AMM Nasir Uddin.

One hundred appeals from 281 to 380 were heard on the day. The hearings of 381 to 480 appeals and pending appeals will be held on Thursday from 10:00am to 5:00pm, while 481 to 510 and pending appeals will be held on Friday from 3:00pm to 5:00pm.

In addition, the appeal hearing process will conclude with the hearing of appeals numbering 511 to 610 on Saturday and 611 to 645 and the remaining pending appeals on Sunday.

Earlier, the returning officers or assistant returning officers declared the nomination papers of 1,842 candidates, out of 2,568, valid.

title: Old cases overshadowed by new ones: probe
body:
The Commission of Inquiry on Enforced Disappearances in its final report said that the cases of forced disappearances were quickly overshadowed by fresh surges of enforced disappearances, particularly heightened during politically volatile periods, such as national elections and opposition mobilisations.

‘This cyclical pattern underscores not merely enforcement deficiencies but a calculated strategy aimed at dual domestic and international audiences – a hallmark of authoritarian resilience globally,’ said the final report of the commission titled ‘Unfolding The Truth: A Structural Diagnosis of Enforced Disappearance in Bangladesh’.

The report said that Bangladesh under the decade and a half of Awami League rule witnessed the systematic entrenchment of enforced disappearances, custodial torture, and extrajudicial killings – practices routinely justified under the banners of ‘counterterrorism’ and ‘violent extremism prevention’.

‘Initially framed as necessary security measures, these practices rapidly evolved into primary instruments of authoritarian control, emblematic of broader global patterns of democratic erosion and the instrumentalisation of security frameworks for political ends,’ the report said.

The report said that the security agencies most deeply involved — particularly the Rapid Action Battalion, Directorate General of Forces Intelligence, Detective Branch and Counter Terrorism and Transnational Crimes unit of the police, originally working as elite units targeting militant threats — increasingly became notorious for assisting the repressive Awami League regime by operating extrajudicial apparatuses of abduction, torture, and intimidation that bypassed judicial accountability.

‘The Awami League’s strategic utilisation of these forces was deliberate and methodical. Even international interventions, exemplified by targeted US sanctions on some senior RAB officials in December 2021, yielded only transient interruptions,’ said the report.

The commission was formed by the interim government on August 27, 2024, to enquire into cases of enforced disappearances that occurred during the tenure of the Sheikh Hasina-led authoritarian Awami League regime that was ousted from power on August 5, 2024 amid a mass uprising.

‘A total of 1,913 complaints were filed with the commission. After intensive scrutiny, 231 were found to be duplicates. In many instances, the same case had been sent through multiple channels, for example, by email, courier, and in-person submission, or both an organisation and the affected individual had submitted separate complaints about the same incident, and left 1,682 unique complaints,’ the final report said.

The report also revealed that it had found evidence that ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina, her military adviser Tarique Ahmed Siddique, and former home minister Asaduzzaman Khan Kamal were directly involved in high-profile enforced disappearances.

After removing 231 duplicate files and 113 files of non-qualifying cases, the report said that they were left with 1,569 complaints involving potential enforced disappearance, which was about 82 per cent of all complaints.

title: On-arrival visa suspended to avert risks before polls: Touhid
body:
The Bangladesh government has issued a set of guidelines restricting the issuance of the on-arrival visa facility between January 15 and February 15 to avoid ‘any unwanted situation’ ahead of the upcoming general election scheduled for February 12.

‘Such instructions have given to prevent the arrival of any unexpected individuals from outside. An unexpected situation may be created during the national poll…We are not suspending issuance of visas,’ foreign affairs adviser Md Touhid Hossain told reporters at his office on Wednesday.

Responding to a question, he said that those having valid purposes of their visit may apply for visas since the regular process would remain open for them.

He said that they did not like to allow anyone unwanted enter the country anytime, availing the on-arrival visa facility.

Touhid, also a former diplomat, expressed hope that there would be a smooth transition through the national election, unlike the situation following the fall of the previous regime in August 2024.

The foreign adviser said that they had already received the new instructions from the home affairs ministry in this regard.

The home ministry is truly better positioned to comment on the matter, he said, but acknowledged that the foreign ministry had received instructions in this regard.

Citizens coming from the Unites States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Russia, China, Japan, Singapore, Malaysia, South Korea, United Arab Emirates, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Kuwait, Oman, Bahrain, Egypt, Turkey, Brunei, and European countries to Bangladesh for tourism, trade, investment, or a government job may get a visa on arrival, according to the home ministry.

The home affairs ministry issued the visa guidelines on Monday to preempt the entry of anyone unexpected ahead of the crucial polls.

As per the new instructions, existing visa requirements and procedures must be strictly followed before the issuance of all types of visas, while the verification of required documents and coordination among concerned agencies should also be strengthened.

title: More migrants are dying in ICE detention under Trump: data
body:
The confrontation tactics used by US Immigration and Customs Enforcement have been in the spotlight since the fatal shooting of protester Renee Nicole Good in Minneapolis, Minnesota, on January 7.

But data released by the agency shows that immigration detention centres can also be deadly environments for those being held in them.

Press releases from ICE reveal that a number of people have died in custody in the just first few days of 2026 — immediately following a year when migrant detainee deaths reached a 20-year high and the number of ICE detentions increased exponentially.

More than 68,000 adults were in ICE detention as of the end of December, up from about 36,000 in December 2023, agency data shows.

At least four people have died while being detained by ICE in 2026, according to the agency.

The deaths all occurred in the first 10 days of the year, with three deaths announced in the period from January 9-10.

The migrants, all men, were aged from 42 to 68 years old. Two were nationals of Honduras, one was a Cuban, and the fourth man was a Cambodian.

The deaths of two of the men were attributed to ‘heart-related health issues,’ with the other two causes of death not clearly indicated.

Only one of the latter cases was listed as ‘under investigation.’

The previous year, 2025, was already the deadliest year for ICE detainees in two decades. At least 30 people died while being held in immigration detention centres — the highest death toll since 2004, the year after the agency was created.

The 2025 figure represents more than the total number of deaths recorded in ICE custody during the entire Biden administration (2021-2025).

In those four years, 26 people died in while in ICE detention, according to data compiled by the American Immigration Lawyers Association from ICE reports.

External observers have raised concerns over the level of medical treatment that detainees receive.

A 2024 report from the American Civil Liberties Union concluded that up to 95 per cent of deaths in ICE detention could have been prevented with appropriate care.

The report analysed deaths in ICE custody between 2017 and 2021 by studying thousands of pages of documents obtained through public records requests.

Medical experts who reviewed these documents found widespread evidence of incorrect or inappropriate treatment as well as severely delayed medical care.

Contacted by AFP, ICE did not respond to a request for comment by time of publication.

title: Israel kills six in Gaza despite ceasefire
body:
The Israeli military said Wednesday it had killed six ‘militants’ in an updated toll from an exchange of fire in Gaza the day before, accusing them of violating the ceasefire in the territory.

The military said in a statement late on Tuesday that it had killed two of six ‘militants’ it had identified adjacent to its troops in western Rafah and that tanks had fired on them.

It said they were killed in an ensuing exchange of fire, including aerial strikes, while troops continued to search for the rest.

In a statement on Wednesday, the military said that ‘following searches that were conducted in the area, it is now confirmed that troops eliminated the six terrorists during the exchange of fire’.

It said the presence of the militants adjacent to troops and the subsequent incident were a ‘blatant violation of the ceasefire agreement’.

A security source in Gaza reported late on Tuesday that Israeli forces had ‘opened fire west of Rafah city’.

Under a truce that entered into force in October following two years of war between Israel and Hamas, Israeli forces in Gaza withdrew to positions behind a demarcation known as the ‘yellow line’.

The city of Rafah is located behind the yellow line, under Israeli army control. The area beyond the yellow line remains under Hamas authority.

Both sides have repeatedly accused the other of violating the ceasefire.

According to the health ministry in Gaza, which operates under Hamas authority, at least 165 children have been killed in Israeli attacks since the ceasefire began on October 10.

The UN children’s agency UNICEF said on Tuesday that at least 100 children — 60 boys and 40 girls — had been killed since the truce.

Israeli forces have killed a total of at least 447 Palestinians in Gaza since the ceasefire took effect, according to the ministry.

The Israeli army says militants have killed three of its soldiers during the same period.

Meanwhile, Hamas officials said Wednesday the group had opened talks with Egyptian mediators in Cairo on the formation of a technocratic committee to govern Gaza as part of the US-brokered truce plan for the Palestinian territory.

Under a 20-point programme proposed by US president Donald Trump in October, Gaza would be administered by a transitional Palestinian committee operating under the supervision of a so-called ‘Board of Peace’ to be chaired by Trump himself.

The Cairo meeting between a Hamas delegation and Egyptian mediators aims to address the formation of the committee, including its operational mechanisms, a senior Hamas official said.

title: ICJ genocide case flawed and unfounded: Myanmar govt
body:
An international court case alleging Myanmar committed genocide against the mostly Muslim Rohingya minority is ‘flawed and unfounded’, Yangon’s foreign ministry said Wednesday.

In a statement published in a state newspaper, the government called on the International Court of Justice to ‘reach its judgement based on fact and settled law strictly within the framework of the Genocide Convention’.

ICJ judges are hearing three weeks of testimony, which began in The Hague on Monday, as they weigh accusations by The Gambia that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya in a 2017 crackdown.

Hundreds of thousands of Rohingya Muslims fled violence by the Myanmar army and Buddhist militias, escaping to neighbouring Bangladesh and bringing harrowing accounts of mass rape, arson and murder.

On the first day of the hearings Gambia’s justice minister Dawda Jallow told the court the Rohingya ‘have been targeted for destruction’.

Lawyers for military-ruled Myanmar will begin their court response on Friday.

‘The allegations made by The Gambia are flawed and unfounded in fact and law,’ said the Yangon foreign ministry statement, printed in the Global New Light of Myanmar newspaper.

‘Biased reports, based on unreliable evidence, cannot make up for truth,’ it added.

The country — ruled by a military junta since a coup in 2021 — was co-operating with the ICJ ‘in good faith’ in a sign of its respect for international law, it said.

The statement did not use the word Rohingya, referring instead to ‘persons from Rakhine state’, adding it was committed to their repatriation.

The Rohingya are not recognised as an official minority by the Myanmar government, which denies them citizenship and considers them Bengali interlopers, despite many having roots in the country stretching back centuries.

Today, 1.17 million Rohingya live crammed into dilapidated camps in Cox’s Bazar in Bangladesh.

Myanmar has always maintained the crackdown by its armed forces was justified to root out Rohingya insurgents after a series of attacks left a dozen security personnel dead.

The Gambia, a Muslim-majority country in west Africa, is taking Myanmar to the ICJ, which rules in disputes between states, alleging breaches of the 1948 UN Genocide Convention.

Under it any state can haul another before the ICJ if it believes genocide is being committed.

Legal experts are watching the proceedings as they could give clues for how the ICJ will handle similar accusations against Israel over its military campaign in Gaza, in a case brought by South Africa.

A final decision could take months or even years, and while the ICJ has no means of enforcing its decisions, a ruling in favour of The Gambia would heap more political pressure on Myanmar.

title: Uphold force’s image: adviser asks new BGB recruits
body:
Home adviser retired Lieutenant General Md Jahangir Alam Chowdhury on Wednesday called on newly recruited Border Guard Bangladesh members to uphold the force’s image by embodying discipline, professionalism and the core values of the organisation.

‘Honesty, intelligence, reliability, loyalty and enthusiasm are the criteria for the discipline and professional skills of a force… The new soldiers will uphold the tradition of the force by reflecting these qualities,’ he told the concluding parade and oath-taking ceremony of 104 batch of the new BGB recruits.

Jahangir, also in charge of the adviser to the ministry of agriculture, was speaking as the chief guest, at the Bir Uttam Mujibur Rahman Parade Ground of the Border Guard Training Centre and College at Baitul Izzat of Satkania in Chattogram.

The adviser said this 230-year-old traditional force has become a well-organized, smart, disciplined and professional patriotic force over the course of time.

He said as the ‘Watchful Guard of the Border’ of the country, the BGB is playing an effective role in safeguarding the integrity of the motherland by ensuring security within the 4,427 km long frontiers.

The BGB has been able to earn the trust of the countrymen by performing its noble tasks with efficiency and professionalism in preventing smuggling, drugs and human trafficking, suppressing any cross-border crime, assisting the civil administration for maintaining the country’s internal law and order,  and dealing with disasters, the adviser also mentioned.

Addressing the newly recruited BGB soldiers, the Home Adviser said, ‘Discipline is the ornament of a soldier’s life.... A real soldier is one who never backs down from carrying out orders and duties.’

Referring to the forthcoming general polls, the adviser said about 8.17 lakh security personnel will be engaged to successfully holding the elections. ‘Some 37,353 members of the BGB will be deployed at some 467 upazilas across the country.’

The adviser lauded the brilliant parade displayed by the BGB recruits and wished them continued success in every aspect of their respective careers.

In the 104th recruit batch, 3023 recruits, 2950 male and 73 female, were provided basic training over a period of about four months.

Senior secretary of the ministry of home affairs Nasimul Gani, BGB director general Major General Mohammad Ashrafuzzaman Siddiqui and Commandant of BGTC&C, among others, were present.

title: Journalist Manik Saha’s 22nd death anniv today
body:
The 22nd anniversary of the death of Manik Chandra Saha, a freedom fighter and Ekushey Padak-winning journalist, will be observed today.

On this day in 2004, he was bombed to death near Khulna Press Club in Khulna.

Manik was a senior staff correspondent for New Age and a Khulna-based stringer for BBC Bangla Service.

He was also the Khulna chapter president of Amnesty International and the president of the Khulna Press Club.

He was posthumously awarded the Ekushey Padak in 2009.

The Sangbadik Manik Sahar Suhridgon, an organisation of the slain journalist’s well-wishers in Dhaka, will hold a commemoration meeting at the Dhaka Reporters’ Unity at 11:00am today.

Manik’s family, Khulna Press Club, Khulna Union of Journalists, Khulna district and city units of the Communist Party of Bangladesh, Bangladesh Chhatra Union, Udichi Shilpi Goshthi, Manik Saha Smriti Parishad and Ratan Sen Public Library will organise separate programmes in Khulna to pay tribute to him.

On November 30, 2016, nine people were jailed for life for killing Manik, but his family members and the journalist community rejected the verdict and demanded a retrial after a reinvestigation into the murder case.

Manik Saha was born at Kalia in Narail on June 10, 1956.

Manik, also a leftist political activist, started his career as the Khulna district correspondent of the Daily Sangbad.

title: Dockyard security guard stabbed dead in Keraniganj
body:
A dockyard security guard was stabbed to death allegedly  by muggers in  Bashundhara River View Balur Math area of South Keraniganj early Wednesday.

The victim is Ahmed Dewan, 60, son of late Mofa Dewan of South Pangaon, Keraniganj. He worked as a security guard at Pangaon Dockyard.

His daughter Rekha said a group of muggers intercepted him in Balur Math area at around 5:30am and stabbed him in the left side of his abdomen before fleeing with his mobile phone.

He was later taken to the emergency department of Dhaka Medical College Hospital at around 9:30am where doctors declared him dead, she said.

Inspector Md Faruk, in-charge of the DMCH police camp, said the body has been kept at the hospital morgue and the death has been reported to Keraniganj south police station.

title: RU staff stage protests for safe workplace
body:
A group of officers and employees of Rajshahi University on Wednesday formed a human chain demanding a safe and secure working environment on the campus.

More than a hundred officers and staff, under the banner of the Rajshahi University Officers’ Association, staged the demonstration on the university’s Paris Road, following the recent arrests of two pro-Awami League officials on Sunday and Monday.

On Monday afternoon, a group of locals detained Ahsan Habib, deputy registrar of Shah Makhdum Hall and a leader of Rajshahi city Awami League’s Ward 30 unit, at Binodpur Bazar while he was returning home from his office.

He was later handed over to Motihar police, who arrested him and sent him to jail in a case filed against him on charge of carrying out an attack on the student-led procession on August 5.

In a separate incident on Sunday, Hanif Md Palash, deputy registrar of Sher-e-Bangla Hall and organising secretary of the Awami League’s Paba upazila unit, was detained by a group of people at the Meherchandi Koraitala intersection in the city.

Police later arrived at the scene and arrested him in a case filed over an alleged attack on a student-led procession on August 5.

Addressing the human chain, Rajshahi University Officers’ Association general secretary Reaz Uddin said that both administrative and academic activities were being hampered as officers faced humiliation, harassment and intimidation during office hours on campus and while returning home after work.

He alleged that incidents of mob intimidation, mental harassment and physical assault against university officers had increased alarmingly in recent days.

Association president Anowarul Islam alleged that even outsiders were entering the campus, harassing the officials and employees, and were dragging them outside their office before handing over to police.

‘Such actions were aimed at creating an unsafe and dysfunctional working environment, causing serious harm to the university’s interests and reputation,’ he said.

Anowarul Islam alleged that despite repeated demands for proper investigation and exemplary punishment of those responsible for creating instability, the university administration had remained silent and acted merely as a spectator.

Condemning the administration’s inaction, association member and Bangladesh Mahila Dal’s Rajshahi divisional organising secretary Roksana Begam said that officers and employees were not aligned with any individual or group and had joined the university solely to discharge their professional duties.

She demanded that the university authorities ensure the safety and security of all officers and employees, warning that stronger protest programmes would be announced if effective steps were not taken to stop mob intimidation on campus.

The speakers also announced a work abstention programme to be enforced from 9:00am to 12:00pm on Thursday in front of the university administration building.

title: EC clarifies postal ballots’ viral video in Bahrain
body:
The election commission on Wednesday clarified a viral video showing a large number of postal ballots delivered to a single address in Bahrain, saying that the incident resulted from differences in the country’s postal delivery system and did not involve any irregularities in the voting process.

EC senior secretary Akhtar Ahmed made the clarification while responding to a question from reporters at Nirbachan Bhaban in the capital in the evening.

Asked about the viral video showing many postal ballots reaching the same address, he said Bangladesh’s postal ballots are being sent through the Universal Postal Union with the assistance of the Bangladesh Postal Department.

‘This has happened in the case of Bahrain as the postal systems of some countries including the Middle East are different. There, about 160 ballots have been left in one place in one box,’ he said.

Akhtar explained that the delivery system there is similar to student hostels, where letters are kept at a designated place and recipients collect their own mail from there.

‘Some 160 [postal] ballots were placed in a box. Later, the expatriate Bangladeshi brothers opened the box and divided it among four or five people—whoever lives in the room next to them takes it or delivers it,’ he said.

The EC secretary said a video of the process was recorded and circulated, which he personally thinks should not have been done. ‘From what we understand, someone posted the video out of excitement at receiving a ballot paper. If you observe carefully, there is no evidence that any envelope was opened.’
