She alleged that some traders were charging Tk 300 to Tk 500 more than the usual price, calling the situation unbearable for middle- and low-income families.

Small restaurant owners said that the shortage had directly affected their businesses, forcing many to shorten operating hours or reduce items to save fuel.

A hotel owner at Saheb Bazar said that his daily operating costs had risen sharply. ‘If this situation continues, we will not be able to keep the business running,’ he said, adding that some restaurants had already stopped business.

Retailers, however, blamed irregular supply from distributors.

Abdus Salam, a gas cylinder retailer at Nawdapara Bazar area in Rajshahi city, told New Age that deliveries had remained inconsistent for weeks.

‘We are receiving far fewer cylinders than demanded. Customers think we are hoarding, but we simply do not have stock,’ he claimed.

An employee of Halima Traders at Alupotti More said that they had not received any supply for several days.

At Malda Colony Market, a trader demanded Tk 1,600 from this correspondent for a single cylinder, citing acute shortages.

Md Pervej, manager of Halima Agency, the official distributor of Jamuna and Sungas, told New Age that they previously sent vehicles every day to collect gas.

‘Now suppliers are delivering one truck after two days, sometimes after three or even four days. Gas is being supplied in limited quantities and not according to demand,’ he said.

Echoing Pervej, Ananda Kumar Saha, distributor of Omera Gas, told New Age that deliveries had become highly inconsistent as they currently received only two batches per week compared to their previous daily supply.

‘Our operations are scheduled to shut down temporarily as the cylinder we received today has already been distributed. A new delivery is supposed to arrive on the following Friday,’ he added.

The distributor of Bashundhara LP Gas Limited said that his supply point had remained closed for nearly a month due to lack of supply.

Energy experts said that Rajshahi’s heavy dependence on LPG, especially in areas devoid of piped gas, had made residents vulnerable to supply disruptions. They warned that repeated crises point to weak regulation and poor oversight of private LPG distribution.

With no immediate relief in sight, residents fear the crisis could worsen further, particularly for low-income families dependent entirely on gas cylinders for cooking.

title: Application deadline for GST admission extended
body:
The application deadline for first-year undergraduate admission under the General, Science and Technology cluster system for the 2025–26 academic year has been extended once again.

Naogaon University has been included in the integrated admission system for the first time.

An official notification, signed by IU acting registrar, also the secretary of the Integrated Admission Committee of GST cluster universities, professor M Manjurul Haque, was issued in this regard on Monday night.

According to notification, applicants will be able to submit their applications from January 12 to January 16.

With its inclusion, Naogaon University will admit students to two departments. The addition raises the total number of universities under the GST admission system to 20.

Earlier, the application process for the integrated admission tests concluded on December 30.

Following the inclusion of Naogaon University, the application window has been reopened to provide prospective students with another opportunity.

Applications will be accepted from 12:00pm on January 12 until 11:59pm on January 16 under existing conditions.

Detailed information regarding the admission process is available on the official website, www.gstadmission.ac.bd.

The GST cluster admission tests for the 2025–26 academic year are scheduled to begin on March 27 with C unit examination, followed by B unit test on April 3 and A unit examination on April 10.

title: The Body Shop announces end of season sale
body:
British-born beauty brand The Body Shop has announced its ‘End of Season Sale’ that will run till February 2, said a press release.

The sale offers enthusiasts a chance to stock up on their much loved beauty essentials with discounts of up to 50 per cent.

The month-long sale spans across categories — Bodycare, Haircare, Skincare and Fragrance.

Highlights of the sale include bestsellers such as Moringa Body Lotion and Strawberry Body Yoghurt, alongside signature scents like White Musk, Full Rose, and British Rose EDT.

For those looking to elevate their skincare routine, staples like the Vitamin C Glow Boost and Vitamin E Intense moisturisers are also featured at significant savings, the release said.

title: Airbus delivers more planes in 2025, but falls short of target
body:
Airbus said Monday it delivered 793 commercial aircraft in 2025, a slight increase from the previous year but falling short of its initial ambitions due to a manufacturing problem.

The European manufacturer had originally targeted a seven per cent increase in deliveries of commercial aircraft to airlines, but fuselage panel quality issues on its flagship A320 model contributed to holding back the gain to four per cent.

Both Airbus and its rival Boeing have struggled to return to pre-pandemic production levels as their entire network of suppliers was disrupted, even as airlines are eager to modernise their fleets with more fuel-efficient aircraft and expand to meet an expected increase in passenger numbers over the coming decades.

Airbus still has considerable ground to cover to reach the 863 aircraft it delivered in 2019, the year before the pandemic upended the global economy.

Investors keep a close eye on delivery figures as airlines pay the majority of the price of aircraft upon taking delivery, making it a key element in the financial performance.

Airbus received 1,000 orders for planes in 2025, with its order book rising by 889 after taking cancellations into account, to a record 8,754 aircraft.

The A320 family of medium-haul, single-aisle aircraft received the largest number of orders at 656.

Boeing was scheduled to publish its annual delivery and order figures on Tuesday.

The US manufacturer delivered 537 aircraft in the first 11 months of the year, its best result for that period since 2018, before the crashes of two 737 MAX aircraft sent the company into a crisis.

Boeing is coming off a particularly difficult 2024, during which it delivered just 348 commercial planes due to labour disruptions and safety setbacks hobbling production.

Analysts forecast Boeing will end up having delivered between 590 and 610 aircraft in 2025.

Boeing also enjoyed a solid 2025 in terms of orders due to the aggressive trade policies of US President Donald Trump’s administration.

It had 6,616 commercial aircraft on its order book, including 4,319 for the 737 MAX, the latest model of its medium-haul, single-aisle aircraft that along with the A320 are the workhorses of the commercial airline industry.

title: US ‘screwed’ if SC rules against tariffs: Trump
body:
President Donald Trump said Monday that the United States would be ‘screwed’ if the Supreme Court rules that some of his tariffs are illegal.

Trump, in a post on Truth Social, said hundreds of billions of dollars would have to be paid back to US companies if the top court rules against his flagship economic policy.

‘And that doesn’t include the amount of ‘payback’ that Countries and Companies would require for the investments they are making... for the purpose of being able to avoid the payment of Tariffs,’ he said.

‘When these Investments are added, we are talking about Trillions of Dollars!’ he said. ‘It would be a complete mess, and almost impossible for our Country to pay.’

‘In other words, if the Supreme Court rules against the United States of America on this National Security bonanza, WE’RE SCREWED!’ Trump said.

The Supreme Court plans to release opinions on Wednesday and the tariffs case, which was argued in November, could potentially be among the rulings it hands down.

During oral arguments in the case, the justices appeared deeply sceptical of Trump’s use of emergency powers to impose ‘reciprocal’ tariffs on nearly every US trade partner and levies targeting Mexico, Canada and China over their alleged roles in illicit drug flows.

Several of the six conservative justices, along with the three liberals, questioned whether the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA) that Trump invoked confers the authority to impose tariffs.

The court’s decision does not concern sector-specific tariffs Trump separately imposed, including on steel, aluminium and automobiles.

Trump has brought the average effective US tariff rate to its highest since the 1930s, and has repeatedly warned of calamity if the duties are overturned.

title: Freelancer ID management software launched
body:
The country’s first government freelancer ID management software has been officially inaugurated as an effort to build a transparent, secure and harassment-free verification system for freelancers.

Chief adviser’s special assistant on posts, telecommunications and information technology Faiz Ahmad Taiyeb inaugurated the software at the meeting room of the ICT Division at Agargaon in the capital on Tuesday.

In his speech, Taiyeb said that the entire process had been kept completely free after seriously considering past experiences, especially allegations of harassment and financial fraud.

As part of this initiative, he said, all types of financial transactions, including application fees, renewal fees and processing fees, have been completely cancelled.

A total of 29 engineers of DOICT will serve as a resource pool in ID verification, he said, adding that four support experts would be there to support freelancers as a shared resource pool for technical support.

Noting that an API-based verification system will be launched very soon, the special assistant commented that a consensus had been reached with the community on two levels of API verification.

He said that the VAPT of the site had already been successfully completed, while sign-up and application for a freelancer ID could be done from Tuesday.

Taiyeb also said that freelancer community leaders and the Bangladesh Call Centre Association would work together to improve the user experience of a significant number of freelancers.

A formal letter will be sent from the ICT Division to Bangladesh Bank, so that banks and financial institutions accept this digital freelancer ID instead of manual ID in the future, he said.

In the meantime, the previous contracts have been cancelled in the wake of allegations of fraud and harassment, and freelancer community leaders have positively accepted the annual margin of US$ 50 on the accepted payment method, the special assistant said.

He also commented that the engineers of the ICT Division who developed this software would maintain it.

With this new freelancer ID card, registered freelancers will be able to easily avail various facilities, including banking services, loan and credit card facilities, financial incentives, and government and private training.

At the same time, this platform will work as a national freelancer database, where the number, skills, and type of work of freelancers will be stored, which will be helpful in future policymaking.

ICT Division secretary Shish Haider Chowdhury, additional secretary Md Mamunur Rashid Bhuiyan and director general of the Department of ICT Md Abu Sayed also spoke at the event.

title: Boeing faces 2nd US trial over fatal 2019 737 MAX crash
body:
A federal court in Chicago began hearing Monday a complaint from a Canadian who lost multiple relatives in a 737 MAX crash, the second trial following the 2019 calamity.

The case is brought by Manant Vaidya, whose sister Kosha and parents Pannagesh and Hansini Vaidya, perished in the March 2019 Ethiopian Airlines crash that killed 157 in all.

Vaidya also lost his brother-in-law and two young nieces. Relatives of these victims sued Boeing separately in a case that was settled out of court in July 2025.

Jury selection is expected to commence Monday, with opening statements possible Tuesday afternoon or Wednesday.

‘It is hard to believe that my entire family was wiped out in an instant incident in such a horrific way,’ Vaidya says in a statement on the website of his attorneys at Clifford Law Firm.

‘I still cry and my wife, Hiral, still cries when we think of the horror of the last moments of our loved ones’ lives.’

The family, who lived in Canada, was on a trip to Kenya, the homeland of Kosha.

Boeing has apologized for the disaster and for a fatal Lion Air crash in Indonesia in October 2018. The MCAS (Manoeuvring Characteristics Augmentation System) flight stabilising software was implicated in both crashes, which together claimed 346 lives.

Boeing is ‘deeply sorry’ to the victims and committed to ‘fully and fairly compensate’ families ‘and have accepted legal responsibility for the accidents,’ a Boeing spokesperson said.

‘While we have resolved the vast majority of these claims through settlements, families are also entitled to pursue their claims through damages trials in court, and we respect their right to do so.’

In November, a US jury in the same Chicago courthouse determined that Boeing must pay $28.45 million to the family of an Indian victim.

title: Ex-Fed chiefs, lawmakers slam US probe into Jerome Powell
body:
Former Federal Reserve chiefs on Monday sharply criticised a US criminal probe into current chair Jerome Powell, calling it an ‘unprecedented attempt’ to undermine the central bank’s independence.

Two Republican senators joined in rebuking the Trump administration and questioned the credibility of the Department of Justice (DOJ) in targeting Powell, whom the US president has long sought to replace in a push for lower interest rates.

On Sunday, Powell revealed that the Fed received grand jury subpoenas and threats of a criminal indictment relating to Senate testimony he gave in June.

The issue at hand was a $2.5 billion renovation of the Fed’s headquarters. Last year, President Donald Trump floated the possibility of firing Powell over cost overruns for the historic buildings’ facelift.

On Monday, ex-Fed chiefs Ben Bernanke, Alan Greenspan and Janet Yellen joined other former economic leaders in slamming the DOJ’s probe.

In a joint statement, they called it ‘an unprecedented attempt to use prosecutorial attacks’ to undermine the Fed’s independence.

‘This is how monetary policy is made in emerging markets with weak institutions, with highly negative consequences for inflation and the functioning of their economies more broadly,’ the statement added.

In an extraordinary statement on Sunday, Powell himself rebuked the administration, dismissing the building renovation and his testimony before Congress as ‘pretexts.’

‘The threat of criminal charges is a consequence of the Federal Reserve setting interest rates based on our best assessment of what will serve the public, rather than following the preferences of the president,’ he said.

He vowed to carry out his duties ‘without political fear or favour.’

Separately, New York Fed President John Williams said that historic precedent of political influence on monetary policy typically leads to ‘unfortunate’ outcomes like inflation.

Despite worries spurred by the probe, US stock indices closed at records.

‘The fact that market measures of inflation expectations have remained calm indicates that markets are brushing off the investigation as having little, if any, impact on Fed independence,’ said Bernard Yaros, lead US economist at Oxford Economics.

The independent Fed has a dual mandate to keep prices stable and unemployment low. Its main tool is setting a benchmark interest rate that influences the price of US Treasury bonds and borrowing costs.

Trump has regularly slammed Powell, calling him a ‘numbskull’ and ‘moron’ for the Fed’s policy decisions and not cutting borrowing costs more sharply.

On Monday, White House spokeswoman Karoline Leavitt told Fox News that Powell ‘has proven he’s not very good at his job.’

‘As to whether he’s a criminal, that’s an answer the Department of Justice is going to have to find,’ she said.

The DOJ’s probe has drawn criticism from both sides of the political aisle.

Republican Thom Tillis, who sits on the Senate Banking Committee, vowed Sunday to oppose the confirmation of any Fed nominee, including for the next Fed chief, until the legal matter is ‘fully resolved.’

‘It is now the independence and credibility of the Department of Justice that are in question,’ he said.

Another Republican senator, Lisa Murkowski of Alaska, supported Tillis’ move, calling the investigation ‘nothing more than an attempt at coercion.’

Top Senate Democrat Chuck Schumer earlier dubbed the probe an assault on the Fed’s independence.

David Wessel, a senior fellow at Washington think tank the Brookings Institution warned of serious consequences if the Fed came under Trump’s control.

Elected politicians could be inclined to set interest rates low to boost the economy ahead of elections, for instance.

If Trump succeeds in influencing the Fed, the US economy could see ‘more inflation, and the willingness of global investors to lend money to the Treasury will diminish somewhat,’ Wessel told AFP.

Trump nominated Powell as Fed chair during his first presidency. Powell’s term as chair ends in May, but he could stay on the Fed’s board until 2028.

Last year, Trump separately attempted to fire Fed Governor Lisa Cook over mortgage fraud allegations.

title: Boeing sells 50 737 MAX jets to leasing group ACG
body:
Boeing said Tuesday that it had secured a firm order from the leasing firm Aviation Capital Group for 50 of its 737 MAX jets, the company’s workhorse jet for the commercial airline industry.

The contract comes as Boeing is scrambling to restore client confidence in the 737 MAX after two fatal crashes involving the jets in 2018 and 2019. Financial terms of the sale to ACG, a major leasing company, were not disclosed in a joint statement.

ACG, a subsidiary of Tokyo Century Corp. based in California, now has 121 737 MAXs on order. Its latest order is for 25 of the MAX 8 versions and 25 of the bigger MAX 10 — a version that has not yet received full certification from the US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA).

‘ACG’s expanded order for the 737-10 reflects strong confidence in the airplane and its appeal to the lessor’s customers worldwide,’ Boeing’s commercial chief Brad McMullen said in the statement.

Boeing was plunged into crisis after a MAX operated by Lion Air vanished from radars shortly after takeoff in October 2018 from Jakarta and crashed into the Java Sea, killing all 189 people onboard.

Less than five months later, in March 2019, another MAX crashed into a field minutes after takeoff from the Ethiopian capital of Addis Ababa. All 157 passengers and crew were killed.

The successive disasters forced the grounding of the worldwide MAX fleet for 20 months as investigators probed defects in its flight control software, the MCAS anti-stall system.

Boeing is scheduled to announce its full-year deliveries for 2025 later Tuesday, a day after its main rival Airbus said that it delivered 793 commercial aircraft last year, a slight increase from the previous year.

Both companies have struggled to return to pre-pandemic production levels as their entire network of suppliers was disrupted, even as airlines are eager to modernise fleets with more fuel-efficient aircraft and expand to meet an expected increase in passenger numbers over the coming decades.

title: RMU terminates three officials
body:
Rajshahi Medical University terminated three officials on charges of misconduct, corruption and unsatisfactory performance, university authorities said on Tuesday.

The dismissed officials are liaison and protocol officer Md Ismail Hossain, section officer and former acting assistant registrar and assistant college inspector Md Rasedul Islam, and section officer Md Jamal Uddin.

The officials were terminated on Monday in accordance with the decisions taken at the university’s 19th syndicate meeting on December 15, said registrar Md Hasibul Hossain on Tuesday.

University officials said that allegations were raised against Ismail Hossain for securing his appointment by submitting a forged BBA certificate allegedly obtained from Stamford University.

Following the allegation, the university formed a probe committee, which found the claim to be true and recommended his termination.

The syndicate also decided to recover all salaries, allowances and financial benefits received by Ismail during his tenure and approved the initiation of criminal proceedings against him on charges of fraud and forgery.

Meanwhile, a departmental case was filed against Rasedul Islam over allegations of misconduct for allegedly assisting Ismail Hossain in obtaining employment through file tampering, as well as involvement in corruption by accepting bribes from a contracting firm.

An investigation committee formed under the Government Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 2018 found the allegations against Rasedul proven under clause 3(b) for misconduct and clause 3(d) for corruption, university officials said.

However, considering his nearly 20 years of service at the University Grants Commission and RMU, the vice-chancellor and syndicate members decided, on humanitarian grounds, to impose compulsory retirement instead of permanent dismissal.

Section officer Md Jamal Uddin, who joined the university on October 8, 2023, was serving a two-year probation period at the time of the decision.

The syndicate concluded that his overall performance during probation was unsatisfactory and decided to terminate his employment in accordance with the terms of his appointment letter.

Contacted, Jamal Uddin rejected the decision, claiming that he had been dismissed without specific reasons and said that he would challenge the move through legal means.

title: UN offers support to combat polls misinformation
body:
UN high commissioner for Human Rights Volker Türk has offered the support of his office to counter the surge of misinformation targeting the February 12 elections as chief adviser Professor Muhammad Yunus sought support of the organisation to address the issue.

‘There has been a flood of misinformation surrounding the elections. It is coming from both foreign media and local sources,’ Yunus said during a phone conversation with Volker Türk on Tuesday, according to the chief adviser’s press wing.

‘They have flooded social media with fake news, rumours and speculation. We are concerned about the impact this may have on the elections,’ the chief adviser added.

High commissioner Türk said he was aware of the problem and offered the support of the UN human rights office to address what he described as a growing misinformation challenge.

‘There is a lot of misinformation. We will do whatever is needed,’ Türk said, adding that the UN rights agency would work closely with Bangladesh to tackle the issue.

During the conversation, the two leaders also discussed the forthcoming referendum, the importance of institutional reforms, the work of the Enforced Disappearance Commission, the formation of the National Human Rights Commission, and the global geopolitical situation.

Türk stressed the importance of establishing ‘a truly independent’ National Human Rights Commission to carry forward the work related to enforced disappearances.

In response, Professor Yunus said the NHRC ordinance has already been promulgated and that a new commission would be reconstituted ahead of the February 12 elections. ‘We will do it before we leave.’

The chief adviser said he had shared the final report of the Enforced Disappearance Commission with the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights, describing it as a crucial document that would go a long way toward ensuring accountability and justice for the victims of enforced disappearances during the autocratic regime from 2009 to 2024.

Türk praised the Chief Adviser’s efforts over the past year and a half. He said his office had supported the work of the Enforced Disappearance Commission and would continue to do so.

SDG coordinator and senior secretary Lamiya Morshed was present during the conversation.

title: Case filed, two Ansar members sent to jail
body:
A Manikganj court on Tuesday sent two members of the Bangladesh Ansar and Village Defence Party to jail over allegedly raping a 16-year-old girl at the 250-bed General Hospital in Manikganj early Monday.

The accused are Shahadat Hossain and Abu Sayeed, who were on duty at the hospital’s main gate on the day of incident.

Manikganj Sadar police station officer-in-charge Md Ikram Hossain confirmed the development.

He also said that the victim’s mother filed a case with the police station on Monday night following the rape incident.

‘A case was filed and the two accused Ansar members were produced before the court on Tuesday and sent to jail,’ Ikram said.

The victim was receiving treatment at Manikganj 250-bed General Hospital.

The police said that the victim and her husband, who was a driver of a battery-run van, were traveling from Narayanganj to their relative’s house in Manikganj on his van on Sunday night.

While they were on the way to Betila in Manikganj sadar upazila, the van’s battery ran out of charge near the Manikganj bus stand at about 2:00am on Monday.

Looking for safety, the couple went to Manikganj 250-bed General Hospital where the accused Ansar members assured the couple of assistance and took them inside the hospital.

The Ansar members then left the husband on the ground floor and took the victim on the first floor of the hospital’s newly constructed building, where they allegedly raped her after intimidating her.

Escaping from the hospital, the couple informed the police following which the police summoned all the Ansar members on duty at the hospital to the police station where the victim identified the two accused.

title: India accuses Pakistan of cross-border drone incursions in Kashmir
body:
India’s army chief accused Pakistan on Tuesday of flying drones into Indian-administered territory in disputed Kashmir, where the nuclear-armed rivals fought a four-day clash last year.

‘They have been told that this is unacceptable to us, and please put a stop to it,’ General Upendra Dwivedi told reporters in New Delhi in an annual briefing to the media.

Heads of military operations of both countries spoke to each other earlier on Tuesday, he said.

India’s army reported sighting multiple drones flying over Indian-controlled border villages last week.

‘These drones, I believe, were defensive drones, which want to come over our territory to see if any action is being planned against them,’ Dwivedi said.

There was no immediate response from Pakistan’s army.

Muslim-majority Kashmir has been divided between India and Pakistan since their independence from British rule in 1947, and both claim the Himalayan territory in full.

The neighbours fought for four days in May 2025, weeks after New Delhi accused Islamabad of backing a deadly attack on tourists in Indian-administered Kashmir, claims Pakistan denied.

The ensuing conflict killed at least 70 people, and saw both sides make extensive use of drones as well as intense missile and artillery barrages.

‘We are fully alert along the Line of Control,’ Dwivedi added, referring to the heavily fortified de facto border.

Dwivedi said several low-flying drones entered Indian-controlled airspace with their lights switched on — as many as seven on Saturday, and another two or three on Sunday.

‘It’s possible they wanted to see if there were any gaps, laxity in our defence, any gaps through which they could send terrorists,’ he added.

Rebel groups in Indian-run Kashmir have waged an insurgency for 35 years demanding independence for the territory or its merger with Pakistan.

title: 6 more arrested over Raozan arson attacks
body:
The police on Tuesday said that they arrested six more people in cases filed over the recent arson attacks targeting houses of Hindu and Buddhist community members at Raozan in Chattogram.

Chattogram range deputy inspector general of police Ahsan Habib Palash disclosed the arrests at a briefing on Tuesday afternoon, saying the suspects were arrested from different parts of Chattogram.

The arrestees are identified as Mohammad Omar Faruk, Mohammad Kabir Hossain, Kartik Dey, Biplab Barua, Mohammad Lokman and Mohammad Parvez.

The police said that they recovered four ‘provocative’ banners, two kerosene containers, a kerosene bottle, three empty plastic sacks, a mobile phone, a CNG-run autorickshaw and a motorcycle from the arrestees.

The DIG said that the arrests were made based on information and evidence provided by Monir Hossain, who was earlier arrested in the case.

With the latest arrests, seven people have so far been arrested over the incidents, the police said.

Without naming any organisation, Ahsan Habib said that all those involved were active leaders and activists of a ‘banned organisation’.

Based on information found in an investigation, the DIG also said that the incidents were planned to create communal tension in the country and to put the government in a difficult position by spreading propaganda abroad that minorities are being persecuted in Bangladesh, with the aim of misleading the international community.

He also said that due to family disputes and a retaliatory mindset of the arrested accused Monir, some people’s names and mobile phone numbers were added to the banners.

The recent incident took place at Sultanpur ward-5 under Raozan municipality early on December 23, 2025, when a house was set on fire after its door was locked from outside.

The house belongs to Sukh Shil, a Qatar expatriate, and his sister and brother-in-law live there, the police said.

The police said that handwritten banners containing names and mobile phone numbers of people from political parties and the administration were seized from near the gutted house.

Earlier, in a similar incident on the night of December 20, two houses belonging to Bimal Talukdar and Rubel Das in Dheuapara area under ward-8 of the municipality were set on fire, the police said.

Locals said that the occupants tried to get out of the houses after noticing the fire but realised that the doors had been locked from outside. The residents, however, managed to escape by cutting through fences of the houses, they said.

They also said that the doors of both houses were found tied with cloth and kerosene-soaked cloth was seen in the yards.

The police said that similar incidents were also reported on the night of December 19 at Kewtia ward-7 at the house of Sadhan Barua and at ward-9 at the houses of Sona Pal and Kamini Mohan Pal.

Kerosene-soaked cloth and papers bearing names and mobile phone numbers of leaders of different political parties and senior government officials were recovered from the yards that night.

On December 26 night, the police said that Md Morshedul Alam, 55, was caught red-handed with a kerosene bottle while trying to set fire to a cloth van at Gahira Bazar at Raozan.

title: Decision on public sector pay hike by elected govt
body:
Finance adviser Salehuddin Ahmed on Tuesday said that the final decision on implementing the pay scale for the government employees would be taken after the National pay Commission 2025 submits the pay scale.

‘We are going to get it soon,’ said the finance adviser while talking to reporters after a meeting of the advisory council committee on government purchase at the secretariat.

The commission, appointed on July 27 under the leadership of former finance secretary Zakir Ahmed Khan, has been asked to submit its recommendations within six months after it starts its operation.

The pay commission that held its first meeting on August 14 is scheduled to complete its tenure on February 14, two days after the Jatiya Sangsad elections on February 12.

On November 9, the finance adviser said that the decision about the pay hike for the public servants would be taken by the new elected government as the issue cannot be settled by the current interim administration.

On Tuesday, the finance adviser once again said that the implementation of the pay commission report was completely different from the issue of submission.

The previous pay commission, headed by former Bangladesh Bank governor Dr Mohammad Farashuddin, was appointed in November 2013.

The Awami League-led regime that was ousted on August 5, 2024 amid a mass uprising implemented the major recommendations of that pay commission in two phases – salary hike since July 2015 and other benefits since July 2016.

Without referring to experiences of the previous pay commissions, the finance adviser said that the main task was detailed and substantive.

According to a pay commission official, a secretary-level committee is usually appointed to chalk out the detailed implementation plan for the pay hike.

title: Myanmar pro-military party claims most seats in election
body:
Myanmar’s dominant pro-military party on Tuesday claimed a majority of elected lower house seats in the country’s junta-run polls, which democracy watchdogs say will prolong the armed forces’ grip.

The military has ruled Myanmar by force for almost all of its post-independence history, before a decade-long democratic experiment gave civilian politicians tentative control.

But the generals took back power in a 2021 coup deposing the government of Aung San Suu Kyi, detaining the democratic figurehead and plunging the country into civil war.

The junta is overseeing a staggered election it pledges will return power to the people after the third and final phase of voting on January 25.

With Suu Kyi detained and her party dissolved, democracy advocates say it has been rigged by a dissent purge and a ballot stacked with military allies in the Union Solidarity and Development Party.

A USDP official — speaking anonymously because they were not authorised to disclose results — said they ‘won 87 seats out of 100’ in Sunday’s second phase of the vote.

Combined with confirmed overwhelming wins in the first phase, the official’s figures give the party 176 lower house seats so far — just over half the 330 elected positions, even before the third phase has taken place.

The UN’s special rapporteur on human rights in Myanmar Tom Andrews said in a statement last week ‘the junta engineered the polls to ensure victory for its proxy, entrench military domination in Myanmar, and manufacture a facade of legitimacy’.

There are 440 seats in Myanmar’s lower house, but 110 are reserved for the armed forces under the military-drafted constitution.

And analysts describe the USDP, many of whose officials are retired officers, as the military’s prime political proxy.

Parliament is due to convene in March, when MPs from the combined lower and upper houses will choose the president, and junta chief Min Aung Hlaing has not ruled out resigning as top general to take over the civilian role.

title: Seizure of 300 properties of Saifuzzaman abroad ordered
body:
The Dhaka Metropolitan Senior Special Judge’s Court on Tuesday asked the Anti-Corruption Commission to take measures to seize more than 300 houses and apartments abroad owned by former land minister Saifuzzaman Chowdhury and his related entities.

Judge Md Sabbir Foyez of the court passed the order responding to separate petitions submitted by ACC deputy director Moshiur Rahman seeking the seizure of the properties.

Among these properties, 40 houses are in the United States, 23 in Thailand, 47 in Malaysia, 59 in Dubai, 117 in Cambodia, four houses and 30 apartments in Vietnam, nine houses in India, and two houses in the Philippines.

The court also ordered the freezing of $1 million that the ex-minister had invested in the US, said ACC assistant director for public relations, Tanzir Ahmed.

Earlier, the court also asked the ACC to seize 580 houses owned by him in the UK, the US, and other countries.

Since the fall of the Awami League regime, AL’s former minister and businessman Saifuzzaman, who has been residing in the United Kingdom, has faced multiple cases filed by the ACC over allegations of money laundering and corruption.

title: Bangladesh to launch MUN Alert, helpline for missing children
body:
Bangladesh is set to introduce its first national emergency alert system—Missing Urgent Notification—to speed up the rescue of missing and abducted children.

Alongside this initiative, a 24/7 toll-free helpline—13219—is being officially introduced to receive information related to missing children across the country.

Criminal Investigation Department chief additional inspector general Sibgat Ullah made the disclosure at a press briefing in its headquarters on Tuesday.

The MUN Alert system has been developed under the leadership of the missing children cell of the CID, Bangladesh police, with technical and coordination support from the Zero Missing Children Platform and international collaboration from the Amber Alert for Bangladesh team.

The initiative draws inspiration from the globally recognised AMBER Alert system, first launched in the United States following the 1996 abduction and murder of child Amber Hagerman.

Similar systems are now in place across Europe and in countries such as Malaysia, Thailand, China, Nigeria, Kenya and Pakistan.

International research shows that the first few hours after a child goes missing are critical, and timely, verified alerts significantly increase the chances of safe recovery.

In the context of Bangladesh, tragic incidents—including the disappearance and murder of five-year-old Muntaha Akhter in Sylhet in 2024—have underscored the urgent need for a fast, integrated and technology-driven response mechanism.

Under the MUN Alert system, when there is reasonable suspicion that a child is missing or abducted, the CID will issue an emergency alert based on verified information.

The alert may be disseminated through an official web portal and mobile app, online and offline media, social media platforms, digital billboards, mobile SMS or cell broadcasting, and other technology-based channels to ensure widespread public awareness and participation.

Authorities emphasized that the dignity, safety and privacy of the child will remain paramount throughout the process.

Members of the public can report information about missing children through the national emergency service 999, the missing children cell hotline—01320017060, or the newly launched toll-free helpline 13219.

The authority to verify information, assess risk levels, and issue, suspend or withdraw alerts will rest solely with the missing children cell of the CID.

Where necessary, Yellow Notices may be issued through INTERPOL in cases involving risks of cross-border movement or child trafficking.

The initiative is being implemented in collaboration with the National Centre for Missing and Exploited Children—the organisation that manages the global Amber Alert system—and Meta, Facebook, working closely with the CID and the Zero Missing Children Platform.

Stakeholders expressed strong optimism that the launch of MUN Alert will establish a state-led, technology-based and integrated national framework for rescuing missing children, significantly strengthening child protection and access to justice in Bangladesh.

title: Qawmi, non-formal edn included in draft policy
body:
The government has recently drafted the Bangladesh National Qualifications Framework Policy, 2026 in which it has newly included qawmi and non-formal education streams.

The policy has been drafted for the National Qualifications Framework which was approved on June 3 in 2021, keeping qawmi and non-formal education outside its purview.

The framework and the policy are part of a strategic initiative the government has undertaken to improve standard of the educational qualification and skills while maintaining compatibility and alignment with the international standard, the draft policy mentions.

According to the policy, one of its main objectives will be to ensure universal definition, standard and transparency regarding qualification across the education sub-sectors of school, Madrassah, technical and vocational education and training, skills, non-formal and higher education.

It would help the mainstreaming of qawmi and non-formal education, said officials.

Most recently on Monday, the Technical and Madrassah Education Division under the education ministry published the draft policy on its website calling for public comments to send via the email address:.

According to the draft, the Bangladesh National Qualifications Framework will help the streamlining of qualifications, competencies, skills and certificates acquired through all the four streams of the country’s education streams: general, technical, madrassah and non-formal education.

The framework was developed based on the National Technical and Vocational Qualification Framework adopted in 2012.

The formulation of the Bangladesh National Qualifications Framework was initiated in 2018 and finalised and approved in 2021.

The government then took initiative to draft policy for the framework.

The draft policy will cover, streamline and standardise lifelong learning, quality improvement, international recognition, mobility of qualifications and establishment of a comprehensive and inclusive education and training system.

For madrassah education, the draft policy defines alia and qawmi madrassahs as two separate sub-streams.

The draft policy defines non-formal education as per the Non-formal Education Act, 2014 covering a provision for lifelong learning for enhancing the capacity of the educated and well-educated population.

Technical and Madrassah Education Division additional secretary (development section) Shamshur Rahman Khan said that the standardisation of the qawmi madrassah-based education had yet to be made against existing general, technical and madrassah education.

Similar standardisation had also been proposed for non-formal education in the policy draft, he said.

title: Schools asked to campaign for referendum
body:
The Directorate of Secondary and Higher Education and the Directorate of Madrassah Education have instructed conducting comprehensive campaigns in all government and private schools, colleges and madrassah to create public awareness among voters about the referendum to be held on February 12.

In light of the July National Charter 2025, the referendum on constitutional reform will be held on the same day of the forthcoming 13th national elections.

All education offices under the two directorates have also been asked to follow these directives.

Separate directives issued by the DSHE and DME have stated that banners and festoons with the referendum’s logo must be displayed in conspicuous places in all government and private educational institutions of the country.

Besides, the referendum’s logo must be used in all government communications and official correspondence.

Two separate letters issued from the DSHE and DME were sent to all educational institutions and education offices across the country on Monday.

On January 12, a directive, signed by DSHE assistant director, general administration, Md Khalid Hossain, said awareness should be created among voters about referendum, the designated ‘logo’ of the referendum must be used in all government communications—letters, orders, notifications, circulars, etc.—until the elections.

In addition, necessary measures must be taken to display at least two vertical banners in visible places in the front of the buildings in all educational institutions, colleges and offices under the directorate.

On January 12, a letter issued by the Directorate of Educational and Madrassah Education Mohammad said this message should be conveyed to families through parent gatherings and students. This campaign should also be carried out through the notice boards of the institutions and social media, it said.

The letter states that this step has been taken in light of the directives of the Cabinet Division.

The referendum will be held to seek the people’s verdict on the fundamental proposals for state reforms mentioned in the July National Charter 2025.

The reform proposals include a maximum term limit of 10 years for the prime minister, the formation of an upper house in the national parliament, a joint role of the government and the opposition in the formation of the election commission and the Bangladesh Public Service Commission, and ensuring the independence of the judiciary.

title: Verdict in plot scam case against Hasina, others on Feb 2
body:
A Dhaka court on Tuesday set February 2 for pronouncing judgment in a case against 18 people, including ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina, and her nieces Tulip Siddiq and Azmina Siddiq, over alleged irregularities in allocating a 10-katha plot in the RAJUK New Town Project.

Judge Robiul Alam of Dhaka special judge court-4 passed the order as the prosecution and defence concluded their arguments in the case on Tuesday, Anti-Corruption Commission public prosecutor Mir Ahammed Salam told BSS.

The court on January 8 had set on Tuesday to place arguments in the case.

On January 5, the court had brought the testimony in the case to an end. Investigation officer, ACC assistant director Afnan Jannat Keya had testified earlier that day as the last prosecution witness and was later cross-examined by the defence.

The commission filed the case against 16 on January 13, 2025, and filed a chargesheet on March 10 against the 18.

title: ENT dept of BMU holds workshop
body:
The ENT department of Bangladesh Medical University organised a structural clinical assessment workshop on Tuesday.

Faculty from eight government medical colleges joined the programme, said a press release.

Lectures were delivered by the Bangladesh Medical and Dental Council president Professor Md Saiful Islam and assistant professor Md Russell Ahmed.

The programme was presided over by ENT department chairman Professor A Allam Chowdhury. The welcome speech was delivered by the associate professor of the department Mohammad Anwar Hossain.

title: Udichi holds exhibition at burnted office
body:
The Bangladesh Udichi Shilpigosthi on Tuesday began a four-day exhibition at its central office on Topkhana Road in the capital Dhaka after 24 days of an arson attack on its central office.

The arson attack burned the cultural organisation’s office on December 19, 2025, amid protests over the death of Inquilab Mancha convener Sharif Osman Hadi at a hospital in Singapore.

The exhibition is displaying the organisation’s scorched office and damaged and charred musical instruments, books, costumes, stage properties and documents of 57 years of the cultural organisation.

The organisation was publicly threatened by the Islami Chhatra Shibir, the student wing of the Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami, and after the arson attack, the interim government did not take any step regarding the issues and the cultural adviser’s silence over the issues created a lot of questions, said Udichi general secretary Jamshed Anwer Tapan.

He also claimed that the ministry excluded Udichi from this year’s annual government grants for cultural organisations.

He also said that after the incident, a case had been filed on behalf of Udichi.

The police and the Fire Service have already collected evidence and completed initial investigations, but they (Udichi) have not heard of any visible progress about the case, Jamshed said.

He made the remarks at a press conference chaired by Udichi acting president Habibul Alam.

Political and cultural activists from different organisations were present in the press conference.

Leaders of Udichi also urged for financial help from cultural activists and organisations to rebuild their office.

At the exhibition, they also recited poems and rendered songs on Tuesday. The show will end on Friday.

title: RUET VC Abdur Razzak elected BUC president
body:
Rajshahi University of Engineering and Technology vice-chancellor Professor SM Abdur Razzak has been elected new president of the Bangladesh University Council.

He was unanimously elected to this position in a recent meeting of the Bangladesh University Council, an organisation consisting of vice-chancellors of public universities.

This organisation of vice-chancellors has been working in a coordinated manner for the overall development of the higher education system in Bangladesh.

Formulating and implementing policies to determine and improve the quality of education at universities, introducing new and up-to-date courses, modernising the existing curricula, and ensuring a conducive environment for research is there aim.

In addition, the council plays an important role in coordinating among different universities in the field of administration and management, adopting strategic plans, and implementing common policies.

Budget planning, ensuring financial transparency and accountability in the financial and asset management of universities, and assisting in collecting research and development funds from external sources are also among the responsibilities of the council.

The council plays an effective role by providing recommendations to the government in formulating laws and policies related to higher education and presenting issues of interest to the universities.

Vice-chancellor Abdur Razzak has been congratulated on behalf of all the teachers, students, officers and employees of RUET. He is a professor in the Department of Electrical and Electronic Engineering (EEE) of RUET.

title: Ochin Pakhi Sangeet Academy remembers Farida Parveen
body:
Ochin Pakhi Sangeet Academy remembered its founder, Farida Parveen, at a programme marking her 72nd birth anniversary at the National Theatre Hall of Bangladesh Shilpakala Academy in the capital on Tuesday.

The event, chaired by the principal of Ochin Pakhi Sangeet Academy Gazi Abdul Hakim, consisted of a discussion session, songs and instrumental performancesw.

Fisheries and livestock adviser Farida Akhter was present as the chief guest at the event which was inaugurated by Social Development Foundation chairman Muhammad Abdul Mazid.

Renowned singers Sabina Yasmin and Fatema Tuz Zohra, BSA director general Poet Rezauddin Ahmed Stalin and Jatiyatabadi Samajik Sangskritik Sangathan convener film actor Helal Khan, among others, spoke as special guests at the event that began with a musical performance titled Achin Pakhi.

The musical performance Achin Pakhi, performed by the academy’s students, depicted the life and philosophy of Fakir Lalon Shah and the musical legacy of Lalon Sangeet exponent Farida Parveen.

Farida Akhter said that Farida Parveen introduced Lalon songs with skilled musical knowledge and deep emotions.

‘Lalon was not a baul, he was a fakir but the younger generation practice his song as baul song and sometimes they overtone the Lalon songs and mix with irrelevant dance,’ she said, adding that Farida Parveen formed the academy to promote Lalon to new generations.

She also claimed that the state did not honour an artist and no government gave proper respect to Farida Parveen.

Sabina Yasmin said that before Farida Parvin, there were very few dedicated singers on Lalon songs and she was able to win people’s hearts.

After the discussion, with musical troupes and Lalon singers, the students and teachers of Ochin Pakhi Sangeet Academy performed at the event.

Farida Parveen died at the age of 71 on September 13, 2025.

She was born at Shawl village of Singra in Natore on December 31, 1954.

Given her outstanding contribution to popularising the Lalon songs, Farida Parveen won various awards, including the Ekushey Padak in 1987, the National Film Award for best female playback singer in 1993 and the Fukuoka Prize from Japan in 2008.

title: NSU, UNDP host workshop on AI
body:
North South University’s department of management, in collaboration with UNDP Bangladesh, organised a focused workshop titled ‘Responsible AI in practice: Civil society, governance, and accountability in Bangladesh’ at the SBE dean’s conference room on its campus in Dhaka on Tuesday.

The session brought together Sheela Tasneem Haq, UNDP Bangladesh, Zulkarin Jahangir, NSU, Syed Ishtiaque Ahmed, University of Toronto, Shafiqul Alam, Victoria University of Wellington, and Quazi Tafsirul Islam, NSU.

The workshop was chaired by Ziaul Haq Adnan, associate professor and chair, department of management, NSU.

Zulkarin Jahangir, assistant professor, NSU, noted, ‘Responsible AI is not only a technical issue but a governance challenge. Without ethical frameworks and local context, AI risks deepening existing inequalities.’

The workshop concluded with an interactive discussion on how academia, NGOs, and development partners can jointly promote more responsible, ethical, and accountable AI practices in Bangladesh.

title: Open Univ holds training on use of AI
body:
The Institutional Quality Assurance Cell (IQAC) organised a daylong training programme titled ‘Use of Artificial Intelligence in the Workplace’ on Tuesday, at the ICT and E-Learning Centre of the Bangladesh Open University’s Gazipur campus.

Professor Abul Hasnat Md Shamim, treasurer of Bangladesh Open University was present as chief guest and resource person at the training programme held under the guidance of the vice-chancellor of Bangladesh Open University, Professor ABM Obaidul Islam.

In his inaugural address, Professor Shamim stated that artificial intelligence is not a competitor to humans; rather, it is a powerful tool that enhances efficiency, transparency and productivity in the workplace.

The inaugural session of the training was chaired by Professor Mohammad Zahir Raihan, director of IQAC. In his remarks, he stated that Artificial Intelligence is a practical and effective technology already being applied in education and administration, improving accuracy in decision-making, saving time and costs, and enhancing human resource capacity.

The training session featured Md Mominul Islam, head of the ICT Unit and ICT Consultant of Bangladesh Open University, as the resource person.

He delivered comprehensive discussions on the fundamentals of Artificial Intelligence and its practical applications in the workplace, including office automation, drafting official letters, notes, and reports, examination-related data analysis and automation, ethics, data security and risk management, as well as administrative decision-making and future planning.

The training programme was conducted by Professor Mohammad Mamunur Rashid, additional director of IQAC. A total of 36 participants from different schools and departments of Bangladesh Open University took part in the training.

title: Freezing rain hampers travel in Central Europe
body:
Freezing rain led to travel disruptions in Central Europe on Tuesday, including flights being temporarily suspended at several airports.

Snow and freezing temperatures buffeted Europe last week, with gale-force winds and storms claiming some 15 lives, causing travel mayhem, shutting schools, and cutting power to hundreds of thousands.

A thick layer of ice on the Vienna airport runways led to a temporary shutdown, with flights gradually resuming around midday on Tuesday.

Austria’s state railway company OeBB also asked travellers to postpone non-urgent journeys, with numerous train connections facing interruptions and cancellations.

In neighbouring Slovakia, the Bratislava airport was also closed temporarily early Tuesday due to bad weather.

Slovak police on Facebook urged people to avoid travel because of ‘extreme’ ice and snow in the west of the country.

In the Czech Republic, ice was also hampering road and rail traffic.

Prague airport came to a virtual standstill, with firefighters having to de-ice the runways.

Around 50 people were treated for injuries because of the icy conditions, according to Prague’s emergency services, cited by the CTK agency.

In neighbouring Hungary, where severe winter conditions have affected a large part of the country since last week, Budapest airport was shut down because of ‘black ice and extreme icing’, the airport said.

Earlier Tuesday, an Ethiopian Airlines cargo aircraft went off the runway while taxiing coming to a standstill in the grass, the airport said in a statement, adding the incident was under investigation.

Trains and flights were also experiencing delays, while authorities reported drift ice on the Danube and the Tisza rivers, where icebreakers have been put on alert.

Lake Balaton in the west of the country is currently frozen — a relatively rare phenomenon seen about once every ten to fifteen years.

However, authorities warned that the ice is still too thin for skating, urging the public to be cautious.

title: Youth lynched on cattle lifting suspicion
body:
A young man was on Tuesday lynched by a mob at Sujanagar in Pabna while he was allegedly lifting cows.

The deceased Sagar Sheikh alias Masud  Rana,23, son of Abdul Matin Sheikh of Hasampur area under Nazirganj union, was a carpenter and van driver by profession.

The body was recovered from the railway station area at Tantiband union of the upazila at about 12 noon on Tuesday. The lynching took place in the area at 5:00am.

‎According to the police and local sources, two or three people, including the deceased Sagar, went to the house of some Nazrul Islam in the Tantiband Station area about 4:00am allegedly for cow lifting.

When Nazrul›s son Monirul Islam realised the matter and shouted, some people of the area gathered, detained Sagar and beat him up, killing him on the spot.

More than fifty serious injury marks were found all over his body. In addition, there were multiple sharp weapon injuries on his head and legs.

Locals informed the police and they came and recovered the body at about 12 noon.

Sujanagar circle assistant superintendent of police Sadiq Ahmed told New Age, ‘Initially, we learnt that a young man was killed in a mob lynching while trying to steal cows. After receiving the information, we visited the scene. The body was recovered and sent to a hospital morgue. Legal action will be taken.’

title: 100 children killed in Gaza since ceasefire: UN
body:
At least 100 children have been killed by Israeli airstrikes and ground forces in Gaza since the start of a tenuous ceasefire three months ago, the United Nations said on Tuesday.

The UN children’s agency UNICEF said that at least 60 boys and 40 girls had been killed in the Israeli-occupied Palestinian territory since early October.

‘More than 100 children have been killed in Gaza since the ceasefire,’ UNICEF spokesman James Elder told reporters in Geneva.

‘That’s roughly a girl or  a boy killed here every day during a ceasefire,’ he said, speaking from Gaza City.

‘These children are killed from airstrikes, drone strikes, including suicide drones. They’re killed from tank shelling. They’re killed from live ammunition. They’re killed from quad copters.

‘We are at 100 — no doubt,’ he said, adding that the true number was likely higher.

‘A ceasefire that slows the bombs is progress but one that still buries children is not enough.’

AFP has sought a response from the Israeli military.

An official at Gaza’s health ministry, which maintains casualty records, has reported a higher figure of 165 children killed during the tenuous ceasefire, out of a total 442 fatalities.

‘Additionally, seven children have died from exposure to cold since the beginning of this year,’ Zaher Al-Wahidi, Director of the Computer Department at the Ministry of Health, said.

Elder stressed that the on-going Israeli attacks came after more than two years of war which has ‘left life for Gaza’s children unimaginably hard’.

‘They still live in fear. The psychological damage remains untreated, and it’s becoming deeper and harder to heal the longer this goes on,’ he said.

In November, authorities in Gaza said more than 70,000 people had been killed there since the beginning of the war waged by Israel in response to Hamas’s October 7, 2023, attack on Israel.

Nearly 80 per cent of buildings in Gaza have been destroyed or damaged in the relentless air and ground offensive, according to UN data.

On January 1, Israel suspended 37 international aid agencies from accessing the Gaza Strip, despite what the UN said at the time was an ‘outrageous’ move.

‘Blocking international NGOs, blocking any humanitarian aid... that means blocking life-saving assistance,’ Elder stressed on Monday.

While UNICEF had managed to significantly increase aid entering the densely populated strip since October, he stressed: ‘You need partners on the ground, and it (the aid) still doesn’t meet the need.’

‘It’s impossible to overstate just how much still is required to be done here.’

He also insisted: ‘When you’ve got key NGOs banned from delivering humanitarian aid and from bearing witness, and when foreign journalists are barred’ it begs the question if the aim is ‘restricting scrutiny of suffering of children’.

title: Jamaat leader killed at West Rajabazar home
body:
A leader of the Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami was strangled to death at his residence in West Rajabazar area in the capital Dhaka early Tuesday.

After the murder, the miscreants fled with gold ornaments and five lakh taka in cash, according to the police and family members.

Family members, however, suspected that this was not a mere theft, but a planned murder.

The deceased, Anwar Ullah, 65, a homeopathy practitioner hailed from Cumilla, was vice-president of the Jamaat-e-Islami Dhaka North’s West Rajabazar ward unit, said the police.

Sher-e-Bangla Nagar police station officer-in-charge Md Monirul Islam said that the incident occurred between 2:30am and 5:00am on the day.

‘Two masked men entered the house by cutting grilles. They tied Anwar Ullah and his wife’s hands and feet, and strangled Anwar to death. They took away gold and cash before fleeing the scene,’ he said.

Filing a case was under process regarding the incident, Monirul said.

‘Primarily, the police believe that it was case of theft. However, an investigation is going on to find out the actual motive behind the killing and efforts are on to identify the perpetrators and arrest them,’ added the police official.

The Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami Dhaka city north in a statement on Tuesday condemned the incident and demanded ensuring exemplary punishment for the perpetrators.

Pointing to the recent killings of political leaders, Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami Dhaka city north in the statement expressed concern over the deterioration of law and order.

‘The reason for the killings must be revealed as soon as possible, and those responsible must be arrested and punished. Otherwise, people will lose trust in the interim government,’ the statement said.

title: VPN barred in four Kashmir districts ‘due to security reasons’
body:
Using magisterial powers, several district administrations in Kashmir have banned the use of virtual private networks due to security reasons, reports The Hindu.

In the past 24 hours, the four districts of Shopian, Kulgam, Budgam and Srinagar have, in separate orders, suspended the usage of VPNs, which allow Internet users to mask their locations and identity.

In the latest order issued by the Budgam administration on Tuesday, various types of VPN services were suspended on mobile phones for a period of two months.

‘Under Section 163 of the Bhartiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 following inputs received from the Senior Superintendent of Police, Budgam regarding unprecedented and suspicious high usage of VPNs across various parts of the district,’ the order said.

The order said such usage has the potential to be exploited for unlawful and anti-national activities, including incitement of unrest, dissemination of inflammatory material, and coordination of activities prejudicial to the maintenance of public order.

‘It was further observed that VPNs enable encrypted data transmission, mask IP addresses, bypass firewalls and website restrictions, and may expose sensitive information to potential cyber threats,’ the order said.

Considering the prevailing circumstances and the need to take immediate preventive measures to safeguard public security and sensitive data, the District Magistrate deemed it necessary to impose the restriction.

Several districts in the Pir Panchal Valley and the Chenab Valley in the Jammu region have also banned VPN services in the past one year. Such orders were implemented in the wake of reporting heightened activity by militants in these valleys.

title: Trump hits Iran trade partners with tariffs
body:
US president Donald Trump on Tuesday said Iranians should continue nationwide protests and take over the country’s institutions as authorities there cracked down on mass demonstrations.

‘Iranian Patriots, KEEP PROTESTING - TAKE OVER YOUR INSTITUTIONS!!!’ Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform.

‘Save the names of the killers and abusers. They will pay a big price.

‘I have cancelled all meetings with Iranian Officials until the senseless killing of protesters STOPS. HELP IS ON ITS WAY.’

Trump did not specify what form the promised ‘help’ would take, in a message that backed regime change in the Islamic Republic — marking a change in the US stance from one day ago.

On Monday, his press secretary Karoline Leavitt told reporters that a channel for diplomacy with Tehran remained open, saying that Iran was taking a ‘far different tone’ in private discussions with Trump’s special envoy Steve Witkoff.

Trump on Monday also announced a 25-per cent tariff on any country doing business with Iran, ramping up pressure as a rights group estimated the crackdown has killed at least 648 people.

Iranian authorities insist they have regained control after successive nights of mass protests that have posed one of the biggest challenges to the clerical leadership since the 1979 Islamic revolution ousted the shah.

But rights groups accuse the government of using live fire against protesters and masking the scale of the crackdown with an internet blackout that has now lasted more than four days.

International phone calls however have resumed in  Iran after being blocked for days, an AFP correspondent in Tehran said on Tuesday, but only outgoing calls could be made.

Trump, who has repeatedly threatened Iran with military intervention, said in a social media post on Monday that the new levies would ‘immediately’ hit the Islamic republic’s trading partners who also do business with the United States.

‘This order is final and conclusive,’ he wrote, without specifying who it will affect.

Iran’s main trading partners are China, Turkey, the United Arab Emirates and Iraq, according to economic database Trading Economics.

The White House said Monday that Trump remained ‘unafraid’ to deploy military force against Iran, but was pursuing diplomacy as a first resort.

The Norway-based NGO Iran Human Rights said it had confirmed 648 people killed during the protests, including nine minors, but warned the death toll was likely much higher — ‘according to some estimates, more than 6,000’.

The internet shutdown has made it ‘extremely difficult to independently verify these reports’, IHR said, adding that an estimated 10,000 people had been arrested.

‘Iranian authorities have significantly intensified their lethal crackdown on protesters since January 8, with credible reports that security forces are carrying out large-scale killings across the country,’ Human Rights Watch said.

Iranian state media has said dozens of members of the security forces have been killed, with their funerals turning into large pro-government rallies. Authorities have declared three days of national mourning for those killed.

The death toll from major anti-government protests in Iran reached at least 2,000 as of Tuesday, according to data published by the US-based Human Rights Activists News Agency, over 16 days of unrest, reports ABC News.

At least 10,721 people have been arrested, HRANA said, in protests that have been recorded in 606 locations in 187 cities across all 31 Iranian provinces. Among the dead are nine children, the group reported.

The HRANA data relies on the work of activists inside and outside the country. ABC News cannot independently verify these numbers. The group earlier on Tuesday said 646 people had been killed. The Iranian government has not provided any death tolls during the on-going protests.

Foreign minister Abbas Araghchi, speaking to Al Jazeera, insisted that the government had been ‘in dialogue’ with the protesters in the initial phase of the movement and the internet was only cut ‘after we confronted terrorist operations and realised orders were coming from outside the country’.

Addressing Trump’s threats, he added: ‘We are prepared for any eventuality and we hope Washington will choose a wise option. It doesn’t matter which option they choose, we are ready for it.’

The government on Monday sought to regain control of the streets with mass nationwide rallies that supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei hailed as proof that the protest movement was defeated, in a ‘warning’ to the United States.

In power since 1989 and now 86, Khamenei has faced significant challenges, most recently the 12-day war in June against Israel which resulted in the killing of top security officials and forced him to go into hiding.

‘When a regime can only hold on to power through violence, then it is effectively finished,’ said German chancellor Friedrich Merz during a trip to India. ‘I believe that we are now witnessing the last days and weeks of this regime.’

Analysts however have cautioned that it is premature to predict the immediate demise of the theocratic system, pointing to the repressive levers the leadership has, including the Revolutionary Guards Corps, which are charged with safeguarding the Islamic revolution.

‘These protests arguably represent the most serious challenge to the Islamic republic in years, both in scale and in their increasingly explicit political demands,’ Nicole Grajewski, professor at the Sciences Po Centre for International Studies in Paris, said.

She said it was unclear if the protests would unseat the leadership, pointing to ‘the sheer depth and resilience of Iran’s repressive apparatus’.

French president Emmanuel Macron issued a statement condemning ‘the state violence that indiscriminately targets Iranian women and men who courageously demand respect for their rights’.

Prize-winning Iranian filmmaker Jafar Panahi told broadcaster France Inter: ‘The Iranian people are defenceless today, and despite all that, they are out on the streets.’

Reza Pahlavi, the US-based son of Iran’s ousted shah who has been vocal in calling for protests, said Trump was a man who ‘means what he says and says what he means’ and who ‘knows what’s at stake’.

‘The red line that was drawn has been definitely surpassed by this regime.’

title: Fair polls, democratic transition stressed
body:
Academics and political leaders at a dialogue on Tuesday said that a credible national election along with political, legal and institutional reforms was crucial to Bangladesh’s return to democracy.

They said that a technically fair election alone would fall short of delivering the country’s long-awaited democratic transition without accountability, institutional reforms and a change in political culture.

The observations came at a divisional dialogue titled ‘Aspirations of the Mass Uprising, Reforms and Election Manifestoes’, organised by Shushashoner Jonno Nagorik (Citizens for Good Governance), at the CIRDAP auditorium in the capital Dhaka ahead of the 13th Jatiya Sangsad elections scheduled for February 12.

Dhaka University professor Kazi Mahbubur Rahman said, ‘At this moment, what Bangladesh needs the most is a democratic transition through a fair election. However, election alone is not democracy. Several reforms are needed so that a new political order can become effective and leaders committed to democratic values can emerge.’

He said that a key obstacle to democratic transition was that bureaucrats instead of elected representatives were making laws, while the absence of a responsible opposition was another major challenge.

‘If there is a strong opposition, debates and discussions will take place in parliament instead of on the streets, and they can play a meaningful role in ensuring democratic transition,’ he added.

Bangladesh Nationalist Party leader Nilufar Chowdhury Moni raised concerns over security during the national polls, saying that 1,365 weapons looted from police stations in the country on August 5, 2024, were yet to be recovered.

‘If violence breaks out at polling centres, voters will stay away, destroying the election environment,’ she warned.

Dhaka University professor Rashed Al Titumir said that voters were not getting proper information about the election and candidates, but were instead being fed with misinformation.

‘Misinformation alone is enough to damage the election environment, as was seen during the Brexit referendum in the United Kingdom,’ he said, adding that the Election Commission should formulate a policy to detect false, misleading and disinformation and take action accordingly.

Jamaat-e-Islami Dhaka south city nayeb-e-amir Md Helal Uddin said that his party supported reforms and was campaigning for a ‘Yes’ vote in the referendum, which will be held simultaneously with the national polls, adding that the Jamaat would soon announce its election manifesto.

Communist Party of Bangladesh presidium member Ragib Ahsan Munna said, ‘We should fight for a system in which all people of the country — workers, porters, farmers and labourers — will enjoy their rights.’

Senior journalist Abu Sayeed Khan said that mob violence, undisclosed money and lack of verification of candidates’ affidavits were major obstacles to a fair election.

He called for election expenditure monitoring, fact-checking units to curb disinformation and stronger democratic practices within political parties.

National Citizen Party joint convener Sarwar Tushar said that uncertainty still prevailed over whether the election would take place, while muscle power and money continued to dominate campaigns.

He alleged that administrative bias and selective law enforcement were creating an uneven playing field.

Dhaka University professor Jasmin Uddin Khan said that political parties should prioritise education in their election manifestoes to build a skilled and capable workforce, and also make clear commitments to forest management and environmental protection.

Writer Sanjib Drong said that before creating a level-playing field in the election, the development and progress of structurally disadvantaged groups must be ensured.

Presenting the keynote paper, Shujan executive director Badiul Alam Majumdar said that Bangladesh had failed to establish a sustainable democratic and electoral system even 54 years after its independence.

‘Following the collapse of the electoral system, the country was trapped under a fascist regime for 15 years. After the 2024 mass uprising, the interim government prioritised justice, reform and election, but a genuine democratic transition requires far more than voting,’ he said.

He said that political parties must make clear, time-bound and measurable commitments in their election manifestoes to fulfil the aspirations of the uprising, particularly of young people who no longer wanted to inherit injustice, inequality and impunity.

title: New political platform likely Friday
body:
Frontline organisers of the July uprising are launching a new political platform on Friday, aimed at laying the foundation for a democratic socialist political party.

‘All preparations are underway for the declaration of the platform, scheduled to be held at the Central Shaheed Minar in Dhaka at 4:00pm on Friday,’ said Meghmallar Basu, one of the organisers of the platform.

Meghmallar, also the president of the Dhaka University unit of Bangladesh Chhatra Union, said, ‘We want to form a democratic political party. By democracy, we mean a society where the human and cultural rights of all people are equally ensured.’

Organisers said that young activists, student leaders, and followers of diverse ideologies, religions, and ethnic communities would join the platform.

The initiative plans to operate as a political platform for six months to a year before evolving into a full-fledged political party, during which time it will develop political and economic theses, a manifesto, and an organisational framework.

Ahead of the upcoming national election, the platform intends to remain active in policy dialogues, citizen mobilisation, social movements, and grassroots organisation-building across the country.

After the election, the organisers aim to formally launch the platform as a political party once its ideological and organisational groundwork is complete.

‘Some top leaders of the July uprising who resigned from the National Citizen Party and dignitaries from all walks of life will remain with the political platform,’ said one of the organisers and July uprising leader, Nazifa Jannat.

Nazifa said that some former student leaders living at home and abroad, teachers, intellectuals, activists of different political parties, including the National Citizen Party, would be involved with the platform.

Though it would begin as a political platform, it would eventually be transformed into a new political party within one year of its launch, she said.

She said that the draft of the party constitution has already been prepared.

Many of those joining the platform are coming from leftist and centrist ideological backgrounds. They also participated in the July mass uprising.

Leaders who resigned from the NCP central committee in September—Anik Roy, Moinul Islam Tuhin (Tuhin Khan), and Alik Mree—are among the founding members.

Anik Roy, a former general secretary of the left student organisation Chhatra Union, joined the NCP and became its joint convener.

Writer and activist Tuhin Khan served as a joint member-secretary of the NCP, while Alik Mree, president of the Bangladesh Adivasi Chhatra Sangram Parishad, was the NCP’s joint chief organiser for the northern region.

The platform will also include former Chhatra Union president Baki Billah, writer and researcher Mir Huzaifa Al Mamduh, writer Ferdous Ara Rumi, Chhatra Union leader and former coordinator of the Anti-Discrimination Student Movement Nazifa Jannat, Dhaka University Chhatra Union president Meghmallar Bosu, and general secretary Main Ahmed, said an organizer of the platform.

On September 8, 2024, the Jatiya Nagorik Committee was formed, led by student leaders of the July uprising, with the goal of restructuring the state, abolishing fascist systems, and successfully establishing the political framework of a ‘new Bangladesh’.

Key leaders from the Nagorik Committee and student movements involved in the July uprising later formed the NCP, with Nahid Islam as convener and Akhter Hossen as member secretary.

However, a number of NCP leaders have recently resigned in opposition to the party’s joining an alliance led by the Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami.

title: DU observes Swami Vivekananda’s 163rd birth anniv
body:
Dhaka University observed the 163rd birth anniversary of Swami Vivekananda through a day-long programme on Tuesday.
