On the occasion, flowers were offered at the base of his sculpture at the Jagannath Hall of the university, said a press release.

On Monday, a discussion meeting on Swami Vivekananda’s life and philosophy was held at the meeting room of Rabindra Bhaban of the hall.

Bangladesh Vivekananda Shiksha O Sangskriti Parishad and its DU unit jointly organised the anniversary observance.

DU pro-vice-chancellor for education Professor Mamun Ahmed attended the discussion as chief guest with president of the parishad Professor Paritosh Mandal in chair.

Jagannath Hall provost Debashish Pal, Professor Tapas Kumar Biswas of the Institute of Education and Research, Professor Shimul Haldar of philosophy department, and Professor Mithun Sarkar of applied chemistry and chemical engineering department were present at the event, among others.

At the programme, Vivekananda scholarships were awarded to 20 students of the university. The cover of the annual magazine ‘Gyandip’ was also unveiled, while educational materials and winter clothes were distributed among students of Vivekananda Vidyalaya and children of Jagannath Hall staff.

title: BRAC Bank distributes winter clothes across Bangladesh
body:
BRAC Bank has distributed more than 62,000 winter clothes nationwide to support marginalised communities affected by extreme cold, said a press release.

As part of the initiative, the bank recently provided 13,000 blankets through the Chief Advisor’s Welfare Fund and the Chattogram City Corporation, ensuring support for vulnerable communities in urban and semi-urban areas.

In parallel, BRAC Bank leveraged its SME and distribution network to deliver 49,653 hoodies at the union level, reaching madrasas, orphanages and communities with limited access to winter protection, particularly children and the elderly, it said.

The programme aims to reduce health risks associated with severe cold and safeguard lives during the winter months, focusing on those most exposed to hardship.

BRAC Bank managing director and chief executive officer Tareq Refat Ullah Khan said, ‘At BRAC Bank, standing beside the vulnerable is not an obligation, it is a responsibility. This winter assistance programme reflects our commitment to inclusion, dignity, and care, translated into action that delivers real impact.’

title: Pubali Bank posts over Tk 3,000cr operating profit in 2025
body:
Pubali Bank PLC recorded operating profit exceeding Tk 3,000 crore in 2025 — marking a significant milestone in the bank’s history, said a press release.

The bank attributed this to sustainable growth strategies, robust risk management and a strong customer-centric approach.

Compared to 2024, the bank’s operating profit grew by approximately 27 per cent in 2025.

The bank recently organised an event celebrating the milestone at its head office in the capital.

Mohammad Ali, managing director and chief executive officer, said, ‘This success is not merely a financial achievement; it is the combined result of the board of directors’ responsible guidance and strong corporate governance, customer trust, employee dedication and effective management.’

‘This achievement will inspire Pubali Bank PLC to deliver even stronger, safer and more reliable banking services in the future—particularly through the expansion of digital and cashless banking,’ he added.

During the year, the bank’s total deposits rose to Tk. 89,552 crore, representing a growth of more than 20 per cent over the previous year. At the same time, the bank continued to support the country’s business and industrial sectors, with advances increasing by 13 per cent to Tk 71,140 crore.

As per the release, in 2025, the bank achieved 7 per cent growth in import financing and over 21 per cent growth in export financing, further strengthening Bangladesh’s trade momentum.

Alongside this, effective risk management and improved asset quality enabled the bank to maintain non-performing loans at 2.14 per cent, while the advance-deposit ratio improved to 72.53 per cent.

title: Actress Tasnia Farin brand ambassador of Erfan Chinigura Aromatic Rice
body:
Actress Tasnia Farin signed a contract on Sunday to become brand ambassador of Erfan Chinigura Aromatic Rice, a product of Erfan Group.

Erfan Group managing director and chief executive officer Mahbub Alam signed the agreement with Tasnia Farin at a hotel in the capital.

As a brand ambassador, Tasnia Farin will participate in various television commercials, OVCs, photo-shoots and different public awareness activities and promotional campaigns for Erfan Chinigura Aromatic Rice.

Among others, Erfan Group DGM — sales and marketing (retail) Mahmud Rahman Bulbul, AGM — sales and marketing (wholesale) Ziaur Rahman, manager (HR and admin) SM Sorman Ali, manager — accounts Md Masud Parvez and brand manager Sazzad Mohammad Zahir were present.

title: Iran worries push up oil price as global stocks diverge
body:
European and Asian stock markets diverged Tuesday as investors awaited key US inflation data while concerns about Iran lifted oil prices.

Tokyo closed at a record high and the yen fell on speculation over a snap election in Japan.

Paris and Frankfurt were in the red nearing the half-way mark, while London was flat.

Wall Street finished at another record high Monday, as investors shrugged off worries about a US criminal probe of the Federal Reserve central bank.

The heads of major central banks have thrown their support behind the US Fed and its chairman Jerome Powell, saying in a joint statement Tuesday that it was ‘critical to preserve’ their independence.

On Sunday, Powell took aim at escalating pressure from president Donald Trump’s administration to lower interest rates.

Investors were treading water ahead of the release of US inflation data later in the day.

‘This is by far the most important metric for the Fed,’ said Kathleen Brooks, research director at XTB trading group.

‘Today’s data is expected to reset inflation expectations and be a clear indicator of what the Fed should do this year and how many rate cuts to expect,’ she added.

In Asia, Tokyo’s Nikkei closed up 3.1 per cent, driven by anticipation that Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi will capitalise on strong poll numbers by calling an election.

Takaichi was appointed Japan’s first woman prime minister in October and her cabinet is enjoying an approval rating of around 70 per cent.

But her ruling bloc has only a slim majority in parliament’s powerful lower house, hindering her ambitious policy agenda.

Hong Kong also gained, while Shanghai closed lower.

Seoul climbed 1.5 per cent after South Korean chip giant SK hynix said it would spend 19 trillion won ($12.9 billion) building an advanced chip packaging plant, as the firm rides the global AI boom.

Oil prices rose after US president Donald Trump announced a 25-per cent tariff on any country trading with Iran, ramping up pressure on Tehran and its friends over its violent crackdown on a wave of protests.

Trump said in a social media post on Monday that the new levies would ‘immediately’ hit the Islamic republic’s trading partners who also do business with the United States.

The move ‘is likely to hit its biggest trading partners like China’, said Victoria Scholar, head of investment at Interactive Investor.

In other company news, shares in Danish renewable energy firm Orsted climbed five per cent after a US judge cleared the way for its offshore wind project to resume work in New England, nullifying a Trump administration order pausing the project.

title: Agrani Bank holds 1000th board meeting
body:
Agrani Bank PLC holds its 1000th board meeting at its head office on Tuesday, said a press release.

Chairman Syed Abu Naser Bakhtiar Ahmed presided over the meeting.

At the meeting, directors Mohammad Fazlul Haque, Kabirul Izdani Khan, Mohammad Sultan Mahmud, Muzaffar Ahmed and Md Said Kutub were present.

Managing director Md Anwarul Islam was also in attendance.

title: BGMEA to work with ActionAid for sustainable transformation
body:
The Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association and ActionAid Bangladesh have signed a Memorandum of Understanding on Tuesday to work as strategic partners in advancing the sustainable transformation of Bangladesh’s readymade garment sector.

According to a press release, the partnership aimed  to ensure human rights and environmental due diligence, strengthen compliance capacity, and improve the overall quality of life of garment workers.

Under the MoU, ActionAid Bangladesh would support the implementation of BGMEA’s Sustainable Strategic Vision 2030 as a strategic partner.

Inamul Haq Khan, senior vice president of the BGMEA, and Farah Kabir, country director of ActionAid Bangladesh, signed the MoU on behalf of their organization at the BGMEA Complex in the capital’s Uttara.

According to the MoU, the key areas of collaboration would include promoting women’s leadership in factories, ensuring a decent work environment, creating a harassment- and discrimination-free workplace, and raising workers’ awareness of their rights.

They would also work to reduce carbon emissions through energy-efficient technologies, encourage green industrialisation, and ensure occupational health, mental well-being, and access to social protection schemes for workers.

The both signatories would focus on enhancing workforce skills, and introducing specialised monitoring tools and training aligned with international standards like the EU Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive, the press release added.

The MoU would also work to strengthen coordination among factory owners, workers, and buyers through regular reviews to maintain transparency.

Speaking at the ceremony, Inamul Haq Khan said that Bangladesh’s garment industry is no longer merely a production hub but has emerged as a trusted global partner in sustainable and ethical business practices.

He expressed hope that the partnership with ActionAid Bangladesh would further strengthen human rights and environmental standards in garment factories and elevate Bangladesh’s reputation and competitiveness in international markets.

Farah Kabir said that sustainable growth of the garment industry is only possible by ensuring workers’ rights and environmental sustainability.

She noted that the organisation aims to build an inclusive ecosystem with all stakeholders where transparency and human rights remain top priorities.

The MoU would remain effective for five years, from January 2026 to December 2030.

Under the agreement, ActionAid Bangladesh would provide financial support for the implementation of the initiatives, while BGMEA would ensure infrastructure and logistical support across its member factories.

BGMEA vice president Md Rezwan Selim, directors Nafis-Ud Doula, Sheikh Hossain Muhammad Mustafiz and Rumana Rashid, along with senior officials of ActionAid Bangladesh, were also present at the signing ceremony.

title: Top textile cos join Heimtextil
body:
Bangladeshi home textile companies are showcasing their products at the Heimtextil Frankfurt 2026.

According to a press release, one of the world’s biggest trade fairs for home and contract textiles has been taking place from Tuesday, which would continue till January 16 at Messe Frankfurt, Germany.

The fair is expected to set the first design and textile trends of the new year and offer a global stage for innovation, creativity, and business growth.

Heimtextil has been featuring a full range of home textiles, including towels, bedding, carpets, bath products, furnishing fabrics, and sun-protection materials.

It has been also highlighting new technologies such as AI-assisted design and sustainable production methods, said the press release.

Bangladesh has continued to grow as a key supplier to the global textile market and the fair would give its exporters a strong opportunity to meet European  buyers, explore new markets and understand emerging international trends.

Shaifun Nahre, chairman of Stylus Towels, said that the fair would be an excellent start with productive interactions with buyers.

‘We have begun on a very positive note, building strong connections and meaningful discussions. It’s been a strong beginning, and we are hopeful for even better opportunities and successful days ahead,’ she added.

This year, Bangladesh is participating with a mix of direct exhibitors and companies supported by the Export Promotion Bureau.

Direct exhibitors, including ACS Textile (Bangladesh) Limited, Artisan House BD Limited, Debonair Padding & Quilting Solution Limited, Hossain Dyeing and Printing Mills Limited (Unit-2), Karupannya Rangpur Limited, Naheed Fine Tex Limited, Noman Terry Towel Mills Limited, Shabab Fabrics Limited, Towel Tex Limited, and Zaber & Zubair Fabrics Limited (NICE Group), are showcasing their products.

Moreover, three companies are taking part with support from the Export Promotion Bureau, namely Jaantex Industries Limited, Maanuri Textile Mills and Stylus Towels Limited.

Heimtextil 2026 will help Bangladeshi companies strengthen their global presence, connect with new customers, and showcase the country’s skills and quality in the international textile industry, according to the press release.

The home textile sector has been regarded as an emerging player in the country’s export basket, which once reached the milestone of $1 billion in export earnings, ranking third after readymade garments, jute, and leather.

However, due to the Ukraine-Russia war and the domestic energy crisis, the sector’s earnings have fluctuated since the financial year 2022-23, said the exporters.

In the 2024-25 financial year, the sector earned $872 million from its global destinations and in the July-December period of FY26, the sector earned $423 million, EPB data stated.

European Union countries, including Germany, Spain, France, and Italy, are the major destinations for the sector, and EU brands such as H&M Home, ALDI, Carrefour, Denantes and OTTO.

The home textile export basket of the country includes bed linen, bed sheets, and other bedroom textiles; bath linen; carpets and rugs; blankets; kitchen linen; curtains; cushions and cushion covers; and covers for quilts, according to the EPB data.

title: Afghan Taliban envoy posted to Delhi
body:
Afghanistan’s Taliban government has appointed their first senior official in India since the group returned to power in 2021, charged with leading their embassy in Delhi.

India has not officially recognised the Taliban government, but the move signals a deepening engagement, with New Delhi seeking to exploit divisions between Islamabad and Kabul.

Noor Ahmad Noor, a Taliban foreign ministry official, assumed responsibility as charge d’affaires, and has already held meetings with Indian officials, the embassy said in a statement.

‘Both sides emphasised the importance of strengthening Afghanistan–India relations,’ the Afghan Embassy said, in a post on X late Monday.

India has not commented, but the Afghan embassy posted a photograph of Noor with senior Indian foreign ministry official Anand Prakash.

The Taliban’s strict interpretation of Islamic law may appear an unlikely match for prime minister Narendra Modi’s Hindu nationalist government, but India has sought to seize the opening.

Nuclear-armed rivals India and Pakistan fought a brief but deadly clash in May 2025, their worst confrontation in decades.

The appointment is significant for the Taliban, which has sought to reclaim control over Afghanistan’s overseas diplomatic missions as part of a broader push for international legitimacy.

In October, India said it would upgrade its technical mission in Afghanistan to a full embassy.

Russia is the only country to officially recognise the Afghan Taliban government.

title: Takaichi urges Lee to help ‘ensure regional stability’
body:
Japanese prime minister Sanae Takaichi called on South Korean president Lee Jae Myung Tuesday to help ‘ensure regional stability’, as Beijing pressures Tokyo over its stance on Taiwan.

The two leaders met in Takaichi’s picturesque home region of Nara in western Japan, days after Lee visited Chinese leader Xi Jinping in Beijing.

They agreed to strengthen cooperation on economic security, regional and global issues, as well as artificial intelligence, according to South Korea’s presidential office.

Looming in the background of the meeting was Japan’s heated diplomatic spat with China, triggered by Takaichi’s suggestion in November that Japan could intervene militarily if China attacks Taiwan.

China, which regards Taiwan as its own territory, reacted angrily, blocking exports to Japan of ‘dual-use’ items with potential military applications, fuelling worries in Japan that Beijing could choke supplies of much-needed rare earths.

Takaichi said she told Lee that ‘while advancing Japan-South Korea relations, both countries should cooperate to ensure regional stability and fulfil their respective roles’.

‘As the environment surrounding both of our countries becomes ever more severe, our bilateral relations, as well as the cooperation among Japan, South Korea and the United States, are assuming greater importance,’ she later told a news conference.

At the beginning of his meeting with Takaichi, Lee said that cooperation between the two US allies ‘is more important than ever’.

‘In this increasingly complex situation and within this rapidly changing international order, we must continue to make progress toward a better future,’ Lee added.

They agreed to continue their ‘shuttle diplomacy’ of regular meetings, according to Takaichi, as well as work towards the complete denuclearisation of North Korea.

Lee and Takaichi, who both took office in 2025, last met in October on the sidelines of the APEC regional summit in Gyeongju, South Korea.

It is Lee’s second visit to Japan since August, when he met Takaichi’s predecessor Shigeru Ishiba.

Lee and Takaichi will have dinner Tuesday, before visiting one of Japan’s oldest temples in Nara on Wednesday.

‘Behind closed doors, the leaders will certainly discuss the current Japan-China crisis, as Beijing’s retaliatory measures, including export controls, will have an impact on Korea as well,’ Benoit Hardy-Chartrand, an East Asian geopolitics expert at Temple University’s Tokyo campus said, with the supply chains of the three nations deeply intertwined.

Lee said in an interview with Japanese public broadcaster NHK aired on Monday that it was not his place to ‘intervene or get involved’ in the Japan-China row.

‘From the standpoint of peace and stability in Northeast Asia, confrontation between China and Japan is undesirable,’ he said. ‘We can only wait for China and Japan to resolve matters amicably through dialogue.’

Hardy-Chartrand said he believed ‘the South Korean government felt that it was necessary for president Lee to visit Japan not too long after going to China, in order to demonstrate that Seoul is not favouring one side over the other’.

Lee and Takaichi were also expected to discuss their relations with the United States because the unpredictable Trump ‘has put in doubt old certainties and highlighted the importance of strengthening their ties’, he said.

On the bilateral front, bitter memories of Japan’s brutal occupation of the Korean peninsula from 1910 to 1945 have cast a long shadow over Tokyo-Seoul ties.

Lee’s conservative predecessor Yoon Suk Yeol, who declared martial law in December 2024 and was removed from office, had sought to improve relations with Japan.

Lee is also relatively more dovish towards North Korea than was Yoon, and has said that South Korea and Japan are like ‘neighbours sharing a front yard’.

title: We choose Denmark over US, says Greenland PM
body:
Greenland’s prime minister said Tuesday that the autonomous territory would choose to remain Danish rather than become part of the United States, following US president Donald Trump’s threats to take over the Arctic island.

‘We are now facing a geopolitical crisis, and if we have to choose between the United States and Denmark here and now, we choose Denmark,’ Greenlandic prime minister Jens-Frederik Nielsen told a press conference in Copenhagen.

Trump has been talking up the idea of buying or annexing the Arctic territory for years, and further stoked tensions on Sunday by saying that the United States would take the territory ‘one way or the other’.

‘One thing must be clear to everyone Greenland does not want to be owned by the United States. Greenland does not want to be governed by the United States. Greenland does not want to be part of the United States,’ Nielsen said.

He was speaking alongside Danish leader Mette Frederiksen, who said it had not been easy to stand up to what she slammed as ‘completely unacceptable pressure from our closest ally’.

‘However, there are many indications that the most challenging part is ahead of us,’ Frederiksen said.

Trump has insisted the US needs Greenland for ‘national security’.

Frederiksen stressed that ‘of course, we want to strengthen cooperation on security in the Arctic with the United States, with NATO, with Europe and with the Arctic states in NATO.’

Danish foreign minister Lars Lokke Rasmussen and his Greenlandic counterpart Vivian Motzfeldt are due to meet with US vice president JD Vance and secretary of state Marco Rubio at the White House on Wednesday.

title: Bangladesh suspends visa on arrival for all countries until Feb 15
body:
The government of Bangladesh has suspended the ‘Visa on Arrival’ facility for all eligible countries, including Bhutan, with effect from January 15 to February 15, 2026.

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs and External Trade informed the general public that the Embassy of the People’s Republic of Bangladesh in Thimphu has officially conveyed that, said the Bhutanese Ministry in a formal notification.

In view of this, all Bhutanese nationals intending to travel to Bangladesh during the above period are advised to apply for a visa in advance through the Embassy of Bangladesh in Thimphu prior to their travel, the notification reads.

The Bhutanese Ministry advised all travellers to take note of this change and make necessary arrangements well in advance to avoid any inconvenience.

title: Uganda shuts down internet ahead of election
body:
Ugandan authorities ordered an internet blackout on Tuesday, two days ahead of elections in which president Yoweri Museveni is seeking to extend his 40-year rule.

The 81-year-old leader, who once said African rulers should not overstay their time in office, is widely expected to win a seventh term on Thursday due to his total control over state and security bodies.

But he is taking no chances against a popular opponent, Bobi Wine, a 43-year-old singer-turned-politician, who has drawn large crowds to his rallies despite violent repression from the security forces.

Museveni held his final campaign rally in the capital Kampala on Tuesday, in a grand show most international media were blocked from covering.

Thousands walked to Kololo National Ceremonial Gardens for the rally, many telling AFP they had been bussed into the capital for the event and given free food.

Foreign journalists were repeatedly denied access to the grounds despite having accreditation from the government, some threatened with arrest.

‘Your camera is not welcome,’ an unidentified Special Forces Command officer told the reporters.

Rights groups and international monitors say hundreds of opposition supporters have been arrested in the run-up to the election.

Another key opposition figure, Kizza Besigye, who has run four times against Museveni, was kidnapped in Kenya in 2024 and brought back to a military court in Uganda, where he is still on trial.

In a letter to internet providers, the Uganda Communications Commission said the internet shutdown, due to come into effect at 1500 GMT on Tuesday, was necessary to prevent ‘misinformation’ and ‘incitement to violence’, and would last until further notice.

The letter’s veracity was confirmed by two government officials to AFP. There was no official statement from the government, with the officials saying no one wanted to ‘own’ the decision.

Uganda shut down the internet during the last election in 2021 — a vote that was marred by widespread allegations of rigging and state violence.

The government repeatedly promised the internet would not be cut this time, stating in a post on X on January 5 that ‘claims suggesting otherwise are false, misleading, and intended to cause unnecessary fear and tension among the public’.

Neighbouring Tanzania also shut down the internet during its election in October, which triggered massive unrest over rigging allegations. Security forces responded by killing hundreds of protesters, according to the opposition.

Despite the heavy security presence on Tuesday, thousands attended the colourful rally in Kampala featuring a life-size mascot of Museveni that waved mechanically at the cheering crowds.

Banura Oliver, 41, said she would vote for the president because of the peace he had brought to the country in the 1980s.

‘Forty years doesn’t even matter, we need even more,’ she said, adding she was dismissive of the opposition candidate.

‘If Ugandan people vote badly and vote for this young boy, we are going to suffer. He is not a good leader,’ she said.

Others said they were only there for the free rice and meat and did not intend to vote for Museveni.

‘You give me food for today, but what is tomorrow?’ Mugaala, 23 and unemployed, who did not want to give his second name, said.

title: Gold prices hit historic high
body:
Gold prices in Bangladesh have reached a historic high after the Bangladesh Jewellers Association increased prices by Tk4,199 per bhori, effective from Tuesday.

Under the revised rates, 22-carat gold is now priced at Tk232,055 per bhori (11.664 grams), the highest level ever recorded in the local market.

Previously, the highest gold price was Tk229,431 per bhori on December 29, 2025.

BAJUS announced the price hike on Monday, citing a rise in the local price of pure (tejabi) gold.

Considering the overall market situation, the association said it revised prices accordingly.

According to the new price structure, 21-carat gold will sell at Tk221,499 per bhori, while 18-carat gold has been fixed at Tk189,890 per bhori.

Gold made under the traditional method will cost Tk156,881 per bhori.

In addition to these prices, buyers will have to pay a government-mandated 5 per cent VAT and a minimum 6 per cent making charge set by BAJUS.

However, making charges may vary depending on the design and quality of the jewellery.

BAJUS last revised gold prices on January 10, when it increased the price of 22-carat gold by Tk1,050 per bhori to Tk227,856.

With the latest adjustment, gold prices have been revised six times so far this year, raised on four occasions and reduced twice.

The price of 22-carat silver rose by Tk408 per bhori to Tk5,949.

Under the new rates, 21-carat silver will sell at Tk5,715 per bhori, 18-carat silver at Tk4,899 per bhori, and traditional method silver at Tk3,674 per bhori.

This marks the fourth adjustment of silver prices this year, with prices increased twice and reduced twice.

title: UN demands independent probe
body:
The United Nations demanded Tuesday a swift and independent investigation after a federal immigration officer fatally shot a protester in the US city of Minneapolis last week.

The UN rights office voiced deep concern at the killing of 37-year-old Renee Nicole Good, who was shot dead in her car by an Immigration and Customs Enforcement agent in the Midwestern city last Wednesday.

‘Under international human rights law, the intentional use of lethal force is only permissible as a measure of last resort against an individual representing an imminent threat to life,’ UN rights office spokesman Jeremy Laurence told reporters in Geneva.

‘We take note of the FBI investigation and insist on the need for prompt, independent and transparent investigation into the killing,’ he said.

Laurence also urged ‘all authorities to take measures to deescalate tensions and refrain from incitement to violence’.

Good’s killing has sparked widespread anger at the use of force in the Trump administration’s immigration crackdown, sparking nationwide protests.

The Trump administration has sought to paint Good as a ‘domestic terrorist’, vigorously insisting the agent who fatally shot her was acting in self-defence.

This narrative is strongly disputed by local officials, who say footage shows Good’s vehicle turning away from the agent and did not pose a threat to his life.

Protesters have demanded a full investigation into the circumstances of the deadly encounter.

Democratic officials are particularly critical of the fact that local authorities have been excluded from the investigation, which is being conducted by the FBI.

title: Long term energy strategy planned, says adviser
body:
The interim government has prepared a long-term energy strategy aimed at strengthening domestic sources, said finance adviser Salehuddin Ahmed on Tuesday.

‘A presentation was made a few days ago, where I was also present,’ said the finance adviser while responding to queries from reporters after a meeting of the advisory council committee on government purchase at secretariat.

He said a comprehensive approach had been taken to bolster offshore drilling initiatives and use of coal, including domestic coal.

He also said energy remained a critical issue for the economy.

On high inflation he said, inflation could not be controlled by monetary policy alone. Inflation control goes beyond economics, he added political governance mattered.

‘You can’t control prices simply by sending inspectors or magistrates,’ he said.

Earlier, the purchase committee approved separate proposals to procure 1 crore litres of refined soybean oil and 40,000 tonnes of fertilizer.

Ministry of Commerce will procure 1 crore litres of soy bean oil through the local tender.

Sonargaon Seeds Crushing Mills Ltd., Dhaka will supply cooking oil at Tk 180.85 core with per liter costing Tk 180.85.

The Ministry of Industries will import 40,000 metric tonnes of bulk granular urea fertilizer from SABIC Agri-nutrients Company, Saudi Arabia at Tk 191.41 crore with per tonne costing $390.

Responding to another proposal from the Road Transport and Highways Division, the day’s meeting entrusted with the Bangladesh Road Transport Corporation for procurement of non-consultancy service for delivery of commercial driver training under Package No: SP (BRTA)-04 with around Tk 230.72 crore under the Bangladesh Road Safety Project, jointly financed by the Government of Bangladesh and the World Bank.

China Road and Bridge Corporation (CRBC), China, was awarded with the construction of the Nalua–Baherchar Bridge over the Pandab–Paira River including approach road, service road, river training works, toll plaza, electro-mechanical and ancillary works at Tk 899.62 crore.

The project is being implemented by the Roads and Highways Department with joint financing from the Government of Bangladesh and the OPEC Fund.

Another meeting of the advisory council committee on economic affairs at the same venue approved a proposal in principle for withdrawing a project titled New Modern Medical College and Hospital of 250 beds on the unused land in Khulna from the Public-Private Partnership project list.

Cabinet Division officials said the Ministry of Railways placed the proposal before the day’s meeting.

title: Syrian army tells Kurdish forces to withdraw from Aleppo city
body:
Syria’s army told Kurdish forces on Tuesday to withdraw from an area they control east of Aleppo after dislodging fighters from two neighbourhoods in the city in deadly clashes last week.

The move raises fresh concerns of further fighting between the two sides, as Syria’s Islamist government seeks to extend its authority across the country and progress stalls on integrating the Kurds’ de facto autonomous administration and forces into the central government.

In Qamishli, the main Kurdish city in the country’s northeast, thousands of people demonstrated against the Aleppo violence, some burning pictures of Syrian president Ahmed al-Sharaa, an AFP correspondent said.

Syrian state television published an army statement with a map declaring a large area east of Aleppo city a ‘closed military zone’ and said ‘all armed groups in this area must withdraw to east of the Euphrates’ River.

On Monday, Syria accused the US-backed, Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces of sending reinforcements to Deir Hafer and said it sent its own personnel there in response.

The SDF is the de facto army of the Kurds’ semi-autonomous administration and controls swathes of the country’s oil-rich north and northeast, much of which it captured during Syria’s civil war and the fight against the Islamic State group.

An AFP correspondent saw government forces transporting military reinforcements including air defence batteries and artillery towards Deir Hafer on Tuesday.

The SDF denied any build-up of its personnel around Deir Hafer.

Syria’s government took full control of Aleppo city over the weekend after taking over its Kurdish-majority Sheikh Maqsud and Ashrafiyeh neighbourhoods and evacuating fighters to Kurdish-controlled areas in the country’s northeast.

Both sides have traded blame over who started the violence last Tuesday that killed dozens and displaced tens of thousands of people.

In Qamishli, thousands of people protested against the Aleppo violence and Syrian leader Sharaa, some carrying Kurdish flags or banners in support of the SDF and its chief Mazloum Abdi.

‘Leave, Jolani!’ they shouted, referring to Sharaa by his nom de guerre as a former Islamist rebel commander, Abu Mohammed al-Jolani.

‘This government has not honoured its commitments towards any Syrians,’ said cafe owner Joudi Ali.

‘There has been bloodshed since it took power, like the Alawite and Druze massacres,’ the 29-year-old said, referring to sectarian violence last year involving the two minority communities.

Most shops were shut in Qamishli as residents adhered to a general strike.

Other protesters burned portraits of Turkish foreign minister Hakan Fidan, whose country has lauded the Syrian government’s Aleppo operation ‘against terrorist organisations’.

Turkey has long been hostile to the SDF, seeing it as an extension of the Kurdistan Workers’ Party and a major threat along its southern border.

Last year, the PKK announced an end to its armed struggle against the Turkish state and began destroying its weapons, but Ankara has insisted that the move include armed Kurdish groups in Syria.

On Tuesday, the PKK called the ‘attack on the Kurdish neighbourhoods in Aleppo’ an attempt to sabotage peace moves between it and Ankara.

A day earlier, Ankara’s ruling party called the clashes an attempt by Kurdish fighters to sabotage the efforts.

Turkey has repeatedly called for the Syrian Kurdish forces’ integration into the new government as part of a March deal between Damascus and the SDF that was supposed to have been implemented last year.

The Britain-based Syrian Observatory for Human Rights reported 45 civilians and 60 soldiers and fighters were killed from both sides in the Aleppo violence.

Aleppo civil defence official Faysal Mohammad said on Tuesday that emergency workers had pulled 50 bodies from the two Kurdish-majority neighbourhoods since the end of fighting, without saying whether they were combatants or civilians.

title: Russia strikes power plant, kills four in Ukraine
body:
Russia battered Ukraine with more than two dozen missiles and hundreds of drones early Tuesday, killing four people and pummelling another power plant, piling more pressure on Ukraine’s brittle energy system.

Moscow has pummelled Ukraine with daily drone and missile barrages in recent months, targeting energy infrastructure and cutting power and heating in the frigid height of winter.

An AFP journalist in the eastern Kharkiv region, where the four people were killed, saw firefighters battling a fire at a postal hub and rescue workers helping survivors by lamp light in freezing temperatures.

Andriy Pidnebesny, a manager at the postal facility, said he was knocked down by the blast wave and tried — but failed — to free several colleagues still alive under the rubble.

‘You never know what will happen to you. You go out to the store and you could get killed. You go to work and the same thing could happen. You could be sleeping at home and the same thing could happen,’ the 31-year-old said.

President Volodymyr Zelensky said ‘several hundred thousand’ households near Kyiv were without power after the strikes, and again called on allies to bolster his country’s air defence systems.

‘The world can respond to this Russian terror with new assistance packages for Ukraine,’ Zelensky wrote on social media.

‘Russia must come to learn that cold will not help it win the war,’ he added.

Authorities in Kyiv and the surrounding region rolled out emergency power cuts in the hours after the attack, saying freezing temperatures were complicating their work.

AFP journalists in Kyiv saw customers walking through a darkened grocery store that was running just one or two cash registers from a rumbling generator.

DTEK, Ukraine’s largest energy provider, said Russian forces had struck one of its power plants, saying it was the eighth such attack since October.

The operator did not reveal which of its plants was struck, but said Russia had attacked its power plants over 220 times since Moscow invaded Ukraine in 2022.

The Ukrainian air force said that Tuesday’s bombardment included 25 missiles and 293 drones.

The Kharkiv governor gave the death toll and added that six people were wounded in the overnight hit outside the region’s main city, also called Kharkiv.

White helmeted emergency workers could be seen clambering through the still-smoking wreckage of a building used by postal company Nova Poshta, in a video posted by the regional prosecutor’s office.

Within Ukraine’s second city, Kharkiv Mayor Igor Terekhov said a Russian long-range drone struck a medical facility for children, causing a fire. No casualties were reported.

The overnight strikes hit other regions as well, including southern city Odesa.

Residential buildings, a hospital and a kindergarten were damaged, with at least five people wounded in two waves of attacks, regional governor Sergiy Lysak said.

The Russian defence ministry acknowledged its attacks, claiming its strikes targeted Ukrainian military facilities.

Russia’s use last week of a nuclear-capable Oreshnik ballistic missile on Ukraine sparked condemnation from Kyiv’s allies, including Washington, which called it a ‘dangerous and inexplicable escalation of this war’.

Moscow on Monday said the missile hit an aviation repair factory in the Lviv region and that it was fired in response to Ukraine’s attempt to strike one of Russian president Vladimir Putin’s residences — a claim Kyiv denies and that Washington has said it does not believe happened.

Ukraine has stepped up long-range drone strikes on Russian military and energy sites in response.

Kyiv said Tuesday its forces had struck a drone manufacturing plant in the western Rostov region and the governor reported a local state of emergency there after two ‘enterprises’ were hit.

title: Mobile traders stage protest
body:
Mobile phone traders under the banner of Mobile Business Community Bangladesh formed a human chain and staged a protest at Gulistan area in the capital on Tuesday, demanding immediate release of detained traders and withdrawal of what they described as false and fabricated cases.

The demonstration began at about 11:00am and drew participation from traders of Gulistan Hall Market, Stadium Market, Underground Market, Baitul Mukarram Market, Sundarban Market, Pir-e-Amini Market and Baitul View Market.

At the protest, speakers said that at least 45 mobile phone businessmen were currently detained, while several MBCB leaders had been accused in what they claimed were baseless cases filed following recent incidents of vandalism at the Bangladesh Telecommunication Regulatory Commission Bhaban after the implementation of National Equipment Identity Register.

The traders alleged that law enforcement agencies carried out harassment and repression during operations, vandalised shops and caused financial losses, creating fear and insecurity among traders and their family members.

They also said that mobile phone shops across the country had remained shut for 13 consecutive days since the implementation of the NEIR on January 1, severely disrupting business activities nationwide.

The protesters demanded the immediate withdrawal of all false cases, unconditional release of detained businessmen and an end to harassment and repression in the name of enforcement operations.

Speakers at the rally argued that unofficial mobile phones had an established and realistic market in Bangladesh, providing livelihoods for hundreds of thousands of people, but the sector was now being unfairly targeted through arrests and legal action.

MBCB vice-president Shamim Mollah told New Age that the nationwide shutdown of mobile phone markets would continue if the cases against traders were not withdrawn.

‘The recent cases against community leaders have created fear among our family members. We are being harassed by law enforcement agencies, which will not be tolerated. If our demands are not met, we are planning bigger protests in the coming days,’ he said.

He also called for clear import guidelines for unofficial mobile phones and the removal of NOC requirements imposed on traders.

title: S Alam-linked suspicious transactions to ex-BB DG found
body:
The Bangladesh Financial Intelligence Unit has detected suspicious transactions in the bank accounts of former Bangladesh Bank deputy governor SM Moniruzzaman and companies of the S Alam Group, raising questions about possible undue benefits exchanged during his tenure at the central bank.

According to the investigation report, Moniruzzaman received Tk 2 crore on August 24, 2021 from S Alam Vegetable Oil Ltd.

The report stated that they could not determine any clear or legitimate reason for such a large transfer to the personal account of a former deputy governor of Bangladesh Bank.

The report described the flow of funds from a business group to a deputy governor as a suspicious transaction.

Moniruzzaman denied the allegations. He said that he did not provide any unethical benefits to the S Alam Group and did not receive any bribe from the group.

He claimed that the Tk 2 crore was paid for a house he sold to the group and that the payment was made through a pay order.

SM Moniruzzaman joined Bangladesh Bank as a deputy governor on December 15, 2016. Right after his joining, the S Alam Group took control of Islami Bank.

Moniruzzaman served as deputy governor until December 31, 2020.

Within a few months of leaving office, he received Tk 2 crore from S Alam. The money was transferred directly to his account through a pay order issued from an account of S Alam Vegetable Oil Ltd.

Despite having more than a hundred bank accounts in his name for years, he did not receive the money through those accounts.  Instead, he opened a new account at Islami Bank and received the funds there.

The BFIU findings showed that a pay order worth Tk 2 crore was issued in Moniruzzaman’s name on August 19, 2021 from an account of S Alam Vegetable Oil Ltd maintained with First Security Islami Bank.

The amount was later credited to his account at Islami Bank Bangladesh through the clearing system.

After retiring from Bangladesh Bank, Moniruzzaman joined SS Power Ltd, another company of the S Alam Group.

Between November 7, 2021 and November 5, 2023, he received Tk 1.38 crore as salary and Tk 25 lakh as car management expenses over 27 months period.

The BFIU has suspected that Moniruzzaman may have extended unethical and unlawful advantages to S Alam Group companies while serving at the central bank.

In return, the report suggests, he may have received the Tk 2 crore payment and later secured employment at SS Power Ltd.

Moniruzzaman also admitted his employment at SS Power Ltd.

Iftekharuzzaman, executive director of Transparency International Bangladesh (TIB), told New Age that as a senior Bangladesh Bank official, it was unethical to do job at S Alam group who was mired in controversies and owned several banks.

He also said that even if he received Tk 2 crore by selling his land, it was also unethical as a central bank officer.

He said that there could be unethical transactions for unethical benefits which draw deep investigation.

He said that BFIU should have find out such unethical transactions long before and it should be accountable for such delay in action.

The government should take measures so that such agencies can act and perform duties properly.

Beyond the Tk 2 crore transaction, the BFIU identified broader financial activities they described as unusual.

According to the findings, Moniruzzaman holds 159 bank accounts across 11 banks, including 153 fixed deposit receipts, four savings accounts and two credit cards, which investigators termed abnormal for a former deputy governor.

The agency found deposits of Tk 20.5 crore and withdrawals of Tk 18.63 crore across these accounts, with a current balance of Tk 1.86 crore.

Abnormal transactions were also detected in the bank accounts of his wife, son and daughter, where deposits of Tk 7.86 crore and withdrawals of Tk 7.55 crore were recorded.

The investigation further found that Moniruzzaman opened a bank account at Prime Bank’s Gulshan branch in March 2023, through which several crores of taka reportedly moved within a short period.

Moniruzzaman denied any suspicious transactions in his accounts or those of his family members.

title: Hanoi to overtake Dhaka as largest cotton importer: USDA
body:
Bangladesh is projected to import 8 million bales of cotton in the 2025-26 marketing year (MY26), a slight decrease from the previous year, according to the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA).

This slowdown follows five consecutive months of negative growth in the country’s readymade garment (RMG) exports. While Bangladesh has recently held the title of the world’s top cotton importer, the latest forecast suggests it may soon be overtaken by Vietnam.

According to recently published data by USDA titled ‘Cotton: World Markets and Trade’, the cotton consumption of Bangladesh is expected to remain the same at 8 million, which was forecast in December of last year.

However, the consumption forecast slightly declined from 8.1 million bales, as forecast in November and August of 2025.

USDA data showed that in MY25, Bangladesh’s cotton imports totaled 8.05 million bales, up from 7.57 million bales in MY24 and 7 million bales in MY23.

In MY25, Bangladesh was the world’s largest importer of cotton, while Brazil emerged as the largest single supplier, surpassing India, although West Africa remained the primary source region.

According to USDA data, Bangladesh imported 1.9 million bales of cotton from Brazil in MY25, accounting for approximately 25 per cent of total imports, thanks to competitive pricing, wide availability during harvest, and stable supply.

The import from India stood at 1.4 million, which was 15 per cent of the total imports, followed by 1.06 million bales from Benin (13 per cent), 616,538 bales from Cameroon (8 per cent), and about 595,902 bales from the United States and Australia, each holding 7 per cent of total imports.

In December, the USDA forecast that Vietnam might surpass Bangladesh as the largest raw cotton importer, with imports projected at 8.1 million bales in MY26.

Moreover, the RMG export trends in Bangladesh showed a negative trend for the fifth consecutive month in December of the financial year 2025-26.

During the July-December period of FY26, the RMG exports also witnessed a negative growth of 2.63 per cent $19.37 billion, down from $19.88 billion in the same period of FY25, said the Export Promotion Bureau.

During the period, Bangladeshi exporters lost ground in most major destinations, including the United States, the European Union, and nontraditional markets, amid mounting domestic and global challenges such as political tensions, weak demand, an economic slowdown, and tariff-related complications.

Moreover, textile millers in the country said that local spinning mills are in a deep crisis due to a sharp rise in low-priced yarn imports from India, threatening the existence of the country’s textile sector.

Recently, in a press conference, Bangladesh Textile Mills Association president Showkat Aziz Russell said that yarn imports from India over the last 22 months have witnessed an alarming 137 per cent surge, as Indian traders have been dumping yarn in Bangladesh at prices around 30 cents per kilogram lower.

He said that due to the import of yarn at bottom prices, nearly 50 spinning mills have shut down - investments worth Tk 500–700 crore.

He also said that the country’s spinning mills have a yarn stockpile worth about Tk12,000 crore.

Moreover, the country’s textile sector is also facing issues related to gas and energy crises and fewer government incentives.

In the USDA January data, outpacing China, Pakistan might become the third-largest importer of cotton in MY26, with imports of 5.9 million bales, while China is expected to import 5.2 million bales.

According to the USDA outlook, global production might decline by nearly 400,000 bales to 119.4 million due to smaller crops in India, the United States, Argentina, and Turkey.

However, global consumption is forecast to increase by more than 300,000 bales to 118.9 million bales.

According to the USDA, in MY26, Bangladesh’s domestic production could be approximately 155,000 bales of cotton on 46,000 hectares, accounting for less than 2 per cent of its total consumption.

title: Bangladesh in Guinness World Records
body:
Bangladesh has set a Guinness world record by flying the highest number of national flags simultaneously during a skydiving operation in Dhaka on Victory Day, December 16, last year, commemorating the country’s 54th Victory Day.

Guinness World Records has officially confirmed that Bangladesh set the record for ‘Most Flags Flown Simultaneously While Skydiving (Parachute Jump)’ by hoisting 54 national flags at the same time, the Inter Services Public Relation Directorate said in a press release on Tuesday.

‘It is indeed a great achievement by our country and it will remain in history until another country breaks the record,’ ISPR director Lieutenant Colonel Sami Ud Dowla Chowdhury said.

The record-setting event, planned and executed by the Armed Forces Division, was carried out in Dhaka by skilled skydivers from Bangladesh Armed Forces, including trained paratroopers and Bangladesh Investment Development Authority executive chairman Chowdhury Ashik Mahmud Bin Harun.

The ISPR said that the achievement was more than just a world record, calling it a reflection of the professionalism, discipline and confidence of the Bangladesh Armed Forces.

The Guinness World Records management team said that the initiative aimed at making Bangladesh’s Victory Day memorable on the international stage while showcasing national collaboration, courage, and capability through a rare and complex aerial display.

title: Try to be Mourinho and I’ll fail: Arbeloa
body:
New Real Madrid coach Alvaro Arbeloa insisted Tuesday he would be himself at the helm of the Spanish giants rather than trying to imitate Jose Mourinho.

Arbeloa, who in his playing days at Madrid was an ally of his then coach Mourinho, has drawn comparisons to the Portuguese veteran for his approach to management.

The 42-year-old former defender was appointed to replace Xabi Alonso on Monday after Real Madrid lost the Spanish Super Cup final against rivals Barcelona on Sunday.

‘I have not spoken to Jose yet. For me it was a privilege and an honour to be coached by Jose Mourinho,’ Arbeloa told a news conference.

‘I have a great relationship with him... and obviously he was someone who influenced me a lot, I carry him within me.

‘(However) I am going to be Alvaro Arbeloa, because while it’s true I am not afraid of failing, and have never been, I’m sure that if I tried to be Jose Mourinho, I would fail spectacularly.’

Mourinho, currently coaching Benfica, led Real Madrid between 2010 and 2013, winning one La Liga title.

During that era he battled against Pep Guardiola’s dominant Barcelona when the fierce rivalry between the Catalans and Real Madrid was at its most bitter.

Barca currently lead Madrid by four points at the top of La Liga and Arbeloa’s job is to revert the situation, although his first match in charge is at Albacete in the Copa del Rey last 16 on Wednesday.

Arbeloa, who was coaching Madrid’s reserve side and previously working with the club’s youth teams before he was promoted, said success is the most important thing for the record 15-time European champions.

‘This club is winning, winning, and winning again. That demand on ourselves, showing the DNA of what brought us here, that has filled our trophy cabinets (is what I want),’ continued Arbeloa.

‘When I was a player I received those values from the players in the dressing room, and for me that is the most important thing... to be able to excite the fans we have all over the world and try to leave those cabinets even more full.

‘That is my work, that is my obsession and what I will be living every day.’

Madrid did not announce how long Arbeloa’s contract as first-team coach would be.

‘What I can tell you is that I’ve been here for 20 years, at home, and I will be at Real Madrid as long as they want me here,’ added Arbeloa.

‘This is my home, that’s how I feel and that’s how it will always be.’

Striker Kylian Mbappe was absent as Arbeloa took charge of his first training session on Tuesday before the visit to face second-tier Albacete.

Mbappe made his comeback from a knee sprain as a late substitute in the Spanish Super Cup final defeat by Barcelona on Sunday, but is likely to keep working on his recovery until next Tuesday’s Champions League match against his former side Monaco.

A Real Madrid source told AFP it was ‘logical’ that Mbappe was absent from training, given his knee issue.

Former coach Alonso had admitted it was a calculated risk to involve Madrid’s top goalscorer in the match against Barca in Saudi Arabia.

Arbeloa said he had a close relationship with Alonso, a former team-mate for Madrid and the Spanish national team.

‘Everyone here knows the bond that connects me to him, the friendship that connects me to him, how much I value him, how much I love him, and I know that’s mutual, has been mutual and will continue to be mutual,’ said Arbeloa.

Alonso, replaced after less than eight months at the helm, said on social media he was leaving the club having done the best he could.

‘Things didn’t go as I would have liked,’ wrote the Basque coach on Instagram on Tuesday.

‘Coaching Real Madrid was an honour and a responsibility. I’m grateful to the club, the players and above all the fans for their confidence and support.

‘I leave respectfully, with gratitude, and the pride of having done the best I could.’

title: WC-bound batters struggling
body:
The ongoing Bangladesh Premier League was seen as an important cornerstone for the preparation of the forthcoming T20 World Cup for the Bangladesh national team, as they don’t have any series prior to the marquee event.

While the participation in the tournament remains uncertain for the Litton Das-led team, Bangladesh also have the concern regarding their batting, as most of the batters included in the squad are struggling.

After the squad was announced, the lack of recognised middle-order batters was evident again. The national selection panel imposed their trust upon the batters playing for the team in recent times despite some of them being out of position.

Captain Litton has got starts in most of his matches for Rangpur Riders so far but has thrown away his wickets. He reached double figures in seven out of eight innings but is yet to reach fifty.

While his strike rate hovers at 135, Litton has been averaging 20.25. His team, Rangpur, has also been struggling.

Litton’s deputy, Saif Hassan, has been experiencing tougher times. He has accumulated only 48 runs in seven innings, while his last two innings have been ducks.

If Dhaka Capitals can’t make it to the play-off, Saif will only have two more innings before the World Cup.

Parvez Hossain, however, has been shining brightly for Sylhet Titans. He was experimented at four for the first five matches before coming to open the innings.

The left-hander left his mark at both, as he has struck three fifties so far, while averaging 41.14. As Sylhet has already booked their place, more fireworks can be expected from the southpaw.

Parvez’s potential opening partner in the national team, Tanzid Hasan, has struck a 76 in the last match of the Sylhet phase for the Rajshahi Warriors.

However, before that, he had had a moderate outing, as his first seven innings yielded only 90 runs.

Tawhid Hridoy, who is in a sense the only recognised middle-order batter in the squad, has been having an inconsistent tournament despite having played two innings of 53 and 97*. However, his highest score came while opening for Rangpur.

In his remaining six innings, Hridoy got out even before reaching seven runs on four occasions.

Shamim Hossain played a splendid unbeaten 81-run innings for Sylhet Titans in a losing cause. But other than that, he couldn’t make headlines. But on the brighter side, Dhaka has been playing him at six or seven—his usual role as a finisher.

Nurul Hasan, who is captaining Rangpur, has got few opportunities due to a heavy batting line-up.

He remained unbeaten on three occasions out of his six innings but is yet to reach double figures.

Mahedi Hasan, one of the all-rounders in the squad, has been contributing with the bat while leading the Chattogram Royals. Mohammad Saifuddin has also shown some sparks for Dhaka Capitals.

title: Trump urges Iranians to oust rulers, says ‘help’ on its way
body:
US President Donald Trump on Tuesday said Iranians should continue nationwide protests and take over the country’s institutions as authorities there cracked down on mass demonstrations.

‘Iranian Patriots, KEEP PROTESTING - TAKE OVER YOUR INSTITUTIONS!!!’ Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform.

‘Save the names of the killers and abusers. They will pay a big price.

‘I have cancelled all meetings with Iranian Officials until the senseless killing of protesters STOPS. HELP IS ON ITS WAY.’

Trump, who has repeatedly threatened Iran with military intervention, signed off with ‘MIGA’ -- ‘Make Iran Great Again.’

The president did not specify what form the promised ‘help’ would take, in a message that appeared to back toppling the government in the Islamic Republic -- marking a change in the US stance from one day ago.

On Monday, his Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt told reporters that a channel for diplomacy with Tehran remained open, saying that Iran was taking a ‘far different tone’ in private discussions with Trump’s special envoy Steve Witkoff.

Trump on Monday also announced a 25-percent tariff on any country doing business with Iran, ramping up pressure as a rights group estimated the crackdown has killed at least 648 people.

Iranian authorities insist they have regained control after successive nights of mass protests that have posed one of the biggest challenges to the clerical leadership since the 1979 Islamic revolution ousted the shah.

But rights groups accuse the government of using live fire against protesters and masking the scale of the crackdown with an internet blackout that has now lasted more than four days.

title: SC describes HC verdict on NU recruitment as an act of ‘judicial tyranny’
body:
The Appellate Division has finally ended a two-decade legal saga involving the service status of 988 National University employees appointed between 2003 and 2004 under the BNP-led alliance government.

The full verdict was delivered by a seven-member bench headed by chief justice Syed Refaat Ahmed. The judgment, written by Justice Zubayer Rahman Chowdhury—now the chief justice—was briefly announced on May 27 and later on January 13, 2026 published on the Supreme Court website.

In its verdict, the Appellate Division declared the terminations illegal and described the earlier handling of the case as an act of ‘judicial tyranny’.

Over the years, the case produced seven different verdicts, exposing judicial inconsistency and leaving hundreds of employees in prolonged uncertainty.

The National University syndicate had repeatedly changed its decisions on their appointments with changes in governments and vice-chancellors.

In 2006, the High Court Division declared the appointments lawful after hearing a public interest litigation filed by former deputy speaker Fazle Rabbi Miah.

Four years later, in 2011, the High Court reversed its position by allowing a review petition filed in 2010 by a third party, former liberation war affairs minister AKM Mozzammel Hossain, and declared the appointments illegal.

On appeal, the Appellate Division scrapped both the 2006 and 2011 verdicts and sent the case back to the High Court Division for rehearing.

After rehearing, the High Court Division in 2012 issued a fresh verdict, which led to the termination of 988 officers and employees of the National University.

The dismissed employees challenged the decision, but in 2016 the Appellate Division upheld the terminations, leaving them without jobs and without effective legal remedy.

Some of the dismissed employees later sought review of the 2016 verdict, but their petitions were rejected.

Eight years later, after Sheikh Hasina was deposed through student-led mass uprising in August 2024, the Appellate Division revisited the matter in a review petition filed by the National University following a syndicate decision taken on September 5, 2024.

The court observed that the matter should have ended with the High Court judgment delivered on August 22, 2006, as neither the petitioner nor the National University had appealed against it.

It noted with ‘anxiety and sorrow’ that some of the affected employees had died while the case remained pending for years.

The court held that the reopening of the case had severely affected not only the careers but also the livelihoods of the employees and their families.

The Appellate Division ordered the reinstatement of all affected employees with their respective seniority, directing that the period they remained out of service be treated as extraordinary leave.

According to sources at the university’s registry office, the reinstated employees rejoined their posts on June 1, 2025, following a syndicate decision taken on May 30.

title: Court attaches ex-MP Momtaz’s properties
body:
A Dhaka court on Tuesday ordered the attachment of the house and lands owned by former member of parliament Momtaz Begum and her associates.

Dhaka metropolitan senior special judge Md Sabbir Faiz passed the order, allowing a plea of the Anti-Corruption Commission.

The properties include a five-storey building with five kathas of land in Mohakhali, Dhaka, registered in the name of Momtaz Begum; a four-storey building with five decimals of land in Manikganj Sadar; a two-storey building with 21 decimals of land in Singair, Manikganj, and another two-storey building measuring 1,312 square feet in the same area; nine kathas of land in Purbachal New Town; 12 decimals of land in Manikganj; and 412 decimals of agricultural land in Singair police station area of Manikganj district.

The ACC plea said that an investigation team has been formed to probe allegations of money laundering against Momtaz Begum and other individuals and institutions linked to her interests. As the investigation against Momtaz Begum is ongoing, the application said it is imperative to freeze bank accounts and movable assets and to attach the immovable properties.

title: 53 nominations reinstated, 17 rejected in 4th-day appeal hearing
body:
The Election Commission on the fourth day of appeal hearings against returning officers’ decisions for the 13th Jatiya Sangsad elections on Tuesday reinstated 53 nominations and cancelled 17.

On the day, the Election Commission heard 68 appeals against returning officers’ decisions to cancel nominations while two appeals seeking the cancellation of valid candidates were heard.

The hearings, held between 10:00am and 5:00pm at the EC auditorium in the capital’s Agargaon, involved candidates, along with their representatives, who had challenged the cancellation of their nominations.

The appeal process is scheduled to continue until January 18.

Over the past four days, the Election Commission heard a total of 278 appeals against returning officers’ decisions on nominations for the Jatiya Sangsad elections.

Of these, 203 nominations were reinstated while 64 were cancelled.

The Election Commission received a total of 645 appeals challenging the returning officers’ scrutiny of nomination papers for the parliamentary elections.

The EC began accepting appeals on January 5 and closed the process on January 9.

Earlier, during the five-day nomination paper scrutiny between December 30 and January 4, the 69 returning officers – two divisional commissioners, 64 deputy commissioners, and three regional election commissioners – declared that the nominations of 1,842 candidates were valid while those of 723 were invalid.

A total of 2,568 aspirants submitted nomination papers for the country’s 300 constituencies by the December 29 deadline to contest the parliamentary elections.

The election commission on December 11 announced the election schedule to hold the JS elections and the referendum on the July National Charter (Constitutional Reform) Implementation Order simultaneously on February 12.

title: July Oikya urges EC to cancel nominations of JP, NDF candidates
body:
A group of protesters under the banner of July Oikya on Tuesday submitted a memorandum to the Election Commission, demanding the cancellation of nomination papers filed by the candidates of the Jatiya Party and the National Democratic Front in the upcoming national election scheduled for February 12.

The group also called for the rejection of nomination papers submitted by the candidates of 14 political parties aligned with the Awami League, who are contesting the 13th parliamentary elections alongside the JP and the NDF.

The National Democratic Front, a newly formed political alliance, is led by a faction of the Jatiya Party led by Anisul Islam Mahmud and another faction of the Jatiya Party is led by Anwar Hossain Manju.

Anisul Islam Mahmud serves as the president of the alliance, while Anwar Hossain Manju is its chief adviser.

In the memorandum, July Oikya alleged that the Jatiya Party led by GM Quader had fielded candidates for 244 constituencies and accused the party of supporting the Awami League in the establishment of authoritarian rule.

The group claimed that both the Jatiya Party and the 14-party alliance had backed enforced disappearances, killings and other serious abuses over the past 16 years.

Earlier in the day, the protesters began gathering beneath the Agargaon Metro Rail Station at about 12:30pm before marching towards the Election Commission.

The police erected barricades outside the Election Commission and deployed additional personnel.

The procession was halted near the Islamic Foundation, as demonstrators chanted slogans against the participation of the Jatiya Party in the election.

title: What Buyers Should Know Before Purchasing a Car Online
body:
Buying a car online has become an increasingly common option for modern buyers. With access to detailed specifications, reviews, comparisons, and digital tools, many people now begin and sometimes complete — their car-buying journey without visiting multiple dealerships. While this shift offers convenience and transparency, purchasing a car online still requires careful consideration and due diligence.

Understanding what to look for before committing to an online purchase can help buyers avoid common pitfalls and make more informed decisions.

Before exploring any online platform, buyers should first define their own needs and requirements. This includes identifying the type of vehicle that suits their lifestyle, budget constraints, and long-term usage plans.

Clear priorities make it easier to navigate online listings and avoid confusion caused by the wide range of available options.

One of the biggest advantages of buying a car online is access to comprehensive information. Buyers can compare models, variants, engine options, and feature lists in detail before shortlisting their preferred options.

It is important to look beyond headline specifications. Variant-level differences can significantly impact the ownership experience, particularly in areas such as safety features, transmission options, infotainment systems, and convenience equipment.

Many buyers use online car-buying platforms, such asACKO Drive, which primarily function as end-to-end digital car-purchasing platforms, offering expert guidance through detailed reviews, comparisons, and variant-level insights. By combining car discovery tools with professional evaluations, such platforms help buyers understand specifications, pricing structures, and feature differences more clearly before making a purchase decision.

Cross-checking information across multiple sources further improves accuracy and confidence.

Pricing is often a key motivation for researching cars online. Digital platforms typically present on-road prices, variant-wise costs, and available offers in a structured manner.

However, buyers should always verify what is included in the displayed price. Registration charges, road tax, insurance, extended warranties, and optional accessories can significantly affect the final on-road cost.

Comparing prices across platforms and locations helps buyers identify discrepancies and understand broader market trends. Transparent pricing allows for better financial planning and reduces the risk of unexpected expenses later in the process.

Online reviews play a crucial role in the modern car-buying process. Expert reviews offer insights into driving behaviour, comfort, safety, and overall usability, while owner feedback highlights real-world reliability and maintenance considerations.

A balanced view formed from both expert analysis and owner experiences leads to better-informed decisions.

Not all online car-buying journeys are the same. Some platforms focus mainly on research and discovery, while others support booking, documentation, and delivery coordination.

Understanding these steps in advance helps ensure a smoother transition from online research to vehicle ownership.

Buying a car online does not remove the need for physical service centres. Routine servicing, warranty repairs, and emergency support still depend on authorised networks.

Evaluating after-sales support ensures that ownership remains convenient well beyond the initial purchase.

Online platforms may also display finance options, but buyers should review these carefully. Interest rates, loan tenure and monthly installments vary between providers.

Careful evaluation helps avoid long-term financial complications.

The ease of browsing cars online can sometimes lead to impulsive decisions. Limited-time offers, highlighted deals, or attractive visuals may influence buyers prematurely.

A considered approach often leads to more satisfying ownership outcomes.

Online car buying offers unmatched convenience, but it should not replace due diligence. Test drives, where possible, remain valuable for assessing seating comfort, driving position, and real-world performance.

Combining digital research with offline validation helps buyers feel confident about their final choice.

Purchasing a car online can be a smooth and rewarding experience when approached thoughtfully. By clearly defining requirements, researching models and pricing carefully, understanding the buying process, and evaluating after-sales considerations, buyers can make informed decisions with greater confidence.

Online car-buying platforms, including ACKO Drive, form part of a broader digital ecosystem that supports informed decision-making by combining purchasing tools with expert reviews and comparisons. Ultimately, the responsibility lies with buyers to evaluate information critically and proceed at a pace that feels right for them.

With the right preparation, buying a car online can provide clarity, control, and confidence throughout the entire process.

title: Salah and Mane meet again with AFCON final place on the line
body:
Three years after they last appeared together, Sadio Mane and Mohamed Salah meet again on Wednesday on opposing sides as Senegal and Egypt clash for a place in the Africa Cup of Nations final.

The last-four showdown in the Moroccan city of Tangiers will be the first time the former Liverpool teammates have shared a pitch since the Anfield club lost to Real Madrid in the Champions League final in May 2022.

Shortly after that, Mane left for Bayern Munich before moving to Al-Nassr in the Saudi Pro League a year later.

Salah, meanwhile, has been heavily linked with a move to Saudi Arabia in the near future but remains for now at Liverpool despite falling out of favour with coach Arne Slot before coming to the Cup of Nations.

The Egypt captain is a man on a mission in Morocco, having scored four goals in four appearances on the Pharaoh's run to the semi-finals as he targets winning AFCON for the first time.

Salah, who turns 34 in June, is running out of time to win a major international honour with his country having suffered the agony of two final defeats in the competition.

After being part of the Egypt side beaten by Cameroon in the 2017 final in Gabon, Salah skippered the team beaten on penalties by Senegal in 2022 in Yaounde.

Mane had a penalty saved in normal time on that dramatic night at the Olembe Stadium, but recovered to score the decisive kick in the shoot-out as Senegal became African champions for the first time.

Salah was due to take Egypt's next penalty but would not get the chance to step up and was already on the verge of tears as Mane prepared to strike the decisive blow.

Less than two months later, the teams met again in a decisive World Cup qualifying play-off and once more penalties were needed -- Salah missed, Mane scored and Senegal won.

They went on to reach the last 16 in Qatar while Egypt failed to qualify for the first World Cup held in the Arab world.

Both have qualified for the upcoming tournament in North America, providing what will perhaps be a last chance for the two veterans to star on the biggest stage of all.For now, however, it is all about continental supremacy as Senegal chase a third final in four editions of AFCON, and Egypt aim to take a step closer to a record-extending eighth title overall.

Mane, who also turns 34 this year, will feel less pressure having already collected a Cup of Nations winner's medal.

‘Nobody, even in Egypt, wants to win this trophy more than me,’ admitted Salah after helping his team beat Ivory Coast in the quarter-finals.

‘I have won almost every prize. This is the title I am waiting for.’

The pair played together under Jurgen Klopp for five years between Salah arriving from Roma in 2017 and Mane's departure.

They formed a formidable front line along with Roberto Firmino and together won the Champions League in 2019 and the Premier League in 2020 -- there were also two defeats to Real in Champions League finals.

But Mane recently admitted that sometimes the pair found it difficult to get along on the pitch.

‘I think Mo is first of all a very nice guy. I think though inside the pitch, sometimes he would pass to me and sometimes he wouldn't,’ Mane said on the Rio Ferdinand Presents podcast.

‘Only Bobby (Firmino) was there to share the balls. Sometimes it was like this,’ he added with a laugh.

‘I still remember one game when I was really, really angry because he doesn't pass me the ball.’

This time they really are on opposing sides, as two former African footballers of the year look to lead their countries to glory -- for the second time, in Mane's case.

‘The pressure for me is over. Before I won the African Cup, sometimes I played badly because of the pressure,’ Mane, who has one goal at this AFCON, admitted on the same podcast.

‘All that on your shoulders is not easy,’ he added, and Salah is well aware of that.

title: Five Chinese nationals among eight arrested over online fraud
body:
The Detective Branch of the police has arrested eight people, including five Chinese nationals, in separate raids in the capital over money allegedly siphoned off through online fraud.

Meanwhile, 51,251 SIM cards, 51 mobile phones and 21 Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP) gateway devices used in cybercrime operations were seized from the arrested.

The arrestees are Chen Ling Feng, Zeng Cong, Zeng Changqiang, Wen Xian Qiu, Huang Zheng Xiang, Md Zakaria, Niaz Masum, and Kamrul Hasan Joy.

DB deputy commissioner for cyber north Hasan Mohammad Naser Rikabder confirmed the arrests at a press briefing at the Dhaka Metropolitan Police’s media centre on Minto Road on Tuesday.

He said that the arrests were made during week-long drives in Bashundhara Residential Area and areas under Uttara West police station.

Niaz and Kamrul were arrested on January 7 during a raid in Bashundhara Residential Area under the Bhatara police.

Based on further information about other active online fraud rings in the capital, another raid was conducted in Sector 9 under the Uttara West police on January 12, leading to the arrest of six people, including five Chinese nationals.

Preliminary investigation suggests that the fraudulent gang used Telegram, WhatsApp and other social media apps to lure people with fake job offers, high-return investment schemes, low-priced products, and ‘work from home’ advertisements, DC Naser said.

Money swindled from victims was later converted into crypto currency and transferred abroad through VoIP gateway machines, the DB official said.

Regarding the arrival and visa status of the Chinese nationals, he said that their passports were being verified.

‘Digital devices seized from them were reportedly found using Chinese software applications,’ he added.

DC Naser further warned the public against making financial transactions through unknown bKash or other mobile financial service accounts.

title: United reach deal to appoint Carrick as interim boss: reports
body:
Manchester United have reached an agreement in principle to appoint Michael Carrick as interim manager until the end of the season, reports said Tuesday.

The former midfielder was pictured arriving at the club's Carrington training ground, with his appointment likely to be confirmed later in the day.

Carrick previously had an unbeaten three-game stint as caretaker boss at Old Trafford in 2021.

The 44-year-old, who won 12 major trophies in his 12-year playing career at United, was appointed manager of Middlesbrough in October 2022.

Carrick guided Middlesbrough to the Championship play-offs in his first season in charge but was dismissed in June after the club finished 10th in the second tier.
