But those trophy-filled years seem a lifetime ago for Fletcher and the furious fans who filled the air with boos throughout the 2-1 loss against Brighton.

United’s first FA Cup third round defeat since 2014 underscored the litany of problems scarring the club at present.

For now, United’s hierarchy plan to hire an interim boss until the end of the season, buying them time to search for Amorim’s permanent successor.

Former United manager Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, who failed in his first spell in charge, and Michael Carrick, a decorated ex-United midfielder sacked by second tier Middlesbrough this season, have been linked with the temporary post.

Few have faith that United will hire the right manager after Amorim lasted just 14 turbulent months following the equally chaotic reign of Erik ten Hag, who was axed in 2024.

United supporters gave their verdict on the shambolic state of their club by chanting against co-owners Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazer family throughout the Brighton defeat.

And with tricky games against Manchester City and Premier League leaders Arsenal next for United, the atmosphere could be even more toxic by the time they host Fulham on February 1, when the ‘1958 Group’ plan a demonstration against the ownership.

United face a 40-game season, their lowest number of matches in a single campaign since before the First World War.

Three points adrift of the Premier League’s top four, with fifth place likely to bring qualification for next season’s Champions League, they can still salvage a modicum of respect by returning to Europe’s elite club competition.

But Fletcher acknowledged the lack of belief in the dressing room at present is a hinderance to United’s hopes of getting back on track.

‘You could see the players are fragile but they’ve got to respond. Confidence is one of the most powerful things in football so when you don’t have it, you have to dig deep and then the confidence comes back,’ he said.

‘It’s over to them, they need to make sure that they have got a lot to play for this season. This team is still good enough to achieve success this season but they have to dig deep.’

United defender Diogo Dalot confirmed Fletcher’s feeling that the club’s turmoil has affected the team’s morale.

‘It’s really difficult,’ Dalot said. ‘It’s always a period that you have to find ways to solve problems really quickly.

‘Overall very disappointed because we wanted to go through. We have to adapt and go again.’

Despite the funereal atmosphere at the final whistle, Fletcher insisted United fans will get behind the players if they show more spirit.

‘Out of cups, only Premier League games to play for, the fans weren’t happy at the end but they have got every right to air their grievances. It wasn’t toxic but they showed their disappointment,’ he said.

‘I’m sure if the payers show the right reaction, the fans will get behind them like they always do because there is still a lot to play for in the Premier League this season.’

United are four games without a win and have tasted victory just once in their last seven games.

Fletcher may not be in charge by the time bitter rivals City visit Old Trafford on Saturday, but he knows a rough road lies ahead for whoever replaces him.

‘They’ve just got to come together. It’s only them in the situation and only them that can do something about it. It might not be pretty at times,’ he said.

title: Flick hails ‘unbelievable’ Raphinha
body:
Barcelona coach Hansi Flick commended Raphinha’s mindset after the forward struck twice to help his team beat Real Madrid and retain the Spanish Super Cup on Sunday.

The Brazilian winger has seven goals in his last five matches, including a brace in the 3-2 win over Los Blancos in Saudi Arabia.

Raphinha was out injured for around two months as Barca’s form dipped in October and November, but has come back strongly.

‘His mentality is unbelievable, his dynamic affects the whole team,’ Flick told reporters.

Raphinha missed a fine chance in the first half but almost immediately fired Barca into the lead in Jeddah. Then with the score tied at 2-2, the 29-year-old struck the winner from outside the area, with the help of a deflection.

‘He missed the first chance but the second one, he was there and (scored) the first goal, and it gave the team more confidence,’ continued Flick.

‘This is what Raphinha brings on the pitch, it’s a lot of intensity and we need this.’

Barca won the Spanish Super Cup against Real Madrid last season on their way to claiming a domestic treble.

Flick said he hoped the victory would help the La Liga leaders achieve their other ambitions this season.

‘We are in a good mood, we have a lot of confidence now,’ said Flick, after Barca’s 10th consecutive victory across all competitions.

‘This final was very important for us because against Real Madrid it’s always something special. Again we won a final, and this is fantastic.’

Flick has won all eight finals he has competed in as a coach, including two last season against Madrid.

‘When we are focused, we concentrate and play like we did today, I have a really good feeling with the team, because it’s important,’ added Flick.

The coach brought on defender Ronald Araujo in the final stages, after the Uruguayan took a mental health break of around a month.

‘To be on the pitch and to win this title means a lot for him,’ said Flick.

‘I’m really happy that he’s back, and happy that it seems like it’s okay -- we will support him always.’

title: Rajshahi, Chattogram, Sylhet book play-off
body:
Abdul Gaffar Saqlain’s four-for before Tanzid Hasan’s 76 set up a comprehensive seven-wicket win for Rajshahi Warriors over Dhaka Capitals in the last match of the Sylhet phase in the ongoing BPL at the Sylhet International Stadium on Monday.

The win put Rajshahi at the top of the table and ensured their place in the play-off. Rajshahi’s win also confirmed Sylhet Titans and Chattogram Royals play-off places.

Dhaka were restricted to 131 in 20 overs as Ripon Mondol claimed a hat-trick. Rajshahi then cruised past the total in 16.1 overs as Tanzid made 76 off 43 balls.

While Ripon’s hat-trick—the third by any bowler this season after Mehedi Hasan Rana and Mrittunjoy Chowdhury—came in the last over of the innings, Dhaka were strangled in the middle phase of their innings after being asked to bat first.

They made a rapid start as Usman Khan hit 41 off 27 with five fours and two sixes as his opening partnership with Abdullah Al Mamun added 54 runs.

However, once Saqlain made the breakthrough by dismissing Usman, Dhaka were under pressure as they lost two more wickets quickly.

They never recovered from that, as only 51 runs were added in the middle overs. Nasir Hossain (24) and Sabbir Rahman (14) contributed, but that wasn’t enough for them. They lost five more wickets in the death overs.

Ripon dismissed Sabbir, Ziaur Rahman, and Taijul Islam in the last three balls of the innings to complete his hat-trick, while Saqlain finished with a figure of 4-24.  Md Rubel also took 2-22 for Rajshahi.

Chasing a moderate total, Rajshahi made a strong start thanks to Muhammad Waseem’s 22 off 13. Tanzid then took on the baton to steer their chase.

The left-handed batter reached his fifty in 29 balls while hitting seven fours and five sixes in his innings.

Mushfiqur Rahim and James Neesham remained unbeaten on 12 and 14, respectively, when Rajshahi ensured their victory.

title: Rangpur suffer 3rd straight defeat
body:
Parvez Hossain Emon’s 52 off 41 and Nasum Ahmed’s 3-19 led Sylhet Titans to a six-wicket win over Rangpur Riders in the ongoing Bangladesh Premier League at the Sylhet International Stadium on Monday.

Bowlers restricted Rangpur to 114 after being asked to bat first, and then Parvez hit an unbeaten fifty to guide Sylhet to 119-4 with 15 balls in hand, with Rangpur suffering their third straight defeat.

With this win, Sylhet boosted their top four chances, having 10 points in nine games, but captain Mehidy Hasan Miraz set his sights on a top two finish.

‘Rangpur is a very good team. We still have one game to go; we will qualify, but we are looking for the top two. Bowlers bowled brilliantly. Emon has been a brilliant talent. He had to bat at number four, but he loves opening the batting,’ said Mehidy after the match.

Tawhid Hridoy came to open the innings for Rangpur again but failed to replicate against Sylhet spinners, who were introduced early in the game.

Moeen Ali started with a maiden, while Nasum made the breakthrough by dismissing Mayers for a duck in the second over, while Hridoy was trapped lbw for four by pacer Shohidul Islam.

Litton Das also fell for just 22 runs off 12 balls, having been bowled by Shohidul.

The Pakistan duo Khushdil Shah and Iftikhar then formed a 40-run stand for a brief reprieve until Moeen removed Iftikhar for 17 to take control.

Khusdil’s run out after 30 off 24 enticed another collapse, as there was no other batter to put on a significant score except Mahmudullah, who contributed 29 off 23.

Apart from Nasum, Shohidul returned with 3-36, while Moeen took 2-8.

Chasing the target, Sylhet openers made a flying start with a 54-run stand between Parvez and Tawfique Khan, who scored 33 off 22.

Sylhet slowed a bit in the middle after losing Ariful Islam for 21 and Afif Hossain for 12, but Parvez, who hit three fours and three sixes in his match-winning knock, ensured their victory for Rangpur, who jumped to second spot.

In the post-match conference, Rangpur coach Mickey Arthur expressed disappointment and urged the players to make a strong comeback.

‘Yeah, we’ve we’ve been poor. We haven’t played well enough, and that’s why we’ve lost. The thing that’s disappointed me was the lack of actual basics and understanding of situations,’ he said.

‘You need somebody in your top three or four to get a big score. And that’s particularly the condition. Confidence is a big thing. You know, after five games, we were flying, and everybody was upbeat. You lose a couple of games and you’re put under pressure, and you’ve got to find a way to counter that and win,’ Arther added.

title: Two Ansar members detained over Manikganj Hospital rape
body:
Two members of the Bangladesh Ansar have been detained allegedly for raping a girl at Manikganj 250-bed General Hospital.

The detainees are Shahadat Hossain and Abu Sayeed who were on duty at the hospital’s main gate.

Manikganj superintendent of police Mohammad Sarwar Alam said that the victim and her husband who was a driver of a battery-run van were traveling from Narayanganj to their relatives in Manikganj on his van.

While they were on the way to their relatives’ home at Betila in Manikganj sadar upazila, the van’s battery ran out of charge near the Manikganj bus stand at about 2:00am on Monday.

Seeking safety, the couple went to Manikganj 250-bed General Hospital where the accused Ansar members assured the couple of assistance and took them inside the hospital, said Sarwar.

The Ansar members then left the husband on the ground floor and took the victim on the first floor of the hospital’s newly constructed building, where they allegedly raped her after intimidating her.

Escaping from the hospital, the couple informed the police of the incident following which the police summoned all the Ansar members on duty at the hospital to the police station where the victim identified the two accused, Manikganj police super Sarwar Alam said.

Manikganj sadar police officer-in-charge Ikram Hossain said, ‘The victim is a minor girl and her mother has already reached the police station to file a case.’

The accused were in police custody and further legal proceedings would be taken after the case was filed, said the OC at about 10:00pm Monday.

Bangladesh Ansar and Village Defence Party district commandant Kamruzzaman said that the two accused Ansar members were suspended and a two-member investigation committee, headed by upazila Ansar and VDP officer Shamima Akhter, had been formed.

He also stated that the crime was the personal responsibility of the accused and the force would not take responsibility for the accused’s criminal actions.

The hospital’s superintendent Mohammad Bahauddin said that the victim was receiving treatment at the hospital.

title: Ikhtiar Uddin Mohammad Mamun appointed new head of BFIU
body:
Bangladesh interim government has appointed National Board of Revenue tax commissioner Ikhtiar Uddin Mohammad Mamun as the new head of the Bangladesh Financial Intelligence Unit.

Finance ministry Financial Institutions Division on Monday issued a formal notification regarding this appointment.

According to the gazette, Mamun will hold the rank and status equivalent to a deputy governor of Bangladesh Bank.

The appointment has been made on a contractual basis for a duration of two years, effective from the date he joins the office.

The notification specified that the appointment is grounded in Section 24(1)(gh) of the Money Laundering Prevention Act, 2012 (amended in 2015) and Rule 22 of the Money Laundering Prevention Rules, 2019.

As a condition of this high-profile role, Mamun is required to sever all existing work-related ties and relationships with other institutions and organisations.

The terms and conditions of this contractual service will be finalised through an approved agreement. The order has been issued in the public interest and is set to take effect immediately.

Earlier, Shahinul Islam served as the head of the BFIU, but the government cancelled his appointment in September last year after a controversial video spread on social media.

The BFIU works as the country’s main financial intelligence agency, monitoring suspicious transactions by banks and financial institutions and helping prevent money laundering.

title: Housewife murdered in Kurigram, husband missing
body:
The police on Monday morning recovered the body of the housewife who was hacked to death in Kurigram on Sunday night.

The husband who was with the victim that night has been missing since the incident.

Babul and Mahima, a couple, slept in the same room at Digdari Baniyarvita village at Bhitarband union of Nageshwari upazila of Kurigram district on Sunday night. Villagers found the body of Mahima, but Babul is missing.

Kafil Mia, a villager, said that after hearing the news of the death, he rushed to the victim’s house and saw Babul’s wife Mahima lying dead with injury marks on her body.

However, if Babul is found, the real reason for the death will be known, he said.

Bhitarband union parishad chairman Shafiul Alam Shafi said that Babul was a fish trader. Babul and Mahima have two sons and one daughter, he said.

Mehedi, the second son of the deceased, said that he could not find his father and his phone was also switched off. ‘We were asleep and did not understand how and what happened,’ he said.

Nageshwari police station officer-in-charge Abdullah Heel Zaman said that the body was sent to Kurigram General Hospital morgue for autopsy.

The preparations are going on to file a murder case in this regard and the accused will be arrested soon, he said.

‘The deceased’s husband Babul is mysteriously missing. If he can be caught, it will be possible to solve the mystery of the incident,’ the police official added.

title: New US ambassador Brent T Christensen arrives in Dhaka
body:
United States ambassador-designate to Bangladesh Brent T Christensen along with his wife, Deanne Dao, arrived in Dhaka on Monday.

‘It is an honour for me to serve the United States as the 19th ambassador to Bangladesh. I look forward to strengthening the ties between our two countries to advance peace and prosperity in the region. My wife and I are thrilled to return to a country that holds many fond memories for us,’ Brent T Christensen said in a statement shared by the US embassy in Dhaka on his arrival.

Brent T Christensen was confirmed by the Senate as ambassador to the People’s Republic of Bangladesh on December 18, 2025.

Ambassador Christensen served most recently as the senior official performing the duties of under secretary of state for Arms Control and International Security in January–October 2025, according to a release of the US embassy.

In this role, he oversaw the Department of State’s global efforts on security cooperation, security assistance, counterterrorism, counternarcotics, and nonproliferation, it added.

A career member of the Senior Foreign Service, Christensen previously served as the foreign policy adviser to the Commander of United States Strategic Command and as counsellor for political and economic affairs at the US Embassy in Dhaka. Christensen has held additional assignments overseas in the US missions to the Philippines, El Salvador, and Vietnam.

His other domestic roles include serving as deputy director at the Office of Regional Security and Arms Transfers, Bureau of Political-Military Affairs, as special assistant to the Special Representative for North Korea Policy, as a fellow on the US House of Representatives Committee on Foreign Affairs, and as Bangladesh country officer in the Bureau of South and Central Asian Affairs, said the release.

Christensen also served as one of two career foreign service members of the Foreign Service Impasses Disputes Panel, part of the US Federal Labor Relations Authority.

A distinguished graduate of the National War College, Christensen earned a Master of Science in National Security Strategy.

Christensen likewise holds a Master of Science in Statistics from Texas A&M University and a Bachelor of Arts in Economics and Managerial Studies from Rice University.

Before joining the Foreign Service in 2002, he worked as a management consultant in Houston and New York City.

title: Bangladesh considering joining ISF for Gaza: CA press secy
body:
Bangladesh interim government chief adviser’s press secretary Shafiqul Alam on Monday said that the government recognised the significance of the UN Security Council decision to establish the international stabilization force for Gaza and is carefully considering the matter of joining the force.

‘We recognise the significance of the UN Security Council decision to establish the ISF and understand that some Muslim countries are interested in participating in the force. We are also carefully considering the matter,’ he told BSS regarding the Bangladesh’s stance in joining the ISF.

As one of the largest contributors to UN peacekeeping forces and an ardent supporter of the Palestinian cause, the press secretary said, ‘Our interest in participating in the ISF is contingent on the fulfillment of a number of principles’.

These include, among others, that the ISF should be temporary and operate under a clear UN Security Council mandate; that there must be permanent ceasefire and complete withdrawal of all Israeli forces from Gaza; and that the responsibities for Gaza will be transferred to the Palestinians, he added.

‘We note that the United Nations Security Council, on 17th November 2025, adopted resolution 2803 which provided for, among other things, the establishment of an international stabilization force (ISF) for Gaza,’ the press secretary said, adding, all Muslim countries members of the Security Council voted for the resolution.

A number of other Arab and Muslim countries jointly recommended the adoption of the resolution by the Security Council, he added.

‘We remain steadfast in our support for the right of the Palestinians to self determination and the establishment of a sovereign Palestinian State based on 1967 borders with Al Quds Al Sharif as its capital,’ Shafiqul Alam said.

As the third largest Muslim nation in the world, he said, Bangladesh has consistently condemned Israeli genocide in Gaza, and called for its immediate end and the complete withdrawal of all Israeli forces from the territory.

title: JU celebrates 55th founding anniversary
body:
Jahangirnagar University celebrated its 55th founding anniversary on Monday, blending festive events with reflection on the institution’s legacy since its establishment in 1971.

The celebrations were inaugurated in the morning when vice-chancellor professor Mohammad Kamrul Ahsan hoisted the national flag and addressed a gathering at the Mritmancha near the old arts building.

Pro-vice-chancellor for academic affairs, professor Mohammad Mahfuzur Rahman raised the university flag, followed by the release of doves and colourful balloons to symbolise peace.

In his address, Kamrul Ahsan congratulated current and former students, teachers, officers and staff, urging the campus community to uphold ethics alongside the pursuit of knowledge.

He said that the university’s students played a leading role during the 2024 uprising and stressed that the post-2024 period demanded renewed commitment to moral values.

‘Not only the acquisition of knowledge, but the practice of ethics must be upheld’, he said, warning that the cost of moral failure could once again be paid in lives.

Pro-vice-chancellor for administrative affairs Professor Sohel Ahmed, treasurer Md Abdur Rob, registrar ABM Azizur Rahman and other officials attended the event.

A colourful procession led by the vice-chancellor later marched through the campus and ended at the Selim Al Deen Muktamancha, where participants observed a minute’s silence in memory of martyrs of the Language Movement, the 1971 Liberation War, later mass movements and the late former prime minister Begum Khaleda Zia.

Cultural performances, blood group testing, reminiscence sessions, puppet shows and friendly football and handball matches between current and former students were held throughout the day.

A pitha fair, alpana painting and graffiti displays were organised across the campus, while evening concerts and alumni honours drew large crowds.

Established on January 12, 1971, by then East Pakistan governor and chancellor Rear Admiral SM Ahsan, the university began operations earlier that month with 150 students in four departments—economics, geography, mathematics and statistics.

The first vice-chancellor was eminent chemist professor Mofiz Uddin Ahmed. The administration has formally observed January 12 as ‘Jahangirnagar University Day’ since 2001.

Despite its cultural prominence and expansion to 36 departments under six faculties and four institutes, academics say that the university continues to face challenges in fully realising its founding goals, particularly in research output, curriculum modernisation and insulation from political instability.

JU has produced thousands of research papers over five decades, but critics argue that limited funding, outdated facilities and campus politics have constrained global competitiveness.

Besides, the university still lacks in establishing a publication house, providing health insurance to its teachers and students in line with the noble practices followed by internationally recognised universities.

‘A fully residential campus was envisioned to foster a research-friendly environment, but maintaining academic standards and values remains an ongoing task’, educationalist professor Rayhan Rhyne said.

title: Bangladesh recalls four mission press officers
body:
Bangladesh interim government has directed four press officers posted at the country’s missions abroad to be relieved of their duties immediately and return home.

The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting issued a notification in this regard on Monday.

The officers are first secretary, press, Sufi Abdullahil Maruf at the Bangladesh High Commission in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia; first secretary, press, Md Arifur Rahman at the Bangladesh Consulate General in Dubai, United Arab Emirates; second secretary, press, Asaduzzaman Khan at the Bangladesh Embassy in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia; and second secretary, press, Md Imranul Hasan at the Bangladesh Embassy in Tokyo, Japan.

According to the notification, the four officials were initially withdrawn from their respective posts on March 17, 2025, and instructed to return to Bangladesh within 15 working days for subsequent posting.

A later notification issued on April 13 revoked that decision, allowing them to continue their duties until new officers were appointed to the missions.

The notification said that new officers have since been appointed to those missions and the necessary government orders have been issued in their favour.

In view of this, the four officials have now been instructed to be mandatorily relieved from their duties with immediate effect and return to Bangladesh.

title: Mustafiz flagged as security risk by ICC
body:
If pacer Mustafizur Rahman is in the squad for the forthcoming T20 World Cup, the security threat will increase for the Bangladesh national team, ICC said in a letter to the Bangladesh Cricket Board, according to youth and sports adviser Asif Nazrul.

After the BCB sent two letters to the ICC requesting to relocate their matches outside of India due to the increasing security threats for the Bangladeshi contingent, they were yet to hear from the governing body regarding the matter.

However, in a different letter sent by the ICC security team, some points were flagged as security threats.

Apart from Mustafiz being included, the two points are the supporters wearing Bangladesh jerseys and the proximity of the national election of Bangladesh.

However, in response to those concerns, Nazrul argued that they clearly demonstrated that Bangladesh was not in a position to play cricket in India.

‘The points made by the security team of the ICC have proved unequivocally that there is no condition for the Bangladesh cricket team to play the T20 World Cup in India,’ Nazrul said in a press conference at the Bangladesh Football Federation premises on Monday.

‘If the ICC hopes that we will form our team without our best ever bowler, our fans can’t wear the Bangladesh jersey, and we will defer our national election for playing cricket, then there cannot be more bizarre, unreal, and irrational expectations,’ he said.

‘We think that the existing extreme communal situation and the anti-Bangladesh environment existing in India, especially the anti-Bangladesh campaigns that have been running for the last 16 months, have made it impossible for Bangladesh to play cricket in India. After the Mustafiz chapter and the letter I have mentioned, it has been proved unequivocally,’ he said.

The adviser also said that they should be granted the opportunity to play the World Cup in Sri Lanka.

'We think no one should have the monopoly over playing cricket. The fate of a tournament or a game cannot be determined based on market management,’ Asif said.

'If ICC is truly a global organisation, if they aren’t dictated by India, then obviously we should be given the opportunity to play the T20 World Cup in Sri Lanka. We don’t bow our heads regarding this matter,’ he added.

On Monday, there were reports published in India that the ICC might propose the BCB change the venues inside India. They were originally scheduled to play their first three matches in Kolkata, followed by a match in Mumbai.

But Nazrul also dismissed this idea. ‘I have said this: India means India. And we’ve said this about India, not [only] Kolkata. If you can shift the venue from Kolkata, then it can be given to Sri Lanka; there should be no problem,’ he said.

‘I have seen in the media, and I don’t know whether it’s true or false, that Pakistan have proposed to host our matches. You can organise our matches there, no problem. You can organise those in the UAE, no problem.

‘But when there is no environment for our team, for a player of our team to play, [and] when the Indian Cricket Board, which is a national authority, says that they shouldn’t be given the opportunity to play after bowing down to the extreme communal force, then what more proof do you need as the ICC? I don’t understand,’ he added.

'The letter sent by the security team of the ICC unequivocally has proven that there is no environment for us to play there. Not in any part of India,’ he concluded.

title: 2 siblings, another dead in Faridpur train accident
body:
At least three people, including two brothers, were killed and 10 more were injured as a pickup van was hit by a passenger train in the Sotashi area of Boalmari upazila in Faridpur on Monday.

The pickup van was crossing the track while there was no authorised level crossing and all the victims were from the van.

A probe committee has been formed by the railways authority.

The deceased were Jabbar Mollah, 15, Musa Mollah, 30, both sons of Saifar Mollah from Beel Kamrail village of Moyna union at Boalmari upazila and Shahan Ara, 25.

Boalmari thana sub inspector Saral Kumar said that the incident took place at about 2:30pm when the Bhatiapara Express was heading towards Bhatiapara from Kalukhali.

When the train reached Sotashi area, the pickup van was trying to cross the road made on the track which has no barrier or structure, he said.

Saral said that 13 day labourers were on the van returning home from a nearby factory, two brothers and a woman were killed immediately and 10 more were injured in the collision.

The injured were rushed to a local hospital and five critically injured were shifted to Faridpur medical college hospital, he added.

Bangladesh Railway’s general manager, west zone, Farid Ahmed said that at the spot there was no legal level crossing and gateman.

Railway’s Paksey divisional railway manager Liakat Sharif said that at the area, the Local Government Engineering Department constructed the road without any level crossing.

‘Recently railway officials went there to evict the illegal level crossing but the locals obstructed them,’ he continued.

A four-member committee had been formed and asked to submit report within seven days, Liakat added.

Boalmari thana sub inspector Saral also said that they already informed Rajabari railway police about the accident.

title: 45 bombs recovered in Shariatpur, four people held
body:
Law enforcers in a joint drive have recovered 45 crude bombs and bomb-making materials from a bamboo grove in Jajira upazila of Shariatpur district on Monday.

Tipped off, a joint force team conducted a drive in the area with a dog squad and recovered huge bomb-making materials and 45 crude bombs from bamboo groves in the morning, said additional superintendent of police (crime and Ops) Md Tanvir Hossain.

The recovery of explosives indicates an organised attempt to create instability in the area, he said.

Police also arrested four people, including three women from the spot.

The drive was conducted following a deadly explosion at Mulai Bepari Kandi in Bilaspur union of the upazila on Thursday that left two people killed.

The deceased were identified as Sohan Bepari and Nobin Sardar.

A case was filed against 53 identified and 150 unidentified people.

Security has been tightened in the area, said police.

title: Trump says United States will take Greenland ‘one way or the other’
body:
President Donald Trump said on Sunday that the United States would take Greenland ‘one way or the other,’ warning that Russia and China would ‘take over’ if Washington didn’t act.

Trump says controlling the mineral-rich Danish territory is crucial for US national security given increased Russian and Chinese military activity in the Arctic.

‘If we don’t take Greenland, Russia or China will, and I’m not letting that happen,’ Trump told reporters aboard Air Force One, despite neither country laying claim to the vast island.

Trump said he would be open to making a deal with the Danish self-governing territory ‘but one way or the other, we’re going to have Greenland.’

Denmark and other European allies have voiced shock at Trump’s threats over the island, which plays a strategic role between North America and the Arctic, and where the United States has had a military base since World War II.

A Danish colony until 1953, Greenland gained home rule 26 years later and is contemplating eventually loosening its ties with Denmark.

The vast majority of its population and political parties have said they do not want to be under US control and insist Greenlanders must decide their own future — a viewpoint continuously challenged by Trump.

‘Greenland should make the deal, because Greenland does not want to see Russia or China take over,’ Trump warned, as he mocked its defenses.

‘You know what their defense is, two dog sleds,’ he said, while Russia and China have ‘destroyers and submarines all over the place.’

Denmark’s prime minister warned last week that any US move to take Greenland by force would destroy 80 years of transatlantic security links.

Trump waved off the comment saying: ‘If it affects NATO, it affects NATO. But you know, they (Greenland) need us much more than we need them.’

title: Bangladesh, Pakistan discuss regional, international issues
body:
Bangladesh and Pakistan have discussed a range of regional and global issues on the sidelines of the extraordinary session of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation Council of Foreign Ministers’ meeting in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia.

Deputy prime minister and foreign minister of Pakistan senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar met with foreign affairs adviser Md Touhid Hossain on the sidelines of the extraordinary session of the OIC CFM meeting and discussed the issues of mutual interest.

Both dignitaries expressed satisfaction over the robustness of Pakistan-Bangladesh relations.

They discussed bilateral relations in diverse fields, especially high-level exchanges, trade and educational collaboration.

Foreign affairs adviser Hossain also spoke with the Pakistani foreign minister ahead of the minister-level meeting of the OIC.

The two counterparts reviewed bilateral matters and discussed recent regional developments, and appreciated the timely convening of the extraordinary session of the OIC CFM.

The extraordinary meeting of the Council of Foreign Ministers was held on Saturday at the OIC headquarters in Jeddah, to discuss the rapidly evolving and dangerous developments in the Federal Republic of Somalia.

The meeting came against the backdrop of recent developments, namely Israel’s declaration — the occupying power — of its recognition of the so-called ‘Somaliland’ region as an independent state, a move that is considered an infringement on Somalia’s sovereignty and territorial integrity.

The meeting formulated a unified Islamic position regarding these developments, and to reaffirm unwavering support for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Federal Republic of Somalia, in accordance with international conventions and relevant resolutions of the OIC.

title: 270-day credit allowed for LPG imports
body:
The Bangladesh Bank has allowed import of liquefied petroleum gas under suppliers’ or buyers’ credit, giving local importers access to longer usance facilities to ease financing pressure in the LPG market.

The central bank issued a circular in this regard on Monday clarifying that LPG will be treated as an industrial raw material for trade credit purposes.

The decision aligns LPG imports with the provisions of a foreign exchange circular issued on December 29, 2025, which permits the import of industrial raw materials under supplier’s or buyer’s credit for a usance period of up to 270 days or the cash conversion cycle, whichever is earlier.

The Bangladesh Bank said that LPG was imported in bulk and later bottled in cylinders for domestic consumption, a process that required time for storage, bottling and other operational activities.

Because of these operational requirements, the central bank recognised the need for extended credit facilities for LPG importers.

Under the revised circular, authorised dealers may allow LPG imports on deferred payment terms of up to 270 days, subject to compliance with existing foreign exchange regulations.

The central bank also advised banks to arrange buyer’s credit facilities for LPG imports from overseas banks and financial institutions.

In addition, banks may facilitate bill discounting through offshore banking units of scheduled banks operating in Bangladesh, provided that such transactions comply with applicable foreign exchange rules and prudential credit norms.

The Bangladesh Bank instructed authorised dealers to inform their relevant constituents, including LPG importers, about the revised facility.

The central bank said that the measure aims to support smoother import operations while maintaining discipline in foreign exchange transactions.

The move comes amid a severe LPG supply crunch on the domestic market that has persisted for over two weeks.

title: Actress Mehazabien, exempted in embezzlement case
body:
A Dhaka court on Monday exempted popular actress Mehazabien Chowdhury and her brother in a case over embezzlement of Tk 27 lakh.

Dhaka executive magistrate Md Adnan Zulfiqar passed the order after hearing, said Advocate Tuhin Hawladar, lawyer of actress Mehazabien.

According to the case statement, Mehazabien took Tk 27 lakh from plaintiff Amirul Islam through Nagad and bKash promising to make him a business partner in a new family venture.

When Mehazabien and her brother did not initiate any business activities for a long period Amirul asked for his money back but they delayed repayment.

On February 11, after Amirul again sought the refund, the accused asked him to meet at Hatirjheel Road on March 16.

Upon reaching the designated spot, Amirul was verbally abused and threatened with death by Mehazabien, her brother and four to five others, it said.

Amirul filed a case with Dhaka executive magistrate on March 24.

On November 10, last year, a Dhaka court issued warrants for the arrest of Mehazabien and her brother Alisan Chowdhury in the case.

On November 16, 2025, a Dhaka court granted them bail in the case upon surrender.

title: Myanmar border tensions on as fisherman loses leg in mine blast
body:
Tensions along Bangladesh-Myanmar border continued on Monday as a   Bangladeshi fisherman lost his leg in a landmine explosion along border in Whykong under Teknaf upazila of Cox’s Bazar district in the morning.

A tense situation prevailed among local people in bordering areas of Teknaf after the landmine blast.

Injured Md Hanif, 28, a shrimp farm worker, lost  his leg in the landmine blast while working on the shrimp farm, according to Border Guard Bangladesh and police officials.

BGB-64 Ukhiya Battalion commanding officer Lieutenant Colonel Md Zahirul Islam said that the incident took place at about 11:15am on Monday.

Teknaf police station officer-in-charge Saiful Islam also said that Hanif was injured in a mine explosion while working on a shrimp enclosure.

‘The explosion created panic among the people,’ the OC added.

A tense situation has been prevailing in areas of Bandarban and Cox’s Bazar districts along border with Myanmar over the past few days amid airstrikes by the neighbouring country’s ruling junta and gunfights between rebel armed groups there.

On Sunday, at least three people — a 12-year-old Bangladeshi girl, Afnan, and two Rohingyas — were injured along border by bullets coming from the conflict-hit Myanmar territory near Whykong under the Teknaf upazila in Cox’s Bazar district.

Chattogram Medical College Hospital director Brigadier General Mohammed Taslim Uddin on Monday afternoon said that bullet-hit Afnan was still undergoing treatment at the hospital intensive care unit in a critical condition.

Amid firings, airstrikes, and mortar shell explosions, 53 Rohingya people entered Bangladesh and were detained by the BGB on Sunday at border points in Whykong, according to BGB officials.

BGB officials also said that conflicts were going on between rebel armed groups in Myanmar, including the Arakan Army, the Arakan Rohingya Salvation Army, and the Rohingya Solidarity Organisation.

BGB Ramu sector commander Colonel Mohammad Mohiuddin Ahmed said that they had been on the highest alert along the Myanmar border for the past two years and the recent incidents forced them to deploy more force along the border.

‘We are raising awareness among the fishermen not to be along the border or cross the zero line while catching fish considering the situation. We are monitoring the issues in Myanmar very closely and seriously,’ he added.

Myanmar and Bangladesh share a 271-kilometre border.

According to BGB officials, almost the entire Myanmar border is occupied by the Arakan Army and there is no presence of the Myanmar Border Guard Police there.

In August 2017, around eight lakh Rohingyas crossed into Bangladesh to save their lives from a military crackdown in Rakhine State, Bangladesh interim government chief adviser Professor Yunus mentioned, saying that Bangladesh now hosted around 13 lakh displaced Rohingyas, including 32,000 newborns in the camps annually.

title: Trump says Iran ‘want to negotiate’ after hundreds of people killed in protests
body:
United States president Donald Trump said on Sunday that Iran’s leadership had called him seeking ‘to negotiate’ after he repeatedly threatened to intervene militarily if Tehran killed protesters.

For two weeks, Iran has been rocked by a protest movement that has swelled in spite of a crackdown rights groups warn has become a ‘massacre’.

Initially sparked by anger over the rising cost of living, the demonstrations have evolved into a serious challenge of the theocratic system in place since the 1979 revolution.

Information has continued to trickle out of Iran despite a days-long internet shutdown, with videos filtering out of capital Tehran and other cities over the past three nights showing large demonstrations.

As reports emerge of a growing protest death toll, and images show bodies piled outside a morgue, Trump said Tehran indicated its willingness to talk.

‘The leaders of Iran called’ yesterday, Trump told reporters aboard Air Force One, adding that ‘a meeting is being set up. They want to negotiate.’

He added, however, that ‘we may have to act before a meeting’.

The US-based Center for Human Rights in Iran said it had received ‘eyewitness accounts and credible reports indicating that hundreds of protesters have been killed across Iran during the current internet shutdown’.

The Norway-based NGO Iran Human Rights said it confirmed the killing of at least 192 protesters but that the actual toll could be much higher.

‘Unverified reports indicate that at least several hundreds, and according to some sources, more than 2,000 people may have been killed,’ said IHR.

More than 2,600 protesters have been arrested, IHR estimates.

A video circulating on Sunday showed dozens of bodies accumulating outside a morgue south of Tehran.

The footage, geolocated by AFP to Kahrizak, showed bodies wrapped in black bags, with what appeared to be grieving relatives searching for loved ones.

In Tehran, an AFP journalist described a city in a state of near paralysis.

The price of meat has nearly doubled since the start of the protests, and many shops are closed. Those that do open must close at around 4:00pm or 5:00pm, when security forces deploy en masse.

There were fewer videos showing protests on social media Sunday, but it was not clear to what extent that was due to the internet shutdown.

One widely shared video showed protesters again gathering in the Pounak district of Tehran shouting slogans in favour of the ousted monarchy.

The protests have become one of the biggest challenges to the rule of supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, 86, coming in the wake of Israel’s 12-day war against the Islamic republic in June, which was backed by the United States.

State TV has aired images of burning buildings, including a mosque, as well as funeral processions for security personnel.

But after three days of mass actions, state outlets were at pains to present a picture of calm returning, broadcasting images of smooth-flowing traffic on Sunday. Tehran Governor Mohammad-Sadegh Motamedian insisted in televised comments that ‘the number of protests is decreasing’.

The Iranian government on Sunday declared three days of national mourning for ‘martyrs’ including members of the security forces killed.

President Masoud Pezeshkian also urged Iranians to join a ‘national resistance march’ Monday to denounce the violence.

In response to Trump’s repeated threats to intervene, Iran’s parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said Iran would hit back, calling US military and shipping ‘legitimate targets’ in comments broadcast by state TV.

Reza Pahlavi, the US-based son of Iran’s ousted shah, who has emerged as an anti-government figurehead, said he was prepared to return to the country and lead a democratic transition.

‘I’m already planning on that,’ he told Fox News on Sunday.

He later urged Iran’s security forces and government workers to join the demonstrators.

‘Employees of state institutions, as well as members of the armed and security forces, have a choice: stand with the people and become allies of the nation, or choose complicity with the murderers of the people,’ he said in a social media post.

He also urged protesters to replace the flags outside of Iranian embassies.

‘The time has come for them to be adorned with Iran’s national flag,’ he said.

The ceremonial, pre-revolution flag has become an emblem of the global rallies that have mushroomed in support of Iran’s demonstrators.

In London, protesters managed over the weekend to swap out the Iranian embassy flag, hoisting in its place the tri-colored banner used under the last shah.

title: Unidentified youth found dead at Kuril Biswa Road in Dhaka
body:
The body of an unidentified young man was recovered from a footpath behind the BRTA counter on Kuril Biswa Road on Monday.

Pedestrians took the youth, aged over 20, to Dhaka Medical College Hospital in an unconscious state at about 10:45am where doctors at the emergency department pronounced him dead.

Inspector Md Faruk, in-charge of the hospital police camp said the body has been kept at the morgue of the hospital’s emergency department.

Khilkhet police station was informed about the incident, he added.

title: KU Bangla Dept teacher suspended on allegation of ‘sexual harassment’
body:
Khulna University administration has suspended Professor Rubel Ansar of Bangla Department for two years following allegations of sexual harassment by a female student.

The information was disclosed on Sunday in a letter issued by the university’s acting registrar Professor SM Mahbubur Rahman.

According to university sources, in August last year, a female student accused Professor Rubel Ansar of indecent behavior, sexual harassment, and proposing an unethical relationship.

Shortly afterward, another female student from a different department submitted a similar complaint.

A seven-member committee was formed to investigate both allegations.

On December 26, Sexual Harassment Prevention Center of the university submitted two reports to the committee.

Both reports were adopted at the university’s 234th syndicate meeting on December 28.

Professor SM Mahbubur Rahman said the syndicate based on the committee’s recommendations decided to relieve Professor Rubel Ansar from one of the allegations.

Regarding the second allegation, he has been suspended from all teaching, examination, and administrative duties in the Bengali Department for the next two years.

The registrar added that although Professor Rubel Ansar is barred from classes and examinations he will continue to receive his salary and other benefits during the suspension period.

When contacted, Professor Rubel Ansar said he had received the university’s letter and would comment on the matter later.

title: Mild coldwave may continue across Bangladesh: Met Office
body:
The Meteorological Department on Monday said that a mild coldwave is sweeping Rajshahi, Pabna, Dinajpur, Panchagarh, Nilphamari, Jashore, Chuadanga, and Kushtia, and it may continue.

Weather is expected to remain generally dry with temporary partly cloudy skies over the country, said a Met office bulletin.

Moderate to dense fog may occur at places over river basins while light to moderate fog is likely elsewhere during late night and morning hours.

The Met Office also forecast that night and day temperatures are likely to remain nearly unchanged across the country.

The lowest temperature was recorded in Tentulia at 8.4 degrees Celsius.

title: Hotel worker killed owner’s daughter at Banasri: RAB
body:
The Rapid Action Battalion on Monday said that a man named Millon Mallick killed Fatema Akter Nili whose throat-slit body was recovered from the capital’s South Banasree area January 10, after the victim had rejected his ‘lewd proposal’.

After primary questioning of arrested Milon, 28, RAB-3 commanding officer Lieutenant Colonel Fayezul Arefin at a press briefing at the RAB media centre said that the accused had given Nili a lewd proposal the night before he killed her and turned vengeful as he met with a harsh refusal.

Millon then went to the victim’s house with a nylon rope and repeated his lewd proposal and again she rejected him.

Rejected, he captured her and fastened a rope around her neck, causing the victim to fall to the ground. Millon then slit her throat with a kitchen knife, said Fayezul.

The elite force officer also said that whether there was any other motive behind the brutal murder would be revealed by the ongoing investigation.

Teams of RAB-3 and RAB-6 in a joint drive in Boro Singha area in Bagerhat district arrested Millon at about 8:30pm on Sunday.

The arrest was made after victim’s father Mohammad Sajib had filed a murder case against unnamed people with the Khilgaon police on Sunday following the recovery of Fatema’s throat-slit body at her rented house in South Banasri area on Saturday.

Khilgaon police officer-in-charge Md Shafikul Islam on Monday evening said that the RAB handed over Millon to them and he would be produced in court today.

Analysing the CCTV footage collected from the location, the RAB found that on January 10, Millon went to the house at 1:36pm and came out at 1:41pm carrying food with the victim’s sister Shova.

Shova stayed at a local gymnasium from 1:42pm to 3:45pm, while Millon again went to the house at 2:25pm and came out at 2:45pm.

During the arrest drive, the RAB also recovered a black pant and blue T-shirt that were allegedly worn by the accused when he killed Nili.

Earlier, the police recovered the nylon rope and kitchen knife used in the killing.

Victim’s family went to their village home in Kalauk area in Habiganj on January 7, leaving Shova and Fatema at their Dhaka home.

Millon used to go to the house to fetch his food as the hotel remained closed for some days and its other employees had gone on holiday, said the victim’s family.

title: Coast Guard rescues ‘abducted’ woman in Khulna, ‘abductor’ held
body:
The Bangladesh Coast Guard base Mongla rescued an abducted woman and detained the kidnapper in the Banishanta area under Dacope in Khulna on Saturday.

The Coast Guard handed over the rescued woman and the kidnapper to Dacope police station for further legal action, said a press release on Sunday.

A woman named Lima Khatun, 18, who had come to visit the Sundarban on December 20 in the past year, was abducted in the Banishanta area under Dacope police station in Khulna.

When the victim did not return home for a long time, her husband filed a general diary with the Sonadanga police station.

On Saturday, the victim’s husband went to Banishanta area and tried to rescue his wife with the help of people of the area.

At that time, the kidnapper named Sagar Molla, 25, followed them and arrived at the Mongla bus stand area and tried to forcibly take her away again by posing as the victim’s brother.

title: Youth shot dead in Khulna
body:
A youth was shot dead by miscreants at Purba Rupsa area in Khulna Sunday.

The victim is Abdul Rashed, also known as Pikul, 30, son of Abdul Awal of Bagmara area under Rupsa upazila in the district.

The incident occurred at around 1.00am in Kadamtala Balu Maath area, where assailants opened fire targeting him with the intent to kill. Hearing the gunshots, locals rushed to the spot and found Pikul critically injured.

He was immediately taken to Khulna Medical College Hospital, where he died from his injuries.

Confirming the incident, Rupsa police station’s inspector-investigation Md Sabur said that several shots were fired at Pikul by a group of miscreants, one of the shots hit him in the chest, causing him to collapse on the spot.

The attackers fled as local residents gathered after hearing the gunshots.

The police official added that Pikul has several allegations against him with the Rupsa police station.

Police have launched an investigation to identify and arrest those involved in the killing.

title: Youth crushed under wheel loader
body:
A day-labourer died after being crushed under the wheel of a wheel loader machine in the early morning on Sunday at Goainghat upazila in Sylhet.

The deceased was Parvej Ahmed, 27, son of Jamal Miah of Chhailakhel area of Goainghat upazila, police said.

Local people said that Parvej along with his several co-workers was illegally extracting sand using a wheel loader machine from the bank of Piyain River at Jumpar area under Purba-Jaflong union of Goainghat upazila in the early morning.

At around 6:00am, Parvej suddenly fell under the wheel of the machine and died on the spot, they said.

Goainghat police station officer-in-charge Md Moniruzzaman confirmed the death of Parvej.

He said that, on information, the police went to the spot and sent the body to Sylhet Osmani Medical College Hospital for post-mortem examinations.

‘Further legal steps will be taken after receiving a written complaint from the victim’s family in this regard,’ he said.

title: IAB seeks ‘Yes’ vote in referendum
body:
Amir of Islami Andolon Bangladesh Charmonai Pir Mufti Syed Muhammad Rezaul Karim on Sunday sought people to cast their votes ‘yes’ in the forthcoming referendum coinciding with general election to uphold July Uprising spirit.

‘The forthcoming 13th National Parliamentary Election offers the nation a golden opportunity to rebuild the country’ by giving its consent for ‘yes’ in the referendum to be staged simultaneously with the general elections, he said in a statement on Sunday.

Karim called upon political parties, candidates and the government to play an active role in building public opinion in support of the July Charter.

He said the opportunity came as the young students and ordinary people risked their lives on the streets in July 2024 to free the country ‘from clutches of fascism’.

Karim, however, feared despite the ouster of ‘Awami fascism’, fascist laws, practices and political culture were not completely eradicated while the July Charter’s implementation could wipe out its remaining elements.

‘The July Charter has been formulated to ensure permanent elimination of fascism from the country,’ he said adding that the endorsement of the referendum would provide it a legal foundation.

The Islami Andolon amir said that the people who took to the streets in July 2024 did not sacrifice their lives merely for an election, but for a greater national purpose.

The charter, he said, largely incorporated the aspirations of the mass uprising if not entirely.

The Charmonai Pir warned that failure to demonstrate overwhelming public support for the July Charter would cast doubts over the interim government, the national election process and the overall political transition.

The statement also underscored the importance of public security for holding a free and fair election, saying the issues still remained a concern and urged the government to take swift and effective measures dispel the sense of insecurity.

title: Natore Poura ex-panel mayor held in Rajshahi
body:
Police arrested former panel mayor of Natore Pourashava and former district organising secretary of Awami League Arifur Rahman Masum in Bhadra area in Rajshahi city on Sunday.

Police said Arifur Rahman remained hiding in the city since August 5, 2024. On a tip-off, a police team from Chandrima police station conducted a sudden raid at the area and arrested him and subsequently, handed him over to Natore Sadar police.

At noon, police produced Masum before the Natore chief judicial magistrate court showing him arrested in Yeasin murder case in the house of former Awami League MP Shafiqul islam Shimul.

Judge Faisal Tareque passed an order for sending him to jail.

Investigating officer of the case Natore thana sub-inspector Shahadat Hossain said they got information of three killing cases against him initially.

He also said they will submit a plea for taking him remand for interrogation.

title: Moni killed for family feuds, business enmity: govt
body:
The government on Sunday clarified that Moni Chakraborty, a grocery shop owner in Narsingdi, was killed due to family disputes and previous business enmity, nullifying the religious link with the killing.

‘It was noted with concern regarding some recent incidents that, due to spreading misinformation, some individuals have attempted or been provoked into actions that could damage communal harmony,’ chief adviser’s senior assistant press secretary Foyez Ahammad said at a briefing at the Foreign Service Academy in Dhaka in the afternoon.

Referring to the recent incident of Moni Chakraborty killing, he said according to preliminary assessments by the police and the victim’s family, he was killed due to family disputes and previous business enmity.

As the individual belonged to the Hindu community, false propaganda was spread in various places claiming that he was killed in a communal attack, Foyez added.

It was observed that, based on such misinformation, several distinguished citizens issued statements, he said, noting, many of these individuals had previously conducted neutral investigations in different incidents in Bangladesh and had visited affected areas firsthand.

‘We hope, if any incident causes concern, such individuals would verify facts carefully before making statements and, if necessary, visit the location to assess whether there is any communal dimension,’ Foyez said.

Otherwise, he said, issuing statements without verifying the facts and spreading false information together can play a significant role in damaging social and communal harmony.

‘The government urged everyone to remain cautious and act responsibly in this regard,’ Foyez added.

Chief adviser’s press secretary Shafiqul Alam and deputy press secretary Mohammad Abul Kalam Azad Majumder were present at the briefing.

Replying to question, Shafiqul Alam said the country’s law and order situation is good now while law enforcement agencies are highly confident over controlling the situation centring the polls.

About Swechchhasebak Dal leader Azizur Rahman Musabbir killing in the capital, he said three, including the main shooter, have already been arrested while over a dozen of persons were also arrested in connection with brutal murder of Dipu Chandra Das in Mymensigh.

title: Rickshaw-van driver hacked to death at Gournadi
body:
A rickshaw-van driver was hacked to death by miscreants while returning home in Gournadi upazila of Barishal district in the early hours of Sunday.

The deceased was identified as Manju Bepari, 50, son of the late Abdur Rashid Bepari of East Kasemabad village.

The incident occurred in the East Kasemabad area of Gournadi upazila.

The officer-in-charge of Gournadi police station, Tariq Hasan Russell, said the police visited the spot after receiving the information.

‘The matter is under investigation, and further details will be revealed after completion of the investigation,’ he added.

According to locals, Manju Bepari was returning home late at night after dropping off passengers when miscreants blocked his path, hacked him indiscriminately, snatched his cash and mobile phone and fled the scene.

Hearing his screams, local residents rushed to the spot and took the critically injured van driver to the Gournadi Upazila Health Complex.

Tipu Sultan, a physician at the hospital, said Manju Bepari had died before he was brought to the hospital.

title: 1 dead, 12 hurt in land dispute clash
body:
A youth was killed and at least 12 others were injured in a clash between two groups of villagers at Osmani Nagar upazila in Sylhet on Saturday night over a land dispute.

The deceased, Shajahan Miah Sourav, 25, is son of Abdul Aziz of Uttar Tilapara village under Burungabazar union of the same upazila, police said.

Local residents said that there was a long-standing dispute between the families of Barik Uddin of the Uttar Tilapara village and his neighbour Abdul Aziz over land ownership.

As a consequence of the previous enmity, family members of Barik Uddin attacked Shajahan in front of their house at about 8:00pm on Saturday when he was returning home from Sylhet sadar, leaving him critically injured, they said.

Hearing the scream, family members of Shahjalal came and locked in a clash with the rival group that injured 12 more people on both sides, the locals said.

They said that two critically injured, including Shahjahan, were sent to Sylhet Osmani Medical College Hospital while the rests were given treatment from the local dispensaries.

Osmani Nagar police station officer-in-charge Murshedul Alam Bhuiyan said that Shahjahan died at the hospital at about 11:00pm on Saturday.

‘None was arrested so far,’ he said on Sunday evening, adding that a case would be filed after receiving a written complaint from the victim’s family.

title: Farmer crushed under Indian truck in C’nawabganj
body:
A Bangladeshi farmer was killed after being run over by an Indian truck in the Sonamasjid land port area of Shibganj upazila in Chapainawabganj on Sunday morning.

The deceased was Abdul Qader, 60, son of Md Kalu Haji of Sonamasjid Baliyadighi Middle Bazar area.

According to local sources, Qader Ali was crossing the road carrying a bundle of grass when an empty Indian truck, returning to India after unloading goods at the Sonamasjid land port, ran him over, leaving him dead on the spot.

Following the incident, local residents chased and seized the truck and the driver, they said.

Humayun Kabir, officer-in-charge of Shibganj police station, said that on information, they rushed to the spot, seized the truck and its driver.

He said that preparation of filing a case was under way.

title: 20,000cft sand seized, 50 boats destroyed in Sylhet
body:
A task force on Sunday seized 20,000 cubic feet of illegally extracted sand and destroyed 50 boats used for sand extraction at Jaintapur upazila in Sylhet.

The taskforce conducted the drive in Rangpani River at Banglabazar area at about 11:00 am, the upazila administration said.

Jaintapur upazila nirbahi officer, Mohammad Golam Mostafa, led the taskforce comprising members of the police and Border Guard Bangladesh.

Jaintapur upazila assistant commissioner, land, Polly Rani Dev said that at that time the taskforce members also destroyed 50 boats used in lifting sand.

title: Miscreants kill microbus driver in Ctg
body:
A microbus driver was stabbed to death by some unidentified miscreants in Kalabagan area under Hathazari Pourasabha of Chattogram early Sunday.

The victim is Mahbubul Alam, 35, son of late Abdul Nabi of Azimpara under ward no-3 of Hathazari Municipality.

Mahbub had been working as a caretaker of Alaol Building in Kolabagan area alongside driving. A group of miscreants attacked and stabbed him indiscriminately at one stage of scuffle between them at around 4:00am.

The attackers fled the scene after committing the crime. After hearing the screaming, locals rushed to the spot and rescued Mahbub in critical condition.

He died from his injuries on way to Chattogram Medical College and Hospital.

Hathazari police said they were trying to arrest the miscreants and the body was sent to CMCH for autopsy. A case was filed with the concerned police station in this connection, the sources added.

title: KU teacher suspended over sexual assault
body:
Professor Rubel Ansar of Khulna University’s Bangla discipline has been suspended for two years over sexual assaults on two female students.

The university’s 234th Syndicate meeting came up with the decision following recommendations submitted by the probe body formed to investigate the sexual harassment allegations against Professor Ansar.

During the suspension period, the chastised teacher will completely be barred from academic and administrative activities. But he will receive salary, allowances and other benefits, said KU acting registrar Professor SM Mahbubur Rahman.

In August last year, a female student filed a complaint against Professor Ansar, accusing him of indecent behaviour, sexual harassment and making proposals for an unethical relationship. Subsequently, another female student from a different discipline lodged a separate but similar complaint against him.

Following the filing of the complaints, the KU sexual harassment prevention centre formed a seven-member investigation committee.

The probe body submitted two separate reports on December 26. The reports were placed at the 234th Syndicate meeting held on December 28.

Contacted, Professor Ansar said he had received the official letter but declined to make any comment.

title: Man jailed for passing off as MBBS doctor
body:
A mobile court on Sunday sentenced a man to jail for posing as an MBBS doctor and practicing medicine illegally for more than half a decade at a private hospital in the Bhawaniganj municipality area of Bagmara upazila in Rajshahi.

The court, led by Bagmara upazila assistant commissioner, land, and executive magistrate Saiful Islam Bhuiyan, sentenced Nurul Islam, a resident of Baharampur area in Rajshahi city, to six months’ rigorous imprisonment and fined him Tk 10,000.

Saiful Islam Bhuiyan said that Nurul Islam concealed his real identity and introduced himself as Dr Md Rafikul Hasan, falsely claiming to hold MBBS and FCPS degrees in medicine and neuromedicine.

‘Despite having no recognised medical qualification, he had been treating patients for brain, nerve, stroke, paralysis, spine and epilepsy-related diseases,’ he said, adding that Nurul had been using a Bangladesh Medical and Dental Council registration number – A-34797 – to impersonate a  neuro-medicine specialist.

The mobile court caught Nurul Islam red-handed while he was providing treatment at his chamber at At-Tabara Model Hospital in the Godown Mor area of Bhawaniganj municipality.

Signboards inside and outside the hospital identified him as ‘Dr Md Rafikul Hasan, MBBS, FCPS (Medicine), FCPS (Neuro Medicine)’ and falsely described him as a neuro-medicine specialist of Jahurul Islam Medical College Hospital in Kishoreganj.

Saiful Islam Bhuiyan said that they found Nurul to be an HSC graduate. ‘He had been treating patients not only in Rajshahi but also at Atrai in Naogaon, Rangpur, Dinajpur, and Manikganj districts,’ he added.

He further said that they had also fined At-Tabara Model Hospital owner Mashiur Rahman Tk 2 lakh under section 52 of the Consumer Rights Protection Act, 2009, for knowingly appointing a fake doctor and exposing patients to serious health risks.

title: Restaurant workers’ strike suspended till Feb 5
body:
Minimum Wage Bastabayan Sangram Parishad has suspended the countrywide work abstention programme of workers and employees slated for January 14 up for 20 days on assurance of beginning the implementation of the wage.

A press release of the sangram parishad on Sunday said that the government officials gave commitment to start taking steps for implementing the announced minimum wage for the hotel and restaurant workers from January 12.

The interim government on May 5 in 2025 announced minimum wage for the hotel and restaurant workers Tk 1,3050 which was not implemented in the hotel and restaurants across the country, sangram parishad leaders alleged.

They announced a daylong work abstention of workers at hotel and restaurants across the country for January 14. Following the government commitment the protest progrmme has been deferred till February 5.

title: Bangladesh backs Somalia’s sovereignty at OIC Meet
body:
Bangladesh has reaffirmed its firm support for Somalia’s sovereignty and territorial integrity at an extraordinary meeting of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation convened to address recent regional developments.

Foreign adviser Md Touhid Hossain expressed the position while addressing the 22nd extraordinary session of the council of foreign ministers of the OIC in Jeddah, Kingdom of Saudi Arabia on Saturday, said a foreign ministry’s press release on Sunday.

‘Bangladesh aligns itself fully with the collective resolve of the OIC to uphold international law, respect for sovereignty and territorial integrity of member states, and the unity and solidarity of the Muslim world,’ said the adviser.

The extraordinary session was convened to deliberate on recent developments concerning Israel’s recognition of the so-called Somaliland and its implications for the

sovereignty, unity and territorial integrity of the Federal Republic of Somalia, as well as broader regional and international ramifications.

During his intervention, adviser Touhid urged the OIC to categorically reject and condemn Israel’s recognition of the so-called ‘Somaliland’ and reaffirm, in the strongest possible terms, its full and unwavering support for Somalia’s sovereignty and territorial integrity.

He further underscored that the sovereignty of OIC Member States is non-negotiable, stressing those illegal negotiations will not be tolerated and that justice, international law and multilateralism must prevail over unilateralism and coercion.

Earlier in the day, a senior officials meeting, serving as the preparatory session for the extraordinary council of foreign ministers, was held with the participation of a large number of representatives from OIC member states.

The meeting also reaffirmed continued solidarity with the Palestinian people and reiterated the centrality of the Palestinian cause to the OIC.

title: Mobile app for metro rail pass recharge to be launched today
body:
A mobile app is set to be launched today using which metro rail passengers will be able to recharge their passes.

Named ‘Rapid Pass Mobile App’ it will allow passengers to recharge both Rapid Passes and MRT Passes by paying through their credit cards issued by any bank and mobile financial service platforms, including Bkash, Nagad and Rocket.

Dhaka Transport Coordination Authority, the implementing agency for the online recharge system for the passes, will officially launch the app at a ceremony this afternoon at its head office DTCA Bhaban in the capital.

The minimum recharge amount through the app has been set at Tk 100 and maximum amount at Tk 5,000.

The DTCA first introduced the recharging facility away from the metro rail stations on November 25 last year by registering their passes in the website www.rapidpass.com.bd.

To complete the process, after website recharge, the cards needed to touch any ‘add-value machine’ set up at the metro stations.

Same process will have to be followed for the mobile app too, said DTCA officials.

The next step in the process will be to do away with the need for the passes to touch the add-value machines for recharge activation, officials said.

Using the website currently more than 13 lakh passes are recharged daily for Tk 4.5 lakh to Tk 5 lakh on average, according to DTCA officials.

Officials also said that the Rapid Pass Mobile App had already been introduced a week ago and till now about 20,000 people registered their mobile numbers there.

After installing the mobile app, under a mobile number a total of five MRT or rapid passes can be registered for recharging.

The first ever metro rail project in Bangladesh—Mass Rapid Transit Line-6—on the Uttara-Agargaon section in the capital was inaugurated on December 28, 2022, which was later extended to Motijheel on November 4, 2023.

Currently, about four lakh passengers on average commute by metro rail daily.

Sheik Moinuddin, special assistant to the chief adviser and attached to the road transport and bridges ministry, and DTCA’s immediately past executive director Neelima Akhter are scheduled to attend the ceremony today as special guests.

The ceremony will be chaired by DTCA executive director (additional charge) Md Moshiur Rahman.

title: Rajshahi div hospitals hard-hit by rabies vaccine shortage
body:
An acute shortage of rabies vaccines has hit the government hospitals hard across Rajshahi division for more than a month, turning animal bite patients away depriving them of lifesaving treatment, health officials and patients said.

Currently, all the public health facilities in the division have completely run out of the vaccine, Rajshahi divisional health director Mohammad Habibur Rahman said.

Private pharmacies have also largely run out of stock of the vaccine in the division, said health directorate officials and patients.

Recent visits to Rajshahi city’s several medicine shops known as ‘Model Pharmacies’, a recognition by the Directorate General of Drug Administration, found they also ran out of stock of the vaccine.

Animal bite patients and their families, however, said that the vaccine was available at a few places at present, but were sold secretly at prices multiple times the government-fixed price, adding to the distress of the affected families.

In some cases, a single dose of vaccine—officially priced at Tk 400—was reportedly being sold for as much as Tk 1,200, patients alleged.

Health officials confirmed that the shortage was not limited to Rajshahi division only, but affected health facilities nationwide.

Suratan Bibi, a resident of Rajshahi city’s Chabbish Nagar area, said that she rushed to Rajshahi Medical College Hospital after being scratched by a dog on Thursday, but was told that the hospital ran out of the vaccine.

‘The hospital told me there was no stock of the vaccine. I then went to the pharmacies outside RMCH, but they also said the same,’ said Suratan scared that she could not get the vaccine.

Patients visiting the district public hospitals and other public health facilities outside the divisional city for rabies vaccination reported similar experiences.

Private hospitals and clinics do not usually administer rabies vaccine.

Rajshahi branch general secretary of Bangladesh Private Hospital, Clinic and Diagnostic Owners Association Zahid Hossain said that no private hospital or clinic administered rabies vaccine.

Officials at the Rajshahi divisional health directorate said that hospitals in the division required around 2,00,000 doses of rabies vaccine to meet the yearly demand.

Rajshahi Medical College Hospital alone needs approximately 1,08,000 doses annually, while district-level requirements include about 24,000 doses in Chapainawabganj, 18,000 in Joypurhat, 12,000 in Natore, 6,000 in Pabna, 5,000 each in Naogaon and Sirajganj, and around 5,000 in Bogura, according to the divisional health directorate office.

Rajshahi Medical College Hospital spokesperson and emergency department in-charge Dr Shankar Kumar Biswas said that between 250 and 300 patients sought rabies vaccination at the hospital every day.

‘Due to the shortage, we are being forced to send patients back without administering the vaccine,’ he said.

‘We have informed the higher authorities and will resume vaccination as soon as supplies arrive,’ he added.

Divisional health director Mohammad Habibur Rahman acknowledged the nationwide crisis, saying that an immediate solution was unlikely.

‘There is a shortage of rabies vaccine throughout the country. Efforts are under way to resolve the situation, but it may take some time,’ he said.

Public health experts have warned that interruptions in rabies vaccination pose serious risks, as the infection is almost always fatal once symptoms appear, stressing the need for urgent government interventions to restore supply and prevent avoidable deaths.

title: GIRL’S THROAT SLIT BODY AT BANASRI: Case filed against unnamed people
body:
A murder case was filed against unnamed people with the Khilgaon police station early Sunday over recovering the throat-slit body of a Class X schoolgirl at her rented house in the South Banasri area in the capital Dhaka the previous day.

Khilgaon police station officer-in-charge Md Shafikul Islam said that the victim’s father, Mohammad Sajib, filed the murder case against unnamed people over the death of Fatema Akter Nili.

‘We are investigating the incident,’ the police official said.

Fatema’s brother, Mohammad Shakil, said that they suspected their restaurant staff over the murder of her sister.

‘Millon remains fugitive after the incident,’ he said, referring to an employee of the restaurant.

Referring to the victim’s sister, Shafikul said that her sister Shova Akter found her sister’s throat-slit body on the floor at about 3:30pm on Saturday.

The police official said that the duty officer at the police station received a call through the national emergency service at about 3:58pm on the day and recovered the body from the kitchen of the victim’s residence.

‘We along with her sister and two pedestrians took her to Farazy Hospital Limited at Banasri where duty doctors declared her dead,’ he added.

Quoting the victim’s sister, Shafikul said that their father, mother, sister, brother and sister-in-law went to their village home at Kalauk area in Habiganj on January 7, leaving Shova and Fatema at their Dhaka house.

title: ICT grants first bail in July uprising case
body:
The International Crimes Tribunal-2 on Sunday granted bail to Awami League leader Humayun Kabir, an accused in a case filed over the alleged crimes against humanity committed during the July 2024 mass uprising, subject to several conditions.

This is the first such order passed in a case filed over the brutal crimes committed during the July uprising.

‘The three-member tribunal, led by justice Nazrul Islam Chowdhury, passed the order, allowing the plea filed by Kabir’s counsel, citing that the accused has long been suffering from liver cirrhosis,’ said prosecutor Md Mizanul Islam.

The senior prosecutor said the tribunal imposed several conditions. Under these conditions, the accused must provide his residential address. He will not be allowed to make any statement through the media or on social media platforms. He will not be permitted to change his residence without informing the investigation officer and the registrar of the tribunal, and he must not influence the witnesses or tamper with evidence of the case.

‘If any of these conditions are violated, the bail will be cancelled,’ the prosecutor added.

Four people were arrested in connection with a case filed over crimes against humanity committed in Lakshmipur during the July–August uprising. Among them is Humayun Kabir, who was the president of the Lakshmipur Sadar Upazila Awami League and chairman of the Char Ruhita Union Parishad.

He was arrested in August, 2024, from Dhaka and was in jail since then.

title: 32 citizens concerned about attacks on minorities
body:
Thirty-two eminent citizens expressed concern about the increasing attacks on religious minorities before forthcoming Jatiya Sangsad election scheduled for February.

They called on the interim government to take immediate steps to stop countrywide attacks on religious minorities and maintain law and order to ensure the security of the people before the upcoming general election.
