Referring to the press reports, they said in a joint statement that Dipu Chandra Das, a Hindu garment worker, was brutally killed in Bhaluka, Mymensigh, Rana Pratap Bairagi was killed in Jessore and Sharat Chakrabortty, along with others, were killed in Narsingdi.

Moreover, religious minorities were attacked and their houses were ransacked in different parts of the country, they said.

Signatories to the statement are, among others, former Jahangirnagar University professor Anu Muhammad and human rights activists Sultana Kamal, Khushi Kabir, Iftekharuzzaman and Rasheda K Chowhury.

title: Govt releases TVC on referendum
body:
The government on Sunday released a Television Commercial on the forthcoming referendum slated for February 12, explaining what citizens will get if cast ‘Yes’ vote and what they will not get if cast ‘No’ votes in the referendum.

The chief adviser’s press wing released the 3.05 minutes TVC with a title ‘in just three minutes, learn what the referendum is and why’.

The TVC was made under the supervision of the ministry of cultural affairs, which brought together voices from diverse backgrounds who explained the implications of the referendum and what outcomes depend on casting ‘Yes’ or ‘No’ votes.

Those featured in the TVC included the sister of July martyr Wasim, the mother of Suman, who was a victim of enforced disappearance, Nabila Idris, a member of the Commission of Inquiry on Enforced Disappearances, Ratul, who stood on the frontlines during the July mass uprising, and Dhaka University Professor Rashed Al Mahmud Titumir.

The mother of July martyr Priyo, the sister of July martyr Rabbi, the sister of July martyr Saikat, Coordinator of Investigation into the Pilkhana killings retired Captain Khan Subael Bin Rafiq and footballer Ritu Porna Chakma also voiced in the TVC.

title: Man fined for illegal pond excavation in C’nawabganj
body:
A mobile court on Saturday night fined a man Tk 1 lakh for illegally excavating a pond on cropland at Shibganj upazila in Chapainawabganj.

The mobile court led by Shibganj assistant commissioner, land, Md Toufik Aziz, fined Md Nahid Islam after conducting a drive on the northern part of the Daniyalpur village of Fatehpur mouza at Mobarakpur union.

Toufik Aziz said that acting on a tip-off, they conducted the mobile court and detained Nahid Islam at the site red handed. He said that mobile court drives against illegal soil cutting and pond excavation on agricultural land would continue regularly to protect farmlands.

According to a Bangladesh Sangbad Sangstha report published on Friday, around 90,000 hectares of triple-cropping land have been lost across Rajshahi, Chapainawabganj, Naogaon and Natore over the past 17 years.

Most of the fertile croplands have been turned into commercial fish ponds, raising serious concerns about food security, soil degradation and sustainable land use amid weak regulatory oversight, the report noted.

title: DU intake test for tech units on April 4
body:
The schedule of the online applications for admission test under the engineering colleges/institutes affiliated with Dhaka University has been announced for the academic year 2025-2026.

According to the schedule, online applications for admission under the Technology Unit will start from January 14. Online applications will be accepted till February 28.

The admission test will be held on Saturday, April 4, from 11:00am to 12:30 pm. The application fee for the admission test is Tk 850.

title: Juba Dal leader expelled over car theft allegation
body:
Jatiyatabadi Juba Dal has expelled the acting office secretary of the Rajshahi city Juba Dal convening committee for violating party discipline.

SM Shafiq Mahmud Tanmoy, leader of the youth font of Bangladesh Nationalist Party, has allegedly taken a car from a workshop garage on the pretext of a trial drive and disappeared with it.

A press release issued by Juba Dal central committee assistant office secretary Minhazul Islam Bhuiyan on Sunday night stated that Tanmoy had been expelled from the party along with his primary membership on clear allegations of involvement in activities against party discipline.

Earlier on Sunday morning, the garage owner, Nur Ahmed, brought the cheating allegation against Tanmoy at a press conference on Sunday.

Nur Ahmed runs a vehicle repair garage in the Bondho Gate area of the city and engaged in buying and selling used vehicles.

He said that Tanmoy visited the garage on November 18 to buy an SUV (Dhaka Metro-G 02-0870) and the price was fixed at Tk 6 lakh.

‘Tanmoy then took the vehicle for a trial drive but did not return. When contacted the following day, Tanmoy allegedly said that he was busy and would respond later,’ he added.

Nur Ahmed said that over the next few days, Tanmoy avoided communication and at one point claimed to be outside the city. Soon after, his phone was switched off.

He alleged that after returning to Rajshahi, Tanmoy allegedly threatened him, saying that no case could be filed against him due to his political position and that he would kill the garage owner if he pursued the matter.

Nur Ahmed said that he went to Rajpara police station on December 14 to file a case, but the officer-in-charge refused to accept it and advised him to seek court remedy.

He later filed a case with the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate’s Court on December 22.

He also said that he legally purchased the vehicle from Md Mizanur Rahman of Lakshmipur area and had all relevant agreements and BRTA documents.

Juba Dal leader Tanmoy called a press conference for Sunday night to refute the allegation against him, but later postponed the press conference.

Contacted over phone, Tanmoy denied the allegation of getting away with the car.

title: Anisul Huq, 5 others sued for laundering Tk 25cr
body:
The Criminal Investigation Department has filed a money laundering case against former law minister Anisul Huq, his girlfriend Taufiqa Karim and four others on charges of extortion and illegal financial transactions amounting to nearly Tk 25 crore.

The CID filed a regular case under Section 4(2) of the Money Laundering Prevention Act, 2012 (amended in 2015) with Bhatara police station on Sunday.

Special superintendent of police-media, CID, Dhaka Jasim Uddin Khan confirmed the matter to BSS.

According to the CID’s financial crime unit, Anisul Huq, Taufiqa Karim, Md Rashedul Kawsar Bhuiyan and Md Kamruzzaman formed an organised crime ring and systematically collected money through illegal means over a long period.

Investigators alleged that the group extorted around Tk 10 lakh every month from various individuals and institutions using accounts of National Bank of Pakistan, Gulshan branch.

The investigation revealed that Md Kamruzzaman, who joined the National Bank of Pakistan as managing director in 2015, regularly transferred funds to Taufiqa Karim’s personal bank account under the guise of a legal consultancy agreement with her law firm—Sirajul Huq Associates.

Until his absconding on August 5, 2024, the group allegedly collected Tk 10.80 crore from the bank alone. Additionally, CID found that Taufiqa Karim’s personal accounts received about Tk 10.60 crore from various individuals and organizations.

CID further stated that after Anisul Huq became law minister, his close aide Taufiqa Karim and Md Rashedul Kawsar Bhuiyan appointed Jiban as his personal assistant.

During this period, they formed an NGO named ‘Legal Assistance to Helpless Prisoners and Persons’. Taufiqa Karim served as its chairperson, Md Rashedul Kawsar Bhuiyan Jiban as secretary general, and Anisul Huq as treasurer.

Investigators found that the NGO collected large amount of money as donations through accounts maintained at Sonali Bank PLC, Supreme Court Branch. From March 11, 2015, to June 30, 2024, Tk 24.53 crore was deposited into the NGO’s accounts.

During the investigation, the Dhaka metropolitan special judge court ordered the freezing of the Tk over 24.53 crore, deposited in 26 bank accounts in the name of complainant Taufiqa Karim.

The case is currently under investigation by the financial crime unit of the CID. Authorities said efforts are ongoing to uncover the full scope of the crime, identify additional suspects, and take further legal action.

The CID reaffirmed its commitment to combating money laundering and financial crimes, stating that all individuals involved in such offenses will be brought to justice.

title: Sri Lanka seal gritty T20 win over Pakistan to level series
body:
Sri Lanka eked out a hard fought 14-run victory over Pakistan in the third T20 at rain-hit Dambulla on Sunday, easing their batting jitters and squaring the three-match series 1-1.

The series, a warm-up for the T20 World Cup with Pakistan set to play all their matches in Sri Lanka due to political tensions with nuclear-armed neighbours India, saw the visitors clinch the opener by six wickets before rain washed out the second game.

‘We were a bit worried about our batting and I'm glad we addressed that today,’ said Wanindu Hasaranga, who walked away with both Player of the Match and Player of the Series honours.

‘The bowlers did a good job too. The ball was wet and it wasn't easy. We tried to bowl wide and slow and asked them to take risks.’

Hasaranga took four wickets in the game and in the process completed 150 wickets in T20Is.

In a contest trimmed to 12 overs a side, Sri Lanka muscled their way to a competitive 160 before choking Pakistan to 146-8.

Having been bowled out inside 20 overs in the series opener, Sri Lanka needed a statement with the bat and duly ticked every box after being put in.

The top order laid the platform and the middle order applied the finishing touches.

Wicket-keeper Kusal Mendis made hay under the Power Play, blasting 30 off 16 balls while Dhananjaya de Silva (22 off 15) and Charith Asalanka (21 off 13) kept the scoreboard ticking.

Skipper Dasun Shanaka then swung the momentum decisively, clubbing 34 off just nine deliveries, peppered with five towering sixes.

The sixth-wicket stand between Shanaka and Janith Liyanage produced 52 runs in just 15 balls and proved the turning point, shifting the game firmly Sri Lanka's way.

Pakistan came out swinging in reply, racing to 50 in just 19 balls with captain Salman Agha hammering 45 off 12 balls, including five fours and three sixes.

But once the field spread, Sri Lanka tightened the screws, applied the choke and forced the asking rate to spiral.

‘We conceded too many runs, but our batting effort was good. Unfortunately, we fell short. We know we are going to play all our World Cup games in Sri Lanka and it's important that we played in similar conditions,’ he added.

title: Kohli surpasses Sangakkara as second-highest scorer
body:
India’s Virat Kohli on Sunday became the second-highest scorer across the three international cricket formats during his match-winning 93 in the first ODI against New Zealand.

Kohli went past Sri Lanka’s Kumar Sangakkara (28,016 runs) to move into second in the list of leading run-scorers in the international game, behind fellow Indian Sachin Tendulkar (34,357).

The top-order batter has 28,068 runs in Test, ODI and T20 cricket since he made his debut for India in an ODI in Sri Lanka in 2008.

‘If I look back at my whole journey then it is nothing short of a dream-come-true for me,’ Kohli said after being named man of the match in Vadodara.

‘I have always known my abilities, but I also knew I had to work extremely hard to get where I am today. God has blessed me with far more than I could ever ask for, I look back at my journey with a lot of grace and gratitude, and I feel really proud of it.’

His 91-ball knock in the ODI opener helped India chase down a victory target of 301 with four wickets and six balls to spare to lead the three-match series 1-0.

But the in-form Kohli missed out on his 54th ODI ton after he registered his fifth 60-plus score in his last five ODI innings, including two hundreds.

‘If I am being brutally honest, the way I’m playing right now, I’m not thinking about milestones at all,’ the former captain said.

‘If we were batting first, I probably would’ve gone harder. But in a chase, with a total on the board, I had to play the situation. I felt like hitting more boundaries, but experience kicks in. The only thing on my mind was getting the team into a position where we could win comfortably.’

Called King Kohli for his prolific run-scoring, the 37-year-old now only plays the ODI format after he and fellow stalwart Rohit Sharma, 38, retired from T20 and Test cricket.

The future of the two stars have been widely debated, with both likely targeting the ODI World Cup in 2027.

title: United knocked out of FA Cup by Brighton
body:
Manchester United crashed out of the FA Cup with a meek 2-1 home defeat to Brighton on Sunday as Gabriel Martinelli's hat-trick fired Arsenal to a 4-1 win at Portsmouth to reach round four.

United interim boss Darren Fletcher could only watch on in horror as the Red Devils' last chance of silverware this season and likely his chances of landing the job until the end of the season went up in smoke at Old Trafford.

Fletcher's men were left to rue not making more of a positive start before Brajan Gruda fired the visitors in front on 12 minutes from Danny Welbeck's cross.

The roles were reversed midway through the second half as Welbeck lashed into the top corner against his former club.

There were persistent chants targeting United co-owners the Glazer family and British billionaire Jim Ratcliffe as the discontent at Old Trafford grew.

And any hope those in charge of the club had for a bounce following the removal of Ruben Amorim has proved very short-lived.

United will play only 40 games this season after exiting both domestic cup competitions at the first hurdle -- their lowest number since 1915.

‘I think you could see the players are fragile but they've got to respond,’ said Fletcher.

‘This team is still good enough to achieve success this season but they have to dig deep.’

Benjamin Sesko's late header set up a grandstand finish, but a red card for teenager Shea Lacey in stoppage time for dissent rounded off United's miserable afternoon.

Martinelli shrugged off the backlash to his clash with stricken Liverpool defender Conor Bradley as Arsenal reached the fourth round for the first time in three years.

Championship side Portsmouth were dreaming of an upset against the Premier League leaders when they went in front after just three minutes through Colby Bishop.

Mikel Arteta had made 10 changes from the side that drew 0-0 with Liverpool on Thursday.

Martinelli drew stinging criticism for trying to push Bradley off the pitch in the closing stages after the Northern Irishman hit the ground with a serious knee injury.

Liverpool confirmed on Sunday the right-back will need surgery and will miss the rest of the season.

The Brazilian apologised to Bradley after the game and did not seem affected by the furore at Fratton Park.

‘That's personality, come in and talk on the pitch,’ said Arteta.

‘To play for a big club you need a big personality because it can be that (being at the centre of a controversial incident), it can be an action that you miss, it can be something that costs you a game, and three days later there is a game, so you need to lift yourself up and make it count.’

Arsenal could rely on their threat from set-pieces to turn the tie around.

The Pompey lead lasted only five minutes as Andre Dozzell turned into his own net under pressure from Christian Norgaard.

Martinelli then flicked in the first of his three goals before Noni Madueke missed the chance to make it 3-1 from the penalty spot when the England international fired wide.

Gabriel Jesus teed up Martinelli to kill the tie off early in the second period before he completed his hat-trick from another Arsenal corner.

West Ham eased the mounting pressure on Nuno Espirito Santo as new signing Taty Castellanos scored his first goal for the club to beat QPR 2-1 after extra-time.

Castellanos has been signed to dig them out of trouble at the bottom of the Premier League and the £26 million ($35 million) arrival from Lazio bulleted home a header from Crysencio Summerville's cross to secure a much-needed win.

Leeds needed a second-half fightback to beat Derby County 3-1 and book their place in the fourth round.

League One Mansfield held off Sheffield United to book their place in round four with a 4-3 win at Bramall Lane.

Norwich, Hull and West Brom also progressed to the last 32.

title: Barca edge Real in thrilling Spanish Super Cup final
body:
Barcelona retained the Spanish Super Cup with a thrilling 3-2 Clasico win over Real Madrid in Saudi Arabia on Sunday.

Raphinha struck twice for the Catalans with Robert Lewandowski also on target as they beat Xabi Alonso's team for a record-extending 16th triumph, despite Frenkie de Jong's late red card.

After Raphinha sent Barcelona ahead Vinicius Junior pulled Madrid level with a fine individual goal to kick-start a frenetic end to the first half in Jeddah.

Lewandowski chipped Barca back in front but Gonzalo Garcia struck deep in stoppage time to send the teams in level at the break.

The battle was decided by a deflected Raphinha effort after 73 minutes, as Barca claimed the fourth trophy of coach Hansi Flick's reign.

His Madrid counterpart Xabi Alonso began with French superstar Kylian Mbappe on the bench after he missed the semi-final win over Atletico with a knee sprain.

His counterpart Hansi Flick, who led Barca to four Clasico wins over Madrid last season in four clashes, opted for Lewandowski up front over Ferran Torres and brought teenage star Lamine Yamal back in on the right wing.

It was a scrappy start in the Saudi evening heat, with Barcelona keeping the ball and Madrid sitting deep to resist them, while looking to find Vinicius Junior on the counter.

The Brazilian had not scored in his previous 16 matches but did offer a potent threat, flying down the left and forcing Joan Garcia into the first save.

Raphinha also sprinted back to slide in on his compatriot as Vinicius tried to break through.

Barca began to turn up the heat on Madrid and Raphinha found a breakthrough after 36 minutes.

Moments after the winger fired a fine chance badly wide, he made up for it with a low, early strike from just inside the area, across Thibaut Courtois and into the bottom corner.

Madrid pulled level with a superb Vinicius strike, floating in from the left, nutmegging Jules Kounde and tucking past Garcia.

Barcelona went back ahead four minutes into first-half stoppage time, with Lewandowski dinking home after being played in by Pedri.

However Madrid rapidly hit back just before the interval through Gonzalo Garcia, who finished well while falling after Dean Huijsen's header bounced back to him off the crossbar.The second half was a calmer affair, with fewer chances as the teams slowed down.

Garcia saved from Rodrygo Goes's low effort, while Courtois beat away a Yamal strike.

Mbappe was warming up on the sideline when Barcelona nosed ahead, with Raphinha's shot from outside the box deflecting in off Raul Asencio to leave Courtois with no chance.

The Brazilian is in superb form and it was his seventh goal in his last five matches across all competitions.

Alonso sent on Mbappe for the last 15 minutes, trying to find a third goal and force a penalty shoot-out.

The French forward could not get a sight of goal but Barca midfielder De Jong was sent off for a high lunge on him.

Despite Madrid's numerical advantage Barca had the best chance in stoppage time with Marcus Rashford firing wide when through on goal.

Asencio might have grabbed an equaliser at the death but headed straight at Garcia.

The last four winners of the Spanish Super Cup have gone on to claim La Liga and Barcelona will be hoping it proves a platform for success once again.

title: Coast Guard arrests 19 robbers in Cox’s Bazar
body:
The Bangladesh Coast Guard arrested 19 robbers along with 1 country-made firearm, 2 rounds of live cartridges and 11 country-made weapons conducting an operation in the Cox’s Bazar sea area on Friday night.

In a press release on Sunday, the Coast Guard said that an organised gang of robbers was stationed in the Kalatali sea area of ​​Cox’s Bazar with the intention of robbing a fishing boat.

Based on the information received, a special operation was conducted in the area by the Coast Guard ship Sabuj Bangla, which was patrolling the sea, at 11:00pm.

During the operation, when a signal was given to stop two suspicious fishing boats, they ignored the signal and tried to escape by turning off their lights.

At this time, when the Coast Guard ship chased the two boats, one boat increased its speed and fled, and another boat fired at the Coast Guard members.

When the Coast Guard members returned fire in self-defence, a member of the robber gang, Md Anis, 40, was shot.

Later, the Coast Guard operation team was able to chase the boat for an hour and arrest it and after searching the seized boat, 19 robbers were arrested along with the firearms.

The injured robber was rescued alive and sent to Cox’s Bazar Sadar Hospital for treatment. On Saturday, the doctor on duty declared the bullet-injured robber dead while undergoing treatment.

The arrested robbers, along with all the seized evidence, were handed over to Cox’s Bazar model police station for further legal action.

title: ULAB, THSnet sign memo to strengthen industry-academia collaboration
body:
The University of Liberal Arts Bangladesh has signed a memorandum of understanding with the United States-based THSnet, Inc on the ULAB campus in Dhaka, marking a step toward strengthening industry-academia collaboration.

The MoU was signed by Azim Fahmi, chairman and CEO of THSnet, Inc, and Professor Muhammad Golam Kibria, head of the department of computer science and engineering at the ULAB, said a press release on Sunday.

This partnership aims to foster meaningful collaboration between THSnet and ULAB in areas such as job and internship opportunities for students, joint capstone projects, collaborative research initiatives and the development of innovative healthcare technologies.

THSnet was represented by Hiron Rahman, managing director. Representing ULAB were Md Foyzul Islam, registrar; Raihan Kibria, senior lecturer; and Md Anowarul Abedin, senior lecturer of the department of CSE.

title: Artist Mahmudul Haque’s death anniv today
body:
Today is the fourth anniversary of death of artist and former Dhaka University professor Mahmudul Haque.

Born at Sreefaltala under Rampal in Bagerhat on January 21, 1945, Mahmudul Haque earned his BFA degree from the then Government Arts and Crafts College and later MFA degree from the University of Tsukuba, Japan. In addition, he received two years of advanced training in printmaking from Japan.

He started his career as a teacher at Dhaka University’s the then fine arts institute in 1969 and retired in 2010.

He served as director of the Fine Arts Institute along with the head of the department of prints and later as director general of Bangladesh National Museum.

Mahmudul Haque’s 39 solo and many joint exhibitions were held both at home and abroad.

title: Chashi Nazrul’s death anniv today
body:
Today is the eleventh anniversary of death of filmmaker and freedom fighter Chashi Nazrul Islam, who is widely known for directing the country’s first feature film on the War of Independence titled Ora Egaro Jan.

Born at Samashpur, Srinagar in Munshiganj on October 23, 1941, Chashi Nazrul Islam directed six films on the war, including Sangram, Kamalpurer Juddha, Hangar Nadi Grenade, Megher Pare Megh and Dhrubatara.

He also directed and gave voice-over to many radio dramas such as Ramer Sumati, Socrates and Sakhina Birangana.

After the independence, Chashi Nazrul started directing films. He directed 22 films and won the National Film Award twice as best director in 1986 and 1997.

Chashi Nazrul Islam passed away in Dhaka on January 11, 2015.

title: DU OSL distributes research methodology programme certificates
body:
The Organisation Strategy and Leadership department of Dhaka University held the certificate distribution ceremony of the fourth batch of research methodology programme at the seminar room of DU MBA Bhaban on Sunday.

DU pro-vice-chancellor, academic, Professor Mamun Ahmed was present as chief guest and distributed certificates among the participants, said a press release.

Presided over by coordinator of research methodology programme Professor Muhammad Shariat Ullah, joint secretary of the research and training division of the Ministry of Planning Sadia Sharmin spoke as special guest at the programme.

Chairperson of the OSL department MdRashedur Rahman delivered welcome speech at the program, which was moderated by the teacher of the department Mehnaz Sadek.

Professor Mamun Ahmed emphasised on contemporary research in higher education and building a knowledge-based society.

Sustainable development, effective policymaking and innovative knowledge creation are not possible without quality research, he said, stating, ‘The proper application of qualitative and quantitative research is one of the prerequisites for knowledge creation.’

Mentioning that methodological skills must be acquired in research, he said, ‘The combination of ethics, analytical skills and critical thinking is very important in research.’

Researchers have to play a responsible role in delivering the benefits of research to society, institutions and policy-making levels, he said, commenting, ‘It is possible to further enrich the quality of research through practical experience and data-based analysis in addition to academic research.’

He also said that through the research methodology programme, students and researchers were acquiring skills in modern research techniques, data analysis and research report preparation, which could make an effective contribution to higher education, professional development and policy-making levels.

title: Photography exhibition under way at Gulshan Lake
body:
Documentary photographer Parvez Ahmed Rony organised an outdoor photography exhibition titled Border that Bleeds, which was set on Gulshan Lake beside the Korail area of Mohakhali in the capital.

A selection of seven photographs from Rony’s long-time project, which depicts the border killing by the Indian Border Security Force (BSF), was inaugurated on January 9 as part of an exhibition.

In memory of Felani Khatun, who was killed by the BSF on 7 January 2011, Rony has worked on this issue of border with India and Bangladesh from 2012 to 2025. Since the killing of Felani, the BSF has brutally killed about 1400 civilian Bangladeshi citizens along the India-Bangladesh border.

‘The outdoor exhibition aims to raise awareness among people regarding the issues. The exhibition is set on the Gulshan Lake, where people of diverse living standards dwell on the banks of the lake and there is hope that all will raise voice against the border killing,’ Rony said, adding that he wanted mass involvement with his photographs so he chose outdoor exhibitions.

Parvez Ahmad Rony worked as a photojournalist for over a decade, covering social, political and environmental issues of the region.

title: SAU sets up agri lab of ecophysiology
body:
The country’s first Agro Ecophysiology Laboratory has been officially inaugurated at Sher-e-Bangla Agricultural University.

The lab was inaugurated by SAU vice-chancellor Professor Md Abdul Latif at a ceremony presided over by Wave Foundation executive director Mohsin Ali organised at the university’s Dr Kazi M Badruduzza Research Centre.

At the inauguration ceremony, the vice-chancellor thanked Palli Karmasahayak Foundation and Wave Foundation and said that this lab would open new horizons in agriculture-related research.

Under the Rural Micro-Enterprise Transformation Project of Wave Foundation, the lab was set up in the Department of Agricultural Botany of SAU. The lab is under the overall supervision of Professor Muhammad Mahbub Islam and Professor AKM Ruhul Amin.

Professor Mahbub Islam said that modern equipment including microbalance, plant and soil desiccation system, flame photometer, plant oven and conductivity meter have been added to the lab.

Through the equipment, it will be possible to determine the levels of various nutrients and harmful elements in soil and plants, check the sensitivity of plants in adverse environments, improve soil health and increase crop productivity and nutritional value by applying smart agricultural technology and nanotechnology.

MS and PhD level students use this lab in their research. This is the first Agro Ecophysiology Laboratory in Bangladesh, the professors said.

SAU pro-vice-chancellor Professor Md Belal Hossain, treasurer Professor Muhammad Abul Bashar and PKSF deputy managing director Akand Md Rafiqul Islam were present as special guests at the event.

SAU Faculty of Agriculture dean Professor AMM Shamsuzzaman, director (planning and development) Professor Md Sarwar Hossain, dean (postgraduate) Professor M Salahuddin Mahmud Chowdhury, director of research FM Aminur Rahman, assistant director of Wave Foundation Nirmal Das, along with teachers, researchers and officials from deferent faculties of the university were also present.

title: Country turns unwelcoming to migratory birds
body:
Wetland depletion driven by agricultural expansion, rapid urbanisation, commercial fish farming and pollution is degrading the habitats of migratory birds that arrive in Bangladesh each winter, researchers warn.

Officials of the Bangladesh Bird Club said that about 20 per cent fewer migratory birds arrived in the country in 2025 than in 2024.

‘Migratory birds are not getting the food they rely on,’ said the club’s general secretary ABM Sarowar Alam, also wildlife biologist at the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) Bangladesh.

Every winter, millions of birds travel thousands of kilometres through the Central Asian and East Asian–Australasian flyways, from Siberia and Central Asia to warmer parts of South Asia and beyond, according to the Convention on the Conservation of Migratory Species of Wild Animals.

The journey depends on intact wetlands, riverine forests and coastal mangroves that serve as crucial stopover sites for rest and refuelling.

Bangladesh lies on both flyways and supports around 240 migratory bird species, including globally threatened ones such as the painted stork, spoon-billed sandpiper, Eurasian oystercatcher, Indian skimmer, great knot and greater spotted eagle, according to the IUCN Red List of Bangladesh.

Bangladeshi ornithologist Sayam U Chowdhury, a researcher at the Conservation Research Institute of the University of Cambridge, said that the shrunk and polluted water bodies were destroying habitats and food resources during the birds’ non-breeding season.

Sarowar said the wetlands for migratory birds were decreasing as haor basins were leased out for commercial fish farming, while low-lying ridges were increasingly used for cattle and poultry rearing.

A joint Bangladesh Bird Club–IUCN study found that Tanguar Haor witnessed 59 migratory bird species between 2008 and 2021.

Another study published in 2021 found that about one-third of shallow-water area of Tanguar Haor was converted into agricultural land between 1989 and 2017.

Along the coast, mudflats are being transformed into hard land through afforestation and climate-related processes, Sarowar said.

A 2025 study identified unplanned fishing, tourism, agricultural expansion, hunting and pollution as major threats for migratory birds in south-central coastal areas.

Sayam U Chowdhury said protecting migratory water birds required stronger management of both freshwater and coastal wetlands.

‘Conservation efforts must protect remaining wetlands, restore degraded ones, and balance biodiversity needs with food production and climate resilience,’ he said.

As part of contributing to conservation-related policymaking, the Bangladesh Bird Club and IUCN launched a coastal bird survey on January 10, while surveys in haor areas and the Sundarbans

are expected to be completed by February, said Sarowar.

title: 3 people, 5 orgs get DNCC Nagorik Padak
body:
The Dhaka North City Corporation has announced the winners of the Nagorik Padak–2025 in recognition of their outstanding contributions to social service, technological innovation, environmental protection and humanitarian activities.

The awards were presented at a grand ceremony held at the DNCC Nagar Bhaban conference room in Gulshan-2 in the capital Sunday morning.

According to a DNCC press release, the award was conferred on three individuals and five reputed organisations in eight different categories this year.

The awarded are Abdur Rashid Sohag, founder and chief executive of Pupil School Bus Limited, in inventor and start-up category; Sruti Rani Dey in personal entrepreneurship; Hawa Begum in advocacy; Uplift Bangladesh in social media content creation; Bhasantek School and College as an environment-friendly institution; Uttara Public Library as a social organisation; PA Foundation for animal protection and the Bangladesh Water Development Board as the highest taxpayer.

LGRD and cooperatives and housing and public works adviser Adilur Rahman Khan, and adviser for environment, forest and climate change Syeda Rizwana Hasan attended the ceremony while DNCC administrator Mohammad Ejaz presided over it.

Award recipient Sohag has introduced the country’s first integrated transport system by developing a technology-based solution to ensure the safe transportation of school-going students in Dhaka and Chattogram.

Some 7,000 students from more than 45 educational institutions are receiving this service through GPS tracking and a mobile app, which is also playing a significant role in reducing traffic congestion and carbon emissions in the cities.

Sruti Rani has set an example in society by actively engaging in tree plantation, cleanliness drives and preventing 12 child marriages.

Uplift Bangladesh has earned wide appreciation for producing documentary content on urban infrastructure and development over the past five years.

Bhasantek School and College has been nurturing a spirit of environmental stewardship among its students since 1980, which earned it the award this year. The institution has long been contributing to the promotion of human values and environmental awareness alongside academic education.

Uttara Public Library has built a strong cultural circle by developing reading habits and recognising distinguished individuals.

PA Foundation received the award for its long-standing role in rescuing endangered animals, providing treatment and protecting animal rights.

Cyclone Sidr-affected Hawa Begum was honoured for her courageous role in protecting the rights of marginalised people and working for their livelihood development in the Advocacy category.

The DNCC honoured the BWDB for its significant contribution to state revenue, as the organisation paid more than Tk 3.89 crore in taxes during the last financial year.

title: Yunus to work on healthcare, youth dev after polls
body:
Chief adviser Professor Muhammad Yunus on Sunday said that his post-election work would focus primarily on three areas - digital healthcare development, youth development and ‘Three Zero’ agenda.

He revealed it as Akie Abe, head of Foundation for Encouragement of Social Contribution, sought to know about the chief adviser’s plans and priorities for the period following the 13th national election at a meeting at the state guest house Jamuna in Dhaka.

Later, chief adviser’s deputy press secretary Mohammad Abul Kalam Azad Majumder briefed the media about the meeting at the Foreign Service Academy, saying that Akie Abe, also wife of late Japanese prime minister Shinzo Abe, is currently visiting Bangladesh leading a delegation over work of her foundation.

During the meeting, Yunus recalled his warm and sincere relationship he had shared with her husband Shinzo Abe, who was assassinated in 2022.

The chief adviser also informed Akie Abe that following the election on February 12, he is scheduled to visit Japan in the third week of March at the invitation of the Sasakawa Foundation.

During the visit, he will participate in a conference organised by the foundation, which conducts research on various issues, particularly ocean research.

Yunus said, during his visit, he will also discuss ways to enhance collaboration between Bangladesh and the foundation in these areas.

title: Charge hearing begins against Joy, Palak
body:
The prosecution at the International Crimes Tribunal-1on Sunday pleaded to frame charges in a crimes against humanity case against ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina’s son and former ICT affairs adviser Sajeeb Wazed Joy and state minister for ICT division Zunaid Ahmed Palak.

Chief prosecutor Muhammad Tajul Islam took part in the hearing in the morning. Later, the tribunal adjourned the hearing till January 15. The defence is scheduled to argue for their discharge petition on that day.

Palak’s counsel, Liton Ahmed and state-defence counsel for fugitive Sajeeb Wazed Joy, Manjur Alam, were present at the court during the hearing.

On December 4, the tribunal issued an arrest warrant against Joy after taking into cognisance the formal charge brought against Joy and Palak.

According to the formal charge, Joy and Palak are accused of shutting down nationwide internet services during the July uprising, allegedly facilitating the commission of crimes against humanity.

‘Palak, being the state minister for the ICT Division at the time, gave a status and made a post on his verified Facebook account after getting approval from prime minister Sheikh Hasina’s ICT affairs adviser Sajeeb Wazed Joy, thereby instigating unprecedented attacks on agitating students and people by police and Chhatra League cadres,’ the prosecution said.

Tajul Islam said Palak, following the order and approval from Joy, first reduced the speed of mobile internet services and subsequently shut them down to create an opportunity to detain, torture and kill the protesters.

‘He then gave a false statement regarding the internet shutdown and later blocked several social networking sites, including WhatsApp, Facebook and TikTok, to keep the world in the dark about the horrific crimes taking place at the time. The conspiracy to block the internet originated from Sajeeb Wazed Joy. He made the decision after taking advice from his mother, Sheikh Hasina, and Palak executed the decision,’ the prosecution added.

The tribunal’s investigation agency submitted the probe report against the accused on December 3, 2025.

title: 431 decimals of land of S Alam, others seized
body:
A Dhaka court on Sunday ordered the seizure of 431 decimals of land registered in the names of S Alam Group owner Saiful Alam and other individuals related to his interest.

Dhaka metropolitan senior special judge Md Sabbir Faiz passed the order allowing an application filed by the Anti-Corruption Commission.

The court also ordered the freezing of 41 bank accounts of former Rajshahi City Corporation AHM Khairuzzaman Liton, his wife Shahin Akter Rini, daughters Anika Fariha Zaman and Maisha Samiha Zaman, allowing a petition filed by Criminal Investigation Department inspector Mohammad Kamruzzaman.

According to the ACC plea, a joint investigation team has been formed to investigate and submit report to the commission over allegations of money laundering against Saiful Alam, his interest-related entities, and individuals linked to those entities.

It was alleged that Saiful Alam and his family members, along with interest-related entities and associated individuals, illegally obtained loans in their own names and in the names of others from various banks in violation of rules. Thus they embezzled the funds and acquired a huge amount of assets at home and abroad in their own names and in the names of their family members.

During the inquiry, information received from various sources revealed that Saiful Alam and his family members were attempting to transfer, shift, or dispose of the interest-related immovable properties.

Therefore, it is necessary to urgently attach the immovable properties of Saiful Alam, his family members, his interest-related entities, and individuals associated with those entities, the plea added.

The CID plea stated that allegations have been brought against former RCC mayor Liton, his interest-related persons and institutions over abnormal and suspicious transactions through bank accounts in Dhaka and elsewhere, involving organised crime and money laundering under the Money Laundering Prevention Act, 2012.

Evidence suggests that the accused transferred proceeds of crime through bank accounts, acquired assets and used the money for luxurious consumption. As the investigation is ongoing, the CID said 41 bank accounts need to be frozen to prevent withdrawal, laundering or transfer of the crime-derived money.

title: Cold feels harsher as day temperature drops
body:
Although the cold wave sweeping over parts of Bangladesh remains mild to moderate, people are feeling unusually cold as daytime temperatures continue to fall, narrowing the gap between day and night temperatures.

According to the Bangladesh Meteorological Department’s analysis of over 50 years’ data, the difference between day and night temperatures — historically about 10 degree Celsius in winter — has shrunk sharply this season, at times dropping to as low as 1.7C amid a steady decline in daytime temperatures.

Meteorological data show that over recent decades, Dhaka’s average daytime temperature has declined by about 0.1C a decade, while nighttime temperature has increased by about 0.5C, with variations across districts.

At the same time, the duration of cold waves has shortened, as they are now starting later in the season, meteorologists said.

BMD senior meteorologist Bazrul Rashid said that the current cold wave was mild to moderate and typical for January, traditionally the coldest month of the year in Bangladesh.

Bangladesh’s all-time lowest temperature — 2.6C — was recorded at Tetulia in Panchagarh on January 8, 2018, breaking the previous record of 2.8C set at Sreemangal in Moulvibazar in 1968.

This season’s lowest temperature, however, was 6.8C, recorded at Tetulia, on Friday.

Bazrul said that although temperatures below 5C were recorded in past winters, the cold felt less severe then.

‘People are feeling colder now because the difference between day and night temperatures has narrowed,’ he said.

‘Earlier, the coldest temperatures were usually at night, when people stayed indoors with warmer clothing,’ he said.

People begin to feel cold when ambient temperatures fall below the body’s comfort zone — generally under 24C — and that prolonged exposure to similar low temperatures during the day increases discomfort, as people remain outdoors for work and daily activities, he explained.

Historically, the gap between minimum and maximum temperatures in winter stood at about 10C, according to BMD records.

On December 29, 2025, the BMD recorded the lowest temperature gap between day and night at 1.7C.

The BMD recorded day temperature 15.5 C when night temperature was 13.8C.

The department currently monitors weather through 48 stations nationwide, compared with 15 observatories in the region in 1947.

In Dhaka, the lowest temperature on record is 9.5C, measured on January 8, 2018, during a severe cold wave.

Meteorological records show that in the 1980s, cold waves typically began in early December in northern districts and reached Dhaka in January. Since 2020, however, cold waves have been arriving at least two weeks later than usual.

BMD assistant meteorologist Kazi Zebunnesa said that widespread smoky air — particularly severe in the capital Dhaka — had been blocking sunlight, keeping daytime temperatures lower.

She said that air pollution mixing with fog had created a persistent haze in many areas, preventing daytime warming.

Daily Air Quality Index readings showed most districts recording unhealthy to very unhealthy air since the start of the year, with Dhaka repeatedly ranking among the world’s most polluted cities.

In Bangladesh, the AQI is measured using five pollutants — PM10, PM2.5, nitrogen dioxide, carbon monoxide, sulphur dioxide and ozone.

Air quality typically deteriorates in winter and improves during the monsoon.

title: Arbitration Council permission mandatory for polygamy: HC
body:
The High Court has upheld Section 6 of the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance, 1961, ruling that a husband must obtain permission from an Arbitration Council before contracting another marriage to protect the rights of existing wives.

The court rejected a public interest litigation filed by Supreme Court lawyer Ishrat Hasan, holding that the provision does not violate the fundamental rights of women.

The verdict was delivered on August 20, 2025 by a bench of Justice Fahmida Quader and Justice Sayed Jahed Mansur, with a certified copy made available on December 11, 2025.

Earlier in 2021, the High Court asked the government to explain why the existing process for allowing a second marriage without ensuring equal rights among wives should not be declared unconstitutional and why guidelines on polygamy should not be framed to protect family life.

In its final verdict, the court holds that Section 6 sets legal safeguards for women by requiring prior approval from an Arbitration Council, consisting of a chairperson and representatives of both the husband and the existing wife or wives.

The law makes it obligatory for the husband to state valid reasons for the proposed marriage and to disclose whether the existing wife or wives have given consent.

The Arbitration Council must assess whether the proposed marriage is necessary and just, giving special importance to the views of the wife or wives, and must record reasons for granting or refusing permission.

Any aggrieved wife has the right to challenge the council’s decision before an assistant judge so that judicial oversight is ensured, while constitutional remedies remain available under the writ jurisdiction.

The court in its final verdict observes that the permission process is neither arbitrary nor discriminatory and does not curtail the legal rights of women or men.

It has also found no violation of the constitutional guarantees of equality and justice under Articles 27 and 28, noting that the law balances religious principles with safeguards for women.

The court notes that under Hanafi School applicable in Bangladesh, polygamy is allowed only when justice and financial capacity can be ensured, and is discouraged where fairness cannot be guaranteed.

The judgment also referred to international examples, noting that some Muslim-majority countries, including Tunisia and Turkey, have banned polygamy through legislation to protect women’s rights.

The High Court has also observed that a clear policy decision—either strictly regulating polygamy under Islamic principles or prohibiting it altogether—could reduce legal uncertainty and strengthen protection of women’s rights.

title: Canada’s Carney plans to talk trade, relations during China visit
body:
Prime minister Mark Carney on Tuesday will begin a state visit to China, the first in eight years for a Canadian leader, with aims to talk trade and rebuild ties after years of diplomatic tensions.

Chinese President Xi Jinping invited Carney last October during a meeting on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, which Carney described as a ‘turning point’ in the two nations’ strained relationship.

The January 13-17 trip seeks to ‘strengthen cooperation in the areas of trade, energy, agriculture and international security,’ a Carney spokeswoman told AFP.

‘It’s a huge step forward,’ said Gordon Houlden, a former Canadian diplomat and director of the University of Alberta’s China Institute.

Houlden told AFP that if ‘some of the commercial problems that are affecting our exports had a political origin, then solving the political origin may, or should, have some positive effect on the trade.’

The last Canadian leader to visit China was Justin Trudeau, in December 2017.

Ties withered in 2018 after the arrest of a senior executive from Chinese tech giant Huawei on a US warrant in Vancouver and China’s retaliatory detention of two Canadians on espionage charges.

China has also been accused of interfering in Canadian elections in recent years.

Carney will meet with Chinese premier Li Qiang and business leaders for the trade negotiations, which will focus on efforts to attract new investors and secure strategic partnerships.

In the face of protectionism and attacks from US President Donald Trump, he also will seek to develop new markets in order to lessen Canada’s economic dependence on its neighbour to the south.

China is currently Canada’s second-largest trade partner, with bilateral trade reaching $118.7 billion Canadian dollars ($85.3 billion) in 2024.

‘This visit is important because China is obviously an inescapable superpower,’ Guy Saint-Jacques, Canada’s ambassador to China from 2012-2016, told AFP.

He said a deal on Chinese energy supplies and electric vehicles were possible outcomes from the talks.

But ‘the elephant in the room,’ he mentioned, is the thorny issue of tariffs.

Since the summer of 2024, Ottawa and Beijing have clashed on trade, with Canada imposing tariffs on electric vehicles and Chinese steel, while Beijing has retaliated with levies on agricultural products including canola.

‘Whatever agreements Canada has with China will be scrutinized in Washington and might have implications’ for three-way talks with Washington and Mexico on a free trade agreement, set to be renegotiated this year, said Vina Nadjibulla, vice president of the Asia Pacific Foundation of Canada.

Carney’s challenge is ‘going to be to advance economic objectives while not sacrificing our national security and economic security priorities,’ she added.

After his trip to Beijing, Carney is scheduled to travel to Qatar for a bilateral visit and then head to Switzerland to attend the World Economic Forum annual meeting in Davos.

title: Community Bank partners with BB to promote entrepreneurship
body:
Community Bank Bangladesh PLC signed a memorandum of understanding with the Bangladesh Bank’s SME and Special Programmes Department to implement Entrepreneurship Development Programme under the Skills for Industry Competitiveness and Innovation Program of the Finance Division.

Bangladesh Bank deputy governor Nurun Nahar and executive director Husne Ara Shikha were present at the signing ceremony held at Jahangir Alam Conference Room of the central bank on January 8, said a press release.

On behalf of BB, director Nawshad Mustafa and programme director and SMESPD additional director Md Nazrul Islam signed the agreement.

Community Bank managing director (current charge) Kimiwa Saddat signed the MoU on behalf of the bank.

Also present at the event were Bangladesh Bank’s Mohammad Wasim, deputy programme director – programmes and joint director, Muhammad Ariful Islam, coordinator – programmes and deputy director, and Community Bank’s Hossain-Al-Safeer Chowdhury, head of SME, and Sharif Hasan Mamun, head of agriculture.

title: Modhumoti Bank hosts annual business confce
body:
Modhumoti Bank PLC held three-day ‘Annual Business Conference 2026’ at Sayeman Beach Resort in Cox’s Bazar, said a press release.

Chairman Humayun Kabir was present as chief guest at the conference that took place from January 8 to January 10.

Executive committee chairman Salahuddin Alamgir, board members Sultana Jahan and A Mannan Khan were present as special guests.

In the conference, all KPIs of the bank were thoroughly discussed, and a strategic business plan for the year 2026 was set to achieve the target.

Managing director and chief executive officer Md Shafiul Azam, additional managing director Shahnawaj Chowdhury and deputy managing director and chief business officer Arab Fazlur Rahman were present.

Among others, management committee members, divisional heads of head office, branch managers, sub-branch in-charges and other senior officials of the bank attended the event.

title: Islami Bank begins rebranding mCash
body:
Islami Bank Bangladesh PLC on Sunday launched rebranding activities of ‘mCash,’ the bank’s mobile financial service, said a press release.

Bangladesh Bank governor Ahsan H Mansur inaugurated the activities as chief guest at an event at Pan Pacific Sonargaon Hotel in the capital.

Islami Bank chairman M Zubaidur Rahman presided over the programme, while BB executive director Arief Hossain Khan was present as a special guest.

Islami Bank managing director Md Omar Faruk Khan delivered the welcome speech.

Among others, Islami Bank executive committee chairman Mohammad Khurshid Wahab, audit committee chairman Md Abdus Salam, risk management committee chairman M Masud Rahman and independent director Md Abdul Jalil attended the event.

Senior executives of the head offices of the Bangladesh Bank and Islami Bank and all head of zones and branches of the bank were present at the time.

Ahsan H Mansur said that more than 3 crore customers were connected with Islami Bank, adding that mCash must be moved forward by utilising Islami Bank’s large network of 400 branches, 271 sub-branches, and approximately 2,800 agent outlets.

mCash should also be utilised in the remittance flow of Islami Bank, he said.

He said that to strengthen mCash, long-term plans must be adopted and customer trust must be earned.

He added, ‘We want the Mobile Financial Services market not to remain monopoly but to expand further. This is convenient for the country’s economy and the customers.’

M Zubaidur Rahman said that with 30 million customers, Islami Bank’s mCash would surpass competitors.

He called upon everyone to encourage mCash transactions.

title: Walton celebrates winning ICSB, ICMAB awards
body:
Walton has received ‘ICSB National Award for Corporate Governance Excellence’ for five consecutive times and ‘ICMAB Best Corporate Award’ for four consecutive times, said a press release.

Walton Hi-Tech Industries PLC, Superbrand, attributed the achievements to its manufacturing of world-class, environment-friendly, innovative and state-of-the-art technology products while it also ensuring strong corporate governance through discipline, transparency and accountability in overall management and publication of financial reports.

To mark these achievements, Walton arranged a grand event titled ‘Celebrating Corporate Award Achievements’ at Walton’s Corporate office at Bashundhara in the capital on Saturday.

BB deputy governor Md Habibur Rahman attended the celebration function as chief guest while Investment Corporation of Bangladesh chairman Abu Ahmed was present as a special guest.

Walton Hi-Tech Industries vice-chairman SM Ashraful Alam, managing director SM Mahbubul Alam and other officials of the company attended the event.

At the function, Walton Hi-Tech deputy managing director and company secretary Md Rafiqul Islam gave the welcome speech.

Md Habibur Rahman said that in terms of product quality, state-of-the-art technology, and affordable pricing, Walton was ahead of many global brands.

He added that Walton’s contribution to Bangladesh’s economy was significant. By breaking the dominance of foreign brands in the market, Walton has reduced import dependency and now it has been earning a large amount of foreign currency by exporting products to many countries, he said.

Abu Ahmed said that Walton’s factory was well-managed and its workforce and production capacity are extensive.

He noted that even 15 years ago, the electronics market in Bangladesh was dominated by foreign brands, but Walton had changed that picture.

SM Mahbubul Alam said that Walton followed proper compliance across all areas — from its factory establishments to production processes, workplace management, financial reporting, tax payment and corporate governance.

While delivering his closing remarks, SM Ashraful Alam said that Walton never compromised on compliance issues.

Walton maintains proper compliance across workplace practices, production, financial reports and tax payments, he said.

title: RYDO introduces eco-friendly electric scooters
body:
RYDO, the electric scooter brand of leading business conglomerate RFL, has made its debut at the Dhaka International Trade Fair, showcasing eco-friendly scooters at affordable prices for the first time.

The company is displaying 9 models of scooters with attractive designs in Pavilion number 23 in the main building of the fair, said a press release.

The main attraction of the ‘RYDO’ stall is the electric scooter priced at just Tk 49,000.

Although the market price of the ‘RYDO’ Leaf model scooter is Tk 55,000, a special discount of Tk 6000 is being offered on the occasion of the fair.

With its attractive design and affordable price, the model has quickly become a centre of interest among young visitors.

RYDO head of marketing, Shariful Islam, said, ‘The company is showcasing various scooter models under the ‘RYDO DITF Fest’ at the trade fair, priced between Tk 55,000 and Tk 1.45 lakh. The scooters are drawing strong customer interest, with discounts of up to Tk 14,000, gifts, surprise coupons, and pre-booking now open.’

He added that the BRTA-approved RYDO scooters feature modern designs, powerful motors, long battery life, and can run at a cost of just 11 paisa per kilometre, making them an affordable and eco-friendly transport option for both urban and rural areas.

PRAN-RFL marketing director Kamruzzaman Kamal said the rising global and local demand for eco-friendly electric scooters has inspired the launch of RYDO in Bangladesh.

He added that RYDO e-scooters offer an affordable and comfortable solution for both urban and rural transportation.

title: MTB Foundation hands over blankets to Cadet College Club
body:
MTB Foundation, as part of its corporate social responsibility initiatives, has recently handed over blankets to Cadet College Club Limited for distribution amongst underprivileged cold-affected people of different regions of the country.

Mutual Trust Bank PLC chairman Rashed Ahmed Chowdhury handed over the blankets to Cadet College Club president Md Ishtiaque Zahir (Titas) at a ceremony held at CCCL premises in Purbachal, said a press release.

MTB deputy managing director and CAMLCO Rais Uddin Ahmad, infrastructure division head Amitav Kaiser, MTB Foundation chief executive officer Samia Chowdhury, former CCCL president Tariq Abul Ala and director — administration and service Tahmina Rahman were present.

Other senior officials of both the organisations were also present on the occasion.

title: Takaful Islami’s investment body holds 12th meeting

Takaful Islami Insurance PLC’s investment committee held its 12th meeting on January 8, said a press release.

Investment committee chairman Md Masudur Rahman presided over the meeting.

The meeting was attended by committee members Tahmina Afroz, Khandaker Mesbahuddin Ahmed, Raihan Kabir, Md Iqbal Hossain and ABM Kaikobad.

Chief executive officer Abul Kalam Azad, additional managing director Mohammad Selim, CFO Mohammad Mamunul Islam and company secretary Mohammad Saheen Miah were also present in the meeting.

title: Cultivation of colourful cauliflower brings smiles to farmers in Khulna
body:
Farmers in Dumuria Upazila of Khulna district are passing a busy time marketing cauliflower as bumper production of yellow cauliflower has brought happiness to them this season.

According to local farmers, favourable weather, timely sowing of seeds and balanced use of fertiliser have resulted in a good yield of cauliflower, particularly the yellow variety.

Low production cost and higher profit margins have made cauliflower cultivation increasingly popular in the area.

The locally produced yellow cauliflower is meeting local demand and is also being supplied to different districts across the country.

Farmers said they are getting good market prices, which has further boosted their confidence.

Data from the Department of Agricultural Extension show that despite various weather challenges this season, an ideal farmer of Khaniya area, Abu Hanif Morol, earned around Tk 1 lakh in profit by cultivating yellow cauliflower on 33 decimals of land.

Besides, he is also engaged in cultivating a variety of winter vegetables.

The agriculture department said yellow cauliflower has been cultivated on about one hectare of land in Dumuria this season.

Thanks to favourable conditions and proper management, bumper yields have been achieved.

Farmers of the upazila said that profit from winter vegetables, especially yellow cauliflower, has encouraged more growers to engage in such cultivation, even amid natural adversities this year.

Dumuria Upazila Agriculture officer Md Nazmul Huda said about 280 hectares of land have been brought under cauliflower cultivation in Dumuria this season, which is significantly higher than last year.

‘Compared to previous years, cauliflower production is much higher this time, and the good yield of yellow cauliflower has put smiles on farmers’ faces,’ he added.

Farmer Abu Hanif Morol said coloured cauliflower -- especially yellow or orange varieties have emerged as a new and profitable trend in Bangladesh’s agriculture.

He noted that the variety, often known as ‘Carotina Yellow,’ contains higher beta-carotene than traditional white cauliflower and enjoys stronger market demand, enabling farmers to earn better returns within a short cultivation period.

Farmers of Magurghona Union of Dumuria Upazila have successfully cultivated coloured cauliflower. Purple, yellow, and broccoli variety cauliflowers have been cultivated in different areas in Khulna.

Shahdat Hossain and Babita Sarkar, farmers of Magurghona union of Dumuriaupazila said, ‘We have experimentally cultivated colourful cauliflower on 20 bighas of land for the second time.’

The price of white cauliflower is Tk 20 to Tk 25 per kilogram (KG) whereas we can sell the yellow, purple cauliflower at Tk 60 to Tk70 per KG. I am very happy with the profit. I will extend the farming land area for the cultivation of the colourful cauliflower in next season, they said.

Besides, we got cauliflower seeds, chemical fertilizers, organic fertilizers, organic herbicides and pesticides free of cost from the government, he added.

Md Rafiqul Islam, additional director of Khulna Agriculture Zone told BSS today that we wanted to justify how suitable the soil and weather exists for the coloured cauliflower farming with a view to make the land suitable for colourful cauliflower farming in future.

‘We have provided cauliflower seeds, chemical fertilizers, organic fertilizers, organic herbicides, pesticides, and necessary advice to the farmers, he said, adding that after getting the good cauliflower seeds and fertilizer, the farmers achieved success. The farmers have got better profit,’ he said.

As a result, local vegetable farmers have become interested in cultivation of colourful cauliflower. The local agriculture department is also very pleased for the success of farming colourful cauliflower, he said.

In the next season, if any farmer wants to cultivate colourful cauliflower, all kinds of support and cooperation will be provided by the Agriculture Department, he said.

Besides, we always provide technical support to the farmers to make the colourful cauliflower farming more profitable, he added.

title: HTC returns to Bangladesh with Wildfire E7 Life launch
body:
Mobile phone brand HTC has made a comeback in Bangladesh, with its devices now being locally manufactured, said a press release.

HTC’s new model, the Wildfire E7 Life, is now available now on the market. The smartphone is being manufactured and marketed by local company Salextra Limited.

The HTC Wildfire E7 Life is positioned as an affordable smartphone. It is powered by a Unisoc Tiger T615 octa-core processor and features a 6.745-inch HD+ display with waterdrop notch and in-cell technology, offering a 120Hz refresh rate and up to 480 nits of brightness.

The handset comes with a 50MP + 0.08MP dual rear camera setup along with an 8MP front camera.

The device is equipped with 6GB RAM and 128GB internal storage, a 5,000mAh battery, and runs on Android 16.

It is available in two colour variants: Grey and Champagne Gold.

Mamun Khan, head of marketing at Salextra Limited, said that the HTC Wildfire E7 Life offered strong value in its segment.

‘At this price point, the HTC Wildfire E7 Life is one of the most powerful and attractive smartphones currently available in the Bangladeshi market,’ he said.

‘The 50MP camera, along with its overall feature set, gives it a competitive edge. Local manufacturing has also allowed us to ensure quality while keeping the price affordable for consumers,’ he added.

Founded in Taiwan in 1997, HTC launched the world’s first touchscreen wireless handset within a year of its establishment, the release said.

The company later began producing Windows Mobile–based PDAs and smartphones in 2004, releasing them under the HTC brand in 2006. In 2008, HTC gained global

recognition as the pioneer of Android smartphones with the launch of the HTC Dream (T-Mobile G1), the world’s first Android phone.

Although HTC’s global market share declined amid intense competition from Apple and Samsung, the brand is now aiming to reclaim its position through strategic markets such as Bangladesh.

title: NRB Bank, BB sign deal for start-up refinancing fund
body:
NRB Bank PLC signed a participation agreement with the Bangladesh Bank for lending to the SME customers under refinancing start-up fund of Tk 500 crore with a view to fostering entrepreneurship and supporting emerging business ventures across the country.

Under this agreement, NRB Bank will extend loans to start-up entrepreneurs on easy terms through the Bangladesh Bank’s refinancing facility, said a press release.

Alongside financing, the bank will help entrepreneurs to manage and scale up their businesses more effectively.

The signing ceremony took place at Jahangir Alam Conference Hall of the central bank on January 6.

NRB Bank deputy managing director Md Shaheen Howlader and Bangladesh Bank SMESPD director Nawshad Mustafa signed the agreement.

BB deputy governor Nurun Nahar was present as chief guest. Executive director Husne Ara Shikha was also present in the event.

Other senior officials from both the organisations were also present at the event.

title: India eyes new markets with US trade deal limbo
body:
India is aggressively seeking trade deals to open markets for exporters and soften the blow of steep US tariffs, as efforts to secure an agreement with Washington remain elusive.

Relations between Washington and New Delhi plummeted in August after president Donald Trump raised tariffs to 50 per cent, a blow that threatens job losses and hurts India’s ambition of becoming a manufacturing and export powerhouse.

That pressure, experts say, has pushed New Delhi into a rapid diversification drive beyond its biggest market.

On Sunday, German chancellor Friedrich Merz left for India for a visit to bolster economic and security ties between the top EU economy and the Asian population giant.

Both Berlin and New Delhi face a turbulent world order and a set of economic and geopolitical challenges from the world’s two largest economies, the United States and China.

Merz’s visit from Monday — his first to an Asian country since he took office last May — comes two weeks ahead of a planned EU-India summit and as India and the bloc are working on a free trade agreement.

‘This agreement is envisioned not just as a trade deal, but as a comprehensive partnership that addresses modern economic realities,’ India’s commerce ministry said on Friday.

During Merz’s two-day visit, prime minister Narendra Modi will host him in Ahmedabad, in the premier’s western home state of Gujarat, before Merz travels to the southern technology hub of Bengaluru.

The two leaders will attend a traditional kite festival and visit the Sabarmati Ashram, the spiritual retreat where Mahatma Gandhi, the leader of the Indian independence struggle, lived for many years.

That Merz chose India for his first trip to Asia as chancellor ‘demonstrates how India, the world’s largest democracy, is an important strategic partner for Germany,’ a government spokesman said on Friday in Berlin.

European Commission president Ursula von der Leyen and European Council president Antonio Costa will be in New Delhi on January 26 for India’s annual Republic Day parade.

India signed or operationalised four trade agreements last year, including a major pact with Britain — the fastest pace of dealmaking it has seen in years — and is now eyeing fresh deals.

Negotiations are underway with the European Union, the Eurasian Economic Union, Mexico, Chile and the South American Mercosur trade bloc, either for new deals or to expand existing agreements.

If successful, India would have trade arrangements with ‘almost every major economy’, said Ajay Srivastava, from the New Delhi-based Global Trade Research Initiative (GTRI).

Srivastava said 2025 was ‘one of the most active years’ for trade agreements, which he said aimed to ‘spread risk’ rather than to pivot from Washington.

For India and Germany, security links could also be bolstered by a potential deal for German’s Thyssenkrupp Marine Systems to build six submarines for the Indian Navy in a partnership with Indian state-run Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders.

That deal remains under negotiation, but would allow India to replace its ageing fleet of Russian-built submarines and likely include technology transfer provisions that would help build up its domestic defence industry.

According to informed sources, the contract is not expected to be signed during the chancellor’s visit, but it should help move the discussions forward.

Merz will be accompanied by a large business delegation, including executives from corporate giants such as Siemens and Airbus.

‘One of the main objectives of this trip is to deepen economic relations with India,’ a German government official said.

For Germany’s exporters, India and its 1.4 billion inhabitants represent significant opportunities, with a bilateral trade volume of almost 50 billion euros.

Sales have slumped in China, and German firms now face fierce global competition from Chinese rivals in many industries.

German-Chinese relations have also become strained, with Beijing limiting supplies of semiconductors and some rare earth elements.

‘German foreign trade is looking for growth markets, and India is precisely that,’ said Florian Wenke of the state-run agency Germany Trade & Invest.

In India, high US tariffs are creating uncertainty and the country is also re-evaluating its stance towards China, said economist Samina Sultan from the German Economic Institute.

‘This is certainly a time when India is striving to expand trade relations, such as with Germany or with Europe as a whole,’ Sultan said.

India offers potential growth markets for German green energy technology and defence exports, Sultan said, with India interested in broader partnerships ‘so as not to become so dependent on Russia, China or even the USA’.

Jan Noether, head of the Indo-German Chamber of Commerce, said the timing of Merz’s visit is ‘absolutely ideal’ –- especially as an EU-India free trade agreement appears within reach.

Discussions will also focus on the recruitment of skilled labour, according to the German government official.

With ageing Germany facing a chronic labour shortage, its companies have long relied on skilled Indian personnel, particularly in the IT sector. Germany is also looking to recruit more workers in the healthcare sector from India.

German universities are also a popular destination for Indian students, and Merz and Modi are expected to discuss mobility rules for workers and students as well as cooperation on research.

title: Faiz joins Dhaka Bank as MD, CEO
body:
Osman Ershad Faiz on Sunday joined Dhaka Bank PLC as managing director and chief executive officer, said a press release.

Prior to joining Dhaka Bank, he served as additional managing director and chief operating officer of Eastern Bank PLC, a role he assumed in January 2025. Prior to that, he was co-founder of Asia FiiT, an international banking and FinTech advisory firm headquartered in Singapore.

Previously, he served as chief information and operating officer of AMTD Digital and managing director and chief operating officer of Standard Chartered Bank Singapore. He also served as managing director and chief information officer (wholesale banking, eastern hemisphere) at Standard Chartered Bank and as a director of Singapore Clearing House Association.

He received ‘Legend’ award at the World CIO 200 Summit 2023. He has also  been featured multiple times in the HERoes Global Role Model lists, supported by INvolve, Financial Times and Yahoo Finance, for his advocacy of women in business. Since 2015, he has been a Fellow of the Institute of Banking and Finance, Singapore.

He holds a BCom (honours) and an MBA from Aligarh Muslim University and has completed executive education programmes at INSEAD and the University of Oxford Saïd Business School.

He began his professional career as a management trainee at American Express in 1993.

Abdul Hai Sarker, chairman of Dhaka Bank, said, ‘On behalf of the board, I am delighted to welcome Osman as managing director and CEO of Dhaka Bank. His appointment comes at a defining moment for Bangladesh’s banking sector, when strong governance, disciplined execution and technology-led transformation are more important than ever. Osman brings deep operational expertise and a proven ability to lead complex organisations through change while maintaining rigorous risk management and compliance.’

‘The board is confident that, under his leadership, Dhaka Bank will sharpen its strategic focus, strengthen its balance sheet, accelerate our digital and SME growth agenda, and deliver sustainable, long-term value for customers, shareholders and the communities we serve,’ he said.

Faiz said stated, ‘My priority will be to work with our team to deepen the trust of our clients and regulators, modernise our platforms and processes, and enhance Dhaka Bank’s service for individuals, businesses and institutions alike.’

title: Net FDI jumps 202pc in July-Sept of 2025: BIDA
body:
The net foreign direct investment saw a robust year-on-year hike of 202 per cent in the July-September quarter of 2025 to $315.09 million, according to recent data published by the Bangladesh Investment Development Authority.

In the corresponding period of 2024, the net FDI was $104.33 million, the BIDA stated, citing the Foreign Investment and External Debt Management Cell, Statistics Department of the Bangladesh Bank as the source.

Cumulatively, total net FDI inflows for January–September 2025 stood at $1.41 billion, marking an 80 per cent increase compared to $780 million during the corresponding period of 2024, said the BIDA.

In the preceding quarter of April-June of 2025, the net FDI was $303.27 million, from which the FDI witnessed a 3.9 per cent positive growth to the next quarter.

During the July-September quarter of 2025, the gross FDI inflow was $1.06 billion, of which $136 million was in the form of equity, $687 million was reinvested earnings, and $244 million was intra-company loans.

By deducting $752 million as an outflow, the net FDI stood at $315.09 million in the July-September quarter of 2025, with $101 million in equity, $211 million in reinvested earnings, and $3 million in intra-company loans.

Chowdhury Ashik Mahmud Bin Harun, executive chairman of the BIDA and the Bangladesh Economic Zones Authority, said that BIDA’s core work is to improve the business climate and develop a credible pipeline of investment.

‘It is encouraging to see this pipeline begin to convert into realized inflows. Although the benchmark remains low, these back-to-back quarterly gains highlight that the investors are placing their trust in Bangladesh,’ he added.

He also said that they expect some moderation in the coming quarter (October-December) of 2025 due to the upcoming elections, but anticipate a rebound post-election, supported by a strong investment pipeline.

Beyond the actualised figures, BIDA’s dedicated investment pipeline for 2025 has already surpassed $1.5 billion, in addition to the traditional registered proposals, the BIDA said.

title: NBR launches tax payments through MFS
body:
The National Board of Revenue on Sunday inaugurated large-value tax payment facilities through mobile financial services by integrating its e-TDS system with the A-Challan System.

The NBR said that through this system, corporate taxpayers could pay taxes, primarily through bKash Limited, marking a new milestone in the country’s digital tax administration and enabling faster, fully online corporate tax payments.

As part of the launch, taxes worth Tk 13 crore as withholding tax and Tk 64 crore as value-added tax were paid on a pilot basis through the online merchant wallet service of bKash.

The move would allow corporate taxpayers to pay taxes digitally without physically visiting banks.

Speaking at the event, NBR chairman Md Abdur Rahman Khan said that the introduction of large-value tax payments through MFS would significantly ease and speed up tax compliance for corporate taxpayers.

‘The initiative would play a key role in modernising the revenue collection system,’ he added, saying that many corporate entities already used MFS platforms to pay employee salaries and the new facility would now enable them to pay withholding tax, VAT and other taxes through the same digital channel.

He said that other MFS providers were also allowed to offer large-value transactions for tax payments, and that any amount of tax payment would now be at taxpayers’ fingertips, aiming to further digitise tax collection and improve ease of doing business.

According to the NBR, under the new arrangement, withholding tax could be paid through the NBR’s eTDS system, while VAT payments are processed through the finance division’s ACS using MFS platforms.

It also said that the initiative would enhance transparency, reduce transaction time and costs, and encourage taxpayers to make large-value tax payments digitally.

The move is part of the government’s broader effort to modernise revenue administration through digital platforms and expand cashless transactions across public financial services, NBR officials said.

NBR member (income tax administration and human resource management) GM Abul Kalam Kaikobad said that the initiative marked another significant step forward in the automation of the revenue system.

bKash finance controller Arifur Rahman said that a single payment would take not more than two minutes to complete and could be made from either a bank account or a mobile wallet.

He also said that the Bangladesh Bank would settle the collected tax amounts by debiting them from BRAC Bank twice a day.

title: NBR links ASYCUDA with BGMEA’s e-UD system
body:
