The Indian high commissioner to Bangladesh, Pranay Kumar Verma, on Saturday paid his first official visit to the Bangladesh Nationalist Party office in Dhaka since taking up his post and met BNP chairman Tarique Rahman.”

The talks between Tarique and Verma focused on enhancing cooperation between the two countries to promote regional stability and explored potential collaboration under a future BNP-led government to ensure peace, security, and stronger bilateral ties, party leaders said.

Following the meeting, BNP joint secretary general Humayun Kabir told reporters that the Indian prime minister Narendra Modi had welcomed Tarique as the party’s newly appointed chairman and expressed hope that under his leadership, Bangladesh would be strengthened further in the future.

Humayun described the meeting as cordial and courteous.

He said that while specific challenges were not discussed in detail, the talks highlighted the BNP’s approach to maintaining positive bilateral relations and pursuing constructive international policies if it assumes power.

Meanwhile, European Union Election Observation Mission chief observer Ivars Ijabs, Turkey’s ambassador to Bangladesh Ramis Şen, and Egyptian ambassador to Bangladesh Omar Mohie Eldin Ahmed Fahmy also met Tarique Rahman on Saturday.

title: 24th DIFF opens with Chinese film
body:
The 24th Dhaka International Film Festival, organised by Rainbow Film Society, began at the main auditorium of Bangladesh National Museum in Dhaka on Saturday.

Written and directed by Chen Xiang, the film titled The Journey to No End, is a 94 minutes film depicting a 16-year old boy Cheng Qi, who has lived with his father since his parents divorced.

He starts searching for his mother in the digital world but Cheng Qi becomes even more confused about what kind of life he wants for his future.

On the opening day, Iranian director Mohammad Asadnia’s debut feature film titled Without Me, a 91 minutes film, was also screened at the main auditorium as part of the opening ceremony.

The festival will showcase 245 films from 91 countries, including Bangladesh.

On Bangladesh panorama, nine full-length films including Agontuk, Ekhane Rajnoitik Alap Joruri, The University of Chankharpul and Ural will be screened while 10 short-films will be screened under the talent section.

Information and Broadcasting adviser Syeda Rizwana Hasan inaugurated the nine day festival while Cultural Counsellor of the Chinese Embassy Li Shaopeng and Croatia-UK based filmmaker Alexandera Markovich spoke as special guest at the opening ceremony chaired by Bangladesh Energy Regulatory Commission chairman Jalal Ahmed.

The festival director Ahmed Muztaba Zamal stressed on a permanent film centre for the festival while delivering the welcome speech at the event.

Syeda Rizwana Hasan said that the idea of film screening at the beach is unique but we need to be careful about lighting and single-use plastic at the world’s longest sea beach.

She also urged to introduce the environment as a category of the festival and organise this festival at divisional and district levels.

Li Shaopeng said that a total of 13 Chinese films will be screened at the festival and a poster exhibition on Chinese films would boost cultural collaboration through cinema.

Alexandera Markovich said that Bangladeshi cinema possesses a rich tradition of storytelling.

Before the discussion, the ceremony featured a theatrical performance by Joltoronggo Theatre Company, directed by Thamid Ahmed Shamim.

title: Bus kills elderly woman at Paltan
body:
An elderly woman was killed after being hit by a bus while crossing the road in front of the Golap Shah Mazar at Paltan in Dhaka on Saturday.

The deceased, Saleha Begum, 75, was a vagrant who had been living around the shrine of Golap Shah.

According to the police, the incident occurred around noon when a bus of Nawabganj Transport struck her as she was crossing the road near the shrine.

Paltan police station sub-inspector Abdul Momin said that the woman was critically injured in the accident and was rescued by locals and taken to Dhaka Medical College Hospital, where doctors declared her dead.

The police have seized the bus involved in the incident. However, the driver fled the scene and remains absconding. Efforts are under way to arrest him, SI Abdul Momin added.

title: UCSI Univ Bangladesh holds orientation for new students
body:
The UCSI University Bangladesh held an orientation for the new students of January 2026 semester on its campus at Banani in Dhaka on Saturday.

Professor Mohd Kushairi bin Mohd Rajuddin, pro-vice-chancellor of UCSI University Bangladesh campus, graced the orientation as chief guest, said a press release.

Welcoming the new students, registrar Professor Shah Samiur Rashid gave an encouraging speech, while dean of the faculty of computer science and digital innovation Professor Syed Akhtar Hossain delivered the closing remarks.

The event was moderated by the university students Shoshi Hossain and Ahanaf Fateh Hossain.

Emphasising that enrolling at UCSI University is a wise decision as it ranks among the top 300 universities in the world and 9th in Asia, Professor Kushairi highlighted that the students were embarking on their higher education journey at a world-class university, creating an opportunity to meet the expectations of themselves, their families, and the nation.

He urged students and parents to trust in the university’s quality of education as it focused on career-oriented and industry-relevant curricula.

Professor Syed Akhtar Hossain mentioned that their journey towards fulfilling their dreams had started at a university that was not only the best in Malaysia but also among the top institutions globally.

He has informed the students that UCSI University Bangladesh is working on establishing a spacious city campus by 2029, which will open new doors for their education.

Professor Shah Samiur Rashid has acknowledged that while this path will present challenges, it also holds immense opportunities, urging them to seize this chance to shape their future effectively.

After the briefing, faculty members provided the new students with information about UCSI University, its curriculum, courses, teaching methods, examinations and extracurricular activities.

title: Coast Guard destroys drugs worth Tk 18cr at Teknaf
body:
The Bangaldesh Coast Guard destroyed drugs worth around Tk 18 crore recovered in a joint operation at Teknaf in Cox’s Bazar on Saturday.

The Coast Guard conducted four anti-drug operations alone and in collaboration with RAB, said a press release.

During this time, 1,61,000 Yaba pills, 990 grams of Yaba-making powder, 2kg of crystal meth and 10kg of hemp were seized. A GD was filed with the concerned police station to take legal action against the seized drugs.

Later, the chief judicial magistrate, Cox’s Bazar issued instructions to destroy the said drugs kept at BCG station Teknaf.

As per the instructions received, the said drugs were destroyed at Coast Guard Station Teknaf.

title: BUET holds admission test
body:
The undergraduate admission test for the 2025-2026 academic year of the Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology was held on Saturday on the BUET campus in a peaceful environment.

The participation rate in the test was 87.44 per cent.

Out of all the applicants, 10,351 students were selected and given the opportunity to participate in the admission test based on their merit. Of them, 7,644 were male and 2,707 were female. But 9,051 participated in the admission test.

Students will be admitted in a total of 13 departments under the faculties of Chemical and Materials Engineering, Civil Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical and Electronic Engineering, and Architecture and Planning.

The probable date for publishing the merit list along with the waiting list for admission is February 7.

title: Rabindra Univ holds seminar on Poter Gaan
body:
A seminar and art exhibition titled ‘Prabhaman Banglar Poter Gaan’ was organised by the music department of Rabindra University at its Gitanjali Studio Theater.

Music department chairman Debosree Dolon presided over the progrmme where Gautam Kumar Biswas, a lecturer at Jashore Fine Art College, read the seminar paper.

Babul Hossain, a lecturer at the music department, moderated the seminar. Essayist Gautam Kumar Biswas discussed in detail on Poter Gaan in the seminar and displayed a slide show.

Assistant Professors Rowshan Alam and Yatsingh Shuvo of the department also spoke at the seminar.

At 3:00pm, an art exhibition was organised in collaboration with the Jashore Nandik Charukla Charcha Kendra in the auditorium of the Academic Building-3 of Rabindra University.

Music Department teachers Tanmay Kumar and Tushar Mahmud, as well as students of the department, students of Jashore Fine Art College, and members of the Jessore Nandik Fine Arts Center were present.

title: Winter vegetables costly in Lalmonirhat despite ample supply
body:
Prices of winter vegetables are still relatively high despite adequate supply at kitchen markets in Lalmonirhat, adding to the woes of people with fixed income already overburdened with soaring prices of daily essentials.

During the peak winter season, kitchen markets in five upazilas of the district, including Patgram, Hatibandha, Kaliganj, Aditmari and Lalmonirhat Sadar, are brimming with winter vegetables.

Cauliflower, cabbage, beans, carrots, radish, tomatoes, spinach and other winter produce are available in abundance, yet their prices remain sharp.

During a visit to the market on Saturday, it was found that potatoes were being sold at Tk 30–40 per kg, eggplant at Tk 50–60 per kg, tomatoes at Tk 70 per kg, carrots at Tk 40 per kg, beans at Tk 60 per kg, pumpkin at Tk 50 per piece, raw bananas at Tk 30 per dozen, ladies finger beans at Tk 60 per kg, pointed gourd Tk 60 per kg, bottle gourd Tk 40–60 per piece depending on size, cauliflower at Tk 40 per piece, cabbage at Tk 50 per piece, papaya at Tk 30 per kg, radish Tk 40 per kg, sponge gourd at Tk 50 per piece, bitter gourd at Tk 50 per kg, red spinach at Tk 20 per bunch and mustard leaves at Tk 20 per bunch.

Customers are negotiating prices with vendors, often moving from one stall to another in search of better deals.

Consumers said the high prices of vegetables throughout the year put pressure on household budgets and while winter usually brings some relief, the relief is minimal this year.

Salma Begum, a housewife from Shialkhowa, said that earlier they used to buy a few vegetables for 200–300 taka. ‘Now, with the same amount of money, one cannot even fill a bag with vegetables and even the variety in the family’s meals is decreasing.’

Another buyer, Samad Mia, an office employee at an organisation, said that because vegetable prices were high, they no longer had the opportunity to eat vegetables regularly. ‘Winter was supposed to be truly comfortable for middle-class people like us, but now it is not.’

Saiful Islam, a vegetable seller, said, ‘Production usually rises in winter, but this year cold weather has affected supply, keeping prices relatively high.’

Mohammad Helal Mia, a seller from Namuri market, added, ‘Farmers should have brought more vegetables to the market, but the sudden cold has disrupted supply.’[

Another seller said that although higher prices increased profit per unit, fewer buyers mean overall sales remained unsatisfactory.

‘If the price is lower, people buy more. This way, our products don’t remain unsold either,’ he said.

According to the stakeholders, if weather conditions are not favourable, vegetable prices may remain high throughout the winter season.

title: Onion cultivation exceeds target in Shariatpur
body:
Onion cultivation has exceeded the official target this season in Shariatpur for the favourable soil conditions and weather in the char areas along the Padma and Meghna rivers.

According to the Department of Agricultural Extension in Shariatpur, onions were cultivated on 4,652 hectares of land this season, about 300 hectares more than the target of 4,352 hectares.

The char lands of Jajira and Naria upazilas proved particularly suitable for onion farming, resulting in a good overall yield.

Officials said that onions had already started arriving in local markets, leading to a decline in prices. Retail prices have fallen to around Tk 50 per kilogram.

The district’s total onion demand stands at 29,772 tonnes, while the production target has been fixed at 61,051 tonnes, more than double the local demand. With cultivation exceeding the target, total production is expected to surpass initial estimates.

Despite the bumper yield, farmers have expressed concern over receiving fair prices.

Onion farmer Tabarak Ali of Naodoba said that he cultivated onions with borrowed money and fears financial hardship if prices fall further. ‘If we do not get a fair price, we will be forced to protest on the streets,’

He urged authorities to ensure reasonable market prices.

Deputy director of DAE Mustafa Kamal Hossain said that favourable weather conditions had contributed to higher-than-expected production this year.

He added that onion prices had already begun to decline as supply increases.

title: Woman with disabilities dies 5-days after clothes catch fire in Rangpur
body:
A woman with disabilities died while undergoing treatment for burn injuries in Rangpur Medical College Hospital on Friday morning after five days of treatment.

The deceased was Hazera Begum, 36, wife of Abdur Rahim from Vishugari union under Gobindaganj in Gaibandha.

Hazera was admitted to the Burn and Plastic Surgery Department of Rangpur Medical College Hospital on January 4 with burns covering nearly 45 per cent of her body. According to her family, she was warming herself near a fire under a large tree in the courtyard on January 4, when her clothes caught fire, causing severe burns to her waist and chest.

Dr Kaniz Fatema, assistant director of Rangpur Medical College Hospital, said that 14 other burn patients were currently receiving treatment at the hospital.

‘Burn cases usually increase two to three times during winter due to open fires,’ she added.

She urged people to take precautions when using fire to keep warm, wear warm clothing and raise family awareness to prevent such accidents.

title: 3 kidnapping gang members held with drugs, weapons
body:
The joint forces, in a special drive, have arrested three members of a kidnapping gang along with drugs and locally made weapons at Rangunia in Chattogram.

The arrested were Shahed Hasan, 35, Md Abdus Salam, 22, and Obaidul Mustafa Sourav, 31. All are the residents of different areas under Rangunia.

The arrested persons along with the seized drugs and weapons were handed over to Rangunia model police Station on Saturday.

The operation led by Major Abu Shaker Bhuiyan resulted in the arrest of the suspects and the recovery of drugs, country-made weapons and cash.

During the drive, the joint force rescued a kidnapped youth, Rubel, 30, from Balughat Ward 8 of Pomra union under the upazila.

The team recovered 882 pieces of Yaba, 3.1 kilograms of hemp and a significant amount of local weapons while conducting a raid in one of the detained house.

The weapons included two axes, two chapatis, 19 knives, four hammers, nine ranges, four pliers, two cutters, two toy pistols, seven screwdrivers, two foil paper pipes, one iron pipe, one trowel, one plastic scale, one chisel and two yellow ranges from their possession.

In addition, three passports, five smartphones, four button phones, and Tk 1 lakh 5 thousand 890 in cash, were seized during the operation.

The joint force reported that Obaidul Mustafa Sourav, who has been detained, is allegedly involved in drug dealing in the area for an extended period.

His mother, Rubina Akhter, also a suspected of being involved in local drug dealing, was not apprehended during the operation.

title: Growth of maize plants raises hope among Rangpur farmers
body:
The growth of maize plants across both mainland and char areas has brightened prospects for a bumper harvest in the current rabi season, lifting hopes of farmers in the Rangpur agricultural region amid expectations of higher yields and better returns.

After exceeding the set target for maize cultivation, farmers have made their all-out efforts to tending to the growing plants in the region’s five districts, Rangpur, Gaibandha, Kurigram, Lalmonirhat and Nilphamari.

The Department of Agricultural Extension has set a target of producing 13,28,993 tonnes of maize from 1,17,043 hectares of land for all five districts of the region this season.

Meanwhile, farmers have already brought 1,17,200 hectares of land under maize cultivation, exceeding the fixed farming target by 157 hectares, as the process of sowing seeds will continue till this month-end.

Additional director of DAE for Rangpur region Md Sirajul Islam said, ‘Maize cultivation had been expanding every year, improving the quality of life of small and marginal farmers, chars and riverine people in the region.’

The growing demand of maize in the country’s flourishing poultry, dairy and animal husbandry sectors and food industries is encouraging farmers to further increase its cultivation as a cash crop to reap more profits.

‘As a result, farmers are showing their keen interests in expanding cultivation of the less irrigation water consuming and highly money-spinning cash crop after getting repeated bumper production with rewarding prices every year,’ he said.

Independence Medal-2018 (food security) winner agricultural scientist MA Mazid said that the expansion of maize cultivation was mainly contributing to poverty reduction and improving livelihoods of the poor in the mainland and riverine char areas.

Braving the adverse impacts of climate change, the riverside and char people have brought more lands under maize cultivation on the Teesta, Jamuna, Brahmaputra, Dharla, Dudhkumar, Karatoa, Ghaghat, Atrai and other riverine areas this season.

‘The government through the DAE distributed high yielding varieties of maize seeds and fertilisers among landless, small and marginal farmers as incentives for further enhancing maize cultivation this season,’ he said.

Md Mamunur Rashid, a PhD fellow in the department of agricultural extension at Haji Mohammad Danesh University of Science and Technology, stressed on cultivation of low-irrigation water consuming maize to save underground water amid changing climate.

‘Farmers should adopt conservation agriculture-based technologies in maize cultivation to reduce irrigation frequency and cultivation time and reduce farming costs to maximise production and earn more profits,’ he said.

There are more potential ways to increase maize yield by bringing vast tracts of char lands in the riverine areas of Rangpur agricultural region, he mentioned.

Farmers Nurun Nabi, Borhan Uddin, Isahaque Ali, Lal Mohammad and Farhad Hossain of different villages in Rangpur said that they had completed sowing of maize seeds on their crop lands after harvesting aman rice.

‘The superbly growing maize plants on the dried-up Teesta riverbed in Paschim Mahipur village of Gangachara upazila in Rangpur is predicting a bumper yield of the crop this season,’ said farmer Anwar Hossain, of Paschim Mahipur village.

title: Shibu Market modern fire station inaugurated in Narayanganj
body:
The newly-constructed Shibu Market modern fire station was inaugurated in Narayanganj on Saturday.

Senior secretary of home ministry Nasimul Ghani inaugurated the fire station as chief guest, said a press release.

He also recalled his early training as a fire service officer during his teen time and described himself as a former volunteer of the Fire Service and Civil Defence.

Expressing satisfaction to inaugurate the modern fire station, he thanked all concerned, including the director general of the Fire Service and Civil Defence.

He also emphasised the need to increase the number of volunteers to cope with future risks, including earthquakes, and stressed strengthening the media wing to enhance public awareness through campaigns.

Ghani called upon all the members of the fire service to remain steadfast in serving the people.

He also planted an amrapali tree on the station premises as part of the programme.

The FSCD department DG Brigadier General Muhammad Jahed along with department directors, the deputy commissioner of Narayanganj, superintendent of police, deputy director of Ansar, officials of the Ministry of Home Affairs and fire service, media personnel, local volunteers, and people from various walks of life were present at the inaugural ceremony.

title: Police hold drills in city
body:
The police held drills at 82 important points in Dhaka city on Saturday afternoon to mobilise the force ahead of the general elections amid deteriorating law and order across the country.

The drill was held from 4:00pm to 6:00pm engaging officers and forces and the photos of their activities were sent to the higher authorities as per an order of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police commissioner Sheikh Md Sazzat Ali issued on Thursday.

The drills were held at Shahbagh crossing, Banglamotor, Press Club, Matstya Bahaban, Moghbazar crossing, Katabon, New Market, Dhanmondi-32, Paltan crossing, Rampura Bridge, Kamalapur Railway Station, Jatrabari Chowrasta, Saidabad Bus Terminal, Palashi crossing, Azimpur Bus Stand and Asadgate crossing and other points.

DMP spokesperson Muhamamd Talebur Rahman, however, claimed that it was a regular drill as part of the force’s activity in the Dhaka city.

An assistant commissioner of the DMP, seeking not to be named, said that the drill was held to mobilise the police force ahead of the election and restore people’s confidence on the force.

The government is yet to restore the law and order across the country just a month ahead of the national election, with people passing their days amid frequent incidents of violence and crimes.

Incidents of murder, robbery, theft, kidnapping, extortion have been going on unabated, raising concern among the people from all walks of life.

The government could not take effective measures against mob violence, attack on shrines, assaulting bauls, and other crimes.

On the other hand, the lack of preventive security measures by law enforcers, assaults on police, low police morale, frequent street protests, and political violence created chaos in maintaining law and order, according to rights activists.

title: Former CJ SM Murshed’s birth anniv today
body:
The 115th anniversary of the birth of former chief justice, Syed Mahbub Murshed, one of the eminent constitutional lawyers in the Indian subcontinent, will be observed today.

Marking the day, the Syed Mahbub Murshed Memorial Committee will place wreaths and organise a prayer session at his graveyard at Banani in the capital this morning, said a press release on Saturday.

Syed Mahbub Murshed, a luminary in the judiciary filed in South Asia and a respected figure in political area, is described by intellectuals as ‘a keeper of national conscience’.

Different socio-cultural organisations will also hold discussion on him, his historical role, and achievements on the day.

He was appointed chief justice of the East Pakistan High Court in May 1964. He resigned from the position in November 1967.

title: SI injured in attack while trying to arrest JL leader in Ashulia
body:
A sub-inspector of Ashulia police station was injured on Friday night when he was attacked while attempting to arrest a local Juba League leader accused in a murder case in Ashulia linked to the July uprising, said the police.

The incident occurred at around 9:30pm in Gomail Banglabazar area in Ashulia, on the outskirts of the capital city Dhaka, when a police team led by Ashulia police sub-inspector Monirul Islam went to arrest Juba League leader Sohel Shikdar.

The police said that Sohel, a suspect in a murder case, was currently the organising secretary of a ward-level unit of Awami League, the party that is led by ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina and whose activities are now banned.

Sensing police presence, attackers launched a sudden assault on SI Monirul Islam, leaving him injured, Ashulia police officer in-charge Md Rubel Hawlader said.

‘The suspect’s family members joined the attack with sharp weapons, rods and sticks,’ he said.

Fellow officers and local residents rescued him and admitted him to a local hospital where he is currently receiving treatment with head and neck injuries.

OC Rubel Howlader said that he had visited the spot and was investigating the incident.

The suspects involved in the attack fled the scene’,’ he said, adding that due legal action would be taken for obstructing government duties.

title: Police stop march towards US embassy
body:
The police on Saturday stopped Ganatantrik Jukta Front’s US embassy-bound march in front of the Confidence Tower in the capital’s Badda area.

Ganatantrik Jukta Front, a combine of seven political parties, started the march towards the US embassy protesting against US aggression in Venezuela and forcibly taking Venezuela’s president Nicholas Maduro and his wife to the United States forcibly.

Jukta Front leaders and activists started their march from in front of the Subashtu Tower in the Badda area and the police stopped the marchers in front of Confidence Tower by erecting a barricade.

Faced with the barricade, the leaders and activists sat beside the road and held a protest rally there.

Addressing the rally as the chair, the combine leader and Socialist Party of Bangladesh general secretary Bazlur Rashid Firoz denounced the US army attack on Venezuela to pick up its president and his wife to take them to the United States.

He said that the US had no right to lead the aggression on an independent country like Venezuela and pick up its president and his wife to take them to the United States.

The aggression aimed to capture the oil resources of Venezuela, Bazlur Rashid said.

Communist Party of Bangladesh president Kazi Sazzad Zahir Chandan called on the world community to be vocal against the US aggression.

Bangladesh Jasod standing committee member Mushtuq Husain criticised the interim government of Bangladesh for not protesting against the US aggression.

Dhaka Metropolitan Police additional deputy commissioner for Gulshan Zone, Md Al-Amin Hossain, said that they had halted the march towards the US embassy at about 3:45pm.

‘We have halted the march to ensure the security of the embassy and avoid any untoward situation,’ he added.

Democratic Revolutionary Party general secretary Mushrefa Mishu demanded an immediate stop to the aggression on Venezuela and the release of its elected president and his wife.

Revolutionary Communist League central leader Nazrul Islam said that the left and democratic political parties would wage a tougher movement to protest against the US aggression.

Central leader of SPB (Marxist) Shima Datta called on the interim government to take a stand against the US aggression in Venezuela.

title: Motorbikes account for 40pc of 2025 fatal accidents: RSF
body:
About 40 per cent of the fatal road crashes in Bangladesh were related to motorcycles in the year 2025, a Road Safety Foundation report revealed on Saturday.

The foundation published the annual report, prepared on the basis of media reports, at a press conference on Saturday at Dhaka Reporters’ Unity, said its press release.

In the year, at least 7,359 people were killed, mostly from working age group, and 16,476 others were injured in 7,584 road crashes countrywide, according to the report.

In the same year, there were at least 3,029 motorcycle-related accidents, the highest number of crashes involving motorcycles, accounting for 39.93 per cent of the total road crashes.

The number of deaths in motorcycle accidents is 2,671, accounting for 36.29 per cent of total deaths. Compared with 2024, the percentages of the number of motorcycle related accidents increased by 9.7 per cent and death by 2.37 per cent in 2025.

Among the fatal victims, 5,723 or 77.76 per cent belonged to working age population, between 18 and 65 years.

Compared with 2024, the percentage of deaths increased by 0.89 per cent, injuries by 37.08 per cent and road crashes by 9.48 per cent in 2025, according to the report.

In 2024, at least 7,294 people were killed and 12,019 others were injured in 6,927 road crashes.

In 2025, as per the report, 519 railway accidents killed 478 people and injured 152 others, while at least 132 waterways accidents killed 149 people and injured 123 others with 34 remained missing.

Of the road fatalities, 1,008 were children. Among the children, 42.03 per cent were killed after three-wheeler vehicles including nasimon and karmon hit them and 36.11 per cent children were killed on regional roads.

The report also mentioned 1,564 pedestrian deaths and 941 transport workers, including drivers, deaths in 2025.

The statistics on vehicle-based fatalities in accidents show that 36.29 per cent or 2,671 motorcycle riders and motorcyclists, 18.69 per cent or 1,376 three-wheeler and battery-powered rickshaws, ‘easy bikes’, CNG-powered auto-rickshaws, and human haulers (Laguna) drivers and passengers, 6.64 per cent or 489 locally made nasimon, karimon, Bhotbhoti, Alamsadhu and Mahindra drivers and passengers, 6.52 per cent or 480 goods-laden vehicles drivers and passengers, 5.65 per cent or 416 bus drivers and passengers, 3.19 per cent or 235 cars-jeep-microbuses drivers and passengers and 1.73 per cent or 128 bicycle and paddle rickshaw pullers and passengers were killed in road crashes.

Regarding the types of accidents, most incidents—40.51 per cent total—occurred by vehicles falling into ditches as drivers lost control over the vehicles, followed by 23.62 head-on collisions, 20.78 per cent by running over pedestrians or ramming into other vehicles, 13.23 per cent by hitting vehicles from behind and 1.83 per cent by other reasons.

As for the location of the crashes, the highest 37.77 per cent incidents took place on regional highways and as for the time of the crashes, the highest 28.5 per cent accident occurred in the morning.

Out of all divisions, Dhaka division has the highest number of accidents, totalling 2,139, and the most fatalities with 2,018, people killed, while Barishal division recorded the lowest number of accidents, 448, and the fewest people, 420, killed.

As per the report, financial loss from the accidents in 2025 was about Tk 25,550 crore.

The foundation blamed movement of fitness defying vehicles, reckless driving, overloading, unskilled drivers, lack of implementation and enforcement of laws and tendency not to follow traffic laws for the frequent road crashes.

It urged the authorities concerned to implement laws and people to follow them.

title: Japan PM mulling snap poll in coming weeks
body:
Japan’s prime minister Sanae Takaichi is considering calling a general election in the coming weeks to capitalise on strong public support for her government, media reports said Saturday.

Takaichi was appointed Japan’s first woman prime minister in October and her cabinet is enjoying an approval rating of around 70 per cent.

But her ruling bloc only has a slim majority in the powerful lower house of parliament, hindering its ability to push through her ambitious policy agenda.

She is considering dissolving the lower house at the start of a parliament session on January 23, the Yomiuri and Mainichi daily newspapers reported, citing unnamed government sources.

That would mean an election would be ‘highly likely to be held in early to mid-February’, the Yomiuri said.

Some in Takaichi’s administration hold the ‘persistent view that it should move to dissolve parliament early while support ratings remain high, in order to solidify its foundation,’ the Mainichi said, without citing sources.

Takaichi became Japan’s fifth premier in as many years when she was elected, initially as the head of a minority government.

Her Liberal Democratic Party and its coalition partner the Japan Innovation Party regained their lower-house majority in November after three lawmakers joined the LDP.

The ruling bloc remains a minority in the upper house.

Takaichi hopes a bigger majority will help her implement her agenda of more ‘proactive’ fiscal spending and stronger intelligence capacities, the Yomiuri said.

It may also help Takaichi break the deadlock in a spat with China, according to the newspaper.

Ties have deteriorated since Takaichi suggested in November that Japan could intervene militarily if China ever launched an attack on Taiwan, the self-ruled island it claims.

Beijing has announced a broad ban on the export to Japan of ‘dual-use’ goods with potential military applications, and has reportedly been choking off exports of rare-earth products crucial for making everything from electric cars to missiles.

Last month, Takaichi said she was ‘always open’ to dialogue with China.

title: Indonesia suspends Musk’s Grok AI over porn
body:
Indonesia suspended Elon Musk’s AI chatbot Grok on Saturday over concerns about AI-generated pornographic content, the country’s communication and digital affairs minister said.

Grok has faced a global backlash after it emerged that its image creation feature allowed users to sexualise pictures of women and children using simple text prompts.

Indonesia is the first country to deny all access to the tool, which has been restricted to paying subscribers elsewhere following the backlash.

‘In order to protect women, children, and the public from the risks of fake pornographic content generated using the artificial intelligence technology, the government... has temporarily blocked access to the Grok application,’ communication and digital affairs minister Meutya Hafid said in a statement.

‘The government views non-consensual deepfake practices as a serious violation of human rights, dignity, and the security of citizens in the digital space.’

The ministry has also summoned representatives from social media platform X to seek clarification on the issue.

According to AFP journalists in Jakarta, the Grok X account was still active and replying to queries, including in Bahasa Indonesia, on Saturday evening.

Musk-owned startup xAI, which developed Grok, was not immediately available for comment in person.

European officials and tech campaigners slammed the move to limit Grok’s features to paying subscribers, saying it failed to address concerns about sexually explicit deepfake content.

Musk said last week in response to a post about the explicit images that anyone using Grok to ‘make illegal content will suffer the same consequences as if they upload illegal content’.

title: Guinea-Bissau bans unofficial press events, statements
body:
Guinea-Bissau’s junta on Friday announced it was banning all unauthorised press conferences and public statements, some six weeks after coming to power in a post-election coup.

After ousting leader Umaro Sissoco Embalo on November 26, just after the presidential vote, the army suspended the electoral process and announced it was taking control of the coup-prone West African country for one year.

On Friday, the high military command, the junta’s governing body, said in a statement that ‘some individuals and ethnic groups, particularly political figures, have promoted secret meetings and used those to incite violence and disobedience’, including to the country’s transitional charter.

The charter was published in early December and is intended to provide a legal framework for the country’s period under military rule.

The High Military Command said that it ‘expressly prohibited the holding of any press conferences or public statements that are not authorised and that jeopardise peace and social cohesion’.

‘Any person or entity that challenges the public order decreed by the transitional authorities will be severely reprimanded, in compliance with the law,’ the statement said.

After toppling Embalo, the junta originally alleged drug barons were conspiring to sow chaos in the country, a cocaine-trafficking hotspot.

But in early December, authorities said instead that the unstable country faced a ‘grave’ political situation in the wake of the ballot ‘which could degenerate into a civil war with ethnic undertones’.

Observers and the opposition have raised the possibility that Embalo engineered the takeover to halt the electoral process as he was losing at the ballot box.

Before November’s coup, Guinea-Bissau had already undergone four military takeovers and a litany of attempted insurrections since gaining independence from Portugal in 1974.

title: Denmark cuts asylum figures to historic low in 2025
body:
Denmark’s strict immigration policies drove asylum admissions to a historic low in 2025, with 839 requests granted by the end of November, the government announced Saturday.

‘It is absolutely critical that as few foreigners as possible come to Denmark and obtain asylum. My main priority is to limit the influx of refugees,’ said immigration minister Rasmus Stoklund in a press release.

According to the ministry, ‘there have been very few years when the annual total remained below 1,000 ... 2025 will be a year with a historically low number of residence permits granted on asylum grounds’.

Denmark registered 1,835 asylum requests by November 2025.

The country’s immigration approach has been influenced by far-right parties for more than 20 years, and prime minister Mette Frederiksen, the head of the Social Democrats, has pursued a ‘zero refugee’ policy since coming to power in 2019.

Copenhagen has over the years implemented a slew of initiatives to discourage migrants and make Danish citizenship harder to obtain.

In 2024, the country of six million people accepted some 860 of the 2,333 asylum requests lodged that year.

title: Tarique Rahman to launch polls campaign from Sylhet
body:
Chairman of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party Tarique Rahman will start election campaign by visiting the shrine of Hazrat Shah Jalal and Shahporan in Sylhet on January 22.

BNP media cell convener Professor Moudud Hossain Alamgir Pavel said that Tarique Rahman would begin election campaign by paying homage at the shrines of Hazrat Shah Jalal and Hazrat Shah Paran.

Earlier in a meeting with editors and senior journalists on Saturday, he said, ‘As a political party, BNP will go to every people to woo their support for vote.’

It is learned that the allocation of symbols for the upcoming national parliament election will take place on January 21.

Officially, the election campaign will begin from January 22 after allocation of the election symbol a day before.

On way to Dhaka from Sylhet, Tarique Rahman will participate in roadside rallies and public meetings at various locations.

title: Don’t want to be Americans: Greenland’s parties
body:
Greenland’s political parties said they did not want to be under Washington as US president Donald Trump again suggested using force to seize the mineral-rich Danish autonomous territory, raising concern worldwide.

The statement late Friday came after Trump repeated that Washington was ‘going to do something on Greenland, whether they like it or not’.

European capitals have been scrambling to come up with a coordinated response after the White House said this week that Trump wanted to buy Greenland and refused to rule out military action.

‘We don’t want to be Americans, we don’t want to be Danish, we want to be Greenlanders,’ the leaders of five parties in Greenland’s parliament said in a joint statement.

‘The future of Greenland must be decided by Greenlanders.’

‘No other country can meddle in this. We must decide our country’s future ourselves—without pressure to make a hasty decision, without procrastination, and without interference from other countries,’ they underscored.

Julius Nielsen, a 48-year-old fisherman in the capital Nuuk, told AFP: ‘American? No! We were a colony for so many years. We’re not ready to be a colony again, to be colonised’.

A Danish colony until 1953, Greenland gained home rule 26 years later and is contemplating eventually loosening its ties with Denmark.

Many Greenlanders remain cautious about making this a reality.

‘I really like the idea of us being independent, but I think we should wait. Not for now. Not today,’ Pitsi Mari, who works in telecoms, told AFP.

‘I feel like the United States’ interference disrupts all relationships and trust’ between Denmark and Greenland, said Inaluk Pedersen, a 21-year-old shop assistant.

The coalition currently in power is not in favour of a hasty independence. The only opposition party, Naleraq, which won 24.5 per cent of the vote in the 2025 legislative elections, wants to cut ties as quickly as possible but it is also a signatory of the joint declaration.

‘It’s time for us to start preparing for the independence we have fought for over so many years,’ said MP Juno Berthelsen in a Facebook post.

According to a poll published on Saturday by Danish agency Ritzau, more than 38 per cent of Danes think the United States will launch an invasion of Greenland under the Trump administration.

Denmark and other European allies have voiced shock at Trump’s threats on Greenland, a strategic island between North America and the Arctic where the United States has had a military base since World War II.

Trump says controlling the island is crucial for US national security given the rising military activity of Russia and China in the Arctic.

‘We’re not going to have Russia or China occupy Greenland. That’s what they’re going to do if we don’t. So we’re going to be doing something with Greenland, either the nice way or the more difficult way,’ the US president said Friday.

Both Russia and China have increased military activity in the region in recent years, but neither has laid any claim to the vast icy island.

Greenland has also attracted international attention in recent years for its vast natural resources including rare earth minerals and estimates that it could possess huge oil and gas reserves.

Danish prime minister Mette Frederiksen has warned that an invasion of Greenland would end ‘everything’, meaning the transatlantic NATO defence pact and the post-World War II security structure.

‘I’m a fan of Denmark, too, I have to tell you. And you know, they’ve been very nice to me,’ Trump said. ‘But you know, the fact that they had a boat land there 500 years ago doesn’t mean that they own the land.’

Secretary of state Marco Rubio is due to meet next week with Denmark’s foreign minister and representatives from Greenland.

A flurry of diplomacy is under way as Europeans try to head off a crisis while at the same time avoiding the wrath of Trump, who is nearing the end of his first year back in power.

Trump had offered to buy Greenland in 2019 during his first presidential term but was rebuffed.

The head of NATO’s forces in Europe, US General Alexus Grynkewich, said Friday the military alliance was far from being in ‘a crisis’, following Trump’s threats to bring Greenland under US control.

title: Robinrafan receives best AI Educator at Dhallywood awards 2025
body:
Artificial intelligence educator, content creator and author Robinrafan received the Best AI Educator in Content Creation award at the Dhallywood Film and Music Silver Jubilee Awards 2025 for his global contributions to AI education.

The award ceremony was held at the Bangladesh China Friendship Conference Centre on Friday, according to a press release. The jury noted that advanced filmmaking and content production are increasingly being shaped by artificial intelligence, and unanimously selected Robinrafan for his role in connecting AI education with professional-level filmmaking and digital content creation.

Robinrafan also received AI Educator of the Year at the London Iconic Star Awards in November 2025.

Several prominent figures from Bangladesh’s entertainment industry, including Shakib Khan, Raihan Rafi, Imran, Adnan Al Rajeev, Irfan Sazzad, Palash, Tanjin Tisha, Mehazabien Chowdhury, and Misha Sawdagor were present and renowned actress Dilara Zaman received the life-time achievement award at the event.

The event also consisted of musical performances, drama segments, and fashion shows.

title: Rights, freedom of speech shrinking ahead of JS polls: speakers
body:
With mob violence, legal repression and partisan control of institutions intensifying ahead of the approaching 13th Jatiya Sangsad elections, political leaders and civil society representatives warned that human rights and freedom of expression were fast dwindling.

Their concerns came on Saturday at a discussion titled ‘Political parties, human rights and freedom of expression’ organised by the Centre for Governance Studies at the CIRDAP Auditorium.

As chief guest, law, justice and parliamentary affairs adviser to the interim government Asif Nazrul, however, argued at the discussion that freedom of expression now belonged to everyone except the government.

Saying that currently criticisms of the government often reached a ‘cruel’ level despite several reforms-centric successes, he stated, ‘At least four advisers of the interim government considered resignation amid “online abuses” hurled at them but eventually remained only to maintain the morale of the government.’

He urged political parties, non-governmental organisations and media to reform themselves first before criticising the government.

Transparency International Bangladesh executive director Iftekharuzzaman said that political parties in the country capitalised on money, power and religion, while what the state was doing was enabling the mob power to increase ever.

He urged political parties to include the rights of the national minority communities in their election manifestos and called for the enactment of an anti-discrimination law.

Kapaeeng Foundation executive director Pallab Chakma said that human rights violations continued to worsen, with inadequate responses from both the interim government and political parties against communal violence.

Bangladesh Legal Aid and Services Trust executive director Sara Hossain said that mob violence particularly impacted specific groups.

She also urged political parties to examine whether their supporters genuinely upheld human rights and freedom of expression.

Defending the government’s record, Asif mentioned several reforms, including transferring financial and administrative control to the higher courts, enacting a South Asia’s ‘best’ human rights law, and expanding legal aid services.

Islami Andolon Bangladesh publicity and dawah secretary Sheikh Fazlul Karim Maruf said mob violence was increasingly being used as a political tool.

Amar Bangladesh Party joint general secretary Nasreen Sultana Mily said that in the process of forming electoral alliances smaller parties were experiencing further divisions and breaks.

She also accused the Election Commission of favouring one major party widely perceived as likely to win the election.

CGS president Zillur Rahman said that as the JS elections approached, human rights and freedom of expression tended to shrink further.

He questioned the interim government’s role as laws were often being turned into political tools while violence, clashes, threats and harassment became difficult to control in the period leading up to the national polls to be held on February 12.

Communist Party of Bangladesh presidium member Ragib Ahsan Munna, Bangladesh Socialist Party-Basad general secretary Bazlur Rashid Firoz, Jahangirnagar University’s government and politics teacher Professor Abdul Latif, Rastro Songskar Andolon joint general secretary Didar Bhuiyan, CGS executive director Parvez Karim Abbasi, and Gono Odhikar Parishad senior vice president Faruk Hasan, among others, also spoke.

title: Temperature may fall further from Monday: BMD
body:
Overall temperature across the country may further fall from tomorrow as the Bangladesh Meteorological Department on Saturday recorded the country’s lowest temperature at 8.3C at Tetulia in Panchagarh and in Chuadanga.

The BMD reported that a mild to moderate cold wave had been prevailing across 19 districts while the highest temperature was recorded 29.2C in Sylhet on Saturday.

The department reported that a deep depression over the southwest Bay of Bengal was moving northwestwards and was likely to cross the north Sri Lanka coast by today, while a ridge of sub-continental high pressure had extended over West Bengal and adjoining western Bangladesh, influencing regional weather.

On Friday, Bangladesh recorded the lowest temperature of the season 6.8C at Tetulia in Panchagarh in Rangpur division.

On Saturday, the lowest temperature in Dhaka district was recorded 12.4C and the highest 26C.

BMD senior meteorologist Muhammad Abul Kalam Mallik said that they predicted one to three mild to moderate cold waves in the country in January with the current one being the first of them.

‘A mild cold wave is sweeping over the districts under Rangpur and Rajshahi divisions and the districts of Jashore, Chuadanga and Kushtia,’ he said.

Tomorrow both night and day temperatures may fall slightly over the country.

Later from Wednesday, day temperature may further fall slightly over the country, keeping the night temperatures overall unchanged.

The BMD predicted that cold and foggy conditions were likely to persist for at least five more days.

On Sunday, the BMD reported that the lowest temperature in Dhaka division remained above 10C, but the lowest temperature in the districts under Rajshahi and Rangpur divisions was reported mostly bellow 10C.

title: SUST Press Club celebrates three decades
body:
Press Club of the Shahjalal University of Science and Technology celebrated completion of three decades and first reunion of the club on Saturday through colourful events.

University vice-chancellor professor AM Sarwaruddin Chowdhury inaugurated the day-long programme by cutting a cake at about 9:00 am at the Gol Chattar on the campus followed by a joy procession.

Later, a discussion meeting was organised in the mini-auditorium of the university, marking the completion of 30 years of the press club.

In the meeting, vice-chancellor Sarwaruddin said that since the beginning of the press club’s journey, the journalists of the club have been playing a vital role for the development of the university, the rights of the students and against irregularities, through their objective news.

He appreciated the professionalism, sincerity and ethical responsibility of the club journalists and hoped that they would maintain the standard of journalism in the future.

Sunamganj University of Science and Technology vice-chancellor professor Md Nizam Uddin, Leading University vice-chancellor professor Mohammad Tajuddin, Northeast University vice-chancellor professor Mohammad Iqbal, SUST pro- vice-chancellor professor Sajedul Karim, treasurer professor Ismail Hossain and Jesshor University of Science and Technology treasurer professor Hossain Al Mamun, among others, addressed the event.

Former and present members of the SUST press club also attended the event which was presided by the club’s 20th executive committee president Zubayedul Haque Robin and moderated by general secretary Naeem Ahmed Shuvo. The club members performed at the events, including the cultural session of the daylong programme.

title: Barring devotees from organising urs at shrine on SC premises protested
body:
Cultural activists staged a protest on Saturday against the police barricade near the Khwaja Sharfuddin Chishti shrine on the Supreme Court premises in the capital, which barred devotees from organising the annual urs at the shrine.

They staged the protest by forming a human chain near the Supreme Court while a huge number of police kept the apex court gate cordoned.

They also condemned the attacks on the devotees who came from across the country to join the annual urs, scheduled to be held on Friday evening.

They alleged that the members of the Dhaka University Central Students’ Union attacked the devotees near the Supreme Court area.

Former student leader Baki Billah, Rahman Mofiz and filmmaker Rafsan Ahmed, among others, addressed the gathering at the human chain.

Several hundred devotees took positions near the Supreme Court area, cooked food and distributed it among people as a part of their ritual during the urs.

DUCSU executive member Sarbamitra Chakma denied the allegation of attacking the devotees.

On January 7, the Supreme Court authorities issued a directive prohibiting processions, slogans, rallies, miking, or demonstrations inside the Supreme Court premises.

title: Four forest workers injured in Fatikchari land eviction drive
body:
Four forest workers were seriously injured in an attack by villagers during an eviction drive to recover encroached government forest land at Fatikchari in Chattogram on Saturday.

They have been admitted to Chattogram Medical College Hospital.

The incident took place in the Dhuilachari New Mosque area of Ward1 of Kanchannagar under the upazila.

Fatikchari police station OC Md Selim confirmed the incident involving forest officers

Abrarur Rahman, Khandaker Mafuz Ali, Bachchu Mia and Biplob.

They were initially taken to Fatikchari upazila health complex and later transferred to CMCH Hospital due to their deteriorating condition.

Kanchannagar UP member Mohammad Enam reported a dispute with locals over the forest department’s efforts to reclaim encroached government land, which escalated into a clash.

Fatikchari upazila nirbahi officer Sayeed Mohammad Ibrahim, accompanied by Bangladesh Army personnel, visited the site after the incident.

The UNO stated that the administration was working to restore order.

OC Md Selim mentioned that the forest officials were attacked by locals during the eviction drive, with one officer being assaulted while trying to escape. ‘Legal action is being taken in response to the incident.’

title: Two Jamaat candidates’ remarks spark uproar
body:
EC issues show-cause notice to Jhalakati 1 Jamaat candidate

Controversial remarks by two Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami candidates — one in Jhalokathi and the other in Rangpur — have prompted widespread criticism and regulatory action from the Election Commission as the country is heading towards the 13th Jatiya Sangsad election.

New Age correspondent in Jhalokathi reported that the EC’s Election Investigation and Judicial Committee on Friday issued a  show-cause notice to Fayzul Haque, Jamaat’s candidate for Jhalokathi-1 (Rajapur–Kathalia), for allegedly violating the electoral code of conduct by invoking religious sentiments in his campaign.

The notice, signed by committee head Rezwana Afrin, said that Fayzul Haque made the remarks during a courtyard meeting in Rajapur upazila on January 7 that could hurt religious feelings and influence voters through religious appeal.

According to the committee, Fayzul Haque suggested that even a biri smoker could be pardoned by Allah if he called for votes for Jamaat election symbol ‘Daripalla’ (traditional weighing scale).

The comment, later circulated on social media and in news reports, made the committee launch a review.

After examining credible information, media reports and online content, the committee concluded that the statement constituted a violation of the Code of Conduct for Political Parties and Candidates in Parliamentary Elections, 2025.

Fayzul Haque has been directed to appear in person before the committee and submit a written explanation on January 12, explaining why an inquiry report should not be forwarded to the EC for further action.

Meanwhile, Jamaat’s Rangpur city amir ATM Azam Khan has also come under fire for remarks comparing his withdrawal from the election to the sacrifice of Prophet Ibrahim.

Azam Khan made the comment at a discussion in the Kadamtala area of Pirgachha upazila on Thursday.

New Age correspondent in Rangpur reported that a one-minute-25-second video of his speech went viral on social media, sparking widespread debate and criticism.

Although Azam Khan had been Jamaat’s nominated candidate for Rangpur-4 (Pirgachha–Kaunia), he did not submit his nomination papers after the party decided, under an electoral understanding with the National Citizen Party, to leave the seat for NCP member secretary Akhtar Hossain.

In the speech, Azam said that he had been informed by the Jamaat central leadership that he had been ‘sacrificed’, and claimed they compared this with — and even greater than — the sacrifice by Prophet Ibrahim, saying that his withdrawal represented the ‘sacrifice of hundreds of thousands of men and women of Pirgachha–Kaunia.’

Following the backlash, Azam Khan, however, told reporters that his statement was a slip of tongue.

‘I did not mean it that way. I seek Allah’s mercy for my unintentional mistake,’ he said, adding that his intention was to explain how the Jamaat had set aside its own position for a greater political purpose, so that voters could develop goodwill towards the NCP.

Protesting such remark, Pirgachha upazila BNP president Aminul Islam said, ‘I have seen and heard the video. Comparing any sacrifice with the sacrifice by Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) is a sinful act. This is a major deception intended to mislead people. We have seen similar propaganda before, including claims that voting for a particular symbol would guarantee heaven.’

BASAD (Marxist) candidate for the Rangpur-4 constituency Pragati Barman said, ‘Religion must not be mixed with politics. When the two are combined, different interpretations and controversies inevitably arise.’

title: Venezuela, US hold talks
body:
Venezuela was set to hold talks on Saturday with US envoys in Caracas on restoring diplomatic ties, days after US forces deposed Nicolas Maduro as its president.

Venezuela said Friday it had launched discussions with US diplomats in the capital, the latest sign of cooperation following the leftist leader’s capture and US president Donald Trump’s claim to be ‘in charge’ of the South American country.

Officials said the US envoys were in Caracas to discuss reopening the country’s embassy, while in Washington Trump met with oil companies over his plans to access Venezuela’s huge crude reserves.

The government of interim president Delcy Rodriguez ‘has decided to initiate an exploratory diplomatic process with the government of the United States of America, aimed at re-establishing diplomatic missions in both countries,’ foreign minister Yvan Gil said in a statement.

John McNamara, the top US diplomat in neighbouring Colombia, and other personnel ‘travelled to Caracas to conduct an initial assessment for a potential phased resumption of operations,’ a US official said on customary condition of anonymity.

Venezuela said it would be reciprocating by sending a delegation to Washington.

Rodriguez in a statement condemned ‘the serious, criminal, illegal and illegitimate attack’ by the United States and vowed: ‘Venezuela will continue to confront this aggression through the diplomatic route.’

Trump said earlier Friday that he had called off a second wave of attacks on Venezuela due in part to the release of political prisoners.

The US president had suggested he might use force again to get his way in Venezuela, which has the world’s largest proven oil reserves.

At a White House meeting on Friday, he pressed top oil executives to invest in Venezuela’s reserves, but was met with a cautious reception—with ExxonMobil chief executive Darren Woods dismissing the country as ‘uninvestable’ without sweeping reforms.

Trump said foreign firms had enjoyed no meaningful protections under Maduro, ‘but now you have total security. It’s a whole different Venezuela’.

He also stressed that the companies would deal only with Washington, not Caracas, when exploiting Venezuela’s oil resources.

Trump earlier said that oil companies promised to invest $100 billion in Venezuela, whose oil infrastructure is creaky after years of mismanagement and sanctions.

He had earlier announced a plan for the United States to sell between 30 million and 50 million barrels of Venezuelan crude, with the money to be used at his discretion.

He promised any funds sent to Caracas would be used to buy only US-made products.

In the meanwhile, Washington has maintained maritime pressure on oil tankers in the Caribbean, where it seized a fifth tanker carrying Venezuelan crude—oil that would be sold, Trump said.

State-owned oil company PDVSA confirmed in a statement that one vessel was returning to Venezuelan waters, describing it as the ‘first successful joint operation’ with Washington.

Anxious relatives waited outside Venezuelan jails for a glimpse of their loved ones as the authorities began releasing political prisoners—a move Washington claimed credit for.

‘When I heard the news, I broke down,’ said Dilsia Caro, 50, waiting for the release of her husband Noel Flores, who was jailed for criticising Maduro.

Venezuela began releasing prisoners on Thursday in the first such gesture since US forces removed and detained Maduro in the deadly January 3 raid.

Some relatives still gathered outside the prison had waited more than 36 hours to see their family members.

‘We’ve been living with this uncertainty for several days now... We are worried, we are very distressed, filled with anxiety,’ said one woman, awaiting the release of her brother.

In Nicaragua, meanwhile, authorities have arrested at least 60 people for reportedly expressing support for Maduro’s capture, according to a local human rights group.

Trump told Fox News he would meet next week with Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado, whom he earlier brushed aside as lacking the ‘respect’ to lead Venezuela.

Exiled Venezuelan opposition figurehead Edmundo Gonzalez Urrutia said that any democratic transition in the country must recognize his claim to victory in 2024 presidential elections.

Maduro was proclaimed the winner of the vote, but his re-election was widely seen as fraudulent.

Gonzalez was hoping Friday for the release of his son-in-law, who was detained a year ago in Caracas.

Maduro was seized in a US special forces raid accompanied by airstrikes, operations that left 100 people dead, according to Caracas.

US forces took Maduro and his wife Cilia Flores to New York to face trial on drug-trafficking and other charges.

Rodriguez insisted Thursday her country was ‘not subordinate or subjugated’ despite her pledge to cooperate with Trump.

Angry protesters rallied in the streets of Caracas on Friday demanding Maduro’s release in the latest of a daily series of demonstrations.

‘We don’t have to give one little drop of oil to Trump after all that he has done to us,’ said one protester, Josefina Castro, 70, a member of a civil activists’ group. ‘Our Venezuelan brothers died [in the attack], and that hurts.’

title: CU teacher harassed on campus by Shibir
body:
A Chittagong University teacher was chased and reportedly humiliated by  a group of students on the campus on Saturday during admission tests over allegations of opposing the July uprising and supporting the violent suppression of the movement in 2024.

Hasan Muhammad Roman, an assistant professor at the university’s law department and a former assistant proctor, was dragged to the proctor’s office, witnesses and university authorities said.

Students said that Roman came to the campus on Saturday morning to perform duties as a hall invigilator for the admission test.

When he sensed that he was likely to be seized by students, he took an attempt to leave the area using a back road avoiding the front road of the law department.

A video spread on social media showed him being dragged and put on a battery-run-auto rickshaw while he appeared panicked.

Students claimed that during the July uprising Roman publicly opposed the movement and supported the brutal suppression and killings during the movement and that he also harassed protesting students at the time.

They also said that he was currently facing three separate investigations over the allegations, but was assigned admission test duties based on an administrative letter despite the ongoing probes.

After learning that he was given admission test duties, Chittagong University Central Student’s Union leaders dashed to catch him.

CUCSU law and human rights affairs secretary Fazle Rabbi Towhid said, ‘There are serious allegations against Roman of opposing the July movement and supporting the killings. During the Awami League period, when he was an assistant proctor, he filed cases branding students involved in democratic movements as militants. He also directly supported Chhatra League and instructed to carry out violent activities.’

University proctor Professor Hossain Shaid Shohrowardhy told New Age at about 4:00pm, ‘Students held former assistant proctor Hasan Muhammad Roman and brought him to the proctor office.’

Saying that the teacher was safe and staying at the proctor office, the proctor added, ‘after talking to him, I learned that he tried to flee fearing that a violent mob would be created against him.’

The proctor also claimed that he had not found evidence of a mob attack.

He said that Hasan Muhammad Roman had previously served as an assistant proctor and was a member of Awami League supporting teachers’ group Blue Panel.

Asked whether students could hand him over to the police, Professor Shohrowardhy said that the matter would be discussed with the administration and he could not immediately say whether there was any basis for police action.

He, however, said that he had asked CUCSU leaders to take ‘proper measures’ regarding his colleague Hasan Muhammad Roman.

Earlier On August 20, 2024, Chittagong University students staged a sit-in at the law faculty, demanding the removal of assistant professor Hasan Muhammad Roman over allegations that he supported killings during the quota reform movement crackdown.

Posters calling for his removal were also put up on the faculty walls at the time.

On December 11, Dhaka University’s sociology professor Abul Kashem Mohammad Jamal Uddin was chased and harassed on campus allegedly by Dhaka University Central Students’ Union social service secretary Zubair Bin Nesary and other students.

Professor Mohammad Jamal Uddin is the convener of the Blue Panel, the group of teachers supporting Awami League activities of which are now banned.

On December 19, in a rally on the Rajshahi University campus, RU Central Students’ Union general secretary Salahuddin Ammar announced that if any teacher, officer, or employee, who was backed by Awami fascism is employed at Rajshahi University, they would drag them by the collar and tie them up in front of the administrative building. ’

title: Bangladesh standoff pressures Jay Shah before T20 WC
body:
The International Cricket Council chair, Jay Shah, is set for a crucial round of talks with senior officials of the Board of Control for Cricket in India on Sunday as the standoff over Bangladesh’s participation in the forthcoming T20 World Cup deepens.

The meeting, scheduled in Vadodara during the first India–New Zealand ODI, aims to find a way out of the impasse formed after Bangladesh expressed strong reservations about travelling to India for the tournament, reported NDTV.

Shah is in the city as a special invitee of the Baroda Cricket Association, but the discussions surrounding  him are far from routine. What began as a straightforward logistical request from the Bangladesh Cricket Board has turned into a sensitive diplomatic challenge for the ICC.

In its first letter, the BCB asked for its World Cup matches to be shifted out of India, opts Sri Lanka as alternate hosts.

A second letter took a sharper tone. The board said the matter had moved beyond logistics and involved national sentiment, heightened by the controversy around Mustafizur Rahman’s abrupt exit from the IPL.

Bangladesh demanded full man-to-man security for every member of its delegation if travel to India becomes unavoidable. This includes players, coaches, support staff, and officials.

The message was clear: Bangladesh felt its concerns were not being heard, and the issue had become one of dignity as much as safety.

Shah’s first task will be to revisit the existing security and tournament plans with both the BCCI and the ICC’s operations team. The review is expected to focus on whether previous communications with Bangladesh were too formal and failed to address the concerns in a more reassuring way.

But resolving the matter will require more than paperwork. Direct engagement with the BCB is seen as crucial to shaping a plan that Dhaka can accept without appearing to bow to pressure. Any compromise must give Bangladesh a sense of agency while ensuring the World Cup schedule remains intact.

Bangladesh’s withdrawal is not a viable option. It would trigger legal complications, require an ICC Board vote, and risk upsetting the balance of relationships within both the ICC and the Asian Cricket Council.

The situation has grown more complex with Bangladesh sports adviser Asif Nazrul publicly opposing the current plan, calling it a blow to national pride.

title: Bangladesh seeks visa bond relief
body:
Bangladesh national security adviser Khalilur Rahman on Friday separately met with Allison Hooker, under-secretary of state for political affairs, and Paul Kapur, assistant secretary of state at the United States State Department in Washington DC, seeking exemption from the recently announced visa bond requirement.

During the meetings, they discussed the upcoming Jatiya Sangsad elections in Bangladesh, economic and trade relations, Rohingya issue, and regional matters,  said a press release issued from Washington by the chief adviser’s press wing.

In the meeting with the under-secretary, the security adviser briefed Hooker about the preparations and arrangements for the upcoming general elections and appreciated for the support of the US to the interim government during its tenure, including for the elections.

Hooker responded that the US continued its strong support for the democratic transition in Bangladesh and looked forward to a free and fair election in February.

Khalilur underscored the prospects of increased trade between the two countries following substantially enhanced Bangladeshi import of American farm products.

He requested Hooker to help ease travel of Bangladeshi businessmen to the US in the context the of the recent visa bond and, if possible, to exempt B1 short term business visa for Bangladeshi businessmen from the visa bond, said the release.

Hooker recognised the issue and assured that the US government would positively consider the step. She also indicated that if the overstay by the tourists declined substantially in the future, the US might review the bond requirements that have been put in place.

She also deeply appreciated the cooperation of Bangladesh to the return of undocumented Bangladeshis.

Khalilur expressed sincere thanks to the US for its continued support to the displaced Rohingya population sheltered in Bangladesh.

He requested the US side to consider granting access to their Development Finance Corporation financing for Bangladeshi private sector and also access to financing for semi-conductor development in Bangladesh while under-secretary Hooker assured US consideration of these proposals.

In a separate meeting with assistant secretary of State Paul Kapur, Khalilur discussed issues of mutual interest, including the forthcoming election in Bangladesh, US-Bangladesh bilateral relations, Rohingya crisis, US visa bond, trade and investment and other regional issues.

As a special invitee, the national security adviser also attended the swearing-in ceremony of Brent Christensen, the newly appointed US ambassador to Bangladesh held in the State Department.

Deputy secretary of state for management and resources Michael J Rigas administered the oath.

The ceremony was attended by Bangladesh ambassador to US, embassy officials, senior State Department and military officials, former US ambassadors to Bangladesh, and US business leaders.

In his remarks, the deputy secretary of state reiterated US commitment to continue to support Bangladesh in its journey to democratic transition.

Ambassador Christensen said, ‘The US supports Bangladesh in its journey towards a bright democratic future. I am excited to see the results and look forward to what the new elected government and I can do together to advance the US-Bangladesh relations.’

The US has recently expanded a visa bond policy to include Bangladesh and 24 other countries, requiring citizens of these nations to post refundable bonds of up to $15,000 as part of their application for a US visitor visa, according to the US State Department web site.

Under the updated programme, passport holders from the newly added countries could be asked to pay a bond of $5,000, $10,000, or $15,000 at the time of their visa interview if they were otherwise eligible for a B1/B2 tourism or business visa.

The US visa category B1 is for temporary business activities while the B2 is for tourism purposes.

title: Fatal Minneapolis shooting sparks US protests
body:
Fresh demonstrations were planned across the United States this weekend in the wake of the fatal shooting of a woman by an immigration officer in Minneapolis, as local officials slammed federal agencies for excluding them from the investigation.

Protest organizers said they expected to hold more than a thousand weekend demonstrations following the killing of motorist Renee Good, 37, by an Immigration and Customs Enforcement agent on Wednesday.

Officials in the midwestern state of Minnesota said their law enforcement agencies have been shut out of the investigation into the shooting.

A local prosecutor said Friday that federal investigators had taken Good’s car and shell casings from the scene.

The Trump administration has sought to paint Good as a ‘domestic terrorist,’ insisting that the agent who fatally shot her was acting in self-defence.

Cell phone footage apparently taken by the officer who fired the fatal shots shows him interacting with Good as he approaches and circles her car, and her saying, ‘I’m not mad at you’.

After he passes in front of the car, another agent can be heard ordering Good to exit the vehicle before she tries to drive off and shots ring out.

The agent filming the video can be heard saying ‘fucking bitch’ at the end of the clip.

The White House insisted the video gave weight to the officer’s claim of self-defence—even though the clip does not show the moment the car moved away, or him opening fire.

‘This is not the time to bend the rules. This is a time to follow the law...the fact that Pam Bondi’s department of justice and this presidential administration has already come to a conclusion about those facts is deeply concerning,’ Minneapolis mayor Jacob Frey, a Democrat, told a briefing on Friday.

‘We know that they’ve already determined much of the investigation,’ he said, adding that the state’s Bureau of Criminal Apprehension, within its department of public safety, has consistently run such investigations.

On Thursday, US Vice President JD Vance said that the ICE officer, named in US media as Jonathan Ross, had ‘absolute immunity’—a claim disputed by local prosecutors.

Court filings seen by AFP showed that in June 2025, Ross was dragged 100 yards along a road by a car driven by a man who was the subject of immigration enforcement activity.

‘When the FBI, when the federal agencies, say they won’t share evidence with the local authorities, the public can’t trust that it’s going to be a true, transparent investigation,’ said local Patrick O’Shaughnessy, 43.

Minnesota officials have said that local investigators were initially invited by the FBI to participate in the inquiry into the shooting of Good, but were subsequently blocked from taking part.

Good was one of four people who have been killed by ICE since Trump launched his immigration crackdown.

Good’s wife Becca Good told local media that they had gone to the scene of immigration enforcement activity to ‘support our neighbours’.

Local prosecutor Mary Moriarty, the Hennepin County attorney, said ‘our goal must be that a thorough investigation is completed at the local level’.

‘The FBI currently has, for example, Ms Good’s car, the shell casings and witness interviews’.

Moriarty unveiled an online evidence portal, calling for submissions so that all available leads could be compiled.

The divide between local and federal authorities widened Friday when US Secretary of Agriculture Brooke Rollins suspended the payment of $129.2 million in federal financial agriculture awards, according to a letter she posted on X.

Federal authorities have openly clashed with Minnesota officials over allegations that Somali immigrants have committed large-scale fraud to extract public benefit funds, with Rollins accusing local officials of turning ‘a blind eye’ to the problem.

Protest action continued Friday with hundreds gathering at a federal facility that has become a focal point of anti-ICE demonstrations, with at least one detention seen.

Federal immigration officers armed with pepper ball guns and tear gas clashed with the noisy crowd.

Several civil society organizations and advocacy groups, including the American Civil Liberties Union, are planning hundreds more protests on Saturday and Sunday.

title: SC SECRETARIAT: 46 cadre posts approved
body:
Immediate past CJ to be included in SC Secretariat Commission

The interim government has approved an organogram for the newly established Supreme Court Secretariat, creating 213 posts, including 46 cadre positions, in a move aimed at strengthening the judiciary’s administrative autonomy.

The cadre posts comprise one senior secretary, four additional secretaries, four joint secretaries, 17 deputy secretaries and 20 senior assistant secretaries.

Other approved vital positions include a chief accounts officer, system analyst, programmer, maintenance engineer, and assistant-level technical posts, according to a gazette notification issued by the SC Secretariat on January 8.

On January 8, the government approved an amendment to the Supreme Court Secretariat Ordinance, 2025, expanding the Supreme Court Secretariat Commission to include the  immediately retired chief justice.

The commission is mandated to issue directives and provide policy advice for improving judicial administration and enhancing the efficiency of the judiciary.

Previously, the commission consisted of the sitting chief justice as chairperson, the law minister or adviser, a chief justice–nominated Appellate Division judge, the National Human Rights Commission chairperson and the attorney general.

Supreme Court media focal person Md Muajjem Hussain, also special officer of the High Court Division, told New Age that the 46 cadre posts would be filled by judicial officers to be posted by the law ministry following proposals from the secretariat, while the Supreme Court would recruit the remaining officials and staff as per the approved organogram.

An seven-member committee headed by senior Appellate Division judge, Justice Md Ashfaqul Islam, had earlier proposed a larger organogram with 489 posts—107 officers and 382 support staff—at its first meeting on December 7, 2025.
