Among the migratory species spotted are dahuk, tirsul, nalkak, bhardi, rangabani, gangchil, ratchara, hutititi, hargila, balihans, jolpipi, comb duck, sharali kaste, chara, patari hans, kadakhocha, hurhur, khaira and sona rijia, many of which are now facing the threat of extinction.

Hosne Ara, professor of the department of zoology at Government Brozolal College in Khulna, said, ‘Every year during winter, migratory birds come to the seashore areas of the Bay of Bengal, riverbanks and paddy fields in Khulna from Siberia, China and the Himalayan region, where severe cold waves prevail.’

‘Bangladesh’s winter climate is suitable for migratory birds. These birds increase the natural beauty of rivers, wetlands and lakes in the country,’ she added.

Abul Hashem, professor of the department of zoology at Government Women’s College, said migratory birds coming from the coldest parts of Central Asia stay in marshlands, forests and plains near rivers in Bangladesh.

During a visit to Dumuria upazila on Thursday, it was found that large numbers of migratory birds were roaming in paddy fields and wetlands. Bird lovers from Khulna city gather there every day to see the beauty of these guest birds.

Meanwhile, indiscriminate hunting of migratory birds has reportedly intensified in Dumuria upazila and several adjoining areas of Khulna, raising serious concern among environmentalists.

According to local sources, a group of unscrupulous poachers has been setting traps under the cover of darkness to hunt migratory birds across Dumuria, Paikgachha and surrounding localities, including Golbunia, Dighi, Dakshin Kainmukhi, Natun Chak and Kharia. The hunting spree reportedly extends to neighbouring upazilas — Dacope, Koyra, Dighalia and Terokhada. The illegal activity usually begins after dusk and continues deep into the night.

Environmental organisations have demanded increased public awareness and stronger administrative action to protect migratory birds from poachers, stressing that community-level awareness is crucial to stopping the illegal practice.

Under the Wildlife Preservation Act of 1974 and the Wildlife Conservation and Security Act of 2012, killing birds carries a maximum punishment of one year’s imprisonment or a fine of Tk 100,000, or both. In case of repeat offences, the punishment increases to two years’ imprisonment or a fine of Tk 200,000, or both. However, despite the existence of these laws, their enforcement remains largely absent, locals alleged.

Talking to BSS, Sheikh Mahtab Hossain, vice-president of the Bangladesh Bird Slaughter Prevention Committee, said killing birds for a mere 100–200 grams of meat causes immense harm to nature.

‘People are destroying entire species for trivial gains without considering the ecological damage,’ he said, urging stronger awareness campaigns and more proactive administrative measures.

Dumuria upazila livestock officer Md Ashraful Kabir said the local administration and social welfare organisations are conducting awareness programmes to discourage bird hunting.

Dumuria upazila nirbahi officer Sabita Sarkar said migratory birds are friends of the environment and protecting them is a collective responsibility.

‘Unless legal action and punishment are ensured against hunters, they will not refrain from bird hunting through persuasion alone,’ she added.

title: Theaterian stages Tartuffe at BSA
body:
Theatre troupe Theaterian staged their second production titled Tartuffe at the experimental theatre hall of Bangladesh Shilpakala Academy on Friday.

Premiered on Thursday at the same venue, the play Tartuffe is a satire on religious hypocrisy written by French playwright Moliere and directed by Dhiman Chandra Barman.

The play revolves on Orgon, the head of a wealthy household, who has become completely devoted to Tartuffe, a man posing as a deeply religious and virtuous figure. Orgon ignores his own family members and invites Tartuffe to live at his house and plans to marry Tartuffe with his daughter Mariane and give his property and wealth. But Tartuffe secretly tries to seduce Orgon’s wife, Elmire, who exposes Tartuffe by tricking him into revealing his true intentions while Orgon is hiding and listening. Orgon confronts Tartuffe and then the fraud Tartuffe use legal documents to evict Orgon from his own house.

Amirul Mamun played the character of Tartuffe while Md Abdul Hai played the character of Orgon and Poly Chowdhury played Orgon’s wife Elmire.

Sumaiya Binte Jaman, Fahmida Ferdous Shammi, Hasibul Islam and Sreekanta Mandal, among others, portrayed various characters of the play.

The stage, light and direction were done by Dhiman Chandra Barman.

The production performed Lokenath Bhattacharya’s Bengali translation, while they adapted some words for better communication, said Dhiman Chandra Barman.

title: Noakhali register maiden win in seventh attempt
body:
Noakhali Express registered their first win of the season in their seventh outing when they beat the Rangpur Riders by nine runs in the ongoing BPL at the Sylhet International Stadium on Friday.

Noakhali, after being put into bat first, made 148 in 19.5 overs. Rangpur, somehow, managed to fall short as Hasan Mahmud took 4-26.

That overshadowed a hat-trick from Mrittunjoy Chowdhury, who became the second bowler of the season to achieve the feat.

Chasing a moderate target, Rangpur lost Litton Das and Dawid Malan early in the innings before Iftikhar Ahmed and Tawhid Hridoy added 63 runs off 51 balls to put them in a comfortable position.

When Zahir had the two set batters in consecutive overs, with Bilal having Mahmudullah in between, Rangpur started to crumble. They went from 86-2 to 112-6 to give Noakhali a final lifeline.

Hridoy and Iftikhar, who made 29 off 28 and 37 off 31, respectively, were cautious before getting out. But their approach put the batters to follow under pressure as the required run rate was climbing up.

Khushdil Shah, who scored 24 off 16, was their last hope. However, with 15 to get from the last over, Khushdil couldn’t cope.

Hasan took three wickets in the last over while giving away only five runs.

Noakhali’s top order—which had been misfiring—put on a much better display as they scored 66 runs for the loss of Shahadat Hossain, who made 14 off 8, in the powerplay.

Habibur Rahman Sohan made a quickfire 30 off 16 balls with three fours and two sixes, while Soumya Sarkar made 31 off 27.

But after Habibur’s departure in the eighth over, Noakhali seemed to have lost the plot as they started to lose wickets in pairs.

First, Soumya and Mohammad Nabi were dismissed by Khushdi in consecutive deliveries before Mustafizur Rahman did the same when he had Jaker Ali and Mehedi Hasan Rana.

Jaker, who came at four, made 38 off 37 before getting the elevation in the death overs. He added 49 runs off 41 balls with Mahidul Islam, while the latter made 28 off 21.

Having become the third bowler of the innings to get wickets in consecutive innings, Mrittunjoy Chowdhury became the second bowler after Rana in the season to get a hattrick in the last over of the match.

Mahidul was his first victim before he had Zahir Khan and Bilal Sami to complete the hattrick. Mrittunjoy, however, had an expensive outing, as he conceded 43 runs in 2.5 overs.

Apart from Mrittunjoy, Mustafiz also took three wickets at the expense of 18 runs. Nahid Rana, who had one for 17, dismantled the Noakhali batting with his fiery spell.

title: Equal rights to justice demanded
body:
Speakers including teachers, lawyers and activists at an award giving ceremony at the National Museum on Friday called for equal rights to justice and demanded justice for Tanwir Muhammad Tawqi.

They also condemn the interim government for delayed justice of Mosarat Jahan Munia, Sohagi Jahan Tonu and journalist couple Sagar Sarowar and Meherun Runi.

The award giving ceremony of the 11th National Twaki Painting and Essay Competition 2025 was organised by Santras Nirmul Twaki Mancha to celebrate the 30th birth anniversary of Tawqi, who was found dead on the banks of the Shitalakhya in Narayanganj at the age of 17, on March 8, 2013.

Dhaka University professor emeritus Serajul Islam Choudhury was present as chief guest while economist-activist Anu Muhammd, lawyer and free speech advocate Sara Hossain, lawyer Jyotirmoy Barua and poet Halim Azad, among others, spoke at the event as special guests, which was chaired by Tawqi’s father and cultural activist Rafiur Rabbi.

Serajul Islam Choudhury said that Santras Nirmul Twaki Mancha organised cultural events regularly and demanded justice creatively, which is inspiring.

‘Injustice and insecurity will be ended from society if we can change the capitalist development policy which has become inhuman,’ Serajul Islam Choudhury said, adding that justice is delayed again and again, which portrays the character of the state.

Teens now form gangs in their vicinity because of a lack of cultural activities and sports in society, he said.

Anu Muhammd said that after the mass-uprising, cultural events were decreased and participation of women were discouraged.

‘The interim government took development projects and suppressed people, almost the same as the Hasina-led government did and they also delayed justice,’ he said.

Sara Hossain urged all political parties and victim families to raise their voice for justice for Tawqi.

Jyotirmoy Barua claimed that equality in justice was not established in this interim government tenure, which is frustrating.

‘The state detained the Bawm community accused of the bank robbery but the interim government could not release them and no one spoke about them,’ he said.

title: Maulana Bhashani’s close associate Syed Irfanul Bari dies
body:
Syed Irfanul Bari, close associate of Maulana Abdul Hamid Khan Bhashani, died at his house at Santosh in Tangail on Friday noon.

Syed Irfanul Bari, also editor of weekly Haque Katha, died at about 12:15 pm. He was suffering from old age complications, according to his family members. He is survived by his wife, three daughters and a host of relatives and admires.

Jatiya Mukti Council secretary Faiezul Hakim and Revolutionary Communist League general secretary Iqbal Kabir Jahid, in separate condolence messages, expressed deep shock at his death.

Irfanul Bari was also a former trustee board member of Maulana Abdul Hamid Bhashani Science and Technology University in Santosh and authored some books on the life and works of Maulana Bhashani.

title: Storms spark travel mayhem, power cuts in northern Europe
body:
Gale-force winds and storms barrelled through northern Europe on Friday, disrupting air and rail travel and cutting power to hundreds of thousands in freezing temperatures.

Some 50 flights were cancelled in London’s Heathrow airport, affecting thousands of passengers, with air travel disrupted across Europe from the Czech Republic to Moscow.

Forecasters from Britain to Germany urged people to stay indoors as they issued weather warnings, including the rare, highest-level red wind alert for the British Isles of Scilly and Cornwall in southwestern England.

Some 57,000 homes in the UK remained without electricity, according to the National Grid energy provider, after Storm Goretti brought strong winds and heavy snow to parts of the country overnight.

More than 250 schools remained closed across Scotland, which has struggled through bad weather for much of the first week back after the Christmas break.

In France, Goretti cut power to some 3,80,000 homes, most of them in the northern Normandy region, the Enedis power provider said.

Overnight, gusts of up to 216 kilometres per hour were registered in France’s northwestern Manche region, authorities said.

The winds felled trees with at least one crashing on residential buildings in France’s Seine-Maritime region, without injuries, authorities said.

Gusts of up to 160 kph lashed England and Wales with the Met Office forecasting agency warning of ‘very large waves’ bringing ‘dangerous conditions to coastal areas’.

It also issued an amber snow warning in Wales, central England and parts of northern England, predicting snow of up to 30 centimetres in some areas.

More than 10 people have died in weather-related accidents this week across Europe.

The latest deaths were reported by Turkish media, where five people were killed.

While two were killed in separate accidents involving dislodged roof tiles, a Syrian man died when a wall fell on him, a construction worker was swept into the Aegean Sea and a pensioner fell off a roof.

Schools remained shut in parts of northern France, where weather alerts have been issued in 30 other regions.

Giant waves crashed over harbour walls across France’s far northwest overnight and, as the storm moved eastwards it brought flooding and forced the closure of roads and ports including Dieppe.

Northern Germany faced severe disruption from heavy snow and high winds brought by Storm Elli, with schools ordered closed in the cities of Hamburg and Bremen and long-distance rail services cancelled.

Flights were cancelled or postponed at Hamburg airport while several main roads were paralysed, including some hundreds of miles to the south in the Frankfurt region.

The German weather service warned of ‘hurricane-force’ winds in areas on the North Sea as well as in the southwest, and up to 15 centimetres of snow in parts of the country on Friday.

Some 600 schools were closed in Moldova until next Monday and around 1,000 homes were without electricity in Romania.

Floodwaters were meanwhile receding in parts of the Balkans on Friday after heavy snowfall and torrential downpours earlier in the week triggered hundreds of evacuations across several countries and killed at least two people.

In Albania, one of the hardest-hit in the region, prime minister Edi Rama said authorities were beginning to count the cost of flooding after hundreds of homes were inundated primarily in the south.

But weather warnings for icy conditions and snowfall remained in effect across most of the region, including Serbia, where parts of the west have been without power for days after a snowstorm knocked out power lines.

title: Meeting on energy, power sector master plan 2026-2050 held
body:
A meeting on energy and power sector master plan 2026-2050 was held at the state guest house Jamuna in Dhaka on Wednesday.

Under the chairmanship of chief adviser Muhammad Yunus, the meeting was, among others, attended by power, energy and mineral resources adviser Muhammad Fouzul Kabir Khan, finance adviser Saleh Uddin Ahmed, planning adviser Wahid Uddin Mahmud, commerce adviser Sheikh Bashir Uddin, industry adviser Adilur Rahman Khan, environment, forest and climate change adviser Syeda Rizwana Hasan, and Bangladesh Rural Electrification Board chairman Major General SM Zia-Ul-Azim, said a press release.

The aim of this master plan is to ensure reliable, affordable and sustainable primary energy and electricity for all the people of Bangladesh through optimal use of domestic resources, ensuring energy security, increasing efficiency and environmental responsibility.

The meeting identified the policy gaps of the previous three master plans and briefly reviewed them.

The implementation of the new master plan in three phases— first phase 2026-2030, second phase 2030-2040 and third phase 2040-50— was discussed.

Chief adviser thanked all those involved for highlighting the details of the power and energy sector in detail.

He has directed to create a separate institution for research related to power and energy.

The meeting presented some recommendations on power generation, transmission, supply, environmental and economic sustainability and institutional reforms and set a goal to make the primary energy sector more secure, efficient, less import-dependent and financially sustainable by 2050.

title: Horse racing revives rural tradition in Pakundia
body:
A traditional horse racing competition, once a common feature of rural Bengal but now on the verge of extinction, drew thousands of spectators to Pakundia upazila of Kishoreganj on Thursday afternoon.

The event was held at Boro Ajaldi ground adjacent to Sukhia Bazar, where people from surrounding villages gathered hours before the competition began.

Men, women, children and elderly spectators lined both sides of the field, creating a festive atmosphere. Many parents lifted their children onto their shoulders so they could get a clear view, while groups of women and girls attended together.

Local residents said the event brought back memories of a tradition that was once regularly practiced in the area. Many spectators expressed excitement at witnessing horse racing after a long gap and said they wanted the younger generation to experience this fading rural sport.

Bangladesh Nationalist Party-nominated candidate for the Kishoreganj-2 constituency, Md Jalal Uddin, attended the event as the chief guest. Former Sukhia Union Juba Dal president Amin Kazi presided over the programme, while current president Wasimul Bari Wasim conducted it.

Chandipasha Union Parishad chairman Md Shamsuddin, upazila BNP joint convener Atiqur Rahman Masud, Municipal BNP president SAM Minhaj Uddin, upazila Juba Dal senior joint convener Rakibul Alam Choton and Sukhia Union BNP convener Monirul Islam Shamim were present, among others.

Former Sukhia Union Juba Dal general secretary Alamin Mia formally inaugurated the competition.

Spectator Ripon Mia said he tries to attend horse racing events whenever possible. ‘I brought my family on Friday because it is close to my house. This tradition may not exist in the future, so I wanted my children to see it.’

Similar sentiments were echoed by spectators Ujjal Mia and Zahirul Islam of Ghagra village, who said that horse racing, once a familiar rural pastime, has now become a rare sight.

Addressing the gathering, Jalal Uddin said traditional rural entertainment plays an important role in shaping the younger generation. He emphasised that organising more such events could help keep youth away from drugs, terrorism and social crimes such as eve-teasing.

title: MUSABBIR MURDER: Protest continues as police yet to identify killers
body:
Protest continued on Friday demanding justice over the murder of Jatiyatabadi Swechchhasebak Dal leader Azizur Rahman Musabbir as his killers has yet to be identified as of Friday night, two days after assailants had shot him dead in Dhaka city.

A group of protesters began their demonstration at West Tejturi Bazar behind Bashundhara City Shopping Mall after Friday prayers and marched to Tejgaon police station and gathered outside its compound.

Tejgaon police officer-in-charge Kya Swee Nue said that protesters took position in front the police station at about 2:00pm, protesting at the murder of Azizur Rahman Musabbir.

They later left the area after around 15 minutes, he said.

The protesters then marched around Farmgate and stopped at Karwan Bazar, pressing for several demands, including immediate arrest of the assailants.

Dhaka Metropolitan Police deputy commissioner for Tejgaon Division Ibne Mizan said that the police were still trying to find out the identities of the two suspects spotted in CCTV footage.

‘Police efforts are on to identify the suspects and arrest them as soon as possible. Apart from the police, Detective Branch and Rapid Action Battalion teams are also actively working on the case,’ he added.

The police suspected ‘extortion’ behind the murder of Musabbir, joint general secretary of the central committee of Swechchhasebak Dal, the volunteer wing of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party.

BNP leadership, however, suspects political opponents behind the murder.

Musabbir and Abu Sufian, general secretary of Karwan Bazar Van Association, were shot at about 8:20pm on January 7 in front of the Ahsanullah Institute of Technical and Vocational Education and Training Centre in Tejturibazar area, beside Star Kabab on Kazi Nazrul Islam Avenue near Karwan Bazar.

The police and eyewitnesses said that Musabbir and Sufian were walking towards the main road through the alley when two miscreants, who were waiting in ambush in a small dark lane in front of the AITVET Centre, opened fire on them before fleeing the scene.

Both Musabbir and Sufian then ran back into the alley and collapsed after going a short distance.

They were taken to BRB Hospital at Panthapath, where Musabbir was declared dead.

Sufian is undergoing treatment at Dhaka Medical College Hospital.

Musabbir’s wife Suraiya Begum filed a case with the Tejgaon police on Thursday morning against four or five unidentified suspects.

title: 5 children among 13 killed in Israeli attacks in Gaza
body:
Gaza’s civil defence agency said Israeli attacks in the Palestinian territory on Thursday killed at least 13 people, including five children, despite a ceasefire that has largely halted the fighting.

Four people, including three children, were killed when a drone struck a tent sheltering displaced people in southern Gaza, agency spokesman Mahmud Bassal said.

In the north of the Gaza Strip, an 11-year-old girl was killed near the Jabalia refugee camp and a strike on a school killed one person, while a drone near Khan Yunis in the south killed a man, the agency added.

Two more Gazans, including a child, were killed in other attacks, reported the agency, which operates under Hamas authority.

Later on Thursday evening, four more people were killed in an Israeli air strike that targeted a house in an eastern area of Gaza City, Bassal said, adding that rescue work to search for several people who were missing had begun.

‘The death toll has risen to 13 as a result of Israeli strikes on the Gaza Strip since this morning in a clear violation of the ceasefire agreement,’ Bassal said.

In a statement Friday morning, the Israeli military said it ‘precisely struck Hamas terrorists and terror infrastructure in the southern and northern Gaza Strip’ in response to a ‘failed projectile’ launch.

‘The projectile that was launched from the Gaza Strip constitutes a violation of the ceasefire agreement,’ the statement added.

Since October 10, a fragile US-sponsored truce in Gaza has largely halted the fighting between Israeli forces and Hamas, but both sides have alleged frequent violations.

Hamas spokesman Hazem Qassem said that the strikes in Gaza on Thursday ‘confirm the Israeli occupation’s renunciation of its commitment to the ceasefire’.

Israeli forces have killed at least 425 Palestinians in Gaza since the ceasefire took effect, according to Gaza’s health ministry.

At least 21 people were killed on November 22 in Israeli strikes, making it one of the deadliest days in Gaza since the ceasefire came into effect.

The Israeli military said militants have killed three of its soldiers during the same period.

Meanwhile, Palestinian vice president Hussein al-Sheikh met on Friday with former UN Middle East envoy Nickolay Mladenov, who is expected to head the US‑backed Board of Peace in Gaza.

The meeting in the occupied West Bank city of Ramallah comes a day after Mladenov held talks with Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu and met with president Isaac Herzog.

Bulgarian diplomat Mladenov served as the United Nations envoy for the Middle East peace process from early 2015 until the end of 2020.

Media reports say he is expected to serve as the representative on the ground in Gaza for the Board of Peace — a transitional body for the war-battered Palestinian territory which US President Donald Trump would theoretically chair.

In a statement on X, Sheikh said that during his meeting with Mladenov, ‘an in-depth discussion took place on all political and field developments in the Palestinian territories’.

He added there was ‘a focus on the situation in the Gaza Strip, means of transitioning to the second phase of the ceasefire, mechanisms for implementing the US president Donald Trump’s plan, and UN Security Council Resolution 2803’.

title: Sheikh Mujib’s homecoming day today
body:
Today is the homecoming day of the country’s founding president Sheikh Mujibur Rahman.

Mujib returned to independent Bangladesh on January 10, 1972, after his  release from solitary confinement for nine months and a half in a Pakistan prison during the War of Independence.

The Pakistan government released him on January 8, 1972. From Pakistan he flew to London where he stayed on January 9 and met the then British prime minister Edward Heath and addressed the international media.

He flew to Dhaka on January 10 with a brief stopover in New Delhi. A huge crowd welcomed him back at the erstwhile Tejgaon airport in the capital Dhaka.

Mujib, who was the president of the Awami League, was earlier picked up by the occupation forces of Pakistan from his residence on Road 32 of Dhanmondi in Dhaka at the midnight of March 25, 1971, after they had started a crackdown on the unarmed Bengalis in what was then East Pakistan.

Traditionally, the Awami League and its associate and front organisations, along with various socio-cultural bodies, used to observe the homecoming anniversary with elaborate programmes every year.

However, since the ouster of the Sheikh Hasina-led Awami League regime amid a student-led mass uprising on August 5, 2024, the day had not been officially observed by the party.

Most of the party’s senior leaders, including its president Sheikh Hasina, are currently facing numerous cases on various charges, including allegations of mass killings during the July uprising, and many of them are either in hiding or staying abroad.

In May 2025, the interim government issued a gazette imposing ban on all activities of Awami League and its affiliated, associate and like-minded organisations until the completion of the ongoing trial proceedings against the party’s leaders and activists at the International Crimes Tribunal.

title: Trump scraps new Venezuela attack after prisoner release
body:
US president Donald Trump said Friday he called off a second wave of attacks on Venezuela after the government, whose leftist president was removed by Washington, began releasing prisoners.

Trump made the comments as he prepared to meet major oil corporations that he said will invest at least $100 billion in Venezuela, which has the world’s largest oil reserves.

Trump was implicitly making clear he is ready again to use force to get his way in Venezuela, which he has vowed to force to enrich the United States, especially oil companies.

‘Venezuela is releasing large numbers of political prisoners as a sign of “Seeking Peace,’’ Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform.

‘Because of this cooperation, I have cancelled the previously expected second Wave of Attacks,’ he said.

The United States on Friday also announced that it had seized another tanker near Venezuela as it enforces an embargo on its oil, which makes Washington the undisputed power on its key export.

Venezuela began releasing prisoners on Thursday in the first such gesture since US forces removed and detained president Nicolas Maduro in a deadly January 3 raid, with his deputy Delcy Rodriguez taking over.

Former Venezuelan opposition candidate Enrique Marquez — who opposed  Maduro in the contested 2024 presidential election — was among those released Thursday.

‘It’s all over now,’ Marquez said in a video taken by a local journalist of him and his wife, accompanied by another released opposition member, Biagio Pilieri.

The White House quickly took credit for winning the prisoners’ freedom.

Trump had earlier played down democracy as a motivating factor for the attack, despite years of the United States saying that Maduro was illegitimate elections were filled with fraud.

But Trump said he would meet next week with Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado, whom he earlier brushed aside as a ‘very nice woman’ who lacked the ‘respect’ to lead Venezuela.

‘I understand she’s coming in next week sometime, and I look forward to saying hello to her,’ Trump told Fox News host Sean Hannity in an interview.

Trump had earlier voiced jealousy that Machado won the latest Nobel Peace Prize and said he deserved it.

Interim leader Rodriguez’s brother, parliament speaker Jorge Rodriguez, said ‘a large number of Venezuelan and foreign nationals’ were being immediately freed for the sake of ‘peaceful coexistence.’

Renowned Spanish-Venezuelan activist Rocio San Miguel was among five Spanish citizens freed, according to Spain’s foreign ministry.

She was imprisoned since February 2024 over a purported plot to assassinate Maduro, which she denied.

On Tuesday, Trump had told Republican lawmakers that Rodriguez’s administration was closing a ‘torture chamber’ in Caracas but gave no further details.

Venezuelan rights NGO Foro Penal estimates over 800 political prisoners are in the country’s jails.

Maduro was seized in a special forces raid accompanied by airstrikes, operations that left 100 people dead, according to Caracas.

US forces took Maduro and his wife Cilia Flores to New York to face trial on drugs charges.

Trump said the United States would ‘run’ the Caribbean country for a transitional period and tap into its oil reserves for years.

Delcy Rodriguez insisted Thursday her country was ‘not subordinate or subjugated.’

‘Nobody surrendered. There was fighting for the homeland’ when the US forces attacked, she said during a ceremony for the Venezuelans killed.

Trump announced a plan earlier this week for the United States to sell between 30 million and 50 million barrels of Venezuelan crude, with Caracas then using the money to buy US-made products.

‘I feel we’ll have more opportunities if the oil is in the hands of the United States than in the hands of the government,’ said Jose Antonio Blanco, 26.

title: Law, order concerns BNP
body:
Leaders of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party on Friday expressed concerns over the law and order across the country ahead of the 12 February Jatiya Sangsad elections, saying that he was not satisfied with the performance of law enforcement agencies.

‘The rate at which political leaders are being killed, particularly some leaders of our party, is truly worrying,’ said BNP secretary general Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir while talking to journalists at his residence in Thakurgaon.

‘We have strongly condemned these murders, but no action has been taken by the government. We hope that the authorities will act responsibly and prevent such incidents during the elections,’ he said.

Reaffirming the BNP’s stance on reform, Fakhrul said that the party had never opposed reform initiatives and had earlier proposed holding a referendum on reforms alongside the parliamentary election.

‘The election and the referendum will be held on the same day. Reform is a continuous process, and there is no reason to say no to reform,’ he said, adding that the proposed reforms were largely in line with the BNP’s earlier 31-point reform proposals announced in 2016 and updated in 2023.

Regarding BNP acting chair Tarique Rahman’s visit to northern districts, Fakhrul described it as a personal goodwill tour.

Tarique Rahman plans to visit Bogura, his home district, then pay respects at the grave of July martyr Abu Sayeed in Rangpur, followed by visits to Dinajpur and Thakurgaon, where he will take part in mass prayers for Khaleda Zia and honour other martyrs.

On student union elections, Fakhrul said that during the previous government, student organisations, especially Chhatra Dal, were prevented from operating in universities, limiting their organisational activities.

He emphasised that university elections had never influenced national elections and hoped that they would not have an impact this time either.

Meanwhile, BNP standing committee member Nazrul Islam Khan on Friday urged the interim government to be active and strategic in maintaining the law and order, stressing that improvement in the situation was essential to ensure a free and fair election.

Speaking to journalists while visiting a photo exhibition on the life of former prime minister and BNP chair Khaleda Zia at the Zia Udyan, Nazrul said that maintaining the law and order was a government responsibility.

Describing Khaleda’s political life, Nazrul said that her vast political life could not be captured in a single programme and should be highlighted through multiple events.

He also said that people wanted to know Khaleda’s life and learn from it, adding that such exhibitions would especially inspire the younger generation.

Referring to her legacy, Nazrul Islam said that Khaleda fought throughout her political life to protect democracy, independence, and national sovereignty.

The large public turnout at her funeral reflected her deep connection with the people, he added.

Regarding rebel candidates within the party, Nazrul said that those who were contesting the polls against party decisions had been asked to withdraw their nominations.

Noting that many had already complied with the party directive, he hoped that the situation would improve within the stipulated time.

title: UGC drafts ord for more power
body:
A more powerful body is likely to replace the University Grants Commission of Bangladesh, the apex body responsible for overseeing higher education in Bangladesh, as the UGC has drafted the Bangladesh Commission on Higher Education Ordinance, 2025.

The proposed commission will have more independence and work directly under the president instead of any ministry, according to the draft ordinance.

The University Grants Commission works under the education ministry.

If approved, the Bangladesh Commission on Higher Education Ordinance, 2025, will repeal the University Grants Commission of Bangladesh Order, 1973 (President’s Order).

As per the draft, the status of the proposed commission’s chairman will of a full minister while the status of the members will be of a judge of the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court.

The proposed commission will be able to formulate necessary guidelines on its own, introduce the ranking system for the country’s universities and give directions and facilitate the universities to be connected with different national and international institutions to create skilled workforce.

The draft ordinance also says that the proposed commission will have a trust fund to facilitate eligible teachers and students to get higher education irrespective of their race, religion, gender, birth place or physical conditions.

The education ministry has already sent the draft ordinance to different stakeholders for taking their opinions. The draft was also published on the ministry’s web site on December 10, 2025, seeking public opinions within 30 days.

UGC member professor M Anwar Hossen told New Age on Wednesday that after getting the opinions, the education ministry would finalise the ordinance.

Currently, the commission is working under the University Grants Commission of Bangladesh Order, 1973 (President’s Order).

According to the commission, the initiative for the draft ordinance was taken in April 2025 when then education adviser Wahiduddin Mahmud shared with the commission chairman Professor SMA Faiz a 15-point suggestion on higher education, sent by the chief adviser for consideration.

At that time, the adviser showed interest in changing the UGC’s name to ‘University Commission of Bangladesh’ or ‘Higher Education Commission of Bangladesh’.

Decision was made then not to keep the word ‘grants’ in the name as it gives the feeling that the commission only transacts money, officials said.

The draft law would outline the framework for the proposed commission and different processes, including the appointment of university vice-chancellors.

It also reads that it becomes inevitable and urgent to transform the UGC to a higher education commission to establish the universities as appropriate institutions and ensure accountability, transparency and good governance.

The appointing authority of the proposed commission will be the president and the commission will be responsible to the president.  The proposed commission can file cases or cases can be filed against it.

Its head office will be in the capital Dhaka and if necessary, it can set up divisional/regional offices.

The proposed commission will consist of chairperson, eight commissioners (full-time members) and 10 part-time members.

Based on recommendations of a search committee, the chairman and the commissioners will be appointed. As per the existing ordinance, they are appointed by the government.

The UGC ordinance says that the number of full-time members will be at least two, but not exceed five, while the number of part-time members are nine.

Like the existing ordinance, the proposed ordinance stipulates that the chairman and other full-time members of the commission will hold office for a period of four years. All of them will be eligible for holding office for a second term, which is allowed only for the chairman under the existing law.

The activities of the proposed commission will include formulating necessary guidelines on its own for the development of higher education, making budget for the public universities, monitoring all universities’ budget implementation process, research, development plans and development projects, introducing ranking system for the country’s universities and publishing ranking in every three years, supporting the universities to improve their curriculum based on international standard, and giving directions and facilitating the universities to be connected with different national and international institutions to create skilled workforce.

The proposed ordinance says that the commission will have its own fund which will comprise grants and loans from the government, donations and endowments, receipts of the commission from its own earnings, grants or aid from any government-approved foreign agency or country and other sources as may be approved by the government or commission.

The existing ordinance says that the commission will have its own und which will comprise grants and loans from the government, donations and endowments, and receipts of the commission from such other sources as may be approved by the government.

Currently, the number of approved universities in the country is 172, including 56 public and 116 private.

title: Severe cold, dense fog threaten crops
body:
As a cold wave continues to sweep over many districts of the country, agricultural experts have warned that prolonged low temperatures and dense fog could damage several winter crops, increasing the risk of disease, plant mortality and lower yields.

The country recorded the season’s lowest temperature of 6.8 degree Celsius on Friday amid the mild to moderate cold wave that has been prevailing for two weeks.

The experts said that a lack of sunlight caused by persistent fog could adversely affect boro seedbeds, potato, tomato and other rabi crops, making them vulnerable to fungal and bacterial infections.

Sher-e-Bangla Agricultural University plant pathology professor Abu Noman Faruq Ahmmed said that farmers should take preventive measures, including timely application of fungicides if fungal infections appear in crops.

He, however, observed that dense fog and severe cold usually reduced insect attacks, which could be considered a limited advantage of the prevailing weather.

Bangladesh Agricultural University genetics and plant breeding professor ABM Arif Hasan Khan Robin said that crop losses could be higher this year as many farmers planted tomatoes, mustard seedbeds and other rabi crops late due to rainfall for an extended period in November past year.

‘If crops do not receive adequate sunlight, their growth and productivity will be seriously affected,’ he said.

The Bangladesh Meteorological Department said on Friday that cold and foggy conditions were likely to persist for at least five more days or more.

A mild to moderate cold wave is sweeping over the Rangpur and Rajshahi divisions and the districts of Narsingdi, Jashore, Chuadanga and Kushtia, and it may continue, the BMD said.

The department reported that a deep depression over the southwest Bay of Bengal was moving northwestwards and was likely to cross the north Sri Lanka coast by today, while a ridge of sub-continental high pressure has extended over West Bengal and adjoining western Bangladesh, influencing regional weather.

The country’s lowest temperature on Friday was 6.8C at Tetulia in Panchagarh under the Rangpur division, while the highest was 29.2C in Sylhet.

On January 6, the season’s previous lowest temperature of 7C was recorded in Rajshahi.

Department of Agricultural Extension additional director Md Jamal Uddin acknowledged the risks to crops and said that farmers had been advised to take precautionary measures to minimise losses.

‘We have not estimated the extent of damage yet,’ he said, adding that the assessment was likely to begin on January 13.

He said that if dense fog persisted for several more days, many crops could rot due to excess moisture and a lack of sunlight.

According to the DAE, the target for boro seedbed cultivation this season is 2,48,000 hectares, of which about 70 per cent has already been planted.

Potato cultivation has a target of 4,67,000 hectares, with nearly 87 per cent already sown.

The government has estimated production of 44 million tonnes of food grains, including 22.7 million tonnes of boro rice, in this rabi season.

Experts warned that a lack of sunlight for an extended period could also trigger late blight disease in potatoes, onions and other crops.

If sunlight is absent for three consecutive days, potato fields may develop late blight, which can destroy entire plants, while boro seedbeds remain at risk of seedling blight, they said.

New Age correspondent in Kurigram reported that boro paddy seedbeds in several parts of the district had suffered due to severe cold and dense fog, causing concern among farmers.

Seedlings in many seedbeds have turned yellowish and reddish, raising fears of seedling shortages and higher prices during the current boro season.

Partial damage to seedbeds was reported in areas, including Kaliganj and Berubari unions of Nageswari upazila, Joymonirhat and Andharijhar unions of Bhurungamari upazila, as well as Kurigram Sadar, Ulipur and Chilmari upazilas.

According to the district agriculture office, the boro cultivation target in Kurigram is 1,17,365 hectares, while the seedbed target is 5,550 hectares.

Farmers are being advised to apply bio-fertilisers, potash, zinc sulphate and chelated zinc to increase disease resistance during severe cold. Other suggestions include removing dew by gently pulling ropes over seedbeds in the morning, covering seedbeds with polythene at night, retaining water in the evening and draining it in the morning, and re-irrigating using deep tube wells.

title: 645 appeals filed, hearings begin today
body:
A total of 645 appeals have been filed with the Election Commission challenging the cancellation of nomination papers and contesting the acceptance of a nomination by returning officers for the 13th Jatiya Sangsad elections.

The commission began accepting appeals on January 5, with the deadline for submissions ending on Friday.

On the final day alone, 176 appeals were lodged, according to commission officials.

The hearing of appeals is scheduled to start today at 10:00am and would continue until January 18.

All hearings would take place at the Election  Commission auditorium at Agargaon, Dhaka from 10:00am to 5:00pm.

A total of 2,568 nomination papers were submitted for the Jatiya Sangsad elections, of which 1,842 were declared valid after the scrutiny.

Three nomination papers had been submitted for former prime minister and BNP chair Khaleda Zia for the Feni-1, Bogura-7, and Dinajpur-3 JS constituencies.

However, following her death on December 30, the EC said that those nominations were not taken up for scrutiny.

The EC data show that nomination papers of the highest number of independent candidates – 338 – were rejected during the scrutiny.

Among the political parties, the Jatiya Party accounted for the largest number -- 59 -- of rejected nominations, followed by Islami Andolan Bangladesh with 39 nominations.

The BNP and the Communist Party of Bangladesh each saw 25 nomination papers rejected.

The Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami had 10 nominations rejected, while three candidates from the National Citizen Party were disqualified.

During the hearings, a maximum of three people, including the appellant, would be allowed in the Election Commission’s appeal hearing room for cases challenging the acceptance or rejection of nomination papers by returning officers.

title: Law, order yet to be restored while polls nearing
body:
The government is yet to restore the law and order across the country just a month ahead of the national election, with people passing their days amid frequent incidents of violence and crimes.

Incidents of murder, robbery, theft, kidnapping, extortion have been going on unabated, raising concern among the people from all walks of life.

The government could not take effective measures against mob violence, attack on shrines, assaulting bauls, and other crimes.

On the other hand, the lack of preventive security measures by law enforcers, assaults on police, low police morale, frequent street protests, and political violence created chaos in maintaining law and order, according to rights activists.

In the morning of December 29, a group of people attacked an anti-extortion human chain in front of the Karwan Bazar kitchen market in the capital.

In the evening of January 7, unidentified assailants shot dead Bangladesh Nationalist Party’s volunteer wing Jatiyatabadi Swechchhasebak Dal central joint general secretary Azizur Rahman Musabbir at Tejturi Bazar in the capital.

Jatiyatabadi Swechchhasebak Dal central general secretary Razib Ahsan said that they suspected the BNP’s political opponent of committing the Musabbir murder to foil the party’s progress before the election while inspector general of police Baharul Alam claimed extortion behind the murder.

Meanwhile, while talking to reporters at his residence in Thakurgaon on Friday, Bangladesh Nationalist Party secretary general Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir said that many political leaders, especially BNP leaders, were killed but the government did not take any effective measures.

‘I hope that the government will play an active role so that recurrence of such incidents would not take place during the elections,’ said Fakhrul.

A number of traders said that they had organised demonstrations protesting at extortion by Abdur Rahman, an expelled leader of the BNP youth wing Jatiyatabadi Juba Dal, and his followers.

In the early morning of January 8, two persons were killed and at least four others injured in a crude bomb explosion allegedly while making such bombs in Shariatpur’s Jajira upazila.

The deceased were identified as Sohan Bepari, 32, and Nobin Hossain, 22 -- both hailing from the upazila.

According to the PHQ crime statistics, 3,785 murder cases, 1,935 robbery cases, 9,762 theft cases, 1,101 kidnapping cases, and 1,815 arms cases were filed across the country in 2025.

At least 197 people were killed in mob beatings between January 1 and December 30 in 2025 but the figure was 128 in 2024, according to rights organisation Ain o Salish Kendra data.

Besides, at least 102 individuals were killed and 4,744 injured in 401 incidents of political violence between January and December of 2025, according to ASK data.

Md Mahbubur Rahman, a businessman in Mirpur, said that he was in fear about the ongoing law and order.

‘We are afraid because of the pre-election- and election-time violence. We want to cast our votes in a free and fair environment,’ he added.

Bangladesh Legal Aid and Services Trust honourary executive director Sara Hossain, also a Supreme Court lawyer, said that there were apprehensions of violence and worsening law and order ahead of and during the election.

‘Although cases were filed and many accused arrested after such incidents, we need preventive measures to ensure security before incidents happen,’ she added.

She urged the police, the army and the political parties to play active roles before the elections in this regard.

The police force lost its morale when 450 of the 664 police stations and 1,000 vehicles across the country were attacked and vandalised following the downfall of Sheikh Hasina-led authoritarian government on August 5, 2024.

The police are yet to recover 1,333 of the 5,763 looted firearms and recapture 700 of the 2,200 inmates that ran away from jails, according to the police headquarters and the Department of Prisons.

Prison officials also said that 27 of the 98 looted firearms remained recovered.

The police have also been facing assaults since the interim government assumed office on August 8, 2024.

In 2025, 601 incidents of police assault took place across the country, according to police headquarters data.

On January 3, after the police arrested Students Against Discrimination’s Habiganj district unit member secretary Mahdi Hasan several hundered leaders and activists besieged the Shaistaganj police station.

Members of the Bangladesh Army were called in and deployed to bring the situation under control.

In the video on the incident that went viral, Mahdi was heard saying, ‘The administration here is our people. You have arrested our activist and are arguing with us. You OC said “what happened as you are activists of the movement”.’

‘We have 17 martyrs here in Habiganj. We burned down the Baniachang police station. We burned sub-inspector Santosh [who later died]. It’s okay that you came here, but I want to know how you dared to say this from your position,’ Mahdi told the OC.

The Habiganj Senior Judicial Magistrate Court-3 on January 4 granted bail to Mahdi, about 14 hours after he had been arrested for obstructing the police in discharging their duties.

Many police officials, ranging from sub-inspector to superintendent of police, told New Age that they lost their morale for carrying out their duties for such kind of issues and they were also aggrieved.

Inspector general of police Baharul Alam on Thursday told New Age that if they could not maintain order during road blocks for any demands, it would be difficult for them to perform duties in the JS elections.

‘Not only police officials but also I am aggrieved at such incidents. I told every meeting of the council of advisers committee on the law and order, “If we can’t contain the street protests over any issues, it would be difficult to hold the elections peacefully,’ said the IGP.

During the tenure of the interim government, several dozen shrines were vandalised and set on fire.

In the early hours of December 27, Hazrat Baba Shah Satyapir Mazar and several adjacent graves were vandalised allegedly by some unidentified miscreants in Thakurgaon town, creating tensions among the local residents and devotees.

Another Supreme Court lawyer and human rights activist, Jyotirmoy Barua, said that the current government would be named number one in the country’s history for its failure to maintain the law and order.

Inquilab Mancha convener Sharif Osman Hadi was shot in the head from a close range by a motorbike rider in Dhaka on December 12, 2025, a day after the announcement of the election schedule.

The 13th parliamentary election is scheduled to be held on February 12.

He had been conducting election campaign as an aspiring independent candidate for the Dhaka-8 constituency in the 12 February JS elections.

He was later flown to Singapore where he died under treatment at a hospital on December 18, 2025.

The murder of Hadi triggered street protests in Dhaka and elsewhere across the country.

In two other incidents on the night of November 18 and in the early hours of November 19, several hundred people in mobs set fire to the offices of the Bangla daily Prothom Alo and The Daily Star in the capital following the death of Hadi.

Members of the law enforcement and security agencies were seen failing to control the situation though the incidents had gone on for several hours.

On December 22, Prothom Alo filed a case against 400-500 unnamed people and The Daily Star filed another case against 350-400 unnamed people in connection with the vandalism, looting and arson on their offices.

The police have arrested 35 people so far in these connections.

Citing the Prothom Alo incident, IGP Baharul said that there were only 25 police members besides the spot, who could not manage enough courage to go forward against a large number of people.

‘People from all walks of society have a responsibility to support police in such situations. Otherwise, it would be impossible to ensure the law and order,’ he added.

On December 26, a bomb explosion at Ummul Quran International Madrassah at Hasnabad in South Keraniganj left four people, including a woman and two children, injured.

On December 27, the police in a drive recovered bomb-making materials, crude bomb, and liquid flammable chemicals at a location in South Keraniganj in Dhaka, a day after the madrassah bomb blast.

On December 22, a senior leader of Jatiya Sramik Shakti, the labour wing of the National Citizen Party, was shot in the ear at an apartment at Sonadanga of Khulna city, allegedly following a clash over the sharing of money from peddling drugs.

The victim, Motaleb Shikder, 45, of the area, is the organising secretary of Jatiya Sramik Shakti’s Khulna Divisional unit.

title: Sangskriti Bangla holds discussion on Shamsur Rahman, Al Mahmud today
body:
Sangskriti Bangla is scheduled to hold a programme titled Nationalism and Religion: Shamsur Rahman and Al Mahmud at the Asma Chowdhury Auditorium of Sangskriti Bikash Kendra at Paribag in Dhaka at 6:00pm on Saturday.

Poet, essayist and journalist Sajjad Sharif will deliver a solo lecture at the discussion, which will be presided over by veteran writer and translator Khaliquzzman Elias, said a press release signed by Sangskriti Bangla member-secretary Soroishwarja Muhommod.

Aimed at establishing human dignity against the discrimination and hatred, Sangskriti Bangla is committed to building a new outline of collective culture centring on the Bangla language, geography and people of the country.

The platform also desires to awaken the cultural aspirations of people of the country regardless of caste, religion, colour and language.

title: Syrian president meets with EU chief
body:
Syria’s president Ahmed al-Sharaa met with European Commission chief Ursula von der Leyen on Friday, state media said, as she became the highest ranking EU official to visit since long-time ruler Bashar al-Assad was ousted.

Von der Leyen is conducting a regional tour alongside Antonio Costa, who heads the European Council. Their visit follows days of deadly clashes between government forces and Kurdish fighters in the north Syrian city of Aleppo.

‘We will continue working together in support of a peaceful and inclusive Syrian-led and Syrian-owned transition,’ said a joint EU-Jordan statement issued on the eve of the EU leaders’ arrival in Damascus.

Syria is struggling to forge a new path after years of war sparked by a brutal crackdown on pro-democracy protests in 2011.

Sharaa has come under pressure to protect Syria’s many minority communities, including the Kurds.

Several EU officials have visited Syria since Assad’s ouster by Sharaa’s forces in December 2024. In March, the EU pledged nearly 2.5 billion euros in aid for Syria for 2025 and 2026.

title: US, Colombia vow joint fight against guerrillas
body:
Colombia’s leftist president Gustavo Petro agreed with his US counterpart Donald Trump to take ‘joint action’ against cocaine-smuggling guerrillas on the border with Venezuela, Bogota’s interior minister said Thursday.

The two leaders held their first phone call on Wednesday, de-escalating tensions after Trump had threatened military action against Colombia following the ouster of Venezuela’s leftist leader Nicolas Maduro by US forces.

Trump and Petro ‘committed to taking joint actions’ against the National Liberation Army, Colombia’s last remaining major armed rebel group, interior minister Armando Benedetti said in an interview with Blu Radio.

Colombia accuses the ELN of launching attacks and kidnappings of Colombian soldiers and retreating to rear-base locations in Venezuela.

Petro asked Trump ‘to help strike hard at the ELN on the border’ with Venezuela, Benedetti said.

He said the guerrillas must ‘be attacked in their rear’ as well as on Colombian soil.

Colombia and Venezuela share a porous 2,200-kilometer border where various armed groups vie for control of the profits from drug trafficking, illegal mining and smuggling.

Carlons Venlandia, a former ELN leader turned conflict analyst, said the rebel group has ‘extensive experience in guerrilla warfare on the ground.’

But he added ‘they can’t do anything in a technological war’ like the one Washington could wage if it took military action against the ELN.

Later Thursday, the leader of a separate rebel grouping summoned other guerrilla commanders to a meeting to discuss the US removal of Maduro.

‘We know we have had our differences in the past but today we are facing a common enemy’ in the United States, said Ivan Mordisco, leader of the remnants of the dissolved FARC armed movement, also thought to have rear-bases in Venezuela.

‘We summon you urgently to a summit of insurgent commanders from Colombia and all over our America,’ he said, in a video sent to media.

Mordisco said the rival rebel groups should work together against ‘all forms of imperialist aggression.’

‘Let us forge a great insurgent front to drive back our enemies.’

Petro accepted Trump’s invitation to meet in Washington, despite fierce exchanges over recent days in which Trump branded him a drug-trafficker and the Colombian leader vowed to take up arms against any US assault.

After Petro criticized the United States for seizing Maduro in Caracas on January 3, Trump told Petro to ‘watch his ass.’

Washington and Bogota have enjoyed security cooperation for decades, but ties have deteriorated since Trump began his second term last January.

title: Bushfires threaten rural towns in Australian heat-wave
body:
Bushfires destroyed houses and razed vast belts of forest in southeast Australia on Friday, firefighters said, as hot winds fanned ‘hectic’ conditions in the tinder-dry countryside.

Temperatures soared past 40C as a heatwave blanketed the region, creating some of the most dangerous bushfire weather since the ‘Black Summer’ blazes of 2019-2020.

Dozens of rural hamlets in the state of Victoria were urged to evacuate while they still could, while three people, including a child, were missing inside one of the state’s most dangerous fire grounds.

‘If you don’t leave now, it could result in your life being lost,’ Emergency Management Commissioner Tim Wiebusch told reporters.

Powerful wind gusts temporarily grounded firefighting aircraft trying to contain some 30 different blazes dotted across the state.

Already, firefighters fear at least 20 houses have burnt to the ground in the small town of Ruffy, about two hours’ drive north of state capital Melbourne.

Country Fire Authority boss Jason Heffernan said the fire danger was ‘catastrophic’ — the most severe rating possible.

‘Victorians should brace themselves for more property loss or worse.

‘Today is going to be quite a hectic and volatile day for firefighters, fire authorities and communities.’

One of the most destructive bushfires has already razed some 28,000 hectares near the town of Longwood, a region cloaked in native forests.

‘Some properties have lost everything,’ said local fire captain George Noye.

‘They’ve lost their livelihoods, they’ve lost their shearing sheds, livestock, just absolutely devastating,’ he told national broadcaster ABC.

‘But thankfully, at the moment, no lives have been lost.’

The worst bushfires have so far been confined to sparsely populated rural areas where towns might number a few hundred people at the most.

Photos taken this week showed the night sky glowing orange as the fire near Longwood — north of state capital Melbourne — ripped through bushland.

‘There were embers falling everywhere. It was terrifying,’ cattle farmer Scott Purcell told the ABC.

Another bushfire near the small town of Walwa crackled with lightning as it radiated enough heat to form a localised thunderstorm, fire authorities said.

Hundreds of firefighters from across Australia have been called in to help.

‘Today represents one of the most dangerous fire days that this state has experienced in years,’ said state premier Jacinta Allan.

Allan urged people to flee rather than stay put and try to save their homes.

‘You will simply not win against the fires of these magnitudes that are created on days like today.’

Millions of people in Australia’s two most populous states — Victoria and New South Wales — are sweltering through the heatwave, including in major cities Sydney and Melbourne.

Power outages left more than 30,000 houses without electricity on one of the hottest days to hit Victoria in years.

Hundreds of baby bats died earlier this week as stifling temperatures settled over the neighbouring state of South Australia, a local wildlife group said.

The ‘Black Summer’ bushfires raged across Australia’s eastern seaboard from late 2019 to early 2020, razing millions of hectares, destroying thousands of homes and blanketing cities in noxious smoke.

Australia’s climate has warmed by an average of 1.51C since 1910, researchers have found, fuelling increasingly frequent extreme weather patterns over both land and sea.

Australia remains one of the world’s largest producers and exporters of gas and coal, two key fossil fuels blamed for global heating.

title: European political order ‘in danger’, France warns
body:
The European political order ‘is today in danger’, France’s foreign minister said on Friday, sharply criticising his country’s long-time ally Washington and hitting back at US claims Europe faced ‘civilisational erasure’.

Jean-Noel Barrot delivered his annual address to France’s ambassadors as European powers were racing to come up with a coordinated response to Washington’s increasingly assertive posture on the world stage and Donald Trump’s designs on Greenland.

‘No, European civilisation will not fade away,’ Barrot said.

‘But yes, our political order is today in danger, despite its precious stability in an unpredictable world, despite its immense scientific, technological, cultural and financial wealth.’

A US national security strategy released in December by Trump’s administration launched a brutal attack on Europe, describing it as facing ‘civilisational erasure’ from migration and calling for ‘cultivating resistance’ among right-wing parties.

‘No, Europe is not on the brink of civilisational erasure, and the presumptuous voices claiming it is would do better to watch out for their own erasure,’ the French minister said.

But the European Union is, in his view, ‘threatened from the outside by adversaries who are trying to unravel the bonds of solidarity that unite us’ and ‘from within by democratic fatigue’.

‘Let’s be clear: nothing guarantees today that we will still be living within the European Union as we know it in 10 years,’ he warned.

He described the United States as ‘allies with whom we are not always aligned.’

‘In a matter of months, the new American administration decided — and that is its right — to rethink the ties that bind us. It is also our right to say ‘no’ to a historic ally, however historic it may be, when its proposal is not acceptable and when we must say ‘no’,’ Barrot said.

France’s top diplomat spoke one day after president Emmanuel Macron warned the United States was ‘gradually turning away’ from some of its allies and ‘breaking free from international rules’, offering some of his strongest criticism yet of Washington’s policies under Trump.

Barrot also warned that the world was ‘facing the risk of nuclear proliferation’ due to the erosion of the legal framework on arms control and the expiration of the New START treaty.

The New START treaty is the last bilateral nuclear arms control agreement between the United States and Russia. It expires on February 5.

Overnight Russia hit western Ukraine, close to the border with EU and NATO member Poland, with its hypersonic Oreshnik missile after rejecting the latest post-war peacekeeping plan from Kyiv’s European and US allies.

title: Experts say oceans soaked up record heat levels in 2025
body:
The world’s oceans absorbed a record amount of heat in 2025, an international team of scientists said Friday, further priming conditions for sea level rise, violent storms, and coral death.

The heat that has accumulated in the oceans last year increased by approximately 23 zettajoules — an amount equivalent to nearly four decades of global primary energy consumption.

This finding — published in the journal Advances in Atmospheric Sciences — was the highest reading of any year since modern record keeping began in the early 1950s, researchers said.

To derive these calculations, more than 50 scientists from 31 research institutions used multiple sources including a thousands-strong fleet of floating robots that track ocean changes to depths of 2,000 metres.

Peering into the depths, rather than fluctuations at the surface, provides a better indicator of how oceans are responding to ‘sustained pressure’ from humanity’s emissions, said study co-author Karina von Schuckmann.

‘The picture is clear: results for 2025 confirm that the ocean continues to warm,’ von Schuckmann, an oceanographer from French research institute Mercator Ocean International, said.

Oceans are a key regulator of Earth’s climate because they soak up 90 per cent of the excess heat in the atmosphere caused by humanity’s release of greenhouse gases like carbon dioxide.

All that additional energy has a powerful knock-on effect. Warmer oceans increase moisture in the atmosphere, providing fuel for tropical cyclones and destructive rainfall.

Hotter seas also directly contribute to sea level rise — water expands when it warms up — and make conditions unbearable for tropical reefs, whose corals perish during prolonged marine heat-waves.

‘As long as the Earth continues to accumulate heat, ocean heat content will keep rising, sea level will rise and new records will be set,’ said von Schuckmann.

Ocean warming is not uniform, with some areas warming faster than others.

The tropical oceans, the South Atlantic, the Mediterranean, the northern Indian Ocean, and the Southern Ocean were among waters that absorbed record amounts of heat in 2025.

This occurred even as average sea surface temperatures decreased slightly in 2025 -- yet still remained the third-highest value ever measured.

This decrease is explained by the shift from a powerful, warming El Nino event in 2023–2024 to La Nina-type conditions generally associated with a temporary cooling of the ocean surface.

In the long term, the rate of ocean warming is accelerating due to a sustained increase in greenhouse gas concentrations in the atmosphere caused mainly by burning fossil fuels.

As long as global warming is not addressed and the amount of heat trapped in the atmosphere keeps rising, oceans will keep breaking records, the researchers said.

‘The greatest uncertainty in the climate system is no longer the physics, but the choices humanity makes,’ said von Schuckmann.

‘Rapid emission reductions can still limit future impacts and help safeguard a climate in which societies and ecosystems can thrive.’

title: ‘War is back in vogue,’ Pope says
body:
Pope Leo XIV told diplomats to the Vatican on Friday that war was ‘back in vogue,’ delivering a speech warning of sabre-rattling and a weakness of multilateralism.

‘A diplomacy that promotes dialogue and seeks consensus among all parties is being replaced by a diplomacy based on force, by either individuals or groups of allies.

‘War is back in vogue and a zeal for war is spreading,’ said the first US pope.

Leo warned that the principle established after the Second World War, ‘which prohibited nations from using force to violate the borders of others, has been completely undermined’.

‘Peace is sought through weapons as a condition for asserting one’s own dominion. This gravely threatens the rule of law, which is the foundation of all peaceful civil coexistence,’ he said.

The pontiff pointed to the ‘weakness of multilateralism’ as ‘a particular cause for concern at the international level’.

He said adhering to international humanitarian law was ‘a commitment that States have made’, and such law ‘must always prevail over the ambitions of belligerents’.

‘We cannot ignore that the destruction of hospitals, energy infrastructure, homes and places essential to daily life constitutes a serious violation of international humanitarian law,’ he said.

title: City win race to sign Semenyo
body:
Manchester City added to their attacking arsenal on Friday with the signing of Antoine Semenyo from Bournemouth for a reported £65 million ($87 million).

The 26-year-old, who has scored 10 Premier League goals this season, has signed a five-and-a-half-year deal.

Liverpool, Manchester United and Tottenham were amongst the other clubs interested in the London-born Ghana international, who had a buyout clause that would reportedly expire on Saturday.

‘I am so proud to have joined Manchester City,’ said Semenyo.

‘I have watched City over the last decade under Pep Guardiola, and they have been the dominant team in the Premier League as well as achieving amazing things in the Champions League, FA Cup and League Cup.

‘They have set the highest of standards and it’s a club with world-class players, world-class facilities and one of the greatest managers ever in Pep.’

His final act after three years with the Cherries was scoring a stoppage-time winner to beat Tottenham 3-2 and end an 11-game winless run on Wednesday.

City are hoping Semenyo can boost their challenge for silverware on four fronts in 2026.

Guardiola’s men trail Arsenal by six points at the top of the Premier League and have FA Cup, League Cup and Champions League fixtures in the coming weeks.

City’s options in the wide areas are currently limited with Savinho out injured and Omar Marmoush representing Egypt at the Africa Cup of Nations.

Semenyo’s transfer is the first major move by Premier League clubs in the January window.

City are also in the market to boost their defensive options after losing Ruben Dias and Josko Gvardiol to injuries.

Crystal Palace captain Marc Guehi, who is out of contract at the end of the season, is their prime target.

Semenyo has enjoyed a meteoric rise since being shipped out on loan three times by Bristol City early in his career.

He eventually earned his move to the Premier League in 2023 and has blossomed into one of the most potent wingers in the English top-flight in the past two seasons under Andoni Iraola.

‘I have so much scope for improvement, so to be at this club, at this stage of my career, is perfect for me. It’s a real privilege to be here,’ added Semenyo.

‘My best football is yet to come, I am sure of that. And City are in a great position –- still involved in four competitions. I really feel I can help them have a strong second half of the season.’

Semenyo could make his debut on Saturday when City host third-tier Exeter in the FA Cup at the Etihad Stadium.

title: BCB director sparks new controversy
body:
A Bangladesh Cricket Board director’s remarks toward Tamim Iqbal sparked new controversy amid the uncertainty over the Bangladesh national team’s participation in the forthcoming T20 World Cup scheduled to be held in India and Sri Lanka between February 7 and March 8.

The chairman of the finance committee of the BCB, M Najmul Islam, dubbed Tamim an ‘Indian agent’ in a Facebook post after the former national team captain gave his opinion on recent matters regarding the BCB’s decision not to travel to India for the World Cup.

Cricketers including Taskin Ahmed, Mominul Haque, Taijul Islam, and the Cricketers Welfare Association of Bangladesh, then raised their voices and demanded Najmul’s apology.

In the jersey unveiling programme of the Zia Inter University Cricket Tournament organised by the Jatiyatabadi Krira Dal on Thursday, Tamim said that the BCB should take a decision after discussing it first and then comment on the matter.

‘I would have taken the decision by thinking about the future. Many things have happened; it’s not easy to comment. But you should bear one thing in mind: that you can solve many things by dialogue,’ Tamim said.

‘What is your position in world cricket? What could be the future of Bangladesh? I would have taken the decision based on everything,’ he added.

Tamim also said that the BCB should take the decision in their jurisdiction as an ‘independent body’.

‘We think of the BCB as an independent body. Of course the government is a part of it, and you have to discuss it with them. But if we think the BCB is an independent body, then they should have got their own decisions. If they think this is right, then they should take that decision,’ he said.

He also urged the BCB to take decisions by considering the future of cricket in Bangladesh, not by being ‘emotional’.

Sharing one of Tamim’s quotes, in a now-deleted Facebook post, Najmul wrote, ‘Now the public of Bengal has seen yet another unveiling of a proven Indian agent.’

However, in another post, Najmul said his comments were solely personal.

But Najmul’s remarks faced backlash from some cricketers.

‘The comments made by BCB director M Najmul Islam regarding the former national team captain Tamim Iqbal are unacceptable and an insult to the country’s cricket. Such behaviour toward a cricket clash with the board’s responsibility and ethics,’ wrote Mominul Haque on Facebook.

‘I am condemning this comment and demanding the director’s apologies. I also demand that he should be held responsible,’ he added.

The CWAB, in a press release, said that they were ‘shocked and aggrieved’ after seeing the comment. They also demand Najmul’s apology and the BCB’s action.

After Mustafizur Rahman was snubbed by the Kolkata Knight Riders upon receiving the BCCI’s ‘advice’, the BCB took a firm stance of not travelling to India.

They sent a letter to the International Cricket Council. However, after receiving ICC’s reply, the BCB sent another letter clarifying their stance.

title: FIFA president mourns Khaleda Zia
body:
FIFA president Gianni Infantino expressed deepest condolence at the death of former prime minister and Bangladesh Nationalist Party chairperson Khaleda Zia, said Bangladesh Football Federation in a media release on Friday.

In a condolence message sent to BFF president Tabith Awal, reads that Begum Khaleda Zia was an important and pioneering figure in the political history of Bangladesh. As the country’s first female Prime Minister, she has left a lasting legacy for future generations.

On behalf of the international football community, FIFA president expressed his deepest condolences to Bangladesh government, BFF and the people of Bangladesh, it reads further.

BFF also expressed its gratitude to the FIFA president and the international football community for this message of condolence, the message concluded.

It can be mentionable that Khaleda Zia passed away on December 30, 2025 while undergoing treatment at a hospital in the capital.

title: Nawaz guides Royals to thrilling win
body:
Hasan Nawaz led the Chattogram Royals to a thrilling two-wicket win over the Rajshahi Warriors in the ongoing Bangladesh Premier League at the Sylhet International Stadium on Friday.

After being put into bat first, Rajshahi were restricted to a below-par total 128-9, thanks to an all-round bowling display led by Aamer Jamal, who took 3-23 from four overs.

Then Nawaz held his nerve and remained unbeaten on 35 off 36 to guide them home in the very last ball as Chattogram retained their top spot.

As many as six batters of Rajshahi touched the double figures, but none could cross the 19-run mark.

The highest partnership of 21 runs came from the opening partnership between Muhammad Waseem and Tanzid Hasan.

Apart from Jamal’s three-for, Shoriful Islam and Tanvir Islam each took two wickets for Chattogram, while Mahedi Hasan and Nawaz took one apiece.

However, Rajshahi had Chattogram at 28-4 inside the first five overs to set a thrilling contest before Nawaz and Mahedi steadied the ship with a run-a-ball partnership of 40.

After Mahedi’s departure, Nawaz added a further 35 runs off 34 with Asif Ali to take Chattogram to a comfortable position.

But Asif’s wicket enticed another collapse into the Chattogram innings as they slipped to 119-8 with 10 runs still needed from eight balls.

After Shoriful conceded two dots in the last two balls of the penultimate over bowled by Tanzim Hasan, Najmul Hossain Shanto opted to bowl with SM Meherob with 10 runs to defend.

The off-spinner gave away eight runs in the first three balls before shooting two dots to set the probability of another super over.

But Nawaz kept his calm to play it along the ground while Shoriful ran his heart out to scamper through a double. Rajshahi, who were otherwise excellent in the field, missed a couple of run-out chances towards the end.

Chattogram skipper Mahedi hailed Nawaz’s batting, which fulfilled the situation’s demand.

‘We thought that whoever was along, if Hasan Nawaz could be in the middle till the last over, he could have finished the game, as he had [the capability] of power hitting. Because he was setting the whole game nicely,’ said Mahedi after the match.

‘I think I have rarely seen him batting like this, as he normally likes to play strokes. But today’s innings was sensible; it was outstanding,’ he added.

Rajshahi captain Shanto, on the other hand, was still proud of the fight shown by his troops.

‘If you see the involvement of the eleven players in the field, we kept our faith. Because anything can happen in cricket,’ said Shanto.

‘So we have that belief. With the bowling lineup we’ve got, we are capable of defending any total. So we’ve had that belief, and the bowlers executed that well,’ he added.

title: Startups go public in litmus test for Chinese AI
body:
Leading Chinese artificial intelligence startup Zhipu AI soared as it went public in Hong Kong on Thursday, a day before rival MiniMax also makes its market debut in a litmus test for the country’s rapidly developing sector.

Shares in Zhipu AI, which runs the Z.ai tool, rose more than 12 per cent on Thursday after its oversubscribed initial public offering raised HK$4.35 billion (US$558 million).

This week’s flotations come before any IPO announcements from top US startups OpenAI, the maker of ChatGPT, and Anthropic, known for its Claude chatbot.

But analysts said profits were unlikely any time soon from either company — the first two IPOs among China’s so-called ‘six tigers’, generative AI providers competing with tech giants such as Alibaba and ByteDance.

‘Zhipu is honoured to stand at this historic juncture as a representative of China’s large model sector,’ company chairman Liu Debing said at Thursday’s listing ceremony.

Zhipu AI was founded in 2019 and is a major provider of large language model (LLM) services to businesses and government clients in the world’s second-largest economy.
