Many household consumers in the city’s Uttara, Dhanmondi, Mohammadpur, Kafrul, Shewarapara, Kathalbagan, Kalabagan, Rampura, and Basabo woke up in the morning of Thursday to find no gas in the pipeline and therefore failed to prepare breakfast.

Households relaying on liquefied petroleum gas also faced problems on the day following a strike called by the LP Gas Traders’ Cooperative Society Limited to press home its demands.

State-owned Petrobangla officials blamed an incident damaging the underground pipeline in the river Buriganga at Aminbazar for the unexpected supply disruption of piped gas in many parts in of the city

The damage has already been repaired but the stabilisation in the supply situation will take more time, said Petrobangla general manager (Production and Marketing) Imam Uddin Sheikh.

Besides, the Petrobangla has been diverting gas to the fertiliser sector over the past two months in line with the government priority amid falling production at the local level by the international oil companies.

The daily gas production at the domestic level fell to 2,578.5 MMCF in January 7-8 from 2,666.8 MMCF a month ago, mainly because of declining production from the international oil companies to 893 MMCFD in January 7-8 from 1,026 MMCFD a month ago.

Petrobangla officials said that supply priority had also been given to the industrial sector so that the production of export-oriented sector stayed uninterrupted.

Imam Uddin said that the supply shortage of around 1,000 MMCFD gas was unlikely to go away soon  because of the limited capacity to increase the import of liquefied natural gas.    .

Positive impacts from initiatives taken by the current interim government to increase gas production by the domestic companies will take at least two years to come, he added.

The household consumers spend roughly 15 per cent of the gas, but constitute 99 per cent of the client base of the Titas Gas which has been in operation since 1964.

Indifferent to the household consumers, the country’s biggest gas distribution company, however, is forcing more and more consumers to buy LP gas over the years.

The LP gas consumption in the country increased 10-fold reaching 1.44 million tonnes in 2024 from 0.15 million tonnes in 2015.

Out of 4.1 crore households in the country, roughly 33 lakh have piped gas connections.

Biomass, notably firewood, is widely used in Bangladesh and still accounts for two-thirds of the home-cooking fuel.

This traditional fuel is being replaced by LP gas quite rapidly, according to Integrated Energy and Power Master Plan 2023.

It has been a relief for growing users of LP gas following the suspension of the nationwide strike by the LP Gas Traders’ Cooperative Society Limited on the day following the assurance from the Bangladesh Energy Regulatory Commission to meet its demands.

The association overnight called the strike to press home its demands, including stopping the ongoing administrative drive across Bangladesh, increasing charges for distributors and retailers.

But uncertainty over the volatility in prices of the item may continue for the current week, said stakeholders.

Calculating the demand for the supply, Humayun Rashid, vice-president of the LPG Operators Association of Bangladesh, said that most of the local importers failed to bring in expected amount of LP gas because of various reasons, including lack of available vessels.

On November 20, 2025, the US Treasury Department imposed sanctions on several individuals, companies, and fuel transport vessels involved in transporting LP gas and crude oil, creating import difficulties in December.

But the supply situation will improve as unsanctioned vessels will hit the dock from the next week, said Humayun Rashid.

By this time, many retailers amid high demand forced consumers to buy 12-kilogram cylinders for Tk 1,900–2,200, about 50-75 per cent higher than the government-declared prices, said the stakeholders.

title: Treasury bill, bond rates rise again amid high govt borrowing
body:
Interest rates on government treasury bills and bonds have risen sharply in recent months as the government stepped up borrowing from commercial banks.

Bangladesh Bank data show that yields on short-term treasury bills climbed notably at the latest auctions.

The yield on the 91-day bill rose to 10.42 per cent on January 5, while the 182-day and 364-day bills reached 10.54 per cent and 10.65 per cent respectively. These rates were significantly lower in October last year, standing at 9.5 per cent, 9.71 per cent and 9.6 per cent.

Yields on longer-term government securities also moved higher in December.

At auctions held on December 12 and December 24, the yield on the 5-year treasury bond rose to 10.84 per cent, while the 15-year and 20-year bonds increased to around 10.9 per cent. In September, yields on these bonds were notably lower, ranging between 9.63 per cent and 10 per cent.

Treasury bills are mainly used by the government for short-term financing needs, while treasury bonds fund longer-term expenditure.

Both instruments remain the primary channels through which the government borrows from the domestic financial system, including commercial banks and the central bank.

Bankers said that the recent rise in yields reflects increased government reliance on bank financing as revenue collection remains weak and economic activity slows.

Bangladesh Bank data showed that government borrowing from the banking sector surged to Tk 45,239 crore during the July 31 to December 8 period of the current 2025–26 fiscal year. This marked a sharp reversal from net negative borrowing of Tk 503 crore during July–October and exceeded the Tk 28,549 crore borrowed in the same period last year.

The pressure on the banking system has intensified as fiscal space narrows.

In the 2024–25 fiscal year, net borrowing from the banking sector fell to Tk 72,372 crore, the lowest in four years, against a target of Tk 99,000 crore.

For the current fiscal year, the government has set a much higher net borrowing target of Tk 1.04 lakh crore from banks.

Higher yields have also drawn growing interest from individual investors seeking safer returns amid volatility in other asset classes.

Individual investment in treasury bills and bonds increased more than sevenfold over the two years ending in June 2025.

Bangladesh Bank data showed that individual holdings rose to Tk 7,941 crore in June 2025, from Tk 3,850 crore a year earlier and just Tk 1,102 crore in June 2023.

Bankers said that yields had briefly fallen below 10 per cent in September last year for the first time since September 2023, before rising again as government borrowing accelerated.

title: Banks asked to credit remittance within a day
body:
Bangladesh Bank has asked banks to credit inward remittances on the same day or the next business day to cut delays and improve efficiency in cross-border payments.

The central bank issued a circular in this regard on Thursday, which took effect immediately.

Banks have been given time until March 31, 2026 to fully align their systems and operations with the new requirements.

Under the circular, all authorized dealer banks must promptly inform customers through secure electronic channels as soon as inward remittance messages are received.

Remittances that arrive during banking hours must be credited to beneficiary accounts on the same business day. Those received after banking hours must be credited on the following business day.

Bangladesh Bank has asked banks to rely more on straight-through processing and risk-based expedited processing to speed up settlements.

Where essential information is available, banks may credit beneficiary accounts even if some documentation or checks remain pending, provided those requirements are completed later.

In cases where post-credit review is not possible, banks must conduct pre-credit verification and complete settlement within three business days.

To further reduce delays, the central bank has instructed banks to cut dependence on end-of-day nostro account statements and instead use intraday credit confirmations.

Banks have also been advised to strengthen reconciliation systems, with reconciliation intervals generally capped at 60 minutes.

Banks have been asked to use the Unique End-to-End Transaction Reference to track inward remittances from the moment they are received until final credit to the beneficiary.

Bangladesh Bank has also instructed banks to strengthen their digital foreign exchange platforms, paving the way for the eventual phase-out of Form C and Form C (ICT).

BB officials said that intraday confirmations and UETR-based tracking would reduce disputes and enhance accountability across correspondent banking relationships.

They said that the measures would strengthen trust among correspondent banks and improve Bangladesh’s standing in the global payments network.

However, bankers said that system upgrades, process changes and staff training could pose operational challenges during the transition period, particularly for smaller banks.

title: Cashless transition faces hurdles despite digital payment growth: PRI
body:
Despite growth in mobile financial services and digital payments, Bangladesh’s transition to a cashless economy is hindered by limited interoperability, uneven infrastructure, cybersecurity risks, and low digital literacy, which keeps cash prevalent in daily transactions.

These issues took centre stage at a stakeholder consultation hosted by the Policy Research Institute of Bangladesh on Thursday, said a press release.

PRI organised the Stakeholder Consultation Workshop with support from the Gates Foundation, titled ‘Toward a Cashless Economy: A Strategic Roadmap for Bangladesh’ at its conference room, bringing together policymakers, regulators, economists, financial institutions, fintech representatives, and development partners to identify policy priorities for advancing digital and cashless transactions.

A recent PRI study highlighted that despite Bangladesh’s progress with mobile financial services and QR-based payments, structural barriers hinder wider adoption.

Key benefits of a successful cashless transition include financial inclusion, reduced transaction costs, and better economic governance, emphasising the need for robust digital infrastructure and coordinated regulation.

Bangladesh Bank executive director Arief Hossain Khan attended the event as chief guest.

He stressed that progress toward a cashless economy depends on close coordination among regulators, financial institutions, and technology providers to ensure the transition remains inclusive and secure.

The session was chaired by PRI chairman Zaidi Sattar.

Highlighting productivity as a key driver of GDP growth, he said the benefits generated by the cashless economy must be properly captured in national accounts.

He called for the Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics to adopt the UN System of National Accounts 2025 to reflect the value added by digital and cashless transactions, a process that will require coordinated efforts and data sharing over several years.

Principal Economist at PRI, Ashikur Rahman, said that digital and cashless instruments should be prioritised for their potential to enhance financial inclusion, reduce informality, increase transparency, and improve economic governance.

An open floor discussion highlighted concerns about merchant adoption, transaction costs, cybersecurity threats, rural outreach, and fintech innovation.

Speakers agreed that addressing these challenges needs coordinated efforts from the government, Bangladesh Bank, the private sector, and development partners.

PRI executive director Khurshid Alam reaffirmed the institute’s commitment to evidence-based policy research and dialogue to support Bangladesh’s digital transformation.

title: Stocks edge higher amid moderate trading
body:
Dhaka stocks on Thursday closed on a positive note with key indices showing slight gains despite a higher number of declining stocks.

The DSE Broad Index, DSEX, rose by 5.85 points to settle at 4,998.55. Similarly, the blue-chip DS30 index saw an increase of 1.56 points, reaching 1,914.94, while the Shariah-based DSES index ticked up by 1.42 points to close at 1,010.80.

A total of 391 companies participated in today’s trading session. The market saw a turnover of Tk 429.11 crore, with approximately 13.30 crore shares and mutual fund units changing hands.

Despite the rise in indices, market breadth remained negative, as the prices of 183 stocks declined, 125 advanced, and 83 remained unchanged.

Trading volume was concentrated in several key players. Based on the total value of trades, the top 10 companies were City Bank, Square Pharmaceuticals, Orion Infusion, Taufika Foods, Uttara Bank, Fine Foods, Jamuna Bank, Robi Axiata, Anwar Galvanizing and Domino Steel.

Fine Foods led the gainers’ list, followed by Sonargaon Textiles, Chartered Life Insurance, and Wata Chemical.

Other notable gainers included Kashem Industries, GQ Ball Pen, Munnu Fabrics, ISN Ltd, Exim Bank 1st Mutual Fund, and EBL 1st Mutual Fund.

On the other hand, the losers’ chart was dominated by the financial sector. Peoples Leasing saw the most significant decline, followed by FAS Finance, Premier Leasing, and Fareast Finance.

Other companies in the top 10 losers list included International Leasing, First Finance, Prime Finance, Family Tex, BIFC, and GSP Finance.

The market’s performance today was like a slow tide — the overall water level rose slightly, even though more individual waves were receding than advancing.

The port city bourse, CSE, also settled on a green zone. The Selective Categories’ Index (CSCX) and All Share Price Index (CASPI) increased by 19 points and 18.68 points, respectively.

title: Experts urge overhaul of SRO 384 to ease duty-free raw material imports
body:
Business leaders and policy experts on Thursday raised concern over the recently issued SRO 384/2025, warning that the current framework for duty-free import of raw materials beyond the bonded warehouse facility could discourage small exporters.

The concerns were voiced at a high-level dialogue titled ’Duty-Free Import of Raw Materials beyond Bonded Warehouse Facility’, organised by Business Initiative Leading Development (BUILD) at its conference room in Dhaka.

In the keynote presentation, Md Nooruzzaman, senior research associate at BUILD, said THAT under the SRO, non-bonded exporters would be allowed to import raw materials duty-free against a 100 per cent bank guarantee.

He said that the requirement would be difficult for many exporters to afford, as the guarantee would be encashed only after export proceeds are realised, creating pressure on working capital and limiting cash flow.

To qualify for the facility, exporters must ensure at least 30 per cent value addition and maintain mandatory VAT compliance through regular online submissions.

Nooruzzaman said that while these conditions aimed to ensure transparency, the facility was currently limited to only eight sectors including furniture, electronics and light engineering, excluding many potential export-oriented industries.

The working session was moderated by Dr Wasel Bin Shadat, research director of BUILD.

Mohammad Naziur Rahman Miah, first secretary of NBR, said that formulating SRO 384 had been a challenging task and stressed that it was not a fixed document.

‘It will be updated over time based on experience and requirements,’ he said, adding that the eight sectors were initially included due to demonstrated interest and the list could be expanded if other sectors come forward.

Referring to recent reforms, he said that NBR had abolished the requirement of coefficients for bonded warehouse holders as well as UD and UP, opting instead for automation.

He said that around 83 per cent of UP processes have already been automated, with BGMEA, Customs and other relevant organisations now integrated, and assured that the system would continue to improve.

Md Shahidulla, senior deputy secretary of BPGMEA, said that local VAT authorities remained the controlling point for the facility.

He said that exporters seeking benefits must hold IRC and ERC licences, which were different from customs bonded warehouse licences.

He also said that while DEDO had become fully operational, 100 per cent duty drawback through DEDO had never been achieved in practice.

Calling for dynamic policy decisions, Saifur Rahman, vice-president of the Bangladesh Stainless Steel Pipe Manufacturers Association, stressed the importance of ease of doing business for export diversification.

He suggested following the Chinese model of PPP-based warehouses, noting that a committee was already working on the issue at NBR.

Md Abdur Rauf, CEO of the Bangladesh Furniture Exporters Association, urged the government to focus on value addition criteria rather than UP, UD and bank guarantees in export facilitation.

He also called for reducing lead time while enforcing strong punitive measures against misuse.

Criticising the 100 per cent bank guarantee requirement, MS Siddiqui, CEO of Bangla Chemical, said that such a provision was not a global practice.

He argued that revenue policies should be formulated by independent bodies instead of concentrating all authority within NBR and said the market should determine exportable products rather than imposing negative lists.

Former BAPA vice-president Shoaib Hasan proposed allowing 30 per cent duty-free import of raw materials based on export performance, saying such an incentive could potentially double export volumes.

Mainul Islam, deputy manager of SME Foundation, urged NBR to align policies with the Ministry of Industries and recommended including priority sectors under the National Industrial Policy 2022 and the Product of the Year declared annually by the Ministry of Commerce in the positive list.

He said that SME Foundation could create a sponsor guarantee fund for SME exporters if legally permitted.

Highlighting operational challenges, Sharif Nawrin Akter, AGM of LFMEAB, suggested that bank guarantee realisation should be done in phases.

She also said that the current export time limit of nine months, extendable by only three months, was too short considering order cancellations and delays in export proceeds, and proposed extending it to at least two tax periods.

Shankar Kumar Roy, executive director of the Bangladesh Cement Manufacturers Association, urged inclusion of the cement sector in the positive list, citing its strong domestic base and export potential.

Summing up the session, Ferdaus Ara Begum, CEO of BUILD, said that the organisation had taken note of all the recommendations and would prepare a detailed report to be shared with NBR.

title: Global stocks retreat as traders eye geopolitics, US jobs data
body:
Stock markets fell Thursday as an early-year rally ran out of steam, with investors locking in profits ahead of the release of key US jobs data this week.

The geopolitical outlook remained a major uncertainty for traders after the US toppled Venezuela’s president and amid simmering tensions between China and Japan.

London, Paris and Frankfurt stock markets were all lower in midday trading.

European defence stocks, however, gained on the geopolitical concerns, with President Donald Trump calling to hike the US defence budget by 50 per cent next year.

Britain’s BAE systems jumped five per cent, while Germany’s Rheinmetall and Italy’s Leonardo also rose.

Investors were also awaiting the release of US data on job openings and unemployment claims later Thursday.

They are followed Friday by the closely watched reading on non-farm payrolls, a crucial guide for Federal Reserve decision-makers, who meet at the end of the month amid debate on whether they will cut interest rates for a fourth successive time.

‘With a March rate cut essentially priced in as a coin-toss, tomorrow’s jobs report does provide the basis for a potential market-moving event if we see any particularly strong deviation from expectations,’ said Joshua Mahony, chief market analyst at Scope Markets.

Equity markets in Asia struggled Thursday, with Hong Kong, Shanghai and Tokyo all closing lower.

Tokyo stocks were weighed down after China announced an anti-dumping probe into imports from Japan of a key chemical used in making semiconductors, a day after it banned the export to the country of goods with potential military uses.

The move adds to rising diplomatic tensions between the Asian giants since Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi suggested in November that Japan may react militarily in any attack on Taiwan.

Seoul edged higher to another record close, though tech giant Samsung fell back after saying it expected its fourth-quarter profit to reach a record $13.8 billion.

Oil prices rebounded after suffering a second steep fall in a row Wednesday on Trump’s comments that Venezuela would turn over millions of barrels to the United States following its ouster of president Nicolas Maduro.

Traders will also be keeping an eye on a US Supreme Court ruling due Friday on the legality of Trump’s punishing tariffs.

The landmark case on his unprecedented use of powers for sweeping global levies strikes at the heart of his economic agenda, and a tariffs reversal could further upend US trade with countries worldwide.

title: Samsung Electronics forecasts record profit in Q4
body:
South Korean tech giant Samsung Electronics said Thursday it expected its fourth-quarter profit to reach a record 20 trillion won ($13.8 billion).

The firm is one of the world’s top memory chip makers, providing crucial components for artificial intelligence and the infrastructure it relies on.

Its strong forecast comes on the back of soaring demand for high-performance memory chips used in data centres and other infrastructure supporting the AI industry.

Samsung said Thursday it expected operating profit to range between ‘19.8 trillion and 20.1 trillion won’, which would surpass its record quarterly profit of 17.6 trillion won set in the third quarter of 2018.

If confirmed in its final earnings report, due to be released later this month, the figure would mark an increase of around 200 per cent year on year.

Sales are expected to range between 92 trillion and 94 trillion won, which would also break the record of 86 trillion won set in the third quarter of 2025.

Soaring global demand for semiconductors fuelled by an AI boom sent South Korea’s exports to their highest-ever level in 2025, official data showed last week.

South Korea is also home to SK hynix, another key player in the global semiconductor market.

Fuelled by strong semiconductor sales, Samsung Electronics’ shares have risen more than 120 per cent over the past six months, a trend shared by other South Korean chip makers.

‘With the AI sector at the centre, demand for semiconductors is rising... with the chip industry entering a super-cycle,’ said Chung Hae-chang, an analyst at Daishin Securities.

South Korean president Lee Jae Myung has vowed to triple spending on AI this year, a move aimed at propelling the country into the ranks of the world’s top three AI powers behind the United States and China.

title: US city names street after Khaleda Zia
body:
A street in Hamtramck City of the US State of Michigan will now be known as ‘Khaleda Zia Street’, in honour of late Bangladesh Nationalist Party chairperson and former prime minister Khaleda Zia.

According to BNP’s media cell, the Hamtramck City Council has approved the decision to rename Carpenter Street after the three-time former prime minister of Bangladesh.

Sharing the news on its official Facebook page, the BNP media cell said the renaming of the street reflects an international recognition of Khaleda Zia’s political leadership, democratic struggle and contribution to Bangladesh’s history.

The street is located in the heart of Hamtramck city.

The proposal covers the section of Carpenter Street between Joseph Campau Avenue and Conant Street, which has now been officially renamed as Khaleda Zia Street.

The media cell said four councillors of Bangladeshi origin are currently serving on the Hamtramck City Council, and their active role made the renaming possible.

Members of the Bangladeshi community living in the United States see the decision as more than a symbolic change of a street name.

They believe it represents an international acknowledgement of Bangladesh’s political struggle and leadership.

BNP’s media cell also said this is not the first time a street in the United States has been named after a Bangladeshi leader.

Earlier, a street in Chicago was named after BNP founder Ziaur Rahman. With the addition of Khaleda Zia Street in Michigan, another chapter of Bangladesh’s political history has found a lasting place on US soil.

Hamtramck is widely known for its diverse population, and the naming of a street after a former Bangladesh prime minister is expected to strengthen social and cultural ties between Bangladesh and the United States.

Khaleda Zia died on December 30 while undergoing treatment at Evercare Hospital. She was laid to rest the following day beside his husband Ziaur Rahman’s grave at Sher-e-Bangla Nagar with state honours.

title: Govt to set prices of 295 essential drugs
body:
The interim government on Thursday approved a revised ‘National Essential Medicines List’ including 135 new drugs in the list and a comprehensive drug pricing guideline, aiming to bring down treatment costs and ensure affordable access to medicines for the people.

With the introduction of new drugs, the updated list of essential drugs now includes 295 drugs. The government will set prices for these essential drugs in phases, as per the drug pricing guideline.

The decision was taken at the meeting of the Council of Advisers on Thursday, chaired by chief adviser professor Muhammad Yunus at his office in Tejgaon, said the chief adviser’s special assistant for health, Md Sayedur Rahman, at a press briefing at the Foreign Service Academy after the meeting.

He said that the move marks the most significant reform in Bangladesh’s pharmaceutical pricing system since the landmark Drug Policy of 1982, which helped make the country self-reliant in medicine production and ensured wider public access to essential drugs.

He said that after the original policy, full price control was gradually reduced. By 1994, only 117 medicines out of around 350 in the market remained under government control.

That system remained unchanged for nearly 30 years, allowing the number of uncontrolled medicines to grow to about 1,300, which led to wide price disparities and rising healthcare costs.

At present, nearly two-thirds of Bangladesh’s healthcare spending comes from people’s own pockets, with most of that going toward medicines, he said.

‘In countries where there are national insurance schemes or pharmaceutical benefit systems, people are protected but Bangladesh has none of these. So state intervention in drug pricing had become unavoidable,’ he added.

A specific pricing formula has been introduced, based  on the cost of active pharmaceutical ingredients, excipients and the existing markup system, which remains unchanged.

‘All essential medicines will have government-determined prices. Those selling above the price must come down, and those selling below may adjust within the permitted level,’ he said.

He said that essential medicines, by definition, are sufficient to treat about 80 per cent of all diseases. So, price control on these drugs will directly improve access to treatment for 80 per cent of the population, he said.

Noting the decision a historic one, he said, ‘It will translate the success of our pharmaceutical industry into real health benefits for the people.’

To protect the pharmaceutical industry, a four-year adjustment period has been provided, during which companies will gradually align their prices with government ceilings, he added.

Sayedur Rahman also said that, besides essential medicines, about 1,100 other drugs will also come under regulation.

‘For medicines produced by more than seven manufacturers, internal reference pricing will be applied and prices will be brought within a defined range based on median market prices. These will be adjusted by 25 per cent each year.’

‘For medicines produced by fewer than seven companies, both domestic and international reference prices will be used, with purchasing power parity adjustments, to determine fair pricing,’ he added.

Separate pricing formulas have also been introduced for newly launched off-patent drugs, patented medicines, and biological drugs such as immunomodulators.

The government also plans to establish an independent National Drug Pricing Authority in the future. Until then, the Drug Price Fixation Committee will oversee implementation.

‘This decision will have a long-term impact. It will remove medicine prices as a barrier to healthcare access,’ Sayedur Rahman said.

The Council of Advisers at the weekly meeting also gave final approval of the drafts of Personal Data Protection (Amendment) Ordinance 2026, the Bangladesh Shilpakala Academy (Amendment) Ordinance 2026 and the Supreme Court Secretariat (Amendment) Ordinance 2026 while the draft of Bangladesh Forest Industries Development Corporation Ordinance 2026 got approval in principle.

Besides, the Third Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC 3.0) got retrospective approval in the meeting.

About the Personal Data Protection Ordinance, press secretary Shafiqul Alam said that the amendment of the ordinance was approved with important revisions made after concerns were raised by global technology companies such as Meta (Facebook) and Google.

The key change involves data localisation, he said, adding, earlier provisions required all data to be stored within Bangladesh, but this amendment withdrew that provision.

Under the revised ordinance, mandatory local data storage will apply only to Critical Information Infrastructure, the press secretary said, adding, there are also some restrictions on personal data.

Noting that the earlier provision included imprisonment for criminal offences by corporate offices, he said, the amendment replaced that punishment with financial penalties only.

title: Farmers enter Paris on tractors to rage against Mercosur deal
body:
French farmers rolled into Paris on tractors Thursday in a show of anger against an EU trade deal with South American bloc Mercosur they fear will create unfair competition, as the government warned against ‘illegal’ protest actions.

Dozens of tractors arrived before dawn and drove through Paris, with some pausing at the Eiffel Tower and others at the Arc de Triomphe, in a protest organised by the Rural Confederation union.

‘We said we’d come up to Paris — here we are,’ said Ludovic Ducloux, co-head of one of the union’s chapters.

One of the tractors bore the message ‘No To Mercosur’, referring to the deal with four South American nations.

The deal would create one of the world’s biggest free-trade areas and help the 27-nation EU to export more vehicles, machinery, wines and spirits to Latin America.

EU member states are expected to vote to give the text the final go-ahead on Friday, paving the way for a formal signature next week.

But farmers fear being undercut by a flow of cheaper goods from agricultural giant Brazil and its neighbours.

‘We’re not here to cause trouble,’ Damien Cornier, a 49-year-old farmer from the northwest Eure region, told AFP.

‘We just want to work and make a living from our profession.’

Surrounded by a heavy police presence, farmers demonstrated in front of French parliament’s lower house, heckling the National Assembly President Yael Braun-Pivet when she came out to meet with them.

She said she would meet all trade unions in the afternoon, before security ushered her out of the tense crowd.

French policymakers have contributed to the ‘death of French agriculture over the past 30 years’, Rural Confederation president Bertrand Venteau told Europe 1 radio.

Agriculture Minister Annie Genevard said farmers had ‘legitimate’ demands but called for ‘calm’ and ‘dialogue’.

In the early hours of Thursday, a small number of tractors briefly parked near the Eiffel Tower and more reached the Arc de Triomphe.

There were 100 tractors in the Paris region, the interior ministry told AFP earlier on Thursday, but ‘most are blocked at the gates of the capital’.

In another protest near the southwestern city of Bordeaux, about 40 farm vehicles blocked access to a fuel depot, according to the local authorities.

As well as the trade deal, the farmers are also upset over a government decision to cull cows in response to the spread of nodular dermatitis, a bovine sickness widely known as lumpy skin disease.

At the end of last month, President Emmanuel Macron met farmers to discuss the trade pact and the cull.

During earlier protests, farmers blocked roads, sprayed manure and dumped garbage in front of government offices.

Belgian farmers have also staged mass protests against the trade deal, rolling some 1,000 tractors into Brussels in December.

More than 25 years in the making, the Mercosur accord would boost trade between the EU and the bloc including Brazil, Paraguay, Argentina and Uruguay.

Plans to seal the deal at a gathering in Brazil on December 20 ran into a late roadblock as heavyweights Italy and France demanded a postponement over concerns for the farming sector.

Germany and Spain are strongly in favour of the agreement, believing it will provide a welcome boost to their industries, hampered by Chinese competition and tariffs in the United States.

Ireland however said Thursday that it would vote against the trade deal.

Rome and Paris have called for tougher safeguard clauses, tighter import controls and more stringent standards on Mercosur producers to protect their farmers.

But Italy hailed the benefits of the agreement on Wednesday and foreign minister Antonio Tajani said the country had ‘always supported the conclusion of the deal’.

Tractors are seen parked in front of the Arc de Triomphe during a demonstration of French agricultural union Coordination Rurale (CR) as part of a nationwide day of protests and actions called by several farmers unions to push the French government to block the Mercosur trade deal and protest against its handling of the nodular dermatitis (CND) epidemic, in Paris on Thursday.  AFP photo

title: DU syndicate to frame charges against four professors over July uprising roles
body:
The University of Dhaka Syndicate on Thursday decided to frame charges against four professors—Sadeka Halim, Zeenat Huda, A K M Jamal Uddin, and Md Mashiur Rahman—and issue show-cause notices, asking why they should not be expelled from the university.

Proctor Saifuddin Ahmed confirmed that the decision was based on recommendations from a fact-finding committee tasked with investigating allegations that the professors had obstructed student movements and contributed to security risks during the July 2024 uprising, which eventually led to the ouster of the Sheikh Hasina government.

In a separate decision, the Syndicate also agreed to forward the issue of renaming five residential facilities, including Sheikh Mujibur Rahman Hall, to the university Senate. These facilities are currently named after members of the Sheikh family.

The decision was made during a syndicate meeting on Thursday, chaired by syndicate president and vice-chancellor Professor Niaz Ahmed Khan.

Professor Saifuddin Ahmed told reporters that the matter was brought before the Syndicate following a written request from the Dhaka University Central Students’ Union, alongside decisions taken in previous university meetings discussing the proposed renaming.

He added that, under university regulations, the final decision on renaming facilities rests with the senate, as the syndicate does not have the authority to make such a change. Therefore, the matter will be forwarded to the senate for a final decision.

Earlier, on December 21, the DUCSU leaders staged a protest by blocking the main gate of the vice-chancellor’s office, demanding the renaming of five residential facilities named after Sheikh family members and calling for strict action against teachers and officials who opposed the July uprising.

title: From music to mind reading: AI startups bet on earbuds
body:
AI companies are on the hunt to design the ideal device to deliver AI’s superpowers, and some new enterprises are convinced that headphones or earbuds are the way.

Startups have for a while tried to beef up headphones beyond their basic functions, like listening to music and making phone calls.

Nearly a decade ago, tech startups Waverly Labs and Mymanu added real-time translation to that list, and Google quickly followed suit, creating a voice-activated AI assistant in 2020.

Riding the AI wave, other tech industry leaders Samsung and Apple have also entered the fray, with noise cancellation now almost a product standard.

Startups, many of which are attending this week’s CES consumer electronics extravaganza in Las Vegas, are now trying to refine this technology and apply it to specific uses.

Such is the case with OSO, which wants to take the concept of a professional assistant further.

Its earbuds will record meetings and retrieve conversation elements on demand using everyday language.

Viaim, a competitor, offers similar services and intends to focus on interoperability in a world controlled by major smartphone manufacturers that impose their own platforms.

‘If you use a different brand of cell phone, it doesn’t have any AI functions at all. That’s the opportunity for our earbuds,’ explained Shawn Ma, CEO of Viaim, whose devices are compatible with all brands, including iPhones in China.

Timekettle, meanwhile, is enjoying success in a completely different context, with ‘90 per cent of its sales coming from schools,’ according to Brian Shircliffe, head of US sales for the Chinese company.

Many schools equip their non-English-speaking students with the devices so they can follow lessons without the need for a translator.

As for whether earbuds can replace smart glasses, connected speakers, or even smartphones as the dominant physical extension of generative AI, remains unanswered.

For now, any AI functionality ‘is really dependent on the phone that it’s connected to,’ said Ben Wood, chief analyst at CCS Insight.

‘Earbuds are certainly a more accessible entry for AI than smart glasses,’ said Avi Greengart, president of Techsponential, a consultancy.

‘They’re a lot less expensive, they’re a product most smartphone users are buying anyway, and they don’t require a prescription.’

However, ‘people generally don’t wear them all the time,’ unlike glasses, ‘and they can only interact with voice, so you’ll need to be in an environment where talking is acceptable,’ the analyst cautioned, adding that the lack of a camera limits the device’s potential.

Some won’t be constrained by the shortcoming, notably Naqi Logix, whose Neural Earbuds are equipped with ultra-sensitive sensors that detect tiny movements.

Thanks to these sensors, a quadriplegic user can control their wheelchair or surf the internet simply by looking at their computer screen.

Operations manager Sandeep Arya sees great potential for these innovations, ‘because people would like to be able to interact with their environment in a more discreet, subtle way,’ without having to call out to Siri on their smartphone, Alexa on their speaker, or Meta on their glasses.

Arya envisions the technology going further, thanks to improved sensors capable of deciphering facial movements that a chatbot can use to find the right tone and words according to mood.

Neurable, another startup whose MW75 Neuro LT headset measures brain activity, dreams of using its equipment to enable communication through thought, without gestures or words.

‘It’s remarkable,’ says Ben Wood of these breakthroughs, ‘but it’s still a niche market for now.’

Until further notice, ‘the hundreds of millions of headphones that have been sold will remain focused on listening.’

title: Defence boom lifts German factory orders
body:
Factory orders in long-struggling Germany unexpectedly posted a sharp jump in November, boosted by higher demand for defence equipment as Europe rushes to rearm, official data showed Thursday.

New orders increased 5.6 per cent month-on-month, according to preliminary figures from statistics agency Destatis, the third straight monthly increase.

Analysts surveyed by the financial data firm FactSet had expected a decline of 1.3 per cent.

Russia’s invasion of Ukraine has prompted Germany and other European countries to start re-arming, with chancellor Friedrich Merz vowing to unleash hundreds of billions of euros on defence.

Demand for defence equipment has lifted orders in recent months, the economy ministry noted in a statement.

‘The trend of increasing demand from Germany and the eurozone is continuing,’ it said.

The jump in orders is some positive news for Europe’s biggest economy, which is struggling through a long decline due to a manufacturing slump, high energy costs and weak demand in key export markets.

LBBW bank analyst Jens-Oliver Niklasch said the higher orders overall were ‘a real sign of a possible turnaround in the economy’.

He cautioned that higher defence spending ‘in itself will not generate permanently higher growth potential’ but said it was nevertheless important that ‘there is finally a sign of life from industry’.

November’s figures were lifted by large-scale orders in the category for transport equipment including military vehicles, aircraft, ships and trains, according to Destatis.

Areas outside defence also contributed, with jumps in demand for electrical and IT equipment as well as machine tools, it said.

Domestic orders jumped 6.5 per cent and foreign orders rose almost five per cent, with demand from the euro area up more than eight per cent.

Despite the rosier picture, the economy ministry noted that orders from some overseas markets had been week since early 2025 due to trade and geopolitical uncertainties, and are expected to remain subdued.

The US tariff blitz has been a heavy blow to German firms as the United States is the country’s top export market.

The government is forecasting meagre growth of 0.2 per cent for 2025, before the economy is expected to pick up speed this year.

title: Industry pushes for practical robots doing more than dancing
body:
Humanoid robots danced, somersaulted, dealt blackjack and played ping-pong at the Consumer Electronics Show this week, but some in the industry are impatient for them to become more useful, not just a promise of things to come.

As robots take their usual spotlight at the annual CES gadget fest, insiders caution that making them truly like humans will take several more years and require lots of training.

To become autonomous, humanoid robots need AI that translates what is seen and heard into actions, which is beyond the scope of today’s large language models that power tools like ChatGPT.

Training a large language model relies on massive amounts of data — mainly vacuumed up from the internet — that is of little use when it comes to human-like robots seeking to be useful in the kitchen or on a factory floor.

‘If you want (robots) to learn embodied things, you have to put them inside a body,’ said Henny Admoni, an associate professor at the robotics institute at Carnegie Mellon University.

Humanoid Guide founder Christian Rokseth, who specializes in the technology, likened the situation to locking a child in a room and expecting it to learn about the world.

Even if the pace of development accelerated last year, particularly on the hardware side, Rokseth expressed a degree of impatience about innovation.

‘They’ve shown robots dancing and doing kung fu; now show us that they can be productive,’ Rokseth said.

EngineAI founder Evan Yao told AFP that the Shenzhen-based company is working with tech titans such as Amazon and Meta to give its creations AI brains.

‘We are trying to simulate humans, but the robots will never become human,’ Yao told AFP as one of his robots kicked in his direction.

Nearby, Yiran Sui was part of a Robotera team whose humanoid robot, developed for researchers, is training to complete the Beijing marathon a few months from now.

According to the Consumer Technology Association that runs CES, the robotics industry is showing dynamism and potential.

It projects the global market will hit $179 billion by 2030.

The bulk of that growth is expected in factories, warehouses and other business operations, where robots — not necessarily humanoid ones — work in controlled environments.

But for Artem Sokolov, founder of the Humanoid robotics startup based in London, humans work in factories so robots copying their bodies can thrive there too.

South Korean automotive giant Hyundai used CES to unveil a humanoid robot called Atlas, created in collaboration with Boston Dynamics, that it plans to test in factories.

Given the training limitations, industry trackers advise caution when it comes to companies claiming to have humanoid robots that can operate without flesh-and-blood managers overseeing them.

‘There has been a ton of new companies claiming that they are developing autonomous humanoid robots,’ Admoni told AFP.

But ‘these systems tend to be teleoperated; you have a person in a suit or using controllers and every movement of that person is then translated into the robot.’

To solve the training problem, new startups are using methods such as having people wear cameras and haptic gloves while doing chores at home, according to Rokseth.

‘To make robots general machines, they need to be let out in the real world,’ Rokseth said, not just assembly lines or warehouses.

title: Good prices encourage Rangpur farmers to expand banana cultivation
body:
Stable profitable prices since the outbreak of the Covid-19 epidemic in 2019, farmers have been encouraged to expand banana cultivation in all five districts of Rangpur agricultural region.

In the last six years, hundreds of farmers have changed their fortunes by cultivating bananas, making huge profits as the price of bananas has not dropped even once.

As a result, the Department of Agricultural Extension officials, experts, and farmers are considering banana cultivation as a highly profitable venture in the mainland and riverine char areas to meet nutritional needs as well as achieve self-reliance.

According to DAE officials, after achieving bumper production and profitable prices in the last six years, farmers are expanding banana cultivation in Rangpur, Gaibandha, Kurigram, Lalmonirhat and Nilphamari districts of the region every year.

‘Farmers have already cultivated bananas on 2,621 hectares of land during the current 2025-2026 Rabi season till last week in the region,’ additional director (in-charge) of the DAE for Rangpur region agriculturist Md Shirajul Islam said.

Transplantation of banana saplings will continue till this month-end in the region.

‘During the last 2024-2025 Rabi season, farmers cultivated bananas on 2,683 hectares of land in the region,’ Shirajul said.

Following massive motivational activities conducted by the DAE, farmers are expanding cultivation of bananas as a cash crop to reap more profits alongside meeting their own nutrition to strengthen body immunity.

The DAE officials are assisting farmers and providing technical support to them in expanding cultivation of ‘Meher Sagar’, ‘Malbhog’, ‘Sobri’ and other varieties of banana on more lands both in mainland and char areas.

Meanwhile, harvesting of early varieties of bananas has already begun with a bumper yield and lucrative market price bringing huge profits to farmers making them happy.

Talking to BSS, farmers Abdur Rahman, Mokhlesur Rahman and Badal Hossain of different villages in Badarganj upazila of Rangpur said that they had been cultivating bananas for the last 15 years and earning rewarding profits every year.

Farmers Mofizar Rahman, Abdul Hye and Nurun Nabi of village Dolapara in Taraganj upazila and Habibur Rahman of village Gopalpur in Badarganj upazila of Rangpur said that they had cultivated bananas on more land areas this time than last season.

Farmers Yusuf Ali, Babul Akhter, Nurul Islam and Mahbubar of different char villages in Nageshwari upazila of Kurigram said that char people had been successfully cultivating bananas on char lands and reaping lucrative profits for the last ten years.

‘We are selling bananas on one side of char lands and cultivating it afresh on the other side on vacant lands round the year. The process of formation and growth of new banana bunches continues all the time giving the gardens fresh looks,’ said Yusuf Ali.

Babul Akhter said that more and more char lands were being brought under banana farming in Nageshwari upazila like in other upazilas of Kurigram every year.

‘We are cultivating bananas afresh round the year with other crops adopting intercropping and relay methods on char lands. Banana farming is largely contributing to our socio-economic development,’ he said.

Retail fruit traders Fazlur Rahman at Rangpur City Bazar and Abdus Samad at Pirgachha Bazar in Rangpur said they are selling every four pieces of ‘Malbhog’ and ‘Sobri’ varieties of bananas at rates between Tk 35 and Tk 50 now.

Deputy director of the DAE’s Burirhat Horticulture Centre in Rangpur Dr Md Abu Sayem said that banana cultivation was expanding in both mainland and char areas, improving farmers’ livelihoods and keeping the rural economy vibrant.

title: Trump to ban major investors from buying single-family homes
body:
President Donald Trump said Wednesday that the United States is moving to bar major institutional investors from buying more single-family homes, an announcement that comes as American households face high costs of living.

‘For a very long time, buying and owning a home was considered the pinnacle of the American Dream,’ Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform.

But he noted that this goal is ‘increasingly out of reach for far too many people, especially younger Americans.’

‘It is for that reason, and much more, that I am immediately taking steps to ban large institutional investors from buying more single-family homes, and I will be calling on Congress to codify it,’ Trump wrote on social media. ‘People live in homes, not corporations.’

He said he planned to discuss this topic and other affordability proposals in a speech at the upcoming Davos World Economic Forum.

Trump has been facing growing voter frustration over the issue of affordability, despite efforts to dismiss it as a ‘hoax’ by Democrats, sparking Republican fears they could be punished in the 2026 midterm elections.

While there has not been a widespread inflation surge since Trump rolled out sweeping new tariffs on various imports from US trading partners, companies have reported higher business costs while analysts note a divergence in the economy.

Higher-income households may be doing well, but those with lower-incomes tend to be struggling with costs.

Within the housing sector, the median sales prices of previously owned homes have been climbing from past years as well, according to the National Association of Realtors.

NAR data showed that the median cost for existing homes was $409,200 in November, up 1.2 per cent from a year prior.

Elizabeth Warren, the top Democrat on the Senate Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs, was quick to urge Trump to take action after his post.

‘Trump should start with getting his own party in the House to support a bipartisan bill to bring down housing costs that passed the Senate unanimously,’ she said in a statement.

‘And Congress should work on legislation to stop corporate investors from buying up homes,’ Warren added.

Shares in Blackstone, an investor in residential real estate, closed around 5.6 per cent lower. Other housing-related companies also saw their shares fall after the announcement.

title: Minority safety reflects quality of democracy: dialogue
body:
The quality of a democracy is measured by how safe and included its minority and vulnerable communities feel, speakers said at a policy dialogue on Thursday.

Amid growing debate over political reforms ahead of the forthcoming 13th Jatiya Sangsad elections, the Centre for Governance Studies organised the dialogue titled ‘Electoral Commitments to Inclusive Democracy and Minority Rights’, at the CIRDAP auditorium in the capital Dhaka.

Political leaders, academics, civil society members and rights activists discussed whether inclusion, minority rights and democratic values are meaningfully reflected in party manifestos.

Opening the discussion, CGS president Zillur Rahman said political parties often made commitments to minority rights that were rarely implemented.

He stressed the need for clear pre-election reform pledges, accountability mechanisms and fear-free participation in elections.

Political scientist Rounaq Jahan said that minority safety was central to democratic quality, noting that rights lose meaning when citizens must prioritise personal security over participation.

She also highlighted the gap between manifesto promises and measurable implementation.

SHUJAN chief executive Badiul Alam Majumder said that a state could not be considered civilised if minority and vulnerable groups remained unprotected.

He described electoral manifestos as a social contract and called for lawful, free and fair elections, warning that democracy cannot survive manipulation.

Nationalist Democratic Movement secretary general Mominul Amin said that inclusive democracy required genuine political will and fair representation of all social groups in parliament, while Bangladesh Open University vice-chancellor Sayeed Ferdous pointed to structural marginalisation of minorities since 1971.

Trans feminist activist Ho Chi Minh Islam said that minority rights could not be dictated by majorities, while national minority community leader Sanjeeb Drong said that Bangladesh’s progress would remain incomplete until minority communities themselves feel safe.

title: MTB inks deal with SMC for cash management
body:
Mutual Trust Bank PLC and SMC Enterprise recently signed an agreement for Cash Management Services in a simple ceremony at MTB Centre, the bank’s corporate head office at Gulshan in Dhaka.

Through this arrangement, SMC Enterprise will be able to process all types of transactions seamlessly through MTB’s corporate banking solution - MTB eBank, said a press release.

Users can approve these transactions conveniently using biometric authentication on the MTB eBank App.

MTB managing director and chief executive officer Syed Mahbubur Rahman and SMC managing director Sayef Uddin Nasir exchanged the document on behalf of their respective organisations.

From MTB, divisional head of wholesale banking division Mohammad Mamun Faruk, unit head of wholesale banking division-1 Eva Rahman, head of SME and agri banking division Sanjib Kumar Dey, head of card division Md Abu Bokar Siddik, divisional head of cash management and transaction banking Mohammad Ashik Iqbal Khan, from SMC, and chief financial officer Abul Bashir Khan, DGM of finance and accounts Mohammad Tanvir Hossain, among others, attended the ceremony.

title: City Bank to build Tk 855cr office complex at Gulshan
body:
City Bank PLC has decided to build a Tk 855 crore worth multi-storied office building in Gulshan-2, subject to obtaining all necessary approvals from the relevant regulatory authorities, according to a disclosure filed with the Dhaka Stock Exchange on Thursday.

The decision was taken at a meeting of the bank’s board of directors held on January 7.

Under the plan, the bank will purchase around 20 katha of land on Gulshan Avenue at a cost of Tk 345 crore, including all related expenses.

Bangladesh Bank approved the land acquisition on January 6, 2026.

The newly purchased plot is adjacent to City Bank’s existing 20-katha land in the same area.

Once combined, the bank will have about 40 katha of land at the site, where it plans to construct a purpose-built, multi-storied office complex for its own use.

The total estimated cost of the project stands at Tk 855 crore, covering construction and all associated expenses, the disclosure said.

The bank noted that implementation of the project will depend on obtaining approvals from relevant regulatory authorities and complying with conditions set by Bangladesh Bank.

The move reflects City Bank’s long-term strategy to consolidate its operations at a prime commercial location in the capital.

Gulshan is one of Dhaka’s most expensive business districts, hosting the headquarters of several banks, multinational companies and diplomatic missions.

City Bank did not provide a construction timeline in the disclosure. The project will proceed in phases once all regulatory approvals are in place, the bank said.

title: Uber Bangladesh, VisionSpring launch ‘See to Be Safe’ initiative
body:
Leading ridesharing app Uber on Wednesday announced a partnership with VisionSpring, a leading global social enterprise dedicated to providing affordable eyeglasses worldwide, to launch See to Be Safe (S2S), a programme focused on strengthening driver safety and wellbeing through professional eye screenings and access to corrective eyeglasses.

As part of the programme, VisionSpring will conduct free vision screenings and provide subsidized eyeglasses for Uber drivers across Dhaka and other key cities, helping address untreated vision impairment, said a press release.

The screenings began this week as part of Uber’s 9-year anniversary in Bangladesh.

Nasheed Ferdous Kamal, country head of Uber Bangladesh, said, ‘Road safety is at the core of Uber’s mission. Clear vision is one of the most essential requirements for driving safely, yet it often goes unnoticed until it becomes a serious concern. Through our partnership with VisionSpring, we are investing in the wellbeing of the people who keep Bangladesh moving, our drivers. We are proud to launch ‘See to Be Safe’ as part of our continued commitment to building a safer, more responsible mobility ecosystem in Bangladesh.’

Misha Mahjabeen, country director of VisionSpring Bangladesh, shared, ‘We are delighted to partner with Uber Bangladesh to provide vision screenings and eyeglasses for thousands of driver-partners. A simple pair of eyeglasses can significantly reduce the risk of road accidents and improve a driver’s earning potential. VisionSpring is committed to ensuring that no one’s vision prevents them from working safely and productively, and this initiative is a valuable step toward that goal.’

title: Mercantile Bank organises training on AML, CFT
body:
Mercantile Bank Training Institute organised a comprehensive training programme on Prevention of Money Laundering and Combating Financing of Terrorism in the bank’s training institute on Wednesday to strengthen awareness and capacity among the officials.

Managing director of the bank, Mati Ul Hasan, attended the programme as chief guest, said a press release.

DMD and CAMLCO of the bank, Shamim Ahmed, attended the programme as a special guest.

The program was chaired by the head of training and development, SM Salim Uddin, where other distinguished speakers, including the bank’s EVP and DCAMLCO Abu Yusuf Md Abdullah Haroon, BIBM faculty Mahmudul Ameen Masud, and faculty of MBTI Muhammad Miaraz Hossen Gazi, attended the event.

The speakers have emphasised the importance of continuous training to prevent financial crimes and ensure regulatory compliance.

A total of 42 participants from the different Branches and Divisions attended the training program.

title: Shibir secures majority posts in JnUCSU elections
body:
Islami Chhatra Shibir has secured 16 posts, including the posts of the vice-president, general secretary and assistant general secretary, in the first-ever elections to the Jagannath University Central Students’ Union and hall union, held on Tuesday.

The panel jointly fielded by Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal and Chhatra Odhikar Parishad secured four posts in the 21-member JnUCSU.

An independent candidate secured the remaining post, according to JnUCSU election results published on Thursday.

The results were declared through a notification signed by the chief election commissioner, Professor Mostafa Hasan, and other election commissioners.

After the voting hours, ballot counting began and continued until Wednesday night.

According to the results, Shibir’s Md Riazul Islam was elected vice-president, securing 5,558 votes, while his nearest rival AKM Rakib of Chhatra Dal and Chhatra Adhikar Parishad panel bagged 4,688 votes.

Abdul Alim Arif of Shibir was elected general secretary by bagging 5,475 votes, while his nearest Chhatra Dal candidate, Khadijatul Kubra, got 2,223 votes.

Shibir’s Masud Rana was elected assistant general secretary by securing 5,020 votes, defeating his nearest Chhatra Dal’s BM Atikur Rahman Tanjil, who received 4,022 votes.

In the central union’s 11 secretary positions, Md Nur Nabi was elected the liberation war and democracy secretary, Ibrahim Khalil education and research secretary, Mosammat Sukhiman Khatun the science and technology secretary, Habib Md Faruk Azam the law and human rights secretary, Naoshin Nawar Joya international affairs secretary, Md Takrim Mia literature and culture secretary, Jeorgis Anwar Naim sports secretary, Md Mahid Hossain transport secretary, Md Riasal library and seminar affairs secretary, Mostafizur Rahman student welfare and affairs secretary, and Nur Mohammad was elected health and environment secretary.

The seven elected executive members of JnUCSU are Shibir’s Fatema Akter, Md Akib Hasan, Shanta Akter, Md Mehedi Hasan, and Md Abdullah Al Faruk, Chhatra Dal’s Md Sadman Amin, and independent candidate Md Jahid Hasan.

Reacting to the results, Chhatra Dal and Chhatra Adhikar Parishad’s VP candidate AKM Rakib described the election as free, fair and transparent and congratulated the winners.

title: Modhumoti Bank opens Keraniganj agent point
body:
Modhumoti Bank PLC inaugurated its ‘Keraniganj Agent Point’ under the control of the Modhumoti Aganagar Branch, located on the Bridge Road in South Keraniganj in Dhaka on Wednesday.

Managing director and chief executive officer Md Shafiul Azam inaugurated the branch as chief guest, said a press release.

Head of agent banking division Suman Roy, branch manager of Modhumoti Aganagar branch Mohammad Musabbir Hossan, among others, attended the ceremony.

title: Haier launches 24/7 call centre, expands service network
body:
Haier Bangladesh has recently introduced a 24/7 customer call centre and significantly expanded its after-sales service network by adding 17 exclusive service centres and 7 direct service centres across the country, said a press release.

This initiative ensures uninterrupted customer support, available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.

By pioneering such a service in Bangladesh’s electronics industry, Haier has set a new benchmark for customer care by offering round-the-clock assistance, faster response times, and enhanced service quality for Haier customers nationwide.

The expanded service infrastructure will deliver standardized and reliable technical support in key regions, reinforcing Haier’s commitment to superior customer experience.

Haier Bangladesh deputy managing director Wang Xiangjing and service head Fazlul Haque attended the launch event.

Speaking at the ceremony, Wang Xiangjing stated, ‘Customer satisfaction is central to Haier’s global vision. By introducing a 24/7 call centre and strengthening our service network, we aim to provide faster, more reliable, and more convenient service to customers across Bangladesh.’

This initiative underscores Haier Bangladesh’s dedication to enhancing customer experience and strengthening service capabilities nationwide.

title: Savor, BGMEA sign deal for BCGTX 2026
body:
Savor International Limited, in collaboration with the Chinese Enterprises Association in Bangladesh, is set to organise the second edition of the Bangladesh-China Green Textile Expo, said a press release.

A memorandum of understanding has been signed between Savor International Limited and the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association, reinforcing bilateral cooperation between Bangladesh and China in the garments and textile sector, with a strong focus on sustainability and green innovation.

The expo is supported by the Embassy of the People’s Republic of China in Bangladesh.

The MoU signing ceremony was held recently at the BGMEA office at Uttara in Dhaka.

The agreement was signed by Sajed Karim, chairman, Standing Committee on Trade

Fair and Events, BGMEA, Md Faizul Alam, managing director of Savor International Limited, on behalf of the organiser, and  Zhou Meimei, executive secretary of CEAB.

The ceremony was also attended by other officials from BGMEA, CEAB, and Savor International Limited.

Through this MoU, BGMEA will actively support the promotion and development of the exhibition as the event’s Knowledge Partner.

BCGTX 2026 is scheduled to take place from May 14-16 at the International Convention City Bashundhara in Dhaka.

title: NCC Bank, BB sign deal on start-up refinance fund
body:
NCC Bank recently signed a participating agreement with Bangladesh Bank to expand financing in the start-up sector.

Through this agreement, NCC Bank will be able to disburse loans to eligible start-up entrepreneurs using refinance funds received from BB, said a press release.

The primary objective of the BDT 5 billion fund is to support the development of new, technology-driven, innovative, and scalable entrepreneurial ventures across the country.

The agreement was signed and exchanged at the head office of Bangladesh Bank in the presence of Bangladesh Bank deputy governor Nurun Nahar.

Managing director of NCC Bank, M Shamsul Arefin, and director of the SME and Special Programme Department of Bangladesh Bank, Nawshad Mustafa, signed the agreement on behalf of their respective institutions.

Executive director of Bangladesh Bank Husne Ara Shikha, deputy managing director Md Habibur Rahman, and SVP and head of the SME division of NCC Bank Sharif Mohammad Mahsin, among others, attended the event.

title: NRBC Bank chair Ali Hossain wins corporate governance award
body:
Md Ali Hossain Prodhania, chairman of NRBC Bank PLC, has been honoured with the ‘Excellence in Corporate Governance Award’ in recognition of his outstanding leadership in promoting excellence, transparency and accountability in corporate governance and for expanding modern, customer-centric banking services.

At the event, Bangladesh Bank governor Ahsan H Mansur handed over the award to Ali Hossain, said a press release.

The award ceremony was held recently in a hotel as part of the NRB Global Convention.

The chief adviser’s special assistant, Sheikh Moinuddin, attended the event as a special guest.

This recognition reflects Ali Hossain Prodhania’s significant role in ensuring good governance, transparency, accountability and ethical standards in the banking sector and the broader corporate arena through effective leadership.

At the same time, the award underscores NRBC Bank PLC’s continued commitment to strengthening corporate governance and delivering sustainable and secure banking services for its customers.

Enamul Haque Enam, founder of NRB World, along with expatriate entrepreneurs, industrialists, business leaders, doctors, engineers, scientists, teachers, and information technology professionals from around 25 countries, attended the programme.

title: IDRA suspends licences of non-life insurance agents
body:
The Insurance Development and Regulatory Authority has moved to suspend licences of all individual agents involved in non-life insurance sector.

As per a press release dated January 7, the regulatory authority said that insurance business could not be conducted through individual agents in the non-life insurance sector effective January 1, 2026.

The release said that there was no scope for appointment of individual agents in non-life insurance business, solicitation of business through agents or provision of any financial benefits in the name of commission.

Violation of this directive is a violation of Section 58(1) of the Insurance Act, 2010 and is a punishable offense.

The press release said that this decision had been taken to eliminate irregularities, commission-based inconsistencies and lack of transparency in the non-life insurance sector.

title: NOVOAIR steps into 14th year
body:
NOVOAIR, one of the Bangladesh’s leading airlines, has successfully stepped into its 14th year of operations on January 9.

To mark the occasion, the airline has begun celebrating the milestone on Thursday, through a series of special initiatives, said a press release.

On this occasion, NOVOAIR has announced a 14 per cent discount on fares for one month for its valued passengers.

To enjoy the offer, tickets can be purchased from NOVOAIR sales centres, website and mobile apps.

Passengers can also purchase tickets from the website and mobile apps using the promo code VQANNI14.

NOVOAIR commenced its journey on 9 January 2013 with its inaugural passenger flight on the Dhaka to Chattogram route.

NOVOAIR managing director Mofizur Rahman said, ‘We are committed to passengers’ expectations by ensuring on-time flight operations and safe travel. Overcoming various challenges, NOVOAIR has emerged as a trusted and reliable name in air travel. Looking ahead, our focus remains on further enhancing passenger services while expanding both domestic and international routes.’

title: US could run Venezuela, tap its oil for years, says Trump
body:
The United States could run Venezuela and tap into its oil reserves for years, President Donald Trump said in an interview published Thursday, less than a week after toppling Nicolas Maduro.

‘Only time will tell’ how long Washington would demand direct oversight of the South American country, Trump told The New York Times.

But when asked whether that meant three months, six months or a year, he replied: ‘I would say much longer.’

His assertion of US dominance over Venezuela comes despite its interim leader Delcy Rodriguez saying there is no foreign power governing Caracas.

‘There is a stain on our relations such as had never occurred in our history,’ Rodriguez said of the US attack to depose her predecessor.

US special forces snatched president Maduro and his wife Saturday in a lightning raid and whisked them to New York to face trial on drug and weapons charges, underscoring what Trump has called the ‘Donroe Doctrine’ of US dominance over its backyard.

‘We obviously have maximum leverage over the interim authorities in Venezuela right now’ following the capture operation, White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt said.

‘We’re continuing to be in close coordination with the interim authorities, and their decisions are going to continue to be dictated by the United States of America.’

Trump has said the United States will ‘run’ Venezuela, which has the world’s largest proven oil reserves.

‘They’re giving us everything that we feel is necessary,’ Trump told the Times.

But Washington has no boots on the ground, and appears to be relying on a naval blockade and the threat of further force to ensure Rodriguez’s cooperation.

Caracas announced on Wednesday that at least 100 people had been killed in the US attack and a similar number wounded.

Among those hurt were Maduro and his wife Cilia Flores, Interior Minister Diosdado Cabello said, though the couple were seen walking unassisted during a New York court appearance earlier this week.

According to Havana, the death toll includes 32 members of the Cuban military. Maduro, like his firebrand predecessor Hugo Chavez, employed specialized Cuban soldiers as bodyguards.

Trump’s administration has so far indicated it intends to stick with Rodriguez and sideline opposition figures, including Nobel Peace Prize winner Maria Corina Machado. But it has given few details about its plans.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio insisted on Wednesday, after meeting lawmakers on Capitol Hill critical of the post-Maduro planning, that the United States was ‘not just winging it’.

But so far, the US plan relies heavily on what Trump said on Tuesday was an agreement for Venezuela to hand over between 30 million and 50 million barrels of oil to the United States for it to then sell.

Trump said Wednesday that under the deal Venezuela ‘is going to be purchasing ONLY American Made Products, with the money they receive’ from the oil.

That would include agricultural products, machinery, medical devices and energy equipment, he added.

Rubio said that in a second ‘recovery’ phase, US and Western companies would have access to the Venezuelan market and ‘at the same time, begin to create the process of reconciliation nationally within Venezuela’.

Venezuela’s state oil firm PDVSA said it was discussing oil sales with the United States for the ‘sale of volumes of oil’ under existing commercial frameworks.

But Washington is looking at longer term control, according to Energy Secretary Chris Wright.

‘We’re going to market the crude coming out of Venezuela, first this backed-up stored oil, and then indefinitely, going forward, we will sell the production that comes out of Venezuela,’ Wright said Wednesday.

Trump and his advisors are considering a plan for the US to exert some control over PDVSA, the Wall Street Journal reported.

The US would then have a hand in controlling most of the oil reserves in the Western Hemisphere, as Trump aims to drive oil prices down to $50 a barrel, the paper reported.

Trump will Friday meet executives from US oil companies, whom he has said will invest in Venezuela’s crumbling facilities, despite no firm having yet made such pledges.

title: Shajgoj opens new outlet in Khilgaon
body:
The e-commerce beauty brand, Shajgoj, has opened its new outlet at Taltola Road, Khilgaon, Dhaka, said a press release.

The new outlet brings together a wide range of popular beauty and personal care brands under one roof, offering customers easier access to their favourite products in a convenient retail setting, mentioned the press release.

Through this expansion, Shajgoj aims to connect brands with consumers across Bangladesh more efficiently and continues to grow as a trusted beauty brand destination both online and offline.

title: SC clears way for BB to list Cumilla-4 BNP candidate as a loan defaulter
body:
The Appellate Division on Thursday stayed for eight weeks a High Court order that barred Bangladesh Bank from listing BNP candidate Manzurul Ahsan Munshi as a loan defaulter, a move that has political implications ahead of the national election in Cumilla-4.

Chamber judge Md Rezaul Haque passed the stay order after hearing separate petitions filed by IDLC Finance Limited and Premier Bank, challenging the High Court’s directive.

Following the Appellate Division’s order, lawyers for the banks said Manzurul Ahsan’s name would now be included in the Bangladesh Bank’s Credit Information Bureau as a loan defaulter.

Manzurul Ahsan, managing director of MAM Power Limited, is contesting the 13th Jatiya Sangsad election from Cumilla-4 as a BNP candidate. His company allegedly owes about Tk 88 crore to Premier Bank and over Tk 12 crore to IDLC Finance Limited.

IDLC’s lawyer said the Election Commission’s appeal tribunal remains the appropriate forum to challenge the returning officer’s decision that validated Manzurul Ahsan’s candidature recently.

The High Court had issued the stay order on December 8, 2025, following a petition filed by Manzurul Ahsan before the election schedule was announced on December 11.

The national election is scheduled for February 12. Manzurul Ahsan challenged the Dhaka Fifth Joint District Judge’s Court that on November 5, 2025 rejected his prayer seeking a directive not to include his name in the defaulter list. He argued that his company has been negotiating for settlement of the defaulted loan.

National Citizen Party chief organiser for the southern region, Hasnat Abdullah, is the main rival candidate in the Cumilla-4 constituency.

Manzurul Ahsan was represented by senior lawyer Ruhul Quddus Kazal and lawyer Muhammad Saifullah Mamun.

IDLC Finance Limited was represented by lawyer Mohammad Hossain while lawyer Bivuti Tarofder defended the Premier Bank.

Deputy attorney general Jahirul Islam Suman represented the state.

title: Bangladesh asks three missions in India to suspend visa services on security grounds
body:
The Bangladesh interim government foreign affairs adviser, Md Touhid Hossain, on Thursday confirmed that they have asked its three key diplomatic missions in India to keep their visa sections closed for a time being on security grounds.

‘What I have done is that I have asked our three missions to keep their visa sections closed for the time being. It’s a security issue,’ he said while responding to a question at foreign affairs ministry.

Though he did not mention the names of the missions, a diplomatic source said the three missions are Bangladesh high commission in New Delhi, Deputy High Commission in Kolkata and Bangladesh Assistant High Commission Agartala.

There are Bangladesh missions stationed in Mumbai and Chennai, too.

Responding to a question on cricketers’ safety issue, the Foreign Adviser said he fully supports what Sports Adviser Asif Nazrul had said.

Sports adviser Asif Nazrul reaffirmed on Wednesday that Bangladesh will not travel to India for the upcoming T20 World Cup, reiterating the nation’s demand to have their matches relocated to co-host Sri Lanka.

Speaking to the media following a meeting with directors of the Bangladesh Cricket Board, Asif Nazrul said while the nation is eager to participate it cannot be at the expense of national dignity or player safety.

‘We have discussed the situation. The Bangladesh team played hard and fought to qualify for the T20 World Cup, and as a cricket-crazy nation, we certainly want to play in the World Cup,’ he said.

‘We will certainly play outside India,’ said foreign adviser Hossain.

Asked about the impact of this in bilateral relations, the foreign adviser said this issue came afresh though at various times various issues came and each issue will have negative impacts to some extent.

Talking about keeping business relations unhurt, the adviser said if they find their interest in purchasing rice at a cheaper price, the business people will go for that.

Asked about Bangladesh’s ‘potential interest’ in procuring the JF-17 Thunder fighter aircraft from Pakistan, the Foreign Adviser said, ‘I can’t tell about this today. Talks are under way. You will know once things are finalised.’

title: LP gas traders call-off strike
body:
The LP Gas Traders’ Cooperative Society Limited on Thursday withdrew its indefinite nationwide strike on LPG marketing and supply.

The organisation in an announcement in the afternoon said the strike was called off following assurances from the Bangladesh Energy Regulatory Commission to meet its demands.

Overnight the association called the strike to press home its demands including stopping the ongoing administrative drives across Bangladesh, increasing charges for distributors and retailers.

title: Bangladesh to seek exemption from US visa bond, says Touhid
body:
