All preparations are made for the first-ever elections at the Jagannath University Central Students’ Union and its hall students’ unions rescheduled for today under heightened security.

JnUCSU polls were initially scheduled for December 30, but were postponed following an emergency syndicate meeting convened after the death of Bangladesh Nationalist Party chairperson and former prime minister Khaleda Zia.

The university administration and the election commission have stepped up security and disciplinary measures across the campus to ensure free, fair, and peaceful voting.

Controlled entry and exit points will be enforced across the campus.

Voting will begin at 8:30am and continue uninterrupted until 3:00pm.

A total of 16,500 students are expected to cast their votes at 178 polling booths set up across 39 polling centres, according to the election commission.

Ballot papers will be distributed to the polling centres in the morning before the voting begins, votes will be counted using digital OMR machines immediately after polling concludes.

To ensure security, CCTV cameras have been installed at every polling centre.

Ahead of the election, the university administration strengthened security in and around the Jagannath University campus. Alongside police, intelligence officers have also been deployed, while a police control room has been set up at Bahadur Shah Park in front of the university.

JnU proctor professor Tazammol Hoque said, ‘Comprehensive preparations had been completed to maintain a secure campus during the election period. Law enforcement agencies have also intensified surveillance in and around the university area to prevent any untoward incidents.’

The election commission has published detailed information on polling centres and booths. Of the 39 polling centres, 38 are designated for the central students’ union and one for the hall union.

There will be one booth for every 100 voters. Separate polling centres have been fixed for different faculties and departments. Voting will be held in science, arts, and social science buildings, as well as auditoriums, halls, and departmental facilities. Polling for the women’s hall union will take place at the Shaheed Sajid Bhaban.

To maintain discipline, the election commission has imposed strict restrictions on entry to polling centres. Only registered voters, authorised election officials, teachers, law enforcement personnel, and approved individuals carrying identification cards will be permitted to enter.

Chief Election Commissioner professor Mostafa Hasan said that the security plan had been finalised in coordination with the Ministry of Home Affairs and the local police administration.

This is the first-ever JnUCSU election since the establishment of Jagannath University. A total of 16,725 students are registered as voters. A total of six panels are contesting the election with more than fifty independent candidates contesting various posts.156 candidates are contesting for 21 central union posts, while 33 candidates are vying for 13 hall union positions.

title: ACC files charge sheet against ex-minister Jabed, 36 others
body:
The Anti-Corruption Commission has submitted a charge sheet to a Chattogram court against former land minister Saifuzzaman Chowdhury Jabed, his spouse, former chairman of United Commercial Bank Rukmila Zaman, and 36 other individuals, accusing them of embezzling Tk 25 crore from the UCB’s port branch through fraudulent activities and money laundering.

The investigation officer of the case presented the charge sheet to Judge Hasanul Islam at the Chattogram metropolitan senior special judge’s court on Monday.

The court accepted the charge sheet and set Wednesday as the date for the hearing in the matter. Earlier, the charge sheet of the case was discussed at the ACC head office on Sunday.

The individuals named in the charge sheet include former land minister Jabed, his spouse, former chairman of UCB Rukmila Zaman, UCB acting managing director Arif Qadri, former vice-chairman of the bank Bazl Ahmed Babul, previous chairman of the risk management committee MA Sabur and former directors of the bank Yunus Ahmed, Haji Abu Kalam, Nurul Islam Chowdhury, Asifuzzaman Chowdhury, Roksana Zaman Chowdhury, Bashir Ahmed, Afroza Zaman, Syed Kamruzzaman, Md Shah Alam, Md Jonaid Shafiq, Aparup Chowdhury and Touhid Sipar Rafiquzzaman.

Additionally, the charge sheet lists former senior officer of UCB port branch, Mohammad Ekram Ullah, former branch head and vice-president of the branch Abdul Hamid Chowdhury, former credit officer Ziaul Karim Khan and the former FAVP and operations manager Mir Mesbah Uddin Hossain.

Furthermore, it includes protocol officer of Aramit PLC and proprietor of Vision Trading Mohammad Farman Ullah Chowdhury, employee of Aramit PLC and proprietor of Model Trading Mohammad Misbahul Alam, AGM of Aramit PLC and proprietor of Imperial Trading Md Abdul Aziz, AGM of Aramit and proprietor of Classic Trading Mohammad Jahangir Alam and Aramit employees Mohammad Hossain Chowdhury, Md Yasinur Rahman, Md Yusuf Chowdhury and Md Saiful Islam.

During the investigation, the ACC uncovered that Mohammad Farman Ullah Chowdhury, who serves as the protocol officer for Aramit Limited, owned by Saifuzzaman Chowdhury, was misrepresented as the proprietor of a paper company named Vision Trading by masquerading as a businessman.

A current account was established at the UCB Chattogram port branch on October 13, 2019, utilising fraudulent information and forged documents.

The report indicated that the senior officer of the branch, Akramullah, along with the then branch head and deputy principal officer Abdul Hamid Chowdhury sanctioned the account unlawfully without conducting any verification.

Subsequently, on February 13, 2020, a time loan amounting to Tk 25 crore was requested for a period of 180 days in the name of Vision Trading, citing the acquisition of wheat, lentils, chickpeas and yellow peas.

It was suggested that the loan be granted without any collateral by presenting false stock, experience and warehouse details.

Ultimately, the loan received approval during the 448th meeting of the bank’s board of directors convened on March 12, 2020.

On July 24, 2025, the deputy director of the organisation, Mashiur Rahman Khan, lodged the case at the ACC’s Dhaka Integrated District Office as the complainant.

A total of 31 individuals were named as defendants in the case, with the number of accused rising to 36 during the investigation process.

title: 2 shipbreaking workers found dead on seashore
body:
Two shipbreaking workers were found dead, with one’s body severed in three parts, on the seashore in Sitakunda upazila of Chattogram on Monday.

A Fire Service and Civil Defence team recovered the bodies in the morning from the coast adjacent to KR Green Shipyard in Kumira area, Fire Service and police officials said.

The deceased were identified as Saiful Islam, 25, and Abdul Khaleq, 27, both from Gaibandha district.

Fire Service officials said that Saiful’s body was found dismembered, with the head, hands and legs separated, while Khaleq’s body was recovered intact.

Kumira Fire Service senior station officer Al Mamun said that shipyard authorities told them that the workers were guarding the nearby coast area at night using a boat when robbers attacked them and killed the two men.

Chattogram Industrial Police-3 superintendent Abdullah Al Mahmud said that the shipyard owner informed them that robbers approached the shipyard in two boats at about 3:30am and that Saiful, Khaleq and several others confronted the gang with two boats from the yard.

Abdullah said that the bodies were recovered about 350 metres (about 1150 feet) away from the shipyard where the confrontation was reported, near another shipyard owned by the same owner.

Sitakunda Model Police officer-in-charge Md Mohinul Islam said that no case was filed as no one had lodged any complaint yet.

He said that the bodies were sent to Chattogram Medical College Hospital for post-mortem.

The police were investigating the incident, he added.

title: Patient killed in Russian strike on Kyiv clinic
body:
Russia bombarded Ukraine early Monday with strikes that hit a medical clinic in Kyiv, forcing night-time evacuations into freezing temperatures and killing two people, including a patient at the facility.

The barrage comes on the eve of a diplomatic summit in France involving Ukraine and its security allies — the latest in a US-led push to end the Russian invasion, which began four years ago next month.

The Russian strikes triggered a fire at a private medical clinic in the capital, killing one person and wounding three others, the authorities said.

Emergency services released images of rescuers removing people on stretchers from a gutted building.

‘Doctors and nurses were forced to evacuate the wounded under fire,’ Ukraine’s prime minister Yulia Svyrydenko said on X.

‘It was a terrible night for us,’ Margaryta Maliovana, the clinic’s CEO, said.

‘One person died. A young man, 30-year-old, was killed,’ she said, adding that there were 26 patients in the clinic at the moment of the strike.

The pre-dawn attack also killed one man in his 70s in the neighbouring city of Fastiv, the Kyiv regional governor said.

The strikes caused power outages in the area, with backup systems activated to maintain water and heating supplies, the official said, as temperatures dropped to —8C.

Russia launched a total of 165 drones and at least nine missiles overnight, the Ukrainian air force said.

European leaders are set to meet in Paris on Tuesday, seeking a breakthrough on a plan to end the fighting that Kyiv says is ‘90 percent’ ready.

‘This week, we will be working with our European and American partners to ensure that Ukraine has the assistance it needs,’ Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelensky said Monday.

To lay the groundwork, security advisers from 15 countries, including Britain, France and Germany as well as representatives from NATO and the European Union, gathered in Kyiv over the weekend.

US special envoy Steve Witkoff joined the talks virtually, a Ukrainian official said, though the United States’ large-scale military attack on Venezuela earlier in the day overshadowed proceedings.

Another preparatory meeting, between chiefs of staff, is scheduled for Monday.

Diplomatic efforts to end Europe’s deadliest conflict since World War II have gained pace in recent weeks, though both Moscow and Kyiv remain at odds over the key issue of territory in a post-war settlement.

Russia, which occupies around 20 per cent of Ukraine, is pushing for full control of the country’s eastern Donbas region as part of a deal.

But Kyiv has warned that ceding ground will embolden Moscow and said it will not sign a peace deal that fails to deter Russia from invading again.

On Monday, Russia said it had seized the village of Grabovske in Ukraine’s northeastern Sumy region, from where Kyiv had last month accused Moscow of forcibly relocating dozens of residents.

Bombarded daily and losing ground, Ukraine has responded with its own drone attacks launched towards Russian territory, targeting in particular energy infrastructure that funds the war effort.

US president Donald Trump on Sunday dismissed claims by Moscow that Kyiv had launched a drone at one of Russian president Vladimir Putin’s residences.

‘I don’t believe that strike happened,’ Trump said in response to a reporter’s question aboard Air Force One. Kyiv has also rejected the accusation.

Russia invaded Ukraine in February 2022, triggering a conflict that has killed tens, if not hundreds, of thousands, devastated eastern Ukraine and forced millions to flee their homes.

Putin has vowed to press on with his military campaign if his hard-line demands are not met at the negotiating table.

Russia in 2025 gained the most ground on the battlefield since the first year of its offensive, according to AFP analysis.

title: Malaysia mulls 10-year term limit for PM
body:
Malaysia’s Anwar Ibrahim said Monday he would introduce legislation this year to limit the prime minister’s term to a maximum 10 years, fulfilling one of his campaign promises.

Speaking to ministers and civil servants after a cabinet meeting, Anwar cautioned against clinging to power and reminded them that ‘everyone has a term limit’ without exception.

‘We will table a bill to limit the term of the prime minister, not exceeding 10 years or two full terms,’ Anwar said in a special New Year’s announcement.

After serving the term, ‘it is better for us to hand it over to the next generation’, he added.

There is currently no term limit and former prime minister Mahathir Mohamad was in power for 22 years during his first tenure until he stepped down in 2003.

Mahathir then came out of retirement to lead a disparate opposition coalition that ousted the graft-tainted government of then prime minister Najib Razak in the 2018 elections.

He became world’s oldest serving prime minister when he was sworn in again as Malaysia’s leader at age 92 that year.

Anwar did not say when the term limits bill would be filed. Parliament will hold its first session of the year this month.

Anwar’s Pakatan Harapan (Alliance of Hope) coalition pledged in its 2022 election manifesto to limit the prime minister’s tenure to two terms.

Separately, Anwar announced the government would also introduce a freedom of information bill in parliament, along with legislation to set up the office of an ombudsman to strengthen the fight against corruption.

‘The ombudsman allows the people to raise any issues because without exception, from the prime minister downwards, everyone must be accountable and open to be questioned,’ Anwar said.

Last month, Malaysia’s High Court sentenced ex-premier Najib to 15 more years in jail after convicting him of abuse of power and money laundering in the 1MDB sovereign wealth fund graft scandal.

The additional years will run after Najib, 72, serves a current six-year jail term in a case related to the now defunct 1MDB.

title: Myanmar pro-military party wins first phase of election
body:
Myanmar’s dominant pro-military party won the first phase of junta-run elections, the last released official results showed on Monday, with the USDP taking nearly 90 per cent of lower house seats.

The military staged a 2021 coup that ousted the democratic government of Aung San Suu Kyi, but is overseeing a month-long phased election it pledges will return power to the people.

Western diplomats and democracy advocates dismiss the poll as a ploy to rebrand military rule, citing Suu Kyi’s jailing, her party’s dissolution, a crackdown on dissenters and a ballot stacked with military allies.

The pro-military Union Solidarity and Development Party won 89 of 102 lower house seats included in the first phase, according to an AFP tally of official results released from Friday to Monday.

The USDP win equates to more than 87 per cent of lower house seats included in the first phase of voting on December 28 — the remainder mostly won by a smattering of parties representing ethnic minorities.

Many analysts and democracy watchdogs describe the USDP as a proxy of the military, citing the large numbers of retired officers serving in senior positions.

Overall results are due after the vote’s third and final phase scheduled for January 25.

Regardless of the vote, a quarter of lower house seats and key cabinet positions will be reserved for members of the armed forces under the terms of the country’s military-drafted constitution.

The USDP was trounced by Suu Kyi’s National League for Democracy party in the last elections in 2020 before the military overturned the vote, alleging widespread fraud and staging a coup.

Suu Kyi, 80, remains jailed incommunicado and the NLD is not appearing on ballots.

The military coup sparked a civil war as pro-democracy protesters formed guerrilla units to fight alongside ethnic minority armed groups which have long resisted central rule.

Rebel factions have pledged to block the vote from the enclaves they control, and the junta has admitted the vote cannot be held nationwide, but is waging offensives in a bid to claw back ground.

title: AUB celebrates 30th founding anniversary
body:
Asian University of Bangladesh inaugurated its two-month-long programme, celebrating its 30th founding anniversary, on the AUB’s permanent campus at Ashulia in Dhaka on Sunday.

Dhaka University vice-chancellor Professor Niaz Ahmed Khan was present as chief guest at the inaugural ceremony, said a press release on Monday.

Also present were founder vice-chancellor and chairman of the board of trustees of AUB Professor Abul Hasan Muhammad Sadeq and vice-chancellor of the university professor emeritus Shahjahan Khan.

Niaz Ahmed Khan remarked that Asian University of Bangladesh was established in 1996 with the vision of expanding higher education beyond urban centres and producing skilled, ethical human resources.

‘After 30 years, that journey has reached a proud milestone. This is indeed a day of honour and achievement. We owe our gratitude to the visionary who founded this institution,’ he said.

Special guest Mahmudur Rahman, editor of Daily Amar Desh, highlighted the AUB’s inspiring journey, stating that for three decades the university had consistently continued its academic activities and contributed ethically grounded graduates to the nation.

Professor Abul Quasem Fazlul Huq, president of Bangla Academy, described AUB as a ‘beacon of higher education’ and expressed his expectation that the university’s light would continue to spread far and wide, enhancing its reputation nationally and internationally.

Professor Abul Hasan Muhammad Sadeq stated that the university had been conducting its academic programmes with globally aligned syllabi and curricula.

Noting that the AUB is now preparing comprehensively to secure a position in international rankings, he said, ‘Over the past 30 years, we have gifted the nation competent graduates enriched with knowledge and ethical values. This commitment will continue.’

Shahjahan Khan emphasised that AUB operated with the guiding principle of providing quality higher education at an affordable cost.

He reiterated the university’s mission to develop honest, skilled, and competent human resources and expressed confidence that AUB would stand tall on the global stage in the future.

To commemorate the milestone anniversary, the university conferred the AUB Founder Award 2026 on three distinguished personalities in recognition of their outstanding professional excellence, ethical leadership and contributions to society.

The awardees were Abul Quasem Fazlul Huq, Niaz Ahmed Khan and Mahmudur Rahman.

The programme was jointly conducted by Mukhtasha Dina Chowdhury, head of the department of business administration and Hizbunnahar Tania, lecturer, department of social work.

title: 11 airguns recovered in Moulvibazar
body:
The members of the Rapid Action Battalion recovered 11 airguns from a bush of a tea garden under Shrimangal upazila in Moulvibazar on Sunday night.

RAB-9 media officer KM Shahidul Islam Sohag said that a team of the battalion, acting on secret information, conducted a drive at Satgaon of Satgaon Tea Garden under the upazila at around 8:00pm on Sunday.

At that time, they found 11 airguns wrapped with two sacks from a bush near the Cha-Kanya Sculpture of the Satgaon Tea Garden, the RAB officer said.

He said that they seized the abandoned airguns and handed them over to Shrimangal police after filing a general diary in this connection.

He said that no one was arrested in this connection.

title: Blankets distributed among Rakhine community in Patuakhali
body:
Amid severe cold and dense fog, the Kalapara upazila administration has extended humanitarian assistance by distributing blankets to the Rakhine community to help them survive the harsh winter.

At around 10:00pm on Sunday, approximately 700 blankets were distributed at eight key locations across Kuakata.

In addition, officials personally visited Amkhlapara, Mistripara and nearby Rakhine villages, where around 100 Rakhine men and women received blankets directly.

Kalapara upazila nirbahi officer Kausar Hamid; assistant commissioner, land, Yasin Sadek; and CPP assistant director Asaduzzaman; among others, were present during the distribution.

Speaking on the occasion, UNO Kausar Hamid said that marginalised and minority communities suffer the most during the winter season.

‘It is the government’s humanitarian responsibility to stand beside cold-stricken people, including the Rakhine community,’ he said, adding that the winter assistance programme would continue throughout the season.

Members of the Rakhine community expressed gratitude to the administration for the timely support, saying that the blankets provided much-needed relief during the ongoing cold wave.

title: Artefactum’s inaugural exhibition under way at Banani
body:
A newly formed contemporary art gallery, Artefactum, organises their maiden group art exhibition titled Artefactum Inaugural Exhibition, which is under way at M & S House at Banani in the capital.

Curated by Artefactum’s gallerist, Rumana Habib, the five-week exhibition, inaugurated on December 12, displayed 23 seasoned and contemporary artist’s artworks depicting nature, urban architecture and landscape, meditative feels with serenity of surrounding.

A total of 56 artworks, mostly mixed media paintings with prints, photographs, watercolour, terracotta, sculptures, jewelleries and handbags, were inspired from traditional textile design of Bangladesh at the exhibition.

Prominent artists including Jamal Ahmed, Kanak Chanpa Chakma, Kuhu Plamondon, Rokeya Sultana, Vinita Karim and Anisuzzaman displayed their artworks at the venue.

Contemporary and young artists including Aidha Cader, Dipu Sadik, Farzana Rahman Bobby, Fazeela Morshed, Imran Hasan, Jolock Saha, Tasmina Khan Majles and Tayabuzzaman Khan also participated in the first exhibition of the gallery which shared the space with KOA, a serene yoga and meditation centre at Banani.

‘Curating concept of the exhibition was inspired by the space, a wellness centre. We selected pieces that felt meditative and immersive, and could bring people along on an inner journey as they walk through the exhibition,’ said Rumana Habib, adding that the gallery aims to be a hub of artists and art lovers of diverse mediums and genres.

Anisuzzaman’s woodcut on paper titled Embrace Friendship – 9 showed two oval-shaped canvases which depicted the autumn of Bangladesh and Japan.

Farzana Rahman Bobby’s mixed media on handmade paper titled Labyrinth shows multiple circles overlapped with each other which created meditative forms.

Aidha Cader’s gouache on Fabriano paper and sealed with gloss finish artwork titled The Mingling of the Two Oceans, a composition constructed with traditional Turkish forms and colours symbolise mughal architectures at the Indian subcontinent.

Fazeela Morshed’s photograph titled Reflections shows trees reflecting on water at the walkway of a street.

title: CU day care centre gets playground
body:
A playground for children at the Chittagong University Day Care Centre was inaugurated by the CU vice-chancellor Professor Muhammad Yahya Akhter on Monday.

Pro-vice-chancellor (academic and administration) Professor Md Kamal Uddin was present at the time, said a .

The vice-chancellor visited the day care centre. He said that arrangements have been made to provide services through the day care center for the convenience of female teachers, students, and officials and employees. The playground has been prepared for the children.

Professor Salma Momtaz, director of the day care center, Moushumi Jahan Meri, in-charge of the day care center, and other officials and employees were also present.

title: Udichi remembers Satyen Sen
body:
Bangladesh Udichi Shilpigosthi remembered its founder, Satyen Sen, at a programme marking his 45th death anniversary at the capital’s Topkhana road on Monday.

The event, chaired by Udichi acting president Habibul Alam, consisted of a discussion session, songs and recitations.

In the discussion, general secretary of Udichi, Jamshed Anwer Tapan condemned government failure to prevent mob violence, and attacks on newspapers, cultural organisations and events.

He also condemned the capture of Venezuela’s president Nicolas Maduro and his wife by the USA.

Satyen Sen was born on March 28, 1907 at Tangibari in Munshiganj of British India. His father was Darinimohan Sen.

He passed the entrance examination in 1924, went to Kolkata and got involved in leftist movement.

He received Adamjee Literary Award in 1969, Bangla Academy Literary Award in 1970 and Ekushey Padak posthumously in 1986.

title: VDP’s role as strong pillar of public defence hailed
body:
The Village Defence Party, a key pillar of Bangladesh Ansar and Village Defence Force, on Monday celebrated its 50th founding anniversary with great enthusiasm and colour at the Bangladesh Ansar and VDP Academy at Safipur in Gazipur.

Director general of Bangladesh Ansar and VDP Major General Abdul Motaleb Sazzad Mahmud attended the programme as the chief guest and delivered the welcome address.

Extending warm greetings to all members, officers, and employees, he highlighted the proud history, present contributions, and future prospects of the VDP.

‘The journey that began with the goal of maintaining peace and order in villages and cities has now transformed into a vast volunteer force of nearly six million members,’ he said, congratulating all concerned on the historic occasion.

Describing VDP as a strong pillar of public defense, the DG said volunteer members play a vital role at the grassroots level by assisting law enforcement, preventing social crimes, curbing child marriage and drug abuse, empowering women, ensuring security during elections and religious festivals, and contributing to disaster management, rescue operations, and humanitarian assistance.

He also emphasized the economic potential of VDP members, noting that under the ‘Sanjivan’ project of the Ansar-VDP Development Bank, members will receive modern, job-oriented training and easy access to loans to become entrepreneurs in agriculture, fisheries, and cottage industries.

This initiative aims to promote self-reliance and strengthen the grassroots economy, he also said.

The DG further informed that initiatives are underway, through memorandums of understanding with the Department of Youth Development, BITAC, and Sohoj.com, to transform VDP and TDP members into skilled manpower for both domestic and overseas employment.

He added that the ‘Sanjivan’ project has already been launched on a trial basis in 12 upazilas across 12 districts.

Highlighting ongoing reforms, he said all VDP members are being included in the digital database AVMIS to ensure transparency and effective deployment, alongside modern training modules to build a disciplined, skilled, and patriotic force.

Calling for unity and dedication, he urged all members to work together with courage, discipline, and patriotism to further strengthen VDP for the future peace, security, and development of Bangladesh.

The jubilee celebration featured the release of pigeons symbolizing peace, cake cutting, and a colorful rally.

Senior officials, including the additional director general, deputy directors general, officers, employees, and a large number of VDP members, were present at the event.

title: Cropland shrinks in Rajshahi
body:
Fertile cropland in Rajshahi is rapidly disappearing as commercial fish ponds and concrete structures expand unchecked, raising serious concerns about food security, soil degradation, and sustainable land use amid weak regulatory oversight.

Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics data reveal that Rajshahi district lost 16,159 hectares of net cropped area between 2015 and 2023.

During the same period, inland water bodies expanded sharply, while built-up areas including housing, roads, and commercial structures also increased, permanently removing large tracts of cultivable land from agriculture.

Inland water areas rose to 24,498 hectares in 2023 from 15,044 hectares in 2015 while built-up areas increased to 62,727 hectares in 2023 from 54,233 hectares in 2015.

Government officials and farmers said that much of the lost high-yield arable land across Rajshahi has been converted into commercial fish ponds, often in violation of soil conservation guidelines and the Agricultural Land Protection and Land Use Act 2018.

According to the district fisheries office, the number of ponds in Rajshahi increased from 40,788 in 2015 to 51,275 in 2025 – a rise of about 25 per cent in a decade.

Farmers and non-governmental organisation officials, however, alleged that the actual figure could be significantly higher as there were a huge number of unregistered and illegal ponds in the district.

In the past fiscal year, Rajshahi produced 84,803 tonnes of fish against a local demand of 52,063 tonnes, underscoring the massive scale of aquaculture expansion.

Officials of the Department of Agricultural Extension, along with farmers and landowners, attribute the shift largely to economic compulsions, as commercial aquaculture offers faster and significantly higher returns than traditional crops like boro rice.

‘From rice cultivation, I can hardly earn Tk 40,000 a year. But leasing the same land for a commercial pond brings Tk 80,000 to Tk 1.2 lakh annually,’ said a farmer in Godagari upazila, requesting anonymity.

A pond owner who recently excavated a pond on 40 bighas of arable land in Godagari said that profits from fish farming were several times higher than those from crop production.

Under existing regulations, pond excavation on cropland requires prior approval from the deputy commissioner’s office following verification by the Upazila agriculture officer and the Soil Resource Development Institute to ensure that the land is not highly fertile.

However, such procedures are frequently bypassed. Excavation often takes place at night to avoid detection, while small-scale farmers claimed that they were sometimes not informed before ponds were dug on their land.

Farmers alleged that the existence of powerful syndicates with political backing facilitates illegal pond excavation for profit.

‘Before the August 5, 2024 political changeover, the Awami League and Juba League activists used to control these syndicates. Now leaders linked to the Bangladesh Nationalist Party and its youth and student wings are involved,’ said a DAE official, seeking anonymity.

BNP Rajshahi district unit member secretary Bishwanath Sarkar, however, said that none had so far complained to them in this connection. ‘We will take action if we get any specific allegation.’

The DAE official added that illegal pond excavation has surged in recent years in the region, particularly in Natore, Naogaon, and Chapainawabganj, while Rajshahi has experienced a steady rise over a longer period.

He noted that fish traders from Rajshahi were increasingly shifting operations to neighbouring districts where land lease costs were much lower.

Resistance to illegal pond excavation has at times turned violent.

On December 17, Ahmed Jubayer, 22, a farmer of Baro Palsha village under Mohanpur upazila, was crushed to death by an excavator while protesting against illegal pond digging at midnight.

‘Most of us are marginal farmers. If ponds are dug in the middle of a beel, surrounding fields become waterlogged and cultivation becomes impossible,’ said Joynal Abedin, another farmer of the village.

Agricultural experts warned that indiscriminate pond excavation removes fertile topsoil and spreads infertile subsoil over adjoining land, rendering fields unsuitable for cultivation even if farming later resumes.

Unplanned digging also disrupts natural drainage, alters the local microclimate, and increases crop disease risks.

‘While profitable for a few in the short term, converting arable land into ponds affects food production, farmers’ livelihoods, and long-term food security,’ said Professor Mohammad Al Baqui Barkotulla of Rajshahi University.

Deputy commissioner and district magistrate Afia Akhtar said that pond excavation required approval following reports from an upazila-level committee comprising agriculture and fisheries officials.

‘In illegal cases, this procedure is not followed,’ she said, adding that they regularly conduct mobile courts and nighttime drives.

She, however, could not immediately provide statistics on cases filed in this connection.

Agricultural economists warn that Rajshahi risks facing a paradox of importing staple food while exporting fish, a scenario with serious long-term consequences for national food security, if strict enforcement of land-use laws is not ensured.

title: Mild cold wave sweeps Rajshahi div, 4 districts
body:
A mild cold wave is sweeping over Rajshahi division along with four other districts—Dinajpur, Jashore, Chuadanga and Kushtia—and will continue today, according to the Bangladesh Meteorological Department.

A BMD bulletin issued on Monday evening said that air navigation, inland river transport and road communication might be disrupted at places until noon today due to thick fog.

On Monday, BMD’s Ishwardi station in Pabna recorded the lowest temperature at 8.4C, while the highest temperature of 26.6C was recorded in Teknaf of Cox’s Bazar.

The forecast for today said that day temperatures might remain nearly unchanged, while night temperatures might fall slightly across the country.

A New Age correspondent in Pabna reported that the biting cold seriously disrupted life and livelihood of people, in particular low-income families, those living along the banks of the Padma River and floating and uprooted communities.

As the mercury fell, visibility was reduced due to dense fog since morning, disrupting vehicular movement on roads and highways.

To escape the intense cold, homeless people living on sidewalks, in the yards of Ishwardi railway junction and in the open were seen burning straw and garbage to keep warm.

Many daily wage earners were living in inhumane conditions as work became scarce in the harsh weather.

Mohammad Ajibar, an elderly homeless man staying in front of the railway booking office, said, ‘I have received blankets, but it’s too thin to keep me warm. I cannot sleep properly; I spend the night sitting and shivering.’

Rehena Akhter, a resident of Kamalpur char in Ishwardi upazila, said that the severely chilled air made her sick.

It had become difficult to run her family as she could not go to work because of the severe cold.

Nazmul Haque Ranjan, an observer at the Ishwardi Meteorological Office, said that the lack of sunlight and the cold wind have made the winter even more intense.

title: Bangladeshi youth dies in BSF custody
body:
A 35-year-old Bangladeshi man died after he was detained by the Indian Border Security Force near the Jahurpurtek border under sadar upazila in Chapainawabganj on Sunday.

The deceased is Rabiul Islam, son of Ejabur Rahman of Satrashia village under Narayanpur union of the upazila.

The victim’s family alleged that Rabiul was tortured to death by the members of the BSF.

Border Guard Bangladesh’s battalion-53 commander Lieutenant Colonel Kazi Mustafizur Rahman said that BSF members chased a group of five or six youths, including Rabiul, immediately after they had entered India illegally early Saturday.

He said that BSF members detained Rabiul, but his companions managed to flee, and the Indian border force took him to a BSF camp.

The BGB official said that their Indian counterpart, in a flag meeting with them on Sunday night, informed them that Rabiul became ill after detention and later died while being rushed to the hospital.

Rabiul’s mother Sefali Begum alleged that BSF members tortured his son to death.

‘Rabiul left home on Saturday afternoon in good health but did not return at night. In the morning, I was told that my son had been shot dead by the BSF. Later in the afternoon, we heard a different account that he had been beaten to death near the border. My son was tortured by the BSF,’ she said.

According to the human rights organisation Ain O Salish Kendra’s yearly human rights report, 34 Bangladeshis were killed by the BSF in 2025. Of them, 24 were killed in BSF firing, and 10 others died after facing physical torture by the BSF.

Apart from the killings in 2025, at least 38 Bangladeshis sustained bullet injuries or were tortured, and 14 Bangladeshis were abducted by the BSF. Of the abducted victims, only four were returned to Bangladesh, according to ASK.

The ASK data also showed that the number of border killings was 30 in 2024, 31 in 2023, 23 in 2022 and 18 in 2021.

title: Tarique vows to restore liberation war ideals
body:
Delegations of political alliances, parties meet him

Bangladesh Nationalist Party acting chair Tarique Rahman on Monday said that his party would work towards restoring the ideals of the 1971 Liberation War while drawing inspiration from the democratic movements of 1990 and the 2024 mass uprising.

He said that the BNP wanted an early democratic transition in the country, which could be achieved through the upcoming Jatiya Sangsad elections scheduled for February 12.

Tarique’s remarks came during separate meetings with delegations from the Ganatantrik Jukta Front, an alliance of seven political parties, Nagorik Oikya, Ganosamhati, and some other parties, which had visited him at the BNP Gulshan office to sign the condolence book for former BNP chair Khaleda Zia, who passed away on December 30.

Speaking to the delegations, Tarique outlined his vision for the country if the  BNP were voted to power, according to leaders who attended the meetings.

Tarique described the upcoming general elections as a crucial opportunity to ensure a genuine democratic transition in Bangladesh while upholding the nation’s historic struggles for liberty and democracy.

‘The upcoming election is a crucial opportunity to bring about a genuine democratic transition in Bangladesh,’ he said, highlighting his commitment to uphold the values of the nation’s historical struggles for freedom and democracy.

Tarique iterated that the BNP would focus on implementing policies that would revive the spirit of the Liberation War and strengthen democratic governance in the country, Jukta Front leaders told New Age after the meeting.

The Jukta Front delegation, led by Socialist Party of Bangladesh general secretary Bazlur Rashid Firoz, emerging from the meeting told New Age that they had urged Tarique Rahman for an early democratic transition of the country restoring the spirit of 1971, stopping current mob violence and repressions on women.

Former president of the Communist Party of Bangladesh Mujahidul Islam Selim, who was in a delegation, told New Age that Tarique had told them that he had a plan to restore the spirits of Liberation War and establish the rights of the people as well as to stop mob violence.

The delegations included CPB president Kazi Sazzad Zahir Chandan, general secretary Abdullah Al Kafi Ratan, SPB assistant general secretary Razequzzaman Ratan, Bangladesh Jasod general secretary Nazmul Haque Prodhan, standing committee member Mushtuq Husain, SPB (Marxist) coordinator Masud Rana.

Also included in the delegations were Democratic Revolutionary Party general secretary Mushrefa Mishu, Revolutionary Communist League general secretary Iqbal Kabir Jahid, central leader Abdus Satter and Bangladesher Samajtantrik Party executive president Abdul Ali.

Nagorik Oikya president Mahmudur Rahman Manna,  Ganosamhati Andolan chief coordinator Zonayed Saki, AB Party chairman Mojibur Rahman Monju,  and Labour Party  and Jamiat-e-Ulema Islam delegations also met Tarique Rahman after signing in the condolence book.

title: Cold, fog bite into Narail’s honey season
body:
A prolonged spell of severe cold and dense fog is wreaking havoc on honey farming in Narail, leaving local beekeepers struggling with mounting losses and uncertainty over this season’s production.

As winter tightens its grip on the region, honey cultivators are increasingly anxious, hoping for clearer skies and warmer days to safeguard their livelihoods. The district has endured several days of biting cold, coupled with thick fog that has disrupted not only daily life but also agricultural activity.

Honey production has been particularly hard hit, with bees reluctant to leave their hives to collect nectar from mustard fields.

During visits to mustard fields and beekeeping sites at Narail Sadar, hundreds of bee boxes were observed near blooming mustard crops. Yet there was little to no movement around them—a worrying sign for farmers who rely on this peak season for their honey harvest.

Beekeeper Md Shompi Sardar explained that daytime fog was preventing bees from leaving their boxes.

‘For good honey collection, fog at night and sunshine during the day are necessary. Now the fog lingers throughout the day, so the bees stay inside and cannot collect nectar,’ he said.

Md Inamul Haque added, ‘Due to the fog, very few bees come out of the boxes. As a result, they consume the honey already stored inside. This year, many bees are also dying due to excessive cold and fog.’

Meanwhile, Md Shahidul Islam expressed fears that honey production could decline sharply if the weather failed to improve.

‘If favourable weather returns in the coming days, the situation may improve. Otherwise, honey production will drop sharply this season,’ he warned.

Highlighting the wider impact of the adverse weather, Md Arifur Rahman, deputy director of the Department of Agriculture Extension in Narail, said that honey production has been disrupted by the unfavourable conditions.

‘Despite the challenges, we are hopeful that honey production may reach 10 tonnes or more this year,’ he added, noting that the department continued to provide technical support to beekeepers to ensure the production of pure honey.

With the region’s honey sector facing a delicate balance between weather and livelihood, farmers now await a change in the elements that could determine the season’s yield.

title: ACC prosecutes LGED engineer over Tk 37 lakh seizure
body:
The Anti-Corruption Commission on Sunday filed a case against an executive engineer of the Local Government Engineering Department and two others over the seizure of Tk 3,695,300 in cash in Natore.

ACC assistant director Md Ismail Hossain filed the case against Md Sabiul Islam, an executive engineer of LGED, Gaibandha, currently posted at the LGED headquarters in Dhaka, and two others with the ACC’s Rajshahi Integrated district office, said ACC lawyer Md. Bazle Towhid Al Hasan Babla.

The two other accused are Sabiul’s driver Bappi Kumar Das, 50, and his son Bistu Kumar Das, 20, residents of Gobindaganj municipality in Gaibandha.

He said that the case was filed under 8(2) and 8(3) of the Money Laundering Prevention Act, 2012, and section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947.

Earlier on March 14 last year, a team of the Natore district police detained Sabiul Islam at a checkpoint on the Natore-Bogura highway near Chalan Beel Gate under Singra at 1:00am while he was traveling to Rajshahi from Gaibandha by a private car.

After checking, the police then found Tk 36,94,300 hidden inside a black bag in the back of the vehicle.

According to the case statement, Sabiul, who was travelling in the back seat, identified the bag as his and claimed that it contained about Tk 20–30 lakh but failed to provide credible explanation regarding the source of the money.

On March 17, 2025, following a court order, the seized money was recounted at Sonali Bank PLC, Fulbagan branch, Natore, in the presence of a magistrate, where the total amount was confirmed as Tk 3,695,300.

The statement stated that neither the driver Bappi Kumar Das nor his son, who was also travelling in the same car, claimed ownership of the money at the time of seizure.

Following police correspondence, the ACC headquarters approved an inquiry on June 22, 2025.

During investigation, the commission found primary evidence that Sabiul Islam abused his official position to accumulate illicit assets and attempted to conceal and transfer the money using the private vehicle.

The ACC also found preliminary evidence that the two other accused assisted Shabiul Islam in concealing the offence and attempting to shield him from legal action.

title: Commission for disbanding RAB
body:
The Commission of Inquiry on Enforced Disappearances on Monday said that it had recommended disbanding the Rapid Action Battalion and reforming the intelligence agencies in its final report.

The commission chairperson, Justice Moyeenul Islam Chowdhury, made the remarks at a press conference held at the commission’s office in the capital’s Gulshan area.

He said that intelligence agencies, including the Directorate General of Forces Intelligence and the National Security Intelligence, required massive reforms.

‘We suggested reforms in the DGFI and the NSI so that they are not engaged in tasks such as bank and media house grabbing or interference in politics. This requires strong political will. We have submitted our recommendations to the interim government, which is non-political,’ Justice Moyeenul said while responding to a question about disbanding the DGFI like the RAB.

The country needs DGFI, but they need reforms, he said.

He said that the DGFI was involved in the Islami Bank grabbing for S Alam group during the Sheikh Hasina regime, which the commission did not want to occur again.

He said that the forces destroyed evidence and the commission asked the authorities not to destroy any evidence further.

‘Destruction of evidence is also a criminal offense,’ he said.

He said that they also recommended reconstituting the National Human Rights Commission.

‘If any human rights violation occurs, there will be no agency except the courts. The courts have 45,00,000 pending cases with only 2,000 judicial officers or judges,’ he said.

He said that Hummam Quader Chowdhury, son of executed Bangladesh Nationalist Party leader Salauddin Quader Chowdhury, was picked up by the Detective Branch of the police and was handed over to the DGFI.

‘We have visited 40 detention centres, including 22 or 23 run by the RAB. These centres have a lot of cells,’ said a commission member, Sazzad Hossain.

He said that they had also found such centres in DGFI, NSI, Dhaka Metropolitan Police’s Detective Branch, and the Counter Terrorism and Transnational Crime unit.

He also said that the RAB destroyed most of the evidence.

Addressing the press conference, the commission chair Justice Moyeenul said that the Bangladesh Army was not involved in enforced disappearances as a force, but many officers on deputation in intelligence agencies like DGFI and NSI from the army, the Bangladesh Navy and the Bangladesh Air Force were involved in such acts.

‘Army high-ups knew about the matter, but they had nothing to do as DGFI was under the defense ministry, overseen by the prime minister, and NSI under the prime minister’s office,’ he said.

Referring to two interim reports, the commission chair said that they had recommended legal action against responsible persons and organisations.

He said that they also recommended organisational reforms and to enact the Enforced Disappearance Prevention and Redress Ordinance, 2025, and the National Human Rights Commission Ordinance 2025 for stopping the recurrence of enforced disappearances.

He said that they also recommended disbanding the RAB, removing the armed forces from maintaining internal law and order, scrapping or fundamentally amending the Anti-Terrorism Act, scrapping clause 13 of the Armed Police Battalion Ordinance 2003, adopting a victim-centric justice system, and ensuring compensation and rehabilitation for victims.

He said that they also suggested transforming the detention centres, commonly known as ‘Aynaghar’, into museums.

Commission member Nur Khan Liton said that political parties should come forward to stand against enforced disappearance and extrajudicial crimes.

The commission in its final report submitted to chief adviser Muhammad Yunus on Sunday, revealed that it had found evidence that the ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina, her military adviser Tarique Ahmed Siddique, and former home minister Asaduzzaman Khan Kamal were directly involved in high-profile enforced disappearances.

The commission was formed by the interim government on August 27, 2024, to enquire into cases of enforced disappearances that occurred during the tenure of the Sheikh Hasina-led authoritarian Awami League regime that was ousted from power on August 5, 2024 amid a mass uprising.

‘A total of 1,913 complaints were filed with the commission. After intensive scrutiny, 231 were found to be duplicates. In many instances, the same case had been sent through multiple channels, for example, by email, courier, and in-person submission, or both an organisation and the affected individual had submitted separate complaints about the same incident, and left 1,682 unique complaints,’ the final report said.

After removing 231 duplicate files and 113 files of non-qualifying cases, the report said that they were left with 1,569 complaints involving potential enforced disappearance, which was about 82 per cent of all complaints.

‘Within these cases, 251 victims never returned and are presumed dead, while a further 36 bodies were recovered after periods of enforced disappearance, often following so-called ‘crossfire’ incidents or discovered in rivers with gunshot wounds,’ the report said.

It said that 287 deaths were plausibly associated with enforced disappearance.

Of the 1,569 potential enforced disappearance complaints,  a total of 1,282 people reappeared after varying periods in illegal custody, the report said.

According to the report, the commission found political identity of 946 reappeared victims, including 476 of Jamaat, 236 of Islami Chhatra Shibir, 142 of the BNP, 46 of Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal, and  17 of Jatiyatabadi Juba Dal.

Of the 253 missing victims, BNP and its affiliates together constitute roughly 68 per cent and Jamaat and Shibir account for roughly 22 per cent.

title: Appeals filed against 42 rejections
body:
Forty-three appeals were filed with the Election Commission on Monday, the first day of filing appeals, 42 challenging the cancellation of nomination papers and one contesting the acceptance of a nomination by returning officers.

Of the 42 appeals that challenged cancellations, the highest 15 were filed in the Dhaka region, followed by seven in Faridpur and five in Rajshahi.

Four appeals were filed in Cumilla, three each in Rangpur and Khulna, two in Chattogram, and one each in Barishal and Mymensingh.

The lone appeal contesting the acceptance of a nomination was submitted in the Cumilla region.

According to the election schedule, candidates as well as banks or financial  institutions can file appeals until January 9 against a returning officer’s decision to accept or reject a nomination.

A total of 2,568 nomination papers were submitted for the 13th Jatiya Sangsad elections, of which 1,842 were declared valid after the scrutiny.

Three nomination papers had been submitted for former prime minister and BNP chair Khaleda Zia for the Feni-1, Bogura-7, and Dinajpur-3 JS constituencies.

However, following her death on December 30, the EC said that those nominations were not taken up for scrutiny.

The EC data show that nomination papers of the highest number of independent candidates – 338 – were rejected during the scrutiny.

Among the political parties, the Jatiya Party accounted for the largest number -- 59 -- of rejected nominations, followed by Islami Andolan Bangladesh with 39 nominations.

The BNP and the Communist Party of Bangladesh each saw 25 nomination papers rejected.

The Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami had 10 nominations rejected, while three candidates from the National Citizen Party were disqualified.

Chief election commissioner AMM Nasir Uddin on Monday visited the appeals submission booth at the Agargaon EC headquarters in Dhaka and told reporters that the overall election environment remained satisfactory.

He expressed the optimism that a credible election could be delivered with cooperation from all stakeholders, adding that the election process was progressing smoothly so far.

‘The current election environment and situation are satisfactory. With cooperation from all concerned, it will be possible to deliver a free, fair and credible election,’ the CEC said.

His inspection coincided with the start of the appeal process against decisions taken by returning officers.

According to the relevant EC rule, each appeal must be submitted in the form of a memorandum, accompanied by one set of original documents and six sets of photocopies.

The appeal hearings would be conducted in phases at the EC auditorium at Agargaon, beginning on January 10.

The hearings are scheduled to run daily from 10:00am in January 10- 8, though the timeframe may be adjusted depending on the number of appeals received.

During the hearings, the returning officers concerned or their representatives, along with the appellant, would be required to be present with all relevant documents.

Among the independent candidates, former NCP leader Tasnim Jara on Monday filed an appeal with the EC, challenging the rejection of her nomination paper for the Dhaka-9 constituency.

Speaking to reporters, Jara said that around 5,000 voters had voluntarily gave their signatures in her support within a short time and many had worked as volunteers at her booths.

‘Out of respect for them, I will continue this legal fight,’ she said, adding that her supporters wanted her to contest the election.

According to the EC, her nomination was cancelled due to discrepancies in the addresses of two supporting voters.

Under electoral rules, independent candidates are required to submit signatures from at least 1 per cent of the total registered voters in their constituency.

As part of the verification process, the EC randomly selected 10 voters from the list of supporting electors submitted by Jara for scrutiny.

While eight of the 10 randomly selected voters were verified, two were found not to be registered voters of Dhaka-9.

Meanwhile, regarding the allegations of obstruction and harassment involving independent candidates in different areas, EC senior secretary Akhtar Ahmed said that he had not received any official complaints.

‘We have not heard about it. If there have been any irregularities, the returning officers will look into it,’ he said.

Responding to questions about complaints from several independent candidates who claimed that they were assaulted while collecting supporter signatures and were feeling insecure, the EC secretary iterated that no such reports had formally reached him.

He said that any aggrieved person had the right to seek redress through the appeal process.

When asked specifically about allegations that an independent candidate had been attacked at the returning officer’s office in Manikganj, Akhtar Ahmed said that such matters fell under the jurisdiction of the returning officer concerned.

On Sunday, allegations emerged that independent candidate and BNP leader Ataur Rahman Ata for the Manikganj-3 constituency had been harassed at the office of the Manikganj returning officer and district administration.

title: At least 7 billionaires in election race
body:
At least seven billionaire candidates have entered the race of the 13th Jatiya Sangsad elections scheduled for February 12, a fact which shows a growing presence of ultra-wealthy individuals in the parliamentary politics.

Election affidavits submitted to the Election Commission in primary scrutiny show that these candidates together control thousands of crores of taka in assets, including business empires, real estate, financial investments, and industrial ventures, making wealth an increasingly visible factor in the country’s electoral landscape.

Bangladesh Nationalist Party vice-chair and former Federation of Bangladesh Chambers of Commerce and Industry president Abdul Awal Mintoo has emerged as one of the wealthiest candidates in the election as his assets are worth Tk 507.80 crore.

Mintoo, who is contesting for the Feni-3 constituency, disclosed that his immovable properties were valued at Tk 333.09 crore, while his movable assets amounted to Tk 174.71 crore.

In the past financial year, Mintoo reported a domestic annual income of Tk 1.50 crore with no income from abroad.

His affidavit also notes that although he had been a citizen of the United States, he renounced the citizenship on December 9, 2025 ahead of the election.

According to the wealth profile that extends to his family as well, his wife Nasrin Fatema Awal, identified as a businessperson, declared assets worth Tk 99.24 crore, including Tk 24.67 crore in immovable property and Tk 74.57 crore in movable assets.

Under jewellery category, Mintoo showed Tk 2 lakh worth of ornaments in his own name, while his wife declared Tk 48.40 lakh.

According to tax records, the couple’s eldest son  Tabith Awal declared assets of Tk 59.42 crore, second son Tafsir Mohammad Awal reported assets worth Tk 49.32 crore and youngest son Tajwar Mohammad Awal declared assets valued at Tk 26.18 crore.

Independent candidate Syed AK Ekramuzzaman, contesting for the Brahmanbaria-1 (Nasirnagar) seat, emerged as another of the wealthiest candidates with assets worth Tk 494 crore.

Ekramuzzaman, managing director of RAK Ceramics, declared his movable assets worth Tk 411.29 crore, including Tk 37.07 lakh in bank deposits, and Tk 314.21 crore in shares.

His immovable properties worth Tk 82.99 crore, including agricultural land worth Tk 5.04 crore, non-agricultural land worth Tk 11.07 crore, and buildings worth Tk 46.22 crore in Dhaka, Chattogram, and Sylhet and a house in the capital’s Uttara valued at Tk 10.02 crore.

His immovable assets also include three luxury flats in Dubai’s Burj Khalifa, Palm Jumeirah, and Marssa.

Ekramuzzaman, also a former BNP leader, is now earing annually Tk 4.46 crore, including Tk 1.16 crore as house rents and Tk 63.81 lakh from businesses.

His wife Naima Akter Jahan owns movable assets worth Tk 2.13 crore and immovable assets worth Tk 2.33 crore.

The couple’s son Sailin Jahan Akbar owns assets worth Tk 11.31 crore and another son Kamar Uz Zaman’s assest worth Tk 40.71 crore.

Ekramuzzaman, who previously contested several elections as a BNP candidate, served as an adviser to former BNP chair Khaleda Zia before being expelled from the party.

He joined the Awami League in 2024 but reportedly resigned shortly after being appointed as an adviser to the party’s Brahmanbaria district committee.

BNP-nominated candidate and party chair’s adviser Mohammad Aslam Chowdhury, contesting the Chattogram-4 constituency, declared his assets worth Tk 456.95 crore.

Aslam’s movable assets are worth Tk 26.16 crore, including cash of Tk 11.35 crore, firearms, and valuables while his immovable wealth is worth Tk 430.78 crore. He, however, has a huge amount of loans.

His primary source of income has been mentioned as business, generating an annual income of Tk 48.37 lakh.

His earnings from shares and bonds are minimal at Tk 5,341, while bank deposits total Tk 1.23 lakh, and foreign currency holdings Tk 62,500.

His businesswoman wife Jamila Naznin Mawla has a yearly income of Tk 6.13 lakh, with movable assets of Tk 12.32 crore and immovable assets worth Tk 6.1091 crore.

Their only daughter Meherin Anhar Uzma earns Tk 9.08 lakh annually, with movable assets worth Tk 4.6632 crore and no immovable property.

Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami-nominated candidate Md Enayat Ullah for the Dhaka-7 constituency is also a wealthy candidate with assets worth Tk 115 crore.

The ‘self-educated’ businessman Enayat Ullah’s movable assets are worth Tk 92.23 crore, including cash worth Tk 45,68,500, bank deposits Tk 7,11,24,454, bonds, loan securities, and shares of Tk 77,22,79,675, savings certificates and fixed deposits of Tk 7,05,00,000, jewelry  of Tk 5,000, and three firearms.

Enayat Ullah’s immovable assets are valued at Tk 23.72 crore, including agricultural land and buildings and non-agricultural land.

Enayat Ullah has two wives, Mosammat Shahnaz Ullah and Raihana Enayet. In his latest income tax return, Enayat Ullah declared assets in his name at Tk 108,77,80,999, and under the names of two wives Tk 1,73,60,322 and Tk20,70,000 respectively and children Tk 7,37,10,154.

Another BNP-nominated candidate Mahmud Hasan Khan for Chuadanga-2 constituency is also one of the wealthiest candidates, with assets worth nearly Tk 100 crore.

According to his affidavit, Mahmud Hasan’s total assets stand at Tk 99.13 crore where Tk 87,00,00,000 accounts for movable assets and Tk 12,10,00,000 for immovable assets.

Among his movable assets, he has Tk 4,00,000 in cash, Tk 1,50,000 in bank deposits, and investments in bonds, securities, and stock market investment worth Tk 86,00,000.

His immovable assets include nearly three and a half acres of agricultural land valued at Tk 48,43,000, buildings on 42 decimals of that land worth Tk 11,50,00,000, and a 625-square-foot apartment valued at Tk 3,46,662.

Mahmud Hasan Khan, also the president of the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association and managing director of Rising Group, declared annual income of Tk 4,83,77,000.

His wife and Rising Group chair Nargis Akter has an annual income of Tk 29,37,000 and she owns assets worth Tk 16,85,00,000. Of these, movable assets account for Tk 16,39,00,000, while immovable assets total Tk 45,57,000.

Emdadul Haque Bharosha, son of the late Rahim Uddin Bharosha, a distinguished industrialist and former BNP lawmaker, is set to contest for the Rangpur-4 constituency and is another of the wealthiest candidates.

Emdadul, a businessman by profession, declared an annual income of Tk 2,00,67,542, immovable  assets worth Tk 60.66 crore, including 58,65,987 in cash, 7.41 acres of agricultural land, 16.68 acres of non-agricultural land, a commercial building, and 11 apartments.

Emdadul’s movable assets are worth Tk 36.83 crore while his wife Selina Jahan owns movable assets worth Tk 5.09 crore.

Emdadul first contested the controversial 11th parliamentary election in 2018 for Rangpur-4.

BNP standing committee member and party candidate Mirza Abbas Uddin Ahmed (Mirza Abbas) for Dhaka-8 constituency is another wealthiest candidate with his and his family’s assets worth Tk 180.51 crore.

Abbas who was former four times lawmaker and a past mayor of the undivided Dhaka City Corporation, disclosed his movable assets worth Tk 70.35 crore.

Regarding immovable property, Abbas reported an acquisition value of Tk 3.75 crore, but left the current market value listed as ‘unknown’.

Abbas’s movable assets include cash of Tk 2.51 crore, foreign currency equivalent to USD 102,875, bank deposits of Tk 71,43,000, savings certificates and fixed deposits worth Tk 3.36 crore, investments in Dhaka Bank shares totaling Tk 51.79 crore  and additional capital market holdings of Tk 6,55,93,000.

Abbas’ wealth extends to his family as well. His wife Afroza Abbas, also president of BNP-affiliated Jatiytabadi Mohila Dal, holds assets worth Tk 36.90 crore.

The couple’s son Mirza Yasir Abbas has assets of Tk 66.64 crore and their daughter Nabila Mirza owns assets worth Tk 6.62 crore.

Transparency International Bangladesh executive director Iftekharuzzaman told New Age that the reliability, completeness and credibility of the election affidavit data on income and wealth has always been doubtful and debatable.

‘The Election Commission could raise questions of validity of candidacy, the NBR could check possible tax evasions while the ACC could investigate possible corrupt practices of owning wealth and income beyond legitimate means,’ he added.

title: Pvt sector credit growth edges up in Nov
body:
Private sector credit growth in Bangladesh edged up to 6.58 per cent in November 2025, driven largely by a rise in loan rescheduling and restructuring ahead of the upcoming national election, rather than fresh lending to businesses.

Bankers said that many companies remained reluctant to take new loans as the business environment has yet to stabilise.

Most investors are adopting a wait-and-see approach until the national election, scheduled for February 12, is held, amid lingering political and economic uncertainty.

The recent uptick in credit growth reflects a surge in loan rescheduling and renewal, particularly by election candidates and business groups seeking to clear their default status, which is a legal requirement for participating in the polls, BB officials said.

As a result, outstanding loan figures rose on paper, pushing up overall private sector credit growth in November, they said.

Despite the marginal improvement, credit expansion remains weak and well below the central bank’s expectations, they said.

The Bangladesh Bank had set a private sector credit growth target of 9.8 per cent for the July-December 2025 period, but actual growth has fallen far short of that goal, underscoring the depth of the slowdown, they added.

Bangladesh Bank data showed that credit growth had been sliding for months. It stood at 6.23 per cent in October 2025, 6.29 per cent in September, 6.35 per cent in August and 6.52 per cent in July.

The downward trend extends further back, with growth at 6.40 per cent in June 2025, 7.17 per cent in May and 7.5 per cent in April.

The decline began early in 2024 and intensified after the political transition following the fall of the Awami League government in August last year.

Economists warned that a prolonged credit slowdown could weaken industrial output, curb private investment and delay job recovery.

With limited access to new financing, many businesses are postponing expansion plans and scaling back operations.

Liquidity shortages, rising defaults and weak depositor confidence have constrained their balance sheets.

Non-performing loans climbed to a record Tk 6.44 lakh crore at the end of September 2025, accounting for about one-third of total loans in the system.

The impact of weak credit growth is already visible across the economy. Imports of capital machinery have declined, slowing industrial expansion.

Reduced investment has weakened money circulation, while many factories are operating below capacity. Consumer spending remains subdued and entrepreneurs are hesitant to borrow amid market volatility and political uncertainty.

High lending rates have added to the pressure. The Bangladesh Bank raised its policy rate to 10 per cent to rein in inflation, pushing commercial lending rates close to 15 per cent.

Bankers said that such borrowing costs had discouraged many potential borrowers, particularly small and medium enterprises.

title: ACC files graft case against former railway official
body:
The Anti-Corruption Commission on Monday filed a graft case against a former Bangladesh Railway official on charges of fraud and bribery for allegedly collecting Tk 6.5 crore from jobseekers by promising them employment in the railway.

ACC assistant director Md Amir Hossain lodged the case with the commission’s integrated district office in Rajshahi under Sections 420 and 162 of the Penal Code, 1860, and Section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947.

The accused, Syed Abzurul Haque, served under the office of the chief mechanical engineer (east) of Bangladesh Railway in Chattogram and is currently on post-retirement leave.

Amir Hossain told New Age that the accused abused his official position to influence the recruitment process for Khalasi posts during the Bangladesh Railway recruitment drives conducted in 2013 and 2015.

According to the case documents, Md Wali Khan of Sagarpara in Rajshahi city filed a complaint with the Rajshahi Metropolitan Senior Special Judge’s Court on September 6, 2021, alleging that Syed Abzurul Haque collected Tk 65 lakh from multiple jobseekers by falsely promising them railway appointments.

Following the complaint, the court ordered an investigation and forwarded the relevant documents to the ACC. Formal approval for the inquiry was later granted by the ACC headquarters in July 2023.

The ACC during its inquiry found that Bangladesh Railway issued circulars in 2013 and 2015 to recruit a total of 865 Khalasis.

Taking advantage of the recruitment process, the accused allegedly received Tk 30 lakh through multiple courier transactions sent via SA Paribahan’s Chattogram branch between March 2017 and May 2018. The funds were sent from Rajshahi using mobile numbers registered in the complainant’s name.

The ACC inquiry also verified the complaints by scrutinising ownership of phone numbers and call details with the assistance from the Bangladesh Telecommunication Regulatory Commission, Grameenphone and National Telecommunication Monitoring Centre.

The ACC inquiry also found Abzurul Haque received Tk 35 lakh more in cash from Wali Khan.

According to its inquiry, the accused had acknowledged receiving the money through at least two notarised declarations in July 2019 and March 2022.

In these documents, the accused admitted to receiving total Tk 65 lakh from the complainant—Tk 30 lakh through courier services and Tk 35 lakh in cash.

The ACC official said that prima facie evidence suggested that Syed Abzurul Haque abused his position as a public servant, accepted illegal gratification and engaged in criminal misconduct by falsely promising jobs.

title: Taxpayers now allowed to digitise returns
body:
The National Board of Revenue has taken a special initiative to digitise all value-added tax paper returns by introducing a new sub-module under the e-VAT System.

To facilitate the entry of all monthly VAT returns that were previously submitted in hard copy format into the online system, NBR introduced a new sub-module titled ‘Hard Copy Return Entry’ to the e-VAT System.

In this regard, the NBR issued a circular on Monday outlining the operational procedures of the new sub-module, said a press release.

According to the press release, by following the circular, taxpayers can enter their previously submitted hard-copy VAT returns into the e-VAT System on their own.

Under the existing system, paper VAT returns submitted by taxpayers are entered into the e-VAT System through the Central Processing Centre (CPC) of the respective VAT Commissionerates.

In this process, VAT officials manually enter data from hard-copy returns. Entering a large volume of paper returns by VAT offices is a time-consuming task.

Due to delays in entering paper returns into the e-VAT System, taxpayers are often automatically charged interest and penalties.

As a result, many taxpayers are unable to submit online VAT returns, as the system does not allow online filing without first paying the imposed penalties.

With the introduction of the Hard Copy Return Entry sub-module, taxpayers who submitted their hard copy VAT returns within the stipulated time as per Section 64 of the VAT and Supplementary Duty Act, 2012, will now be able to enter those returns into the e-VAT System themselves without any penalty or interest.

Taxpayers will receive notifications containing the e-VAT System link via email and mobile phone, enabling them to access and use the new sub-module easily, said the press release.

Taxpayers may enter all previously submitted hard-copy VAT returns into the system without penalty or interest until March 31 of this year.

Once all past paper returns are entered into the e-VAT System, taxpayers will be able to submit all VAT returns online seamlessly.

The NBR sought the wholehearted cooperation of all taxpayers in its ongoing initiative to digitalise all tax administration activities and to ensure transparency and accountability in the tax system.

title: Chattogram to be made rabies-free by vaccinating stray dogs: city mayor
body:
Terming rabies in dogs as a 100 per cent preventable disease, city mayor Shahadat Hossain announced that Chattogram city would be made rabies-free by vaccinating 15,000 stray dogs.

‘Pet dogs and cats should also be protected through regular vaccination. A programme has been launched, and its success depends on the conscious cooperation of city residents,’ he added.

The mayor made the remarks while inaugurating the stray dog vaccination programme in front of the city’s divisional commissioner’s office on Monday.

Hossain said, ‘Public health has been prioritised to create a safe and healthy urban environment. Currently, there is widespread concern over the rising population of stray dogs, incidents of dog bites, and the threat of rabies.’

‘To address these issues in a humane and scientifically sound way, we have initiated a vaccination programme instead of resorting to killing dogs,’ he added.

Explaining that rabies is a deadly viral disease, primarily transmitted to humans through the bite or scratch of a rabid dog, the mayor said, ‘However, not all dog bites cause rabies; the risk exists only if the dog carries the virus.’

He noted that excessive salivation, aimless running, a tendency to bite everything and difficulty walking might indicate a rabid dog.

He urged the public to avoid any dog showing such symptoms and to immediately contact the City Corporation health department or the nearest hospital.

title: BMU VC signs condolence book for Khaleda
body:
Bangladesh Medical University vice-chancellor Professor Md Shahinul Alam signed a condolence book to pay tribute to the late BNP chairperson Khaleda Zia, the three-time former prime minister of Bangladesh.

He signed the condolence book at the office of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party chairperson at Gulshan in Dhaka on Monday morning.

In the book, the vice-chancellor wrote, 'We are deeply saddened at the death of Begum Khaleda Zia. We pray for the salvation of her departed soul. We have lost the symbol of our national unity.'

BMU pro-vice-chancellor (administration) Professor Md Abul Kalam Azad, pro-vice chancellor (research and development) Professor Md Mujibur Rahman Haolder, treasurer Professor Nahrin Akhtar, registrar Professor Md Nazrul Islam, proctor Sheikh Farhad, director (planning and development) Erfanul Haque Siddiqui, additional director of Super Specialised Hospital Md Shahidul Hasan Babul and others were also present there.

Earlier on December 30, the vice-chancellor Professor Md Shahinul Alam expressed his deep condolences and sympathy to the bereaved family on the death of Khaleda Zia.

On the occasion, the government declared a one-day general holiday for December 31 and three days of state mourning for 31 December and January 1 and 2. BMU administration observed the programmes with due respect to the deceased.

title: Biman stages fire drill at Balaka
body:
A fire drill on fire prevention, fire extinguishing, rescue operations and emergency evacuation was held at the Balaka Bhaban, the head office of Biman Bangladesh Airlines Limited, on Monday.

The drill was organised at the initiative of the Fire Section of the Flight Safety Department and with the support of the Bangladesh Fire Service and Civil Defense Department.

Bangladesh Biman managing director and CEO Md Shafiqur Rahman, along with all the officers and employees of Biman Bangladesh Airlines working at Balaka Bhaban took part in the drill.

A 16-member expert team led by Nahid Mahmud, senior station officer of Bangladesh Fire Service, conducted the drill.

During the drill, participants were provided with practical concepts and guidelines on fire prevention, fire extinguishing and control, rescue operations, emergency evacuation procedures and first aid.

title: Oil prices ease as investors track Venezuela fallout
body:
Oil prices dipped Monday after the United States ousted Nicolas Maduro, leader of crude-rich Venezuela, raising the prospect that billions of barrels could be added to the global market in coming years.

Shares prices of defence companies and gold miners rallied on the new geopolitical risks in the wake of the US invasion, while prospects of more US interest-rate cuts this year and a booming technology sector lent additional support to equity markets.

The dollar traded mixed while gold, seen as a safe haven investment, jumped along with silver.

The prices of Brent North Sea crude oil, an international oil benchmark, and the main US contract WTI were slightly lower after US forces seized Maduro on Saturday, with the former reaching $60.66 per barrel and the latter $57.29 per barrel.

Leftist strongman Maduro, 63, faces narcotrafficking charges along with his wife, who was also seized and taken out of Caracas in the shock US assault that involved commandos, bombing by jet planes, and a massive naval force off Venezuela’s coast.

The oil market, which is currently oversupplied, ‘will likely absorb this short-term supply uncertainty, with a limited impact on oil prices’, said Helge Andre Martinsen, senior energy analyst at DNB Carnegie.

Trump said he wanted to allow American oil companies to head back into Venezuela to tap its massive crude reserves, boosting their share prices in limited trading Monday ahead of the Wall Street open.

Venezuela has the largest proven oil reserves in the world, at around 303 billion barrels, according to OPEC.

But its output is very low because of a lack of investment in the country’s infrastructure.

The first full week of business for 2026 will also see the release of key US jobs data that could play a role in the Federal Reserve’s decision-making on borrowing costs.

But the stock gains in Asia and Europe on Monday suggest investors are brushing off worries that valuations in the tech sector have become stretched, amid doubts about the timing and size of returns on huge investments in artificial intelligence.

title: Obaidur joins SME Foundation as chairman
body:
Industries secretary Md Obaidur Rahman has assumed office as the 9th chairperson of the SME Foundation.

He formally joined the foundation at its office on Monday, according to a press release.

The Ministry of Industries issued a gazette notification on January 1, 2026, appointing him to the post in addition to his duties as industries secretary, until a new chairperson is appointed.

Obaidur holds bachelor’s and master’s degrees in management from the University of Dhaka.

A member of the 15th BCS (administration) cadre, he has served in field administration and held key positions in several ministries and departments, including the Ministry of Public Administration.

title: Hong Kong reclaims top global IPO spot in 2025
body:
Hong Kong reclaimed its position as the world’s top spot for initial public offerings in 2025 after it raised more than HK$285 billion (US$36.6 billion), a 225 per cent increase on-year, accounting giant PwC said Monday.

The Chinese finance hub saw 119 new listings last year, with big-ticket sales including Chinese battery giant CATL and miner Zijin Gold putting it ahead of the New York Stock Exchange, Nasdaq and the National Stock Exchange of India.

‘Despite uncertainties in the global geopolitical landscape, the demand for international financing by Chinese enterprises and investors’ interest in high-quality Chinese companies remain strong,’ PricewaterhouseCoopers’ Hong Kong capital markets leader Eddie Wong said.
