At Venezuela’s request, the UN Security Council will meet Monday to discuss the crisis, the Somali presidency of the Council said.

title: Sparklers blamed in deadly Swiss bar fire
body:
Swiss investigators worked Saturday to identify the victims and exact cause of the blaze that killed 40 New Year revellers at a packed bar in the ski resort of Crans-Montana.

Dozens of people badly burnt in the fire early Thursday in the glitzy Alpine town were taken to nearby countries for urgent treatment, while authorities pointed the finger at lit sparklers attached to champagne bottles igniting foam on the ceiling.

People continued to bring flowers, candles and messages on Saturday to a makeshift memorial near the scene of the tragedy at Le Constellation bar, where people have often simply stood in stunned silence.

‘Courage to all the victims’ families, we’re thinking of Stefan and hoping he’s okay; a hero,’ said one message. Cards read: ‘We’re thinking of you’ and ‘May they rest in peace.’

The tragedy remains the topic of every conversation, filled with pain, sadness, and also incomprehension.

The disaster has left Switzerland reeling, with families of the overwhelmingly young partygoers waiting for news of their loved ones. Most of the 119 people wounded in the fire remained in a serious condition.

Of those injured, 113 have been identified, the Wallis canton’s regional police commander Frederic Gisler said Friday, adding that officials were working ‘relentlessly’ to finish the job.

Many of those injured were foreign nationals, and given Crans-Montana’s international popularity, non-Swiss citizens are also widely expected to figure among the dead.

Among those bracing for the worst was Laetitia Brodard, who said that the last text she received from her son, Arthur, was ‘Mother, Happy New Year, I love you’.

‘It’s been 40 hours. Forty hours since our children have disappeared. So we should know by now,’ she told journalists Friday near the memorial.

The exact number of people who were at Le Constellation when it went up in flames remains unclear.

The Crans-Montana website said the venue had a capacity of 300 people plus 40 on its terrace.

Le Constellation’s two French managers have been taken in for questioning, with one of them, Jacques Moretti, insisting to the Swiss press that all safety norms were followed.

But the chief prosecutor of the Wallis region, Beatrice Pilloud, said that the standards were among the focuses of the investigation.

Pilloud told reporters Friday that the leading hypothesis was that ‘sparklers or Bengal candles attached to champagne bottles and lifted too close to the ceiling’ had ignited the deadly blaze.

One video showed the low wooden ceiling—covered with soundproofing foam—catching alight and the flames spreading quickly, but revellers continuing to dance, unaware of the death trap they were in.

Eyewitnesses described scenes of chaos as people tried to break through the windows to escape, while others, covered in burns, poured out into the street. Nathan, who had been in the bar before the fire, saw burnt people streaming out of the site.

‘They were asking for help, crying out for help,’ he said, declining to give his last name.

Edmond Cocquyt, a Belgian tourist, told AFP he saw bodies ‘covered with a white sheet’ and ‘young people, totally burnt, who were still alive ... screaming in pain’.

Of the injured, police chief Gisler said that 71 were Swiss, 14 were French, 11 were Italian, and four were from Serbia, along with victims from Bosnia, Belgium, Poland, Portugal and Luxembourg.

Swiss authorities warned it could take days to identify everyone who perished, leaving an agonising wait for family and friends, while desperate appeals to find those missing circulated online.

Several memorial masses for the victims are planned, including one on Saturday evening in Crans-Montana.

‘It’s very sad, deeply sad,’ said a French tourist on Saturday in Crans-Montana, skis in hand, who wished to remain anonymous.

But it seemed ‘a familiar scenario: a bar that, according to initial reports, wasn’t necessarily meeting the standards, and young people who didn’t necessarily notice the risks,’ he told AFP.

‘This kind of tragedy has already happened elsewhere. If only this one could make young people, and not so young people, aware of the risks, of checking emergency exits.’

title: 6.5-magnitude quake kills two in Mexico City
body:
A 6.5-magnitude earthquake rattled Mexico’s capital and a tourist hotspot on the Pacific coast on Friday, killing at least two people and causing moderate damage in a small town near the epicentre.

The US Geological Survey said the quake struck shortly before 8:00 am near Acapulco, a major port and beach resort.

It was felt around 400 kilometres away to the north in Mexico City, where alarms sent people rushing into the street for safety, disrupting a holiday weekend.

A 60-year-old man died after falling while evacuating his second-floor apartment in the capital, local authorities said.

Twelve others were injured, city Mayor Clara Brugada wrote on social media, but there were no reports of major damage in the country’s largest city.

President Claudia Sheinbaum was forced to evacuate the presidential palace during her regular morning press conference.

Mexico’s National Seismological Service said that the earthquake’s epicentre was situated 14 kilometres southwest of the town of San Marcos in the state of Guerrero.

Sheinbaum said there were no immediate reports of major damage, but in San Marcos, the effects were visible.

A woman in her fifties ‘lost her life when her house collapsed on top of her,’ said Guerrero governor Evelyn Salgado.

San Marcos mayor Misael Lorenzo Castillo said around 50 houses were destroyed and ‘all the houses have cracks.’

Residents showed an AFP journalist the cracks in the walls of their homes and sections of collapsed walls.

‘San Marcos has been badly affected, devastated,’ lamented Rogelio Moreno, a resident, standing in front of his damaged home.

Mexico is situated between five tectonic plates and as such is one of the world’s most seismically active countries.

Karen Gomez, a 47-year-old office worker living on the 13th floor of an apartment building in Mexico City, told AFP she was roused from her sleep by a street siren.

‘I woke up in terror. My cellphone alert said it was a powerful earthquake.’

Norma Ortega, a 57-year-old kindergarten director, living in a 10th-floor apartment, said she could feel her building shake.

In Acapulco, Ricardo, a tourist from the central Mexican state of Morelos, fled his hotel shirtless after sirens sounded.

The centre of Mexico City is built on the muddy subsoil of what was once the bed of a lake, making it particularly vulnerable to earthquakes.

The quakes most strongly felt usually originate off Guerrero state on the Pacific coast.

On September 19, 1985, an 8.1-magnitude earthquake devastated a vast swathe of Mexico City, leaving nearly 13,000 dead, mostly in the city, according to official figures.

In 2017, also on September 19, a 7.1-magnitude quake killed 369 people, also mostly in Mexico City.

Early warning systems, including smartphone apps, have been developed to warn citizens strong quakes and urge them to reach safety.

Mexico City has also installed loudspeakers on lampposts to broadcast the alerts.

title: Trump invites Japan PM to US
body:
President Donald Trump invited Japan’s prime minister Sanae Takaichi to the United States during a phone call late on Friday and they agreed to work towards a meeting early this year, officials said.

Trump has already said he will visit China in April, with Tokyo and Beijing in dispute over Takaichi’s suggestion in November that Japan could intervene militarily in case of any attack on self-ruled Taiwan.

China claims the democratic island as part of its territory and has threatened to use force to bring it under its control.

Takaichi’s comments triggered a sharp diplomatic backlash from China, which has urged its citizens to avoid travelling to Japan and suspended Japanese seafood imports.

She and Trump spoke for 25 minutes, agreeing to further strengthen economic and security cooperation, the foreign ministry in Tokyo said in a statement.

Trump invited Takaichi to visit the United States and ‘the two leaders concurred to coordinate in detail to realise the visit to the United States this spring’, it said.

The statement did not make clear whether they talked about China, but Trump and Takaichi also ‘exchanged views mainly on the Indo-Pacific region and confirmed the close cooperation between Japan and the United States’, it said.

China launched missiles and deployed dozens of fighter jets, navy ships and coastguard vessels around Taiwan in live-fire drills last week.

The drills drew a chorus of international criticism, including from Japan, Australia and European countries.

Trump advised Takaichi not to provoke China over Taiwan in their previous phone call on November 25, the Wall Street Journal reported, but Tokyo denied the report.

title: DRC forces-M23 clashes near key city
body:
Violent fighting broke out Saturday between the Rwandan-backed M23 armed group and pro-Kinshasa forces in several towns around the strategic eastern DR Congo city of Uvira, local sources said.

The resource-rich east of the Democratic Republic of Congo, which borders Rwanda as well as Burundi, has been beset by 30 years of continual violence.

The situation has worsened since 2021 amid the resurgence of the M23.

Having seized the two main eastern cities of Goma and Bukavu late last year, the group launched a new offensive in December in South Kivu province and gained control on December 10 of Uvira, a strategic city of several hundred thousand people near Burundi, DRC’s ally.

The group also took control of border areas at a time when the DRC and Rwanda were signing a peace accord in Washington brokered by US President Donald Trump.

‘Since 3:00am [0100 GMT], violent clashes between M23 rebels and Wazalendo [pro-Kinshasa militias] and the armed forces of the Republic have been reported in several localities in the territory of Uvira,’ in South Kivu province, Kelvin Bwija, Uvira civil society coordinator, told AFP.

Bwija cited the localities of Kashombe, Lubanda, Musingwe, Katongo, and Kigongo, located about 10 kilometers from the city as seeing fighting.

‘So far, the sound of gunfire can be heard in Uvira,’ he said.

A resident of Kigongo, also reached by telephone, confirmed to AFP that ‘clashes resumed this morning, with loud explosions and gunfire’ heard.

Lieutenant Reagan Mbuyi Kalonji, regional spokesman for the Congolese army, confirmed to AFP ‘clashes in Kigongo and Katongo, specifically in the hills of Kashombe and Lubanda in the territory of Uvira.’

Under US pressure, the M23 announced on December 17 its withdrawal from Uvira, while asking mediators to ensure the city’s protection from violence and ‘remilitarisation.’

There have also been reports of intense fighting in the neighbouring province of North Kivu since Friday, where at least six people were killed and 41 wounded in a bombing attributed to the Congolese army in  Masisi territory in North Kivu province, according to local sources.

Doctors Without Borders meanwhile stated on social media that ‘42 people, including many children and women, wounded by shrapnel and suffering from other injuries, were admitted to Masisi General Hospital following an air strike in a residential area of Masisi’.

title: MSF warns of halting Gaza work by March
body:
Banned from the Gaza Strip with 36 aid bodies, medical charity Doctors Without Borders said Saturday it will have to end its operations there in March if Israel does not reverse its decision.

UN secretary general Antonio Guterres called on Friday for Israel to end a ban on humanitarian agencies that provided aid in Gaza, saying he was ‘deeply concerned’ at the development.

Israel confirmed on Thursday it is barring 37 major international humanitarian organisations from entering the Gaza Strip, accusing them of failing to provide the list of their employees’ names, which is now officially required for ‘security’ reasons.

MSF called this demand a ‘scandalous intrusion’ but Israel says is needed to stop jihadists from infiltrating into humanitarian structures.

‘To work in Palestine, in the occupied Palestinian territories, we have to be registered ... That registration expired on December 31, 2025,’ said Isabelle Defourny, a physician and president of MSF France, on France Inter.

‘Since July 2025, we have been involved in a re-registration process and to date, we have not received a response. We still have 60 days during which we could work without being re-registered, and so we would have to end our activities in March’ if Israel maintains its decision, she said.

MSF has around 40 international staff in the Gaza Strip and works with 800 Palestinian staff across eight hospitals.

‘We are the second-largest distributor of water [in the Gaza Strip]. Last year, in 2025, we treated just over 100,000 people who were wounded, burned, or victims of various traumas. We are second in terms of the number of deliveries performed,’ the president of MSF France said.

According to her, the Israeli decision is explained by the fact that NGOs ‘bear witness to the violence committed by the Israeli army’ in Gaza.

title: Salvadoran journalist arrested in Spain
body:
A Salvadoran photo journalist was arrested Friday in Spain under an international warrant while requesting asylum, a press association said.

At least 50 journalists have fled El Salvador over the past six months out of fear of being arrested for criticizing President Nayib Bukele, the Salvadoran Press Association said.

The photographer, identified as 25-year-old Diego Andres Rosa Rosales, was filing papers for asylum at a police station in Seville when he was arrested under an Interpol warrant initiated by Bukele’s government, the association said in a post on social media platform X.

In El Salvador, Rosa has been subject to police harassment, threats and baseless charges of criminal association, the association said.

The latter charge is what Bukele applies to alleged members of street gangs, using it to jail thousands of people without trials in a notoriously harsh prison.

Bukele doubled-down on Rosa’s arrest Friday, writing in a statement posted to X: ‘The new immunity is being a ‘journalist.’’

‘Political immunity is discredited and lacks international validity, but self-identifying as a journalist is enough to obtain total impunity from any crime, protected by NGOs, legacy media, governments, and international organizations,’ Bukele continued.

On Saturday, Rosa will go before a judge to decide if Spain will go ahead with extradition proceedings.

Rosa has worked for prominent Salvadoran news organizations and foreign outlets like The Guardian and Spain’s El Pais newspaper, the press association said.

Bukele is wildly popular at home for his crackdown on gangs that used to terrorize the country, acting under emergency laws that allow people to be arrested without a warrant.

Human rights activists say the government is also applying this policy to critics of the president.

title: Cambodia demands Thai troop withdrawal amid truce
body:
Cambodia called on neighbouring Thailand on Saturday to pull out its forces from areas Phnom Penh claims as its own, one week since a truce halted deadly clashes along their disputed border.

The decades-old dispute between the Southeast Asian neighbours erupted into military clashes several times last year, with fighting in December killing dozens of people and displacing around one million on both sides.

The two countries agreed a truce on December 27, ending three weeks of clashes.

Cambodia says that during that period, Thailand seized several areas across four border provinces.

In a statement on Saturday, Phnom Penh’s foreign ministry demanded the withdrawal of ‘all Thai military personnel and equipment from the territory of the Kingdom of Cambodia to positions fully consistent with the legally established boundary’.

The Thai army has rejected claims it had used force to seize Cambodia territory, insisting its forces were present in areas that had always belonged to Thailand.

The Cambodian foreign ministry also called on Thailand to immediately end ‘all hostile military activities’ along the frontier and ‘within Cambodian territory’.

The two nations’ border conflict stems from a dispute over the colonial-era demarcation of their 800-kilometre border, where both sides claim territory and centuries-old temple ruins.

On Friday, Cambodia’s information minister Neth Pheaktra accused Thailand of launching the ‘illegal annexation’ of the border village of Chouk Chey.

The Thai army disputed Phnom Penh’s narrative, and prime minister Anutin Charnvirakul said his country ‘has never breached another country’s sovereignty and has acted in line with international regulations’.

Anutin was speaking on Friday while visiting troops deployed to the border province of Surin.

title: 2 looted firearms recovered, 2 arrested in Chandpur
body:
The police have recovered two firearms, 30 rounds of bullet and various kinds of police equipment looted from police stations during the August 2024 political changeover and arrested two people in Chandpur on Friday night.

Among the recovered items, there were a 9mm Taurus pistol, a magazine of it and six rounds of the pistol’s bullet, a 7.62mm pistol, three magazines of the pistol and its 24 rounds of bullet, said Chandpur district additional superintendent of police, crime, Md Lutfar Rahman on Saturday.

He said that a team of Shaharasti police station conducted a drive in a house at Uplata village on information and recovered the looted firearms and ammunitions.

Faisal Hossain Shakil and his mother Lovely Begum were arrested during the drive, said the police personnel, adding that the arrestees in primary questioning confessed their connection with looting firearms and other equipment from police stations.

The recovered items also included one gasmask, one belt, one shoulder light and two eyeglasses used by the police.

‘Legal actions against the arrestees under the arms act are under way,’ said Lutfar.

According to the Police Headquarters data, 1335 looted firearms could not be recovered till January 1.

According to the PHQ data updated on December 7, 2025, a total of 1,337 firearms and 2,57,189 ammunitions and explosives were unrecovered among 5,763 firearms and 6,52,008 ammunitions and explosives looted from police stations during the August 2024 political changeover.

title: Threat of rape on ‘Victor Classic’ bus, 2 detained
body:
A driver of the ‘Victor Classic’ bus service has been accused of threatening a woman with rape at Tongi in Gazipur.

Following the incident, a case was filed with the Tongi West police station on charges of assault and attempted murder after another passenger was beaten for protesting the act.

Police have detained two individuals in connection with the incident.

Officer-in-charge of Tongi West police Md Shahin Khan on Saturday said that the driver and his assistant were detained on the day of the incident.

During preliminary interrogation, they admitted the truth of the incident. The bus has been seized, and necessary legal action will be taken in accordance with the law, he said.

According to the victim’s complaint, on 1 January, the wife of Md Naim Islam, a 16th batch student of the history department of Jagannath University, began her journey on a ‘Victor Classic’ bus from the Uttara BNS area to Hossain Market in Tongi. She was seated in the reserved seat for women beside the driver.

The complaint states that after the woman introduced herself as a member of a Jagannath University student’s family, the driver began making provocative and obscene remarks. At one point, when the bus reached the traffic police box in front of Safiuddin Sarkar Academy, Naim Islam attempted to record a video on his mobile phone. At that time, the driver pushed him against the bus window and threw his phone away.

When the victim asked the driver to stop the bus in front of the police box, he refused. As she started screaming, the driver allegedly threatened her with rape inside the bus. A passenger named Nur Nabi came forward to protest the incident, leading to a scuffle among the driver, his assistant and other passengers.

Later, when the bus stopped at the Hossain Market area, the woman was safely helped off the bus with the assistance of passengers.

However, after everyone else had gotten off, Nur Nabi was attacked when he was alone. The driver, his assistant, and another person allegedly beat him with iron rods and injured him seriously.

Subsequently, with the help of local residents, the bus was stopped. Although the driver and his assistant managed to flee, another driver was detained and handed over to the police.

In this incident, Md Naim Islam filed a case with the Tongi West police on charges of threatening rape and attempted murder.

He alleged, ‘After the incident, around 3:30am, 15–20 people from the bus owners’ association came to the police station and threatened us to withdraw the case.’

He further claimed that the accused driver had been released on bail four days earlier in a drug-related case from Uttara East police station.

title: EC prepares 80 lakh leaflets, 57,000 banners
body:
The Election Commission has begun extensive campaigning across the country using banners and leaflets as the 13th Jatiya Sangsad election and referendum is scheduled to hold on February 12.

Ahead of the referendum, around 80.42 lakh leaflets and 57,000 banners are being prepared for nationwide distribution, according to the EC.

The leaflets will be distributed throughout the country, while large banners measuring 10 feet by 4 feet will be displayed in public places and 3 feet by 5 feet banners will be placed in front of polling centres, EC secretariat’s director, public relations and information, Md Ruhul Amin Mallik said on Saturday.

He said that the printing of leaflets was under way at BG Press, and distribution would begin from January 5.

‘In addition, nearly 15 thousand large banners (10 ft x 4 ft) will be displayed in front of returning officers’ offices and public spaces, and 42,766 banners (3 ft x 5 ft) will be placed in front of polling stations. Those are also being prepared,’ he added.

The EC-approved leaflets and banners for the referendum campaign contain the following message, ‘Do you express your consent to the proposals related to the implementation of the July National Charter (constitutional amendment), 2025, and the constitutional reforms recorded in the July National Charter? (yes/no).’

The leaflets and banners outline the main proposals, ‘The caretaker government during elections, the Election Commission, and other constitutional institutions will be formed according to the process described in the July Charter.’

The next national parliament will have a two-chamber structure, with an upper house of 100 members formed proportionally according to votes obtained by parties in the parliamentary election, and any constitutional amendment will require approval by the majority of the upper house members.

Implementation of 30 specific measures agreed in the July Charter, including increased representation of women in parliament, election of deputy speaker and parliamentary committee chairs from opposition parties, protection of fundamental rights, independence of the judiciary, local government, prime minister’s tenure, president’s powers, among others, will be mandatory for political parties winning the next parliamentary election.

Other reforms described in the July Charter will be implemented as per political parties’ commitments.

Finally, the leaflets and banners provide options for voters to cast their response as ‘yes’ or ‘no’.

title: 14 jailed by mobile court over drug abuse at Ashulia
body:
A mobile court at Ashulia, on the outskirts of Dhaka, has sentenced 14 people to jail after they were arrested during a special anti-drug drive at the area, authorities said.

The detainees were produced before a mobile court led by executive magistrate Sadiya Akter, also the assistant commissioner, Land, of the Ashulia Revenue Circle.

The operation was conducted from the evening until about 9:30pm in the Jamgora area and nearby localities, following repeated complaints of drug abuse and trafficking, police said.

The court sentenced each of them to six months’ simple imprisonment and imposed a fine of Tk 500.

The police said that the special drive was aimed at curbing the long-standing presence of drug users and dealers in the area.

‘Operations like this will continue as part of our zero-tolerance policy against drugs,’ magistrate Sadiya Akter said, adding that the administration remains committed to eliminating narcotics from society.

title: Labour leader Shahidullah Chy remembered
body:
Politicians and labour leaders on Saturday at a commemoration meeting in Dhaka called on the labour right bodies to carry forward the unfinished works of labour leader Shahidullah Chowdhury who worked for establishing rights of the workers.

Communist Party of Bangladesh organised the commemoration meeting at the party’s central office in the city to mark first anniversary of death of the labour leader who was also president of the party.

Former president of the party Mujahidul Islam Selim and Trade Union Centre acting president Mahbub Alam said that Shahidullah dedicated his whole life to ensure labours rights.

Chaired by CPB president Kazi Sazzad Zahir Chandan, general secretary Abdullah Al Kafee Ratan, central leader Ruhin Hossain Prince, labour leader Mantu Ghosh and Sadekur Rahman Shamim, spoke at the commemoration meeting.

Shahidullah Chowdhury died on January 3 last year at his Demra house from old age complications at the age of 82.

title: Experts urge coordinated initiatives to curb mosquito menace
body:
Experts and city officials on Saturday underscored the need for joint initiatives involving the administration, specialists and citizens to effectively tackle the growing mosquito threat in the capital, stressing science-based planning and increased public awareness.

They said although the presence of dengue-carrying Aedes mosquitoes is currently low, the population of Culex mosquitoes is on the rise and could peak by March, warning that timely and coordinated measures are crucial to prevent a worsening situation.

The observations came at a discussion titled “Mosquito Menace and Public Sufferings,” organized by the Dhaka Utility Reporters Association (DURA) at the Sagar-Runi Auditorium of Dhaka Reporters Unity.

Former DURA general secretary Shahjahan Molla presided over the event, while DURA general secretary Zahirul Islam conducted the session.

Speaking as the chief guest, Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) Chief Health Officer Dr. Nishat Parveen said efforts by the city corporation alone are insufficient to reduce dengue and mosquito nuisance.

“Every citizen must keep their homes and surroundings clean and remain vigilant. We are working at the field level, but success is not possible without public participation. Together, we can achieve a mosquito-free Dhaka,” she said.

Jahangirnagar University zoology professor and entomologist Dr. Kabirul Bashar said mosquito problems in Dhaka have become structural and scientific rather than seasonal.

“Strengthening surveillance activities and using scientific data can bring the situation under control, while citizens’ responsible role remains crucial,” he added.

Urban planner Dr. Md. Ariful Islam stressed the importance of long-term solutions through planned urbanization, improved drainage systems and effective waste management.

DSCC Assistant Health Officer Md. Sadman Sakib said a month-long special programme has been launched in anticipation of a possible rise in Culex mosquitoes, including ward-based activities and awareness campaigns.

Dhaka Reporters Unity General Secretary Mainul Hasan Sohel also urged both authorities and citizens to play active roles in controlling all forms of mosquito menace in the capital.

title: Wild elephant kills man
body:
A man was trampled to death by wild elephant at Baishari under Naikhyangchari in Bandarban on Saturday.

The victim, 30-year-old Abdus Salam, a resident of the same area, was a local tubewell mechanic. According to witness, the elephant entered the locality around 6.30am, sparking curiosity among the residents. As the people of the area came out to see the wild animal, a dog began barking, disturbing the elephant. In a sudden act of aggression, the elephant started chasing the people.

Abdus Salam, attempting to flee, tripped and fell down unfortunately. The elephant trampled him, causing serious injuries. He died on the spot.

Baishari police investigation centre in-charge Md Anwarul Islam said that they visited the scene upon receiving the report. ‘It has been initially confirmed that the person died as a result of a wild elephant attack.’

Officer-in-charge Md Abdul Baten Mridha of Naikhyangchari police said that necessary legal actions were being taken.

title: Tens of thousands in Berlin face days without power
body:
Tens of thousands of homes in Berlin will be without electricity until Thursday as authorities struggle to repair power cables seriously damaged in a suspected arson attack, officials said.

Some may also be without heating as the outage has affected local systems, at a time when the German capital is blanketed in snow and temperatures are hovering around freezing.

Emergency services were alerted early Saturday that several high-voltage cables on a bridge near a power plant had gone up in flames.

Firefighters quickly extinguished the blaze, but about 45,500 households and 2,200 businesses in districts in southwest Berlin were left without power, according to grid operator Stromnetz Berlin.

The extensive damage means that around 35,000 households will be without electricity until Thursday afternoon, Berlin authorities said in a statement. Power should be restored to other homes by early Sunday.

‘We are dealing with a particularly serious power outage affecting tens of thousands of households and businesses, including care facilities, hospitals, numerous social institutions, and companies,’ said Franziska Giffey, Berlin senator for economic affairs.

The local district heating system—which transports heat around a pipe network in the area—is affected as it is powered by electricity.

Stromnetz Berlin warned that repair work ‘will take a very long time’, with media reports saying that cold weather was hindering efforts to lay new underground cables.

Police deployed about 160 officers to the site of the incident in the Lichterfelde area and said they were ‘investigating on suspicion of arson’.

They drove vans equipped with loudspeakers through the affected areas, urging residents to stay with friends or relatives elsewhere if possible, use mobile phones sparingly and ensure they have torches at hand.

Local train stations were impacted, with electronic information signs and ticket machines not working—although the trains were still running.

Giffey said Saturday’s outage was worse than one in September, when tens of thousands were also left without power in Berlin after a blaze hit electricity pylons.

Police also suspected arson in that case, and an unnamed anarchist group claimed responsibility online for starting the blaze.

Germany has been on high alert for sabotage activities directed at its infrastructure, including from foreign actors such as Russia.

title: Ukraine’s allies meet as Russia makes biggest gains since 2022
body:
Security advisers from Ukraine’s top allies met in Kyiv on Saturday for talks on a US-brokered plan to end the war with Russia, days after Kyiv announced a deal was ‘90 per cent’ ready.

Officials from 15 countries including Britain, France and Germany as well as representatives from NATO and the European Union joined the meeting, the first of several planned for the new year.

US special envoy Steve Witkoff also joined virtually, a Ukrainian official told AFP, though the United States’ large-scale military attack on Venezuela earlier in the day overshadowed proceedings.

A follow-up summit of European leaders was expected to take place in France on Tuesday, according to Ukraine.

‘National security advisers from European countries have arrived in Kyiv,’ Ukraine’s chief negotiator Rustem Umerov said in a post on Telegram. He announced in a later post that the meeting had started.

‘The first part of the meeting focused on framework documents, including security guarantees and approaches to the peace plan, as well as the sequence of further joint steps,’ he said.

Diplomatic efforts to end Europe’s deadliest conflict since World War II have gained pace in recent weeks, though both Moscow and Kyiv remain at odds over the key issue of territory in a post-war settlement.

Russia, which occupies around 20 per cent of Ukraine, is pushing for full control of the country’s eastern Donbas region as part of a deal. But Kyiv has warned ceding ground will embolden Moscow and said it will not sign a peace deal that fails to deter Russia from invading again.

Meanwhile, Russia’s battlefield gains in Ukraine last year were the highest since 2022, an AFP analysis showed.

The Russian army captured more than 5,600 square kilometres, or nearly one per cent, of Ukrainian territory in 2025, according to an analysis of data from the Institute for the Study of War, which works with the Critical Threats Project.

This includes areas that Kyiv and military analysts say are controlled by Russia, as well as those claimed by Moscow’s army.

The land captured is more than in the previous two years combined, though far short of the more than 60,000 square kilometres Russia took in 2022, the first year of its all-out invasion.

Moscow has kept up its aerial barrage of Ukraine, with the latest strike on a residential area of the major city of Kharkiv, reducing parts of multi-storey buildings to smouldering piles of rubble.

Saturday’s meeting capped a week marked by deadly strikes, as well as a Russian claim—denied by Ukraine—that Kyiv had launched drones at a residence of president Vladimir Putin in an unsuccessful attack.

Russia accused Kyiv of firing drones at a hotel and cafe in the Moscow-held part of Ukraine’s southern Kherson region early Thursday, killing what it said were 28 people celebrating the New Year. Ukraine says it was a military gathering.

As the year kicked off, Zelensky announced sweeping changes to his top circle, naming a new chief of staff and defence minister on Friday while announcing plans on Saturday to replace several regional leaders.

Russia launched its invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, describing it as a ‘special military operation’ to prevent the expansion of NATO—a war aim that Kyiv has called a lie.

Moscow has since fired on Ukrainian towns and cities in daily drone and missile attacks while waging battles that have reduced entire urban areas to rubble.

title: Bangladesh look to move T20 World Cup matches from India amid Mustafiz row
body:
Bangladesh will ask the ICC to relocate their T20 World Cup matches from India to Sri Lanka, after Kolkata Knight Riders were instructed to release Mustafizur Rahman as a result of deteriorating political ties between Bangladesh and India.

The BCB is expected to write to the ICC to raise their concerns about player safety in Kolkata, where Bangladesh are scheduled to play their first three matches of the World Cup next month.

Following the BCB's emergency meeting of board directors over Zoom on Saturday, the media committee chairman Amzad Hussain told reporters: ‘We have three matches of the T20 World Cup in Kolkata, so we will write to the ICC regarding what has happened today.’

Bangladesh's sports adviser Asif Nazrul said that he has doubts about the team's safety in India, after the BCCI cited ‘recent developments’ in their explanation for Mustafiz's removal from the IPL, adding that he will instruct the BCB to write to the ICC about moving their matches to Sri Lanka.

‘I have asked the BCB to explain the entire matter to the ICC,’ Nazrul wrote on his official Facebook page. ‘The board should inform that where a Bangladeshi cricketer cannot play in India despite being contracted, the entire Bangladeshi cricket team cannot feel safe going to play in the World Cup. I have also instructed the Board to request that Bangladesh's World Cup matches be held in Sri Lanka.’

Nazrul added that he has requested the country's information and broadcasting ministry to stop showing the IPL in Bangladesh.

Following the BCCI's instructions, KKR confirmed that they have released Mustafiz from their squad for the 2026 IPL. KKR had acquired the left-arm fast bowler's services for 9.2 crore in the IPL auction last month, though they faced a backlash for their selection in the last few days from Indian spiritual and political leaders.

Interestingly, the BCB had announced their home schedule for 2026 on Friday, including white-ball matches against India, a series that was postponed from 2025.

Bangladesh's T20 World Cup matches are scheduled to be held in Kolkata and Mumbai, with their opening fixture against West Indies at Eden Gardens on February 7.

title: 2,73,554 applications submitted for GST admission test
body:
A total of 273,554 students have applied to sit for the undergraduate first-year admission tests for the 2025–26 academic session under the general and science and technology cluster admission system, reflecting strong competition for public university seats.

Professor Dr Manzurul Haque, registrar of Islamic University in Kushtia and secretary of the Central Committee of the GST admission tests, confirmed the figures on Saturday morning.

He said that among the total applicants, 159,189 students applied for A unit (Science), 90,408 for B unit (Humanities), and 23,957 for C unit (Business Studies).

According to the published schedule, the C unit admission test will be held on March 27, followed by B unit on April 3 and A unit on April 10.

The tests will be conducted at Islamic University in Kushtia, Mawlana Bhashani Science and Technology University, Patuakhali Science and Technology University, Noakhali Science and Technology University, Jatiya Kabi Kazi Nazrul Islam University, Jessore University of Science and Technology, Begum Rokeya University, Pabna University of Science and Technology, Gopalganj Science and Technology University, University of Barishal, Rangamati Science and Technology University, Rabindra University, University of Frontier Technology Bangladesh, Netrokona University, Jamalpur Science and Technology University, Kishoreganj University, Chandpur Science and Technology University, Sunamganj Science and Technology University, and Pirojpur Science and Technology University.

title: 802 workers killed in 713 workplace accidents in 2025
body:
A total of 802 workers were killed in 713 workplace accidents across the country in 2025, highlighting persistent and widespread insecurity in workplaces, according to a survey released on Saturday by Safety and Rights Society.

The survey shows a rise in fatalities compared with 2024, when 758 workers were killed in 639 workplace accidents nationwide.

Of the total deaths recorded this year, 385 occurred in the transport sector, making it the deadliest sector for workers. At least 78 workers were killed in road accidents while travelling to and from work.

Safety and Rights Society said the findings were based on an analysis of reports published in 15 national and 11 local newspapers. The organisation noted that media-based data often underrepresent the true scale of workplace fatalities.

According to the sector-wise breakdown, transport-related accidents accounted for the highest number of deaths. Service institutions, including workshops and gas and electricity supply entities, recorded 145 fatalities.

The construction sector saw 120 deaths, while 58 workers were killed in factories and other productive institutions. The agricultural sector accounted for 94 deaths.

An analysis of causes shows that road accidents were responsible for the majority of fatalities, claiming 479 lives. Other causes included electrocution 96, lightning strikes 78, falls from heights or scaffolding 50, drowning 28, being hit by or crushed under heavy or solid objects 25, fire and explosions 20, collapse of soil, hills, bridges, buildings, roofs or walls 14, and exposure to toxic gases in chemical plants, septic tanks or water tanks 8. Four workers died from other causes.

The survey identified poor road infrastructure, unfit vehicles, unskilled or inefficient drivers, an uncontrolled transport system, weak law enforcement and reckless driving as key factors behind the high number of transport-related deaths.

In the manufacturing and construction sectors, major risks included unauthorised factory construction, lack of safety training, unsafe use of chemicals, hazardous electrical connections, working at heights without protective barriers and inadequate precautions while working in confined spaces such as septic or water tanks.

Releasing the survey, the executive director Sekender Ali Mina said that the actual number of deaths was likely higher, as many accidents go unreported.

He noted that at least 76 workers were killed this year while commuting to work, stressing the need to ensure safety during travel to and from workplaces. He also warned of an alarming rise in deaths caused by lightning, particularly among agricultural workers, many of whom receive no compensation. He called for effective social protection measures for these workers.

Safety and Rights Society said most of the workers killed this year were aged between 21 and 40. The organisation urged the government to ensure decent and safe working conditions through legal reforms and stricter enforcement in line with the ratification of the occupational safety and health conventions of the International Labour Organization, including Conventions 155 and 187.

title: DNCC, DSCC inaugurate BUET-made e-rickshaws
body:
The two Dhaka city corporations inaugurated relatively environment-friendly ‘e-rickshaws’ on Saturday on pilot basis in three areas in the city in a bid to ensure discipline on the roads and safe commuting.

Local government, rural development and cooperatives adviser Adilur Rahman Khan at the inauguration event of the DNCC said that its main objective was to bring back discipline in the urban transport system by establishing control on the haphazardly run battery-run rickshaws and ‘easy bikes’.

The battery-run rickshaws introduced in the pilot have been manufactured by the Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology experts and are run by lithium-ion batteries, according to the officials at the city corporations, who also said the BUET named them ‘e-rickshaws’.

A press release, issued by Dhaka North City Corporation on Saturday, read that the rickshaws were introduced in Rampura, Motijheel and Dhanmondi in separate events organised at Rampura’s Aftabnagar and Dhamondi’s Jigatola.

The DNCC gave approval to the lithium-ion e-rickshaws to run on the Badda-Rampura road connecting Aftabnagar on pilot basis.

DNCC administrator Mohammad Azaz said that their target was to bring the rickshaw-pullers under training and licence.

Trained rickshaw-pullers with licences would be allowed to drive battery-run rickshaws in fixed areas, he added.

Most battery-run rickshaws are run by lead-acid batteries in the country.

title: Parties urged to underscore inclusivity in manifestos
body:
Amid growing political realignments ahead of the 13th Jatiya Sangsad elections scheduled for February 12, civil society platform Citizens for Good Governance—Shujan on Saturday demanded that political parties’ election manifestos highlighted the aspirations of the July uprising.

Speakers at a press conference, organised by Shujan at the Zahur Hossain Chowdhury Auditorium of the National Press Club in the capital, said that young voters would not accept repetitions of an undemocratic and discriminatory ruling system devoid of accountability.

At the conference, school of business and economics dean at North South University Professor AKM Waresul Karim presented the keynote in which he observed that citizens were confused whether the alliances being forged ahead of the polls were ideological or merely electoral arrangements.

‘As the election draws closer, people increasingly want to know what the parties will do if they win, how they will do it and when,’ Karim observed, saying that the answers must be clearly reflected in their election manifestos.

Having said that the 2024 July uprising was the eruption of the young generation’s desperate aspiration for a just, inclusive and democratic country, Karim stated that voters would no longer keep silent if the next government sided against them.

Regarding the implementation of the July National Charter and the recommendations of the reform commissions, Karim said that the political parties and alliances must make clear commitment for its full implementation.

People would not accept selective implementation of the charter, he said.

He added that the election manifesto of the parties must include commitments to sustainable and institutional measures to prevent the misuse of the state apparatus against political opponents.

Karim suggested that the Election Commission, Public Service Commission, Anti-Corruption Commission, National Human Rights Commission, Information Commission, and Anti-Corruption Commission must be strengthened and made accountable to protect people’s fundamental rights after the change of government.

He also said that to establish a democratic state, political parties must adopt democratic practices and remain financially transparent.

He said the manifesto must highlight the pathway to inclusive and sustainable economic development.

While saying that sustainable development was impossible without women’s full participation, he called on the political parties to ensure women’s political empowerment and their rights to education, health and safety.

Chairing the conference, SHUJAN secretary Badiul Alam Majumder, also formber member of the National Consensus Commission, demanded that political parties clearly state in their manifestos whether they supported a ‘yes’ or ‘no’ vote in the event of a referendum.

Shujan treasurer and trustee Syed Abu Naser Bakhtiar Ahmed, national committee member Ekram Hossain, and central coordinator Dilip Kumar Sarker, were also present.

title: EEE dept of DUET holds first reunion
body:
The first alumni reunion of the Department of Electrical and Electronic Engineering of Dhaka University of Engineering and Technology in Gazipur was organised by the department.

The daylong event was inaugurated by DUET vice-chancellor Professor Mohammad Joynal Abedin on Saturday with a colourful procession and through releasing pigeon and balloon.

In his speech as chief guest, the vice-chancellor said, ‘The students of this department are keeping the modern life dynamic through power grid, communication system and silicon technology, and making important contributions at the national and international levels.

The special guest of the event, pro-vice-chancellor Professor Md Arefin Kawsar said, ‘EEE Alumni Reunion is an effective platform to accelerate academic progress, create realistic connections between industry and academia and develop future leadership.’

The dean of the Faculty of EEE, Professor Ruma, director (student welfare) Professor Utpal Kumar Das and first batch alumni Md Abdus Salam Khan also spoke.

The programme was presided over by the head of the department of EEE and convener of the programme Professor Mohammad Zakir Hossain.

Besides, the organising chair of the programme and director (physical education center) Professor Kazi Rafiqul Islam and organising secretary associate professor Md Mizanur Rahman also spoke.

In addition, director (research and extension) Professor Md Anwarul Abedin and Professor Md Raju Ahmed of the EEE department were also present on the stage.

At the beginning of the programme, prayers were offered for the salvation of the soul of the late Khaleda Zia, a three-time former prime minister of Bangladesh.

Organised with the theme of ‘Celebrating the Power of Togetherness’, the alumni reunion witnessed open discussions, sharing experiences and lively exchanges on future research, technological innovation and potential in the industry.

Other parts of the event included documentary screenings, reminiscences, batch-based discussions, group photo sessions, raffle draws and prize distribution.

title: Winter clothes distributed among poor in Rangamati
body:
The Baghaihat battalion of Border Guard Bangladesh distributed winter clothes among poor and needy families at Baghaichari in Rangamati on Saturday.

Battalion commander Lieutenant Colonel Md Mohiuddin Faruki handed over warm clothing to the beneficiaries in the Sealdah Para and Jampara areas. Mentioning that alongside its responsibility of maintaining law and order in the remote hilly border areas, Lt Col Faruki said, ‘The BGB is also committed to the welfare of local people.’

He added that such humanitarian activities would continue in the future to support underprivileged communities. Local dignitaries, including BOP commander Nayak Subedar Md Mashiur Rahman, were present at the event.

More than one hundred poor and needy families received winter clothes during the programme.

title: Chobi Mela to feature artists from five continents
body:
The upcoming 11th edition of Chobi Mela, scheduled for January 16-31, will feature 58 artists from 18 countries across five continents under the theme ‘Re’.

The biennial festival will showcase nine exhibitions across five venues in Dhaka - the Bangladesh National Museum, Bangladesh Shilpakala Academy, Alliance Française de Dhaka, DrikPath Bhobon, and the Bangladesh National Parliament.

Besides the exhibition, a four-day evening programme comprising artist talk, panel discussion, lecture and film screening will be held at Joyeeta Foundation at Dhanmondi.

The festival would also organise six workshops conducted by international artists.

The announcement was made at a press conference held at the Drik Gallery of the Drikpath Bhaban in Panthapath area on Saturday.

The festival’s chief advisor Shahidul Alam, festival director ASM Rezaur Rahman, artistic directors and curators Munem Wasif and Sarker Protick, photographer-researcher Jannatul Mawa, and education director and head of photography department of Pathshala South Asian Media Institute Khandaker Tanvir Murad were present at the event.

Shahidul Alam said, ‘Chobi Mela has always questioned power. This time too, both internationally and in our own country, the extent to which we are questioning power will be evident in the works.’

ASM Rezaur Rahman said that in 2021, amid COVID realities, they held a limited special edition Chobi Mela titled 0 (Shunno).

‘The 11th edition is organised in full scale, under the theme ‘Re’. The prefix ‘Re’ resonates again, anew, or otherwise. As the world and Bangladesh face a new era and looking forward to a new timeline, we have reimagined and reshaped Chobi Mela to reflect that.’ he said.

title: BMU opens specialised clinic
body:
Bangladesh Medical University vice-chancellor Professor Md Shahinul Alam inaugurated the specialised clinic at the former Betar Bhaban of the east campus of BMU on Saturday.

Only patients referred from the outpatient department of BMU can get their necessary medical services there. Currently, from 8:00am to 2:30pm every day, patients can get medical services in rheumatology at room 97, geriatric medicine at room 99, ERRT Center room No 95 and 96, operative dentistry room No 20, dental (periodontology division) room No 98.

After the auspicious inauguration of this programme, the vice-chancellor visited the conference room on the 2nd floor and the classrooms on the 3rd floor of the east campus building.

At this time, BMU’s pro-vice chancellor (administration) Professor Md Abul Kalam Azad, pro-vice chancellor (research and development) Professor Md Mujibur Rahman Howlader, treasurer Professor Nahrin Akhtar, dean of the Faculty of Medicine Professor Shamim Ahmed, director (hospital) Brigadier General Irteka Rahman, chief engineer Md Zafar Iqbal, additional director (super specialised hospital) Md Shahidul Hasan Babul, additional director (hospital) Hasnat Ahsan, deputy director (hospital) Sharif Md Ariful Haque, assistant director of the general emergency department Riyadul Jannat and others were present.

title: Samotol premieres Lutfar Pradeep
body:
New theatre troupe Samotol premiered their maiden production titled Lutfar Pradeep at the Bangladesh Mahila Samity on Saturday.

The premiere show was inaugurated by legendary actress Ferdousi Majumder.

The play, written by renowned filmmaker-translator Tanvir Mokammel and directed by Sagir Mostafa, depicted the story of Lutfa, wife of the last independent ruler of Bengal Nabab Siraj-ud-Daulah, who used to kindle a lamp at Siraj’s grave.

Every evening Lutfa came to the graveyard and recalled the post and pre events of the battle of Plassey.

She narrated the discussion with Siraj’s aunt Ghoseti Begum, Mir Madan’s son Mir Toki, Mohonlal’s younger brother Maniklal, Bakshi Monsur Hossain Khan and two rebel soldiers Hikmat Khan and Govindo Valla who took part in the battle of Plassey.

She refused to visit Jinjira Palace with Siraj’s mother for the safety of her daughter named Umme Jahura.

She also hoped that one day the people of the Bangla will revolt against the British ruler.

After her death, Umme Jahura lights the lamp at the graveyard of Siraj-ud-Daulah who was killed after the battle of Plassey. The monodrama was performed by renowned actress Chitralekha Guha with a special appearance of Umme Jahura performed by Agnila Hazra.

The stage and lighting was designed by Uttam Guha and costume was designed by Wahida Mollicka Jolly.

title: DU geology dept observes 75th anniv
body:
The 75th anniversary celebration of the Department of Geology of Dhaka University was held at the department on Saturday in cooperation with the DU Geology Alumni Association.

Dhaka University vice-chancellor Professor Niaz Ahmed Khan was present as chief guest at the event, chaired by the convener of the organising committee Professor Kazi Matin Uddin Ahmed, also president of the Geology Alumni Association.

Pro-vice chancellor (administration) Professor Saima Haque Bidisha, pro-vice chancellor (education) Professor Mamun Ahmed, treasurer Professor M Jahangir Alam Chowdhury and dean of the Faculty of Earth and Environmental Sciences Professor Md Humayun Kabir spoke as special guests at the event.

Ministry of Local Government Joint secretary Md Shamsul Islam Mehdi, chairman of the department Professor Md Badruddoza Mia and president of Bangladesh Geological Society Professor Badrul Imam delivered the welcome address.

Professor of the department Subrata Kumar Saha expressed his vote of thanks. Professor Sanjida Murshed conducted the programme. Twenty-two retired teachers and professionals of the department were honoured at the programme.

Vice-chancellor Professor Niaz Ahmed Khan called on the alumni to play an effective role in strengthening industry-academia relations, strengthening the relationship between the university and the society, and bridging the gap between academia and professionals.

It is worth noting that a one-minute solemn silence was observed at the beginning of the programme in memory of former prime minister Khaleda Zia.

title: Agriculture cluster admission test held
body:
The agriculture cluster admission test for the 2025–26 academic session, covering first-year undergraduate, honours, programmes of nine public agricultural universities, was held across the country on Saturday.

The examination began simultaneously at 2:00pm countrywide and concluded within the scheduled one-hour duration, said a press release.

Comprehensive preparations had been undertaken well in advance under the leadership of Gazipur Agricultural University, the coordinating institution of this year’s agriculture cluster to ensure the smooth and transparent conduct of the examination.

Against a total of 3,701 available seats, 88,228 students applied for admission, resulting in an intense competition of approximately 24 candidates per seat.

Among the total applicants, 6,336 candidates appeared at examination centres hosted by Gazipur Agricultural University.

The examination results will be announced within January 7.

Detailed results and all admission-related information will be made available on the official agricultural cluster website: https://acas.edu.bd.

During the examination, the overall situation was closely monitored through on-site visits by GAU vice-chancellor Professor GKM Mustafizur Rahman.

Expressing satisfaction after visiting examination centres, the VC said that the nationwide, synchronised cluster-based admission test was conducted smoothly through collective planning, sincere cooperation and timely preparation.

Emphasising student welfare, he highlighted the provision of special transportation services, information centres and essential humanitarian support, including safe drinking water.

Praising the efforts of teachers, officers, staff and student volunteers, he further noted that Gazipur Agricultural University viewed the admission test not merely as an evaluation, but as the first step in shaping students’ futures and reaffirmed the university’s continued commitment to a humane, transparent and student-friendly education system.

The examination was held in a fair and peaceful manner at the Chittagong Veterinary and Animal Sciences University (CVASU) and its three sub-centres — University of Science and Technology Chittagong, Chittagong Government Mahila College and Pahartali College.

CVASU vice-chancellor Professor Mohammad Lutfur Rahman inspected the examination centres. Deputy director (external programmes) Professor AKM Saifuddin, deputy director (One Health Institute) Professor Md Ahsanul Haque, deputy director (student welfare) Professor Mohammad Rashdul Alam and proctor Professor Mohammad Mahbubur Rahman accompanied him.

The vice-chancellor expressed his gratitude to all concerned for conducting the examination peacefully at the University and its three sub-centres.

CVASU registrar Ramiza Faruk Imam said that a total of 6,167 candidates took the exam at four centers in Chittagong. The attendance rate was 90.88 per cent.

title: 2025 low on cultural events
body:
Most of the cultural institutions could not hold events in 2025 because of mobbing, often attributed to Tawhidi Janata, and the government’s failure to stop mobbing.

Popular events such as Sharat Utsab, concerts and fairs were either postponed or interrupted across the country on security reasons.

Cultural activists alleged that the cultural affairs ministry had failed to create an inclusive environment and claimed success in large-scale events that the ministry held.

The Bangladesh Shilpakala Academy and the Bangla Academy, however, faced a lack of funds.

Chattogram-based theatre activist Sahriar Hannan said that many theatre troupes’ shows were postponed after the July uprising due to previous Facebook posts of theatre activists.

‘In 2025, many cultural events, including the Bengali New Year celebration, were cancelled due to mob attacks. The administration did not permit outdoor cultural events, even protest events, due to security concerns,’ he said.

He said that theatre shows and festivals are held regularly only at Chattogram Shilpakala Academy and Theatre Institute Chattogram but the shows are not allowed to be held at any other places in the city now.

Artist and singer Amal Akash said that the failure of the government to ensure the safety and security affected the cultural events and overall cultural practice in 2025.

‘After the mass uprising, mob violence, attacks on shrines and national and religious minorities created frustration. Some Kawali events raised voices for inclusive cultural practice but the hopes had faded due to mob violence,’ Amal Akash said.

He said that the activities of middle-class cultural activists had decreased after the fall of the Awami League regime, as most of them were associated with the party.

Amal Akash, also a Narayanganj-based cultural activist, said that the Narayanganj Sangskritik Jote and cultural organisation Samageet organised cultural events regularly but the situation across the country was not like Dhaka and Narayanganj.

He urged the cultural activists to stand fearlessly in every district to change the situation.

Theatre troupe Bottala founder and creative director, Mohammad Ali Haider, said that the interim government-supported mobs interrupted the cultural events and practices, and festivals across the country.

‘The ministry of cultural affairs organised some grand events and attempted to identify them as the culture of Bangladesh. The cultural practices in marginal areas, mostly baul events, jatra shows and seasonal festival-related fairs, were hampered a lot, but the government focused on mega events which helped mob violence,’ he said.

He alleged that the interim government worked against the cultural practice in the country.

Bangladesh Jatra-Shilpo Unnayan Parishad president Gazi Belayet said that professional Jatra troops had to suffer huge losses as there was no permission to organise shows anywhere in the country during the peak season.

‘Although some local organisers attempted to organise Jatra festivals, political unrest and poor law and order situation forced them to postpone the festivals,’ he said, adding that the troupe owners and artistes have been suffering from financial crisis.

Ferdous Ara Rumee, an organiser of civil society platform Sampriti Jatra, said that after the mass uprising, vested groups attacked cultural activities and women but the interim government remained silent regarding the issues.

‘The vested political forces targeted women in the name of Islamisation in the society, but the government did not take any action to save the citizens of the state,’ she said.

She said that the mobs and online bots targeted women cultural activists.

The cultural activist alleged that the police did not come to save the cultural activists when the July Mancha attacked an event titled ‘Ganer Aartonad’ in the capital’s Shahbagh area, protesting against the arrest of baul singer Abul Sarkar.

The police also did not save the victims when bauls came under attack in various parts of the country, she alleged.

‘The government ensured the security neither for cultural events nor for activists but organised mega events which promote anti-cultural activities in the country,’ she alleged.

Cultural affairs secretary Md Mafidur Rahman, however, denied the allegations made by the cultural activists and claimed that there was a lack of information on which they made the allegations.

He said that the funds and number of events organised by the ministry had increased in number in 2025.

Besides regular events, he said, the ministry had organised the 36 July and Lalon Utshab across the country.

He claimed that the ministry was the first to respond to any problem faced by any organisations in holding any programme.

title: COLD-RELATED DISEASES: 44 dead, 95,000 hospitalised
body:
At least 44 people died of winter related infections of Acute Respiratory Infection and diarrhoea and 95,378 others were hospitalised until Saturday 8:00am since November 1 this year.

According to the Directorate General of Health Services, 40 of the deaths were caused by ARI and four people died of diarrhoea.

ARI is a general term for short-term infections affecting the sinuses, throat or lungs, often viral but sometimes bacterial, causing symptoms, including cough, fever and breathing difficulty, and is a major health concern, especially for young children.

According to the World Health Organisation, ARI typically ranges from mild conditions like the common cold to severe illnesses, such as pneumonia and bronchiolitis.

The DGHS reported that of the ARI deaths, the highest 16 deaths were recorded in Chattogram division,  two were reported in Dhaka division, nine in Mymensingh, two in Rangpur, seven in Khulna and four in Sylhet.

All the four diarrhoeal deaths happened in Chattogram.

The Bangladesh Meteorological Department reported that a mild cold wave that had been sweeping through nine districts would continue before intensifying into a moderate one from Tuesday.

Both the day and the night temperatures will fall further after 48 hours.

In its monthly weather forecast released on January 1, the BMD forecast around two severe cold waves to sweep across the country.

The BMD in its daily forecast on Saturday morning said that the mild cold wave was sweeping over districts, including Rajshahi, Pabna, Naogaon, Sirajgonj, Nilphamari, Kurigram, Jashore, Chuadanga and Kushtia, which would continue.

The minimum temperature of 9C was recorded at Rajshai, Ishurdu and Badalgachi and the maximum temperature of 27C was recorded in Teknaf in the past 24 hours ending at 8:00am, said Kazi Jebunnesa, assistant meteorologist at the BMD.

Public health experts say that during winter, virus and bacteria survive for long time in the air, infecting more people, while worsening air pollution at the same time was causing serious public health issues.

They have advised people to take preventive measures, including wearing masks and warm clothes, limiting outdoor exposure, and refraining from smoking and alcohol consumption.

title: Knife, arson attack victim trader dies
body:
A trader, who was critically injured in a knife and arson attacks in Shariatpur’s Damudya upazila on Wednesday, died while undergoing treatment at Dhaka Medical College Hospital on Saturday.

The victim, Khokon Chandra Das, 45, son of Paresh Chandra Das of Tilai village in Kaneshwar union under Damudya upazila, succumbed to his injuries at DMCH at about 8:00am, according to the police and family sources.

Khokon’s father Paresh filed a case with Damudya police station against three people — Sohag Khan, 27, Rabbi Mollah, 21, and Palash Sardar, 25, early Friday.

However, the police have yet to arrest the attackers.

The attack took place at about 9:30pm on Wednesday near Tilai bazaar in Kaneshwar, according to additional superintendent of police for crime and operations Tanvir Hossain.

‘Efforts are on to identify and arrest the accused at the soonest,’ he added.

Miscreants suddenly attacked Khokon while he was returning home after closing his pharmacy. They first intercepted him and stabbed him in the abdomen and head, leaving him critically injured, according to the police.

Police and relatives said that the attackers set him on fire presumably as he recognised them. Hearing his screams, locals rushed to the spot, forcing the attackers to flee.

To save himself from the flames, Khokon jumped into a nearby pond. Local people rescued him and took him to Shariatpur Sadar Hospital in critical condition.

After initial treatment at the emergency department, doctors referred him to DMCH around 11:30pm the same night as his condition worsened.

Khokon underwent surgery on Thursday afternoon, but he succumbed to his injuries Saturday morning, said the family members.

The police said that preliminary findings suggested that the attackers targeted him for the cash he was carrying.

Bangladesh Puja Udjapan Parishad’s Shariatpur district president Amit Ghatak Chowdhury expressed deep sorrow at the death and demanded the highest punishment for the attackers.

title: Inquilab Mancha campaigns for justice
body:
Inquilab Mancha on Saturday campaigned at different points in Dhaka city under its preannounced ‘March for Insaf’ programme, demanding arrests and trial of the killers of its convener Sharif Osman Hadi.

On the day, Inquilab Mancha leaders and activists campaigned at Shahbagh, Ramna, Farmgate, Karwan Bazar and other spots, pressing the platform’s four-point demand, said its publication secretary Fahim Abdullah.

The demands include an ultimatum for the interim government to complete the trial against Hadi’s killers by January 20 and the cancellation of work permits for Indians currently staying in Bangladesh.

Their demands also include filing a case against India with an international court if it refused to return convicted asylum seekers, and identifying what the platform described as ‘collaborators of fascists’ within civil and military intelligence agencies and their arrest and trial.

Fahim said that Inquilab Mancha would continue its ‘March for Insaf’ campaign till January 6 and was likely to announce tougher street demonstrations, including indefinite sit-in or countrywide general strike, after January 7 if the authorities failed to identify and arrest Hadi’s killers and submit the charge sheet of the Hadi murder case.

Foreign affairs adviser Md Touhid Hossain, meanwhile, said that there was no scope for haste in the trial process and the government was trying to bring back those involved in Hadi murder, reported New Age correspondent in Munshiganj.

Addressing questions from journalists after attending commemorative programmes on July uprising martyrs in Munshiganj, Touhid said that the whereabouts of the accused were not identified yet.

The government was working to bring those involved in Hadi murder to justice and was also at work to complete the trial proceedings as soon as possible, said the adviser.

Earlier, Inquilab Mancha blocked the Shahbagh crossing for four days—from December 27 to 29— and also blocked different highways pressing their demands.

Hadi was shot in the head in Dhaka on December 12 while he had been conducting campaign as an independent candidate for the Dhaka-8 constituency in the next general election.

After treatment at Dhaka Medical College Hospital and Evercare Hospital in Dhaka, he was flown to Singapore for advanced treatment and died there on December 18.

Law enforcers have so far arrested 11 people as suspects in the case.

The Dhaka Metropolitan Police on December 28 said that the prime suspect, Faisal Karim Masud, alias Daud, alias Rahul, and his associate Md Alamgir Sheikh fled to India’s Meghalaya.

title: World leaders condemn US attack in Venezuela
body:
World leaders and chiefs of different organisations on Saturday condemned a large scale US strike on the South American country, as Spain offered to mediate for  a peaceful settlement.

US president Donald Trump said earlier that US forces had captured Maduro and flown him and his wife out of the country.

The Venezuelan government decried what it termed an ‘extremely serious military aggression’ by Washington and declared a state of emergency as several leaders allied with Caracas denounced the US action.

United Nations secretary-general Antonio Guterres is ‘deeply alarmed’ after Washington’s strikes on Venezuela, his spokesman Stephane Dujarric said in a statement, adding it could ‘constitute a dangerous precedent.’

The European Union called for ‘restraint’ and respect for international law in Venezuela. ‘The EU has repeatedly stated that Mr Maduro lacks legitimacy and has defended a peaceful transition’ in Venezuela, the bloc’s top diplomat Kaja Kallas wrote on X after speaking with her US counterpart Marco Rubio.

European Commission chief Ursula von der Leyen and European Council president Antonio Costa echoed the message.

‘We stand by the people of Venezuela and support a peaceful and democratic transition. Any solution must respect international law and the UN Charter,’ von der Leyen said on social media.

Costa said he was following developments in Venezuela ‘with great concern’, adding that ‘the European Union calls for de-escalation’.

China firmly opposes US military strikes on Venezuela, calling it a violation of international law. ‘China is deeply shocked and strongly condemns the US’s blatant use of force against a sovereign state and its action against its president,’ Beijing’s foreign ministry said in a statement.

‘Such hegemonic behaviour by the US seriously violates international law, infringes upon Venezuela’s sovereignty, and threatens peace and security in Latin America and the Caribbean. China firmly opposes it,’ it added.

France said US operation in Venezuela undermined international law while no solution to the country’s crisis can be imposed from the outside. Maduro ‘gravely violated’ the rights of Venezuelans, but the military operation that led to him being grabbed ‘contravenes the principle of non-use of force, which underpins international law’, foreign minister Jean-Noel Barrot wrote on X.

Iran, which has close links with oil-rich Venezuela, also ‘strongly condemns the US military attack on Venezuela, saying it was a flagrant violation of the country’s national sovereignty and territorial integrity’.

Colombian President Gustavo Petro called the attack an ‘assault on the sovereignty’ of Latin America which would lead to a humanitarian crisis.

Cuba, a traditional regional ally, denounced what it called ‘state terrorism against the brave Venezuelan people’ according to a statement by president Miguel Diaz-Canel, who urged a ‘response from the international community’ following a ‘criminal attack’ on Caracas.

Russia condemned the action as ‘an act of armed aggression against Venezuela.’ ‘This is deeply concerning and condemnable,’ the Russian foreign ministry said in a statement. ‘The pretexts used to justify such actions are untenable. Ideological hostility has triumphed over business-like pragmatism,’ it added.

Germany’s foreign ministry told AFP that ‘we are monitoring the situation in Venezuela very closely and following the latest reports with great concern. The foreign ministry is in close contact with the embassy in Caracas.’

The office of Italy’s prime minister, Giorgia Meloni, said she was ‘closely monitoring the situation in Venezuela, remaining in constant contact with the minister of foreign affairs and international cooperation, Antonio Tajani, also in order to gather information about our fellow citizens.’

Mexico’s left-wing government condemned the US strikes in Venezuela, saying any form of military action ‘seriously jeopardizes regional stability.’

British prime minister Keir Starmer said all countries should ‘uphold international law’. Calling the situation ‘fast-moving’, Starmer added that ‘the UK was not involved in any way in this operation’ as he urged patience in order to ‘establish the facts’.

Brazilian president Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva slammed the US attacks on Venezuela as a ‘serious affront’ to the country’s sovereignty, echoing criticism made by fellow regional heavyweight, Mexico.

Turkey called on all parties to act with ‘restraint’ after the attack. ‘In order to prevent the current situation from leading to negative consequences for regional and international security, we call on all parties to act with restraint,’ the foreign ministry said in a statement.

US senator Brian Schatz, a Democrat, said on X: ‘We have no vital national interests in Venezuela to justify war. We should have learned not to stumble into another stupid adventure by now.’

title: US bombs Venezuela, picks up Maduro, wife
body:
President Donald Trump on Saturday hailed the capture by the US military of Nicolas Maduro, as his attorney general vowed the Venezuelan leader would face the ‘full wrath’ of American justice.

Maduro and his wife both face drug and terrorism charges in the United States, which has waged a months-long pressure campaign against the leftist president.

In a stunning denouement, the US army’s elite Delta Force snatched the Maduros as bombs fell on Caracas, US media reported, with Trump set to give further details in a press conference at 1600 GMT.

‘The United States of America has successfully carried out a large scale strike against Venezuela  and its leader, president Nicolas Maduro, who has been, along with his wife, captured and flown out of the Country,’ Trump said on Truth Social.

‘This operation was done in conjunction with US Law Enforcement,’ added Trump, who is at his Mar-a-Lago residence in Florida, near the end of a two-week Christmas and New Year’s vacation.

In a brief phone interview with The New York Times, Trump said ‘it was a brilliant operation, actually.’

‘A lot of good planning and lot of great, great troops and great people,’ the paper quoted Trump as saying—adding that he did not answer a question about whether he had sought congressional approval.

US attorney general Pam Bondi said Maduro and his wife Cilia Flores had been indicted in the Southern District of New York on charges including ‘Narco-Terrorism Conspiracy,’ conspiracy to import cocaine, and charges related to machineguns.

‘They will soon face the full wrath of American justice on American soil in American courts,’ Bondi said on X.

The indictment against Maduro was lodged in 2020 while the indictment against his wife was not previously known. Trump’s administration in August doubled a reward for information leading to his capture to $50 million, accusing him of leading the alleged ‘Cartel of the Suns’ drug trafficking organization.

The US military action was now complete with ‘no further action in Venezuela now that Maduro is in US custody,’ a senator quoted secretary of state Marco Rubio as saying.

The strikes on Venezuela were designed to ‘protect and defend those executing the arrest warrant,’ said Mike Lee, a Republican initially critical of the operation, wrote on X.

Rubio meanwhile reposted a social media message from earlier this year in which he said Maduro was not the legitimate president of Venezuela following elections that international observers said were riddled with irregularities.

Rubio’s number two hailed a ‘new dawn’ for Venezuela. ‘The tyrant is gone. He will now—finally—face justice for his crimes,’ Deputy secretary of state Christopher Landau wrote on X.

Trump has given differing arguments for his campaign against Venezuela, including the claim that the country is a major drug exporter to the United States and that Venezuela seized US oil interests.

Trump’s claim of Maduro’s capture comes just two days after the Venezuelan attempted renewed engagement, offering cooperation on fighting drug trafficking and illegal migration.

The capture of Maduro came—coincidentally or not—on the anniversary of Panamanian leader Manuel Noriega’s surrender to US forces on January 3, 1990. Noriega was then tried and jailed in the United States.

It also comes on the anniversary of a US strike that killed Iranian Revolutionary Guards commander Qasem Soleimani on January 3, 2020, in Baghdad.

title: BNP leader shot dead
body:
A local leader of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party was shot dead by unidentified miscreants near the office of a ward councillor at Shankarpur in Jashore town on Saturday night.

The deceased is Alamgir Hossain, 55, general secretary of ward number 7 of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party under Jashore Municipality.

Syed Saberul Haque Sabu, president, Jashore district unit of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party, confirmed the victim’s political identity without further details.
