But the Bangladesh bowling attack proved too much for the USA batters, nabbing consistent scalps in the second half of the innings. Nahida Akter was the pick of the bowlers, finishing with bowling figures of 4/24 from her four overs.

Ritu Moni played a second fiddle to her with 3-24 to further wreck havoc as USA managed to put up 137-9 in 20-over allocation before losing the game.

Bangladesh will take on Papua New Guinea, Namibia and Ireland tomorrow, 22 and 24 respectively in their next three matches of Group A.

The top three teams from Group A will advance to the Super Six stage, where they will face the top three sides from Group B.The Group B included hosts Nepal, Thailand, Zimbabwe, Netherlands and Scotland.

The top four teams from the Super Six will, qualify for the ICC Women’s T20 World Cup, be held in England and Wales in June-July this year.

title: Hridoy hits ton: Rangpur beat Naoakhali in BPL Cricket
body:
Rangpur Riders beat Noakhali Express by eight wickets in their tenth match of the Bangladesh Premier League (BPL) Cricket at the Sher-e-Bangla National Cricket Stadium in the capital’s Mirpur on Sunday.

Chasing Noakhali’s fighting total of 173 for the loss of two wickets in the allotted 20 overs, Rangpur romped home making 174 for the loss of two wickets when they had just two balls to hand.

Opener Towhid Hridoy of Rangpur Riders led his team from the front line making a superb 109 from 63 deliveries. He hit 15 fours and two sixes before he was bowled out by Hasan Mahmud when Rangpur’s total was 165 for the loss of two wickets.

It is the second century in this year’s ongoing BPL Cricket. Najmul Hossain Shanto of Rajshahi Warriors hit the first century (101*) in the 12th edition of BPL Cricket.

Towhid Hridoy reached the fifty-run landmark using 27 deliveries with nine fours and one sixer. Towhid Hridoy was adjudged the Player of the Match for his match-winning innings.

Rajshahi Warriors confirmed their play-off berth gaining 16 points from 10 matches, while Chattogram Royals reached the play-off berth bagging 12 points from nine matches. Chattoram were set to face Dhaka Capitals in their last league match on Sunday.

Rangpur Riders confirmed their play-off berth grabbing 12 points from 10 matches.Sylhet Titans also reached the play-off berth earning 10 points from 10 outings.

Earlier, Hassan Eisakhil of Noakhali express remained unbeaten with 107 runs. His 72-ball innings was belted with 11 sixer and four fours. It is the third century in this year’s BPL Cricket.

Rangpur Riders had a solid start with two openers Towhid Hridoy and Dawid Malan put on together 78 runs in the opening stand before Dawid Malan (15) was dismissed by Zahir Khan when Rangpur’s total was 78.

After Dawid Malan’s dismissal, Towhid Hridoy and Litton Das built a worthy partnership scoring together 87 runs in the second wicket stand before Hridoy was dismissed.

Litton Das remained unbeaten with 39 runs. His 35-ball knock had two fours and a sixer.

After Hridoy’s departure. Litton Das and Khushdil Shah helped their side to reach the winning target.

Hasan Mahmud and Zahir Khan got one wicket each conceding 23 and 27 runs respectively.

Noakhali made a good start as their openers Hassan Eisakhil and Rahmat Ali put up 32 runs for the opening stand before Rahmat Ali (9) was caught by Litton Das off Nahid Rana.

After Rahmat Ali’s departure, one-down Jaker Ali (3) was bowled out by Aliss Al Islam when Noakhali’s score was 36 for the loss of two wickets.

Then, Hassan Eisakhil and Haider Ali made a notable partnership scoring together 137 runs in the unbroken third wicket stand before Noakhali’s innings came to an end.

Haider Ali remained unbeaten with 42. His 32-ball knock had three fours and a sixer.Aliss Al Islam and Nahid Rana took one wicket each for 22 and 40 runs respectively.

title: Chris Woakes joins Sylhet Titans
body:
The line-up for the last four of the Bangladesh Premier League (BPL) Cricket has already been finalised.

Sylhet Titans have reached the playoffs, and immediately after confirming the playoffs, they have added English star pacer Chris Woakes to the team. This time, the franchise has brought Sam Billings into the team.

Woakes arrived in Bangladesh from England on Saturday. He joined the team’s practice on Sunday.

The English star sweated in the nets of the BCB-NCA Ground of the Sher-e-Bangla National Cricket Stadium in Mirpur in the afternoon.

Another teammate of Woakes, Sam Billings, is also joining Sylhet. On Sunday the team’s advisor Fahim Al Chowdhury confirmed his inclusion in the team on social media.

Like Woakes, Billings has also been brought into the team by Sylhet on a direct contract. Franchise sources said the English star is scheduled to arrive in the country today.

Moeen Ali and Ethan Brooks are already with the team. Oakes has already joined. Billings’ arrival is also confirmed.

title: Perfect start for Carrick with derby win: Arsenal held by Nottingham Forest
body:
Michael Carrick debuted with the best possible result on Saturday as Manchester United beat local rival Manchester City 2-0 at Old Trafford.

Bryan Mbeumo finished off a perfect counterattack to put United ahead in the 65th minute, and Matheus Cunha then squared the ball for Patrick Dorgu to double the lead in the 76th minute and seal the points for the home side.

City struggled to contain its neighbor’s pace throughout the match, and once again Erling Haaland struggled to make an impact at Old Trafford.

Arsenal was unable to take full advantage of Manchester City’s defeat, as a solid defensive display from Nottingham Forest held Mikel Arteta’s side to a 0-0 draw, although the result still stretched its lead at the top of the table to seven points.

Joao Pedro’s first-half goal from Enzo Fernandez’s assist steadied nerves and put Chelsea on the way to a 2-0 home win over Brentford in Liam Rosenior’s league debut as Chelsea coach.

Brentford started the day above Chelsea in the Premier League, but Cole Palmer’s 76th-minute penalty assured Rosenior’s side three points that lifted Chelsea above its South London neighbor.

Florian Wirtz continued his positive scoring run to put Liverpool ahead against struggling Burnley, but Scott Parker’s side again showed its fighting spirit, with Marcus Edwards equalizing in the 65th minute with Burnley’s only shot on target.

Liverpool had 11 shots between the posts but was unable to find a way past Martin Dubravka in the Burnley goal.

Enzo Le Fee and Brian Brobbey got Sunderland back to winning ways with a 2-1 home victory over Crystal Palace.

Yeremy Pino had put Crystal Palace ahead, but 24 hours after coach Oliver Glasner announced he would leave at the end of the season, his side was unable to hold on.

Lukas Nmecha’s low strike at the start of injury time gave Leeds United a 1-0 win at home to Fulham, a result made even more significant as West Ham gave itself a lifeline with a 2-1 win away to Tottenham.

Callum Wilson scored a 93rd-minute goal for West Ham, after the match had looked to be heading for a draw with Crysencio Summerville putting West Ham ahead after 15 minutes and Cristian Romero leveling from Pedro Porro’s assist with 26 minutes left.

title: Sabalenka belatedly comes good to win AO opener
body:
An error-strewn Aryna Sabalenka made a stodgy start to her Australian Open (AO) title charge with a 6-4, 6-1 win over French wildcard Tiantsoa Rakotomanga Rajaonah on Sunday.

The world number one, who is chasing a third Melbourne crown in four years, faces Anastasia Pavlyuchenkova of Russia or Chinese qualifier Bai Zhuoxuan next.

The 27-year-old Belarusian, fresh from winning the season-opening Brisbane International, made a sloppy start in losing the first three points of the match when serving.

In front of the watching Roger Federer, Sabalenka clawed back to deuce but then misfired again to fall a game down in front of a shocked Rod Laver Arena.

Sabalenka, who is favourite to add a fifth Grand Slam title to her career haul, pulled back level but if she expected the spirited world number 118 to melt away, it did not immediately happen.

The reigning US Open champion offered an apology to her underdog opponent at 4-4 when she unleashed a forehand into the 20-year-old’s head.

Sabalenka’s error count was rising but she finally broke Rakotomanga Rajaonah’s resistance to claim the first set, then eased home in the second.

Sabalenka was stunned in the Melbourne final by Madison Keys of the United States a year ago.

title: Bangladesh 3-3 draw with Bhutan
body:
Bangladesh women’s team played out to a 3-3 goal draw with Bhutan in their second match of SAFF Women’s Futsal Championship was held at Nonthaburi Stadium in Bangkok, Thailand on Saturday.

Although Bangladesh fell behind twice in the match, they eventually came back to win with a point.

Bhutan took a one-goal lead in the first half of the match. Bangladesh equalized through Sumaya Matsushima’s goal. She scored with a long-range shot from midfield. As a result, the first half ended in a 1-1 draw.

Bangladesh missed a few opportunities at the beginning of the second half. But Bhutan again took the lead scoring two goals in a span of three minutes. Sonam Lhamo scored the second goal in the 27th and third for her team in the 30th minute.

Despite falling behind, Sabina continued to fight. Skipper Sabina Khatun reduced the margin scoring the second goal for Bangladesh in the 35th minute and Masura Parvin leveled the margin scoring the third goal in the 36th minute of the match.

Bangladesh secured four points from two matches while Nepal bagged two points playing the same number of matches.

Earlier, Bangladesh made a winning start in the tournament beating India by 3-1 goals in their opening match.

Thanks to skipper Sabina Khatun who played a key role behind the Bangladesh victory scoring a brace. On the other hand, Bhutan played out to a 1-1 goal draw with Pakistan in their opening match.

Bangladesh will play their next matches against Nepal (January 19), Sri Lanka (January 21), Pakistan (January 23) and Maldives (January 25) at the same venue.

The table toppers at the end of all seven rounds of matches will be crowned in the SAFF Women’s Futsal champions.

title: Tigresses take on USA to open ICC T20 WC Qualifiers
body:
Bangladesh Women’s team will take on USA to kick-start their ICC Women’s T20 World Cup Qualifiers campaign today at Upper Mulpani Cricket Ground.

Drawn in Group A, Bangladesh will also face off Ireland, Namibia and Papua New Guinea to qualify to the ICC T20 World Cup to be held in England and Wales in June-July this year.

The Bangladesh Women’s team however had a superb preparation in the build up to the tournament as they won both of their official warm-up matches.

They had beaten Netherlands by 26 runs in the first game before registering a dominating 34-run victory over Thailand in the second and final warm-up match.

Bangladesh will take on Papua New Guinea, Namibia and Ireland on January 20, 22 and 24 respectively.

The top three teams from Group A will advance to the Super Six stage, where they will face the top three sides from Group B.

The top four teams from the Super Six will qualify for the ICC Women’s T20 World Cup.The Group B team is formed with Nepal, Thailand, Zimbabwe, Netherlands and Scotland.

title: BCL to begin January 25
body:
The Bangladesh Championship League (BCL), the second tier-professional football league of the country will begin from January 25 with three matches billed for the opening day at three separate venues.

In the first round matches on the day, Khelaghar Samaj Kalyan Samity will take on City Club at Fortis ground Jalshiri, Wari Club will face Dhaka Wanderers Club at Bashundhara Kings arena practice ground and Little Friends Club will play against BRTC Sports Club at Shaheed Barkat Stadium in Gazipur.

In the remaining first round matches on the following day (January 26), Dhaka Rangers Football Club will meet Chittagong Abaani Limited at Shaheed Barkat Stadium in Gazipur while Chattogram City Football Club will take on Shuktara Jubo Sangsad at Fortis Grond (Jalshiri).

title: Rangpur advance to play-offs after eliminating Dhaka
body:
Rangpur Riders secured a place in the BPL playoffs by defeating Dhaka Capitals by 11 runs at the Sher-e-Bangla National Cricket Stadium on Saturday.

Contrasting half-centuries from openers Dawid Malan and Towhid Hridoy powered Rangpur Riders to an 11-run victory over Dhaka Capitals confirming their place in the Bangladesh Premier League (BPL) playoffs as the final qualifying team.

Dhaka Capitals, along with Noakhali Express, have also joined the list of teams eliminated fromthe tournament. On the other hand, Rajshahi Warriors, Chattogram Royals and Sylhet Titanshave secured the play-offs ahead of Rangpur.

Despite the win, Rangpur are set to play the Eliminator against Sylhet Titans, with Rajshahi Warriors and Chattogram Royals having already secured the top two spots on the points table.

Former England opener Malan starred with a fluent 78 off 49 balls, an innings laced with eight fours and four sixes.

Hridoy, in contrast, went through a scratchy knock. He survived three chances and struggled for timing for much of his stay but still managed a crucial 62 off 46 balls, hitting five fours and four sixes.

Together, they added a record 126 runs for the opening wicket, Rangpur’s highest opening partnership in BPL history, surpassing the previous best of 124 set by Soumya Sarkar and Steven Taylor.

The stand laid the platform for Rangpur to post a competitive 181-4.Rangpur then leaned on their bowlers, led by a venomous spell from fast bowler Nahid Rana, who returned outstanding figures of 3-11.

Nahid dismantled Dhaka’s middle order, dismissing Saif Hassan and Sabbir Rahman in his first spell before coming back to remove skipper Mohammad Mithun for 25, leaving Dhaka reeling at 99 for 6 in the 14th over.

Although Mohammad Saifuddin mounted a late counterattack with an unbeaten 58 off 30 balls, support from the other end was minimal and his effort ultimately proved in vain as Dhaka were restricted to 170-7.

Earlier, Fahim Ashraf also played his part for Rangpur by claiming 2-43 to check Dhaka’s top order.

Saifuddin contributed with the ball as well, taking 2-33 to prevent Rangpur from pushing past the 200-run mark despite their strong start.

Kyle Mayers was the only other Rangpur batter to make a notable contribution, scoring 24 off 16 balls, while the rest of the lineup failed to reach double figures.

title: Army suffer first defeat in WFL
body:
Bangladesh Army Sports Club suffered their first defeat in the Women’s Football League ( WFL) when they were beaten by Farashganj Sporting Club by a lone goal was held at Bir Shreshtha Shaheed Shipahi Mohammad Mostafa Kamal Stadium in the city’s Kamalapur on Saturday.

After the barren first half, Shamsunnahar Jr. scored the all-important goal for Farashganj in the 82nd minute of the match. Farashganj’s striker Shamsunnahar Junior has been named the best player for five consecutive matches.

Shamsunnahar Junior has scored 19 goals in 5 matches in the ongoing league.“This match was a challenge for us.

I won with my goal, it feels good. I was the best in all five matches. After being the best in four consecutive matches, it felt like a record,” Shamsunnahar said.

Farashganj captain Maria Manda said, “Not all the matches in the league are over. There are tough matches. It will be tough to win the title.

But we are confident. Most of the army team is from the national team. We were able to beat them.”

Unnoti Khatun of Bangladesh Army was shown direct red card by the referee in the 90th minute for her unsporting behavior in the match.

title: U19 World Cup at toss in Bangladesh vs India match
body:
The captains of the Bangladesh and India under-19 teams abstained from exchanging customary handshakes at the toss ahead of the match between the two sides at the Under 19 World Cup.

The development comes amid cricket ties between the two countries taking a hit after the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) ousted Bangladesh fast bowler Mustafizur Rahman from the Indian Premier League (IPL) citing “recent developments”.

The toss saw the Bangladesh skipper seeing the rub of the green going his way. After winning the toss, he opted to bowl first.

It was then that Mhatre took a step back voluntarily as he snubbed the customary handshake at the toss. Even the Bangladesh captain did not take a step forward as he marched ahead to talk to the broadcaster.

Mhatre and Abrar even avoided eye contact, and the two just went about their business separately.

A few minutes later, the two teams made their way to the middle for the national anthems.

There was also no interaction between the players from both teams. Not just this, India’s opening batter, Vaibhav Suryavanshi, was also seen having a word or two with the Bangladesh players as the latter tried their best to distract him.

It is worth noting that tensions between India and Bangladesh continue to rise, and Bangladesh has even refused to travel to India for the upcoming T20 World Cup, set to begin on February 7.

The Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB) has sent multiple emails to the ICC, requesting that the ICC shift its matches to Sri Lanka.

title: Tigresses complete good preparation with victory
body:
Bangladesh women’s cricket team are in Nepal to participate in the upcoming T20 World Cup Qualifiers. Nigar Sultana Joty played two warm-up matches before the start of the Qualifiers.

The Tigresses won both matches. In the last warm-up match, the red-green representatives defeated the Thailand women’s cricket team by 34 runs on Friday.

Bangladesh came out to bat at the beginning of the match held at Mulpani in Nepal. Opener Juairia Ferdous was dismissed for 31 runs off 29 balls after hitting two fours and a six.

Then, Sharmin Akter and Captain Nigar Sultana Joty gifted the team a 51-run partnership. Sharmin was dismissed for 28 runs off 31 balls and Joty for 28 runs off 22 balls.

And in the end, Shorna Akter scored 15 off just 14 balls, while Shabana Mostari remained unbeaten on 24 runs. Bangladesh scored 149 runs for the loss of 4 wickets in 20 overs.

In reply to 150 runs, Thailand started losing wickets from the start. Only two batters were able to touch the 10-run mark with the bat. Nannapat Koncharekai scored a fifty.

He scored 52 runs off 48 balls. Chanida Suthiruag scored 25 runs off 18 balls. Thailand scored 117 runs for the loss of 7 wickets in 20 overs.

Faria Trishna took the highest two wickets for Bangladesh. Three bowlers took one wicket each.
